Present-count dumps are not scene-exact across runs (load times shift the A-mash route); dump many frames and pair them by image difference.
- **Lighting preset (2026-11-12, `SNAP_LIGHTING=high`, `host/mods/gamemods.cpp`, `runtime/nvn/nvn_draw.cpp` `ShadowDistanceOnBind`, `runtime/nvn/nvn_entry.cpp`):** `SNAP_SHADOW_RES` (dynamic + static maps), `SNAP_SHADOW_DISTANCE=<1..16>` (new, original 1), `SNAP_SSAO_QUALITY`, `SNAP_SSAO_RADIUS`, `SNAP_SSAO_STRENGTH` (new, SimpleAO only); `SNAP_LIGHTING=high` = 2048 maps + 2x distance + SSAO high, every explicit switch wins; default is the original lighting. Findings: (1) the dynamic shadow is ONE 1024 ortho map refit every frame around the subject (ortho half-extent about 64 units in the lab yard, 1.4 units near a Pokemon); the cast light view-projection is a 64-byte VS uniform buffer at slot 9 of the ShadowCast draws (rows 0-2 w=0, row 3 w=1, row-vector convention), the receivers read the same matrix remapped to texture space (0.5x, 0.5 offset) at floats 16..31 of a 132-byte buffer at slot 9. `SNAP_SHADOW_DISTANCE` scales the x/y columns by 1/k in guest memory in the `BindUbo` replay op before the GPU mirror sync (idempotent); no guest code was changed and the guest function that fits the ortho box was NOT found (`DynamicShadowFarClip` consumer unknown). The static shadow is 3 further 1024 maps whose receiver matrix has about 290-unit extent; `StaticShadow` pass was off (`+0xf0`=0) in the pass dump, so static resolution only matters if it renders (not scaled separately; `SNAP_SHADOW_RES` covers it). (2) The course render has NO SSAO: the live SSAO objects are HBAO 8x32 and executed only near present 20000 (photo select); contact darkening in the course is baked, so SSAO quality switches do not change it. (3) A/B (`analysis/mods/compare/light_*.png`): 4096 gives cleaner Pokemon ground-shadow edges; the gain is small; 2x distance showed no visible change in ride frames (same-view pairs differ only in UI/butterflies). Frame-time cost could not be measured (6 runs in parallel, SNAP_PERF needs exclusive; 25-30 ms per present noise). Debug: `NVN_SHADOW_LOG=<present>` prints caster/receiver uniform buffers. Hooks need an exe linked against a main lib newer than `snap_gen.py` (the pre-10:00 `build\snap` exe had no `rt_gm_ao_*` hooks).
- **Anti-aliasing (2026-11-12, `runtime/nvn/nvn_aa.cpp`, `nvn_aa_spv.h`, shaders in `host/mods/shaders/`; SMAA and CAS are MIT, notices in `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`):** default is `ssaa2+smaa` with CAS 0.3. `SNAP_AA=off|original|fxaa` is the original path, `none` removes the game's FXAA and adds nothing, tokens combine with `+` (`ssaa2+smaa`). `ssaa2` sets render scale to 2x the window height over 1080 (an explicit `SNAP_RENDER_SCALE` beats the default ssaa2). `SNAP_SHARPEN=0..1` is CAS. `SNAP_AA_AB=<P>` (SMAA/CAS only while present/P is odd) and `SNAP_AA_DUMP=<dir> SNAP_AA_DUMP_AT=<presents>` (writes `aa_p<N>_{before,smaaonly,after}.bmp` of the SAME frame, no UI; 4K pairs in `analysis/mods/compare/4k/`) are test aids; `SNAP_AA_LOG=1` logs each hooked draw, `SNAP_AA_SPLIT=1` shows the original on the left half and the result on the right of one frame. Finding: the game's runtime tonemap is `TonemappingLutPS` (key 5729ba114d4b, no FXAA), so the original has effectively no AA. The four FXAA tonemap variants are patched in SPIR-V (edge test forced false); SMAA and CAS run in place on the tonemap output before the UI pass. The downsample at the present blit is exact 2x2 box only when scale/window is exactly 2; other ratios are plain bilinear. The saved photo JPEG also gets the AA, but the score reads Evaluation data (1920 depth target is untouched). Verified: SMAA and ssaa2+smaa+CAS 0.5 run on `florio_eval` without pipeline errors, crops in `analysis/mods/compare/aa_*.png`. The default run (`4-20261112_114559`, 3840x2160 render) reached photo scoring (Dodrio +2,413; scores vary per run, so equality to the original is not proven). Unverified: frame times, LOD bias/aniso with ssaa2, tex_combo crops, a same-scene original-vs-new pair (the route is not deterministic).
- **NEO-ONE speed and photos per expedition (2026-11-13, `host/mods/neofilm.cpp`, off unless env set; F1 Photos > Expedition, settings keys `neo_speed`, `film`):** `SNAP_NEO_SPEED=0.5..3` scales only the rail ride. Rail object R (x19 in the rail update `0x4c0090`): R+0x30 curve (length at curve+0x3c), R+0x70 progress float, advanced per frame at main+0x4c2de8..0x4c2df0; camera chain `0x38b710` (controller, rail = *(ctrl+0x68)) -> `0x4bf670` -> builder `0x295170` (eye at obj+0xd0), `0x294a50`. Inline hook `rt_gm_neo_speed` at main+0x4c1df4 stores `last + (new-last)*speed`; clock, Pokemon scripts and scoring are untouched. Florio speed 2: leg-1 rate 1.87x, course end about 1.4x sooner. `SNAP_FILM=<n>` (1..999) sets the per-expedition counter: HUD object field +0x2b8 (72 on Florio), live per-frame update `0x393c90` decrements it (main+0x393d98..0x393f84); hook `rt_gm_film_c` at main+0x393d9c (x26 = HUD) overwrites it once per HUD object while it reads 72. The earlier candidate sites 0x37fa48 and 0x3807fc never ran. Florio `SNAP_FILM=100`: HUD read 77 after 23 shots. The album keeps its 1200-entry limit and the game still decides which shots to save. Gotcha: `scripts/elf_xref.py func` prints addresses shifted by +0x1000 against real vaddrs (use `scripts/knobs_lib.py dis`). Dev tracer (`SNAP_NEO_DUMP`, `SNAP_NEO_WATCH`, `SNAP_NEO_CAMFN`, `SNAP_NEO_WATCH_OBJ`; hardware write watchpoints on all threads) lives in the same file; `SNAP_NEO_LOG=1`, `SNAP_FILM_LOG=1` log the mods. Hooks changed: `MAIN_INLINE_HOOKS` gained `rt_gm_neo_speed`, `rt_gm_film_c`.
- **Split LOD / draw-distance switches (2026-11-12, `host/mods/lodanim.cpp` `lod_apply`, hooks unchanged: `0x337ca8`, `0x337ab8`):** `SNAP_LOD_DIST=<1..8>` scales only the LOD0/LOD1/LOD2 switch distances (ratio x m^2), `SNAP_LOD_FORCE0=1` makes every not-culled model LOD0, `SNAP_DRAW_DIST=<1..8>` scales the cull (LOD3, not drawn) distance and never goes inside the LOD switches (cull multiplier = max of the two); the legacy `SNAP_DRAW_DISTANCE=<m>` still scales both. The hook re-runs the compare chain with the model's own 3-float table (`[sp+0x28]` + group*12) and writes `s0` back only when the wanted LOD differs (the exact threshold of that LOD, 0 for culled). F1 Graphics > View rows `gfx_lod_dist` (Detail distance 1-8), `gfx_lod_force0` (Always full detail), `gfx_draw_distance` (now env `SNAP_DRAW_DIST`, 1-8), `gfx_full_rate_anim`; all restart rows, in NO preset (scoring unproven). Camera far plane: NOT found (no builder argument traced); the visible cut-off in the lab yard and Florio ride is the per-instance LOD3 cull, so `SNAP_DRAW_DIST` is the draw-distance control; terrain and sky are not model instances and are not touched. Evidence (4K, `SNAP_RENDER_SCALE=2`, route `lod_yard`, run `1-20261112_215223`, `SNAP_LOD_DIST=8 SNAP_LOD_FORCE0=1 SNAP_DRAW_DIST=8 SNAP_DRAW_DISTANCE_AB=8`, same-pose frames p8487 original and p8495 modded): `analysis/mods/compare/lod_yard_beds_orig_top_lod8_bottom.png` (opened: the mid-distance flower beds go from sparse stems to dense full flowers and grass tufts; the far trees and hill look the same, they were already LOD0) and `lod_yard_changed_px_mask.png` (670k of 8.3M pixels differ: beds, near tree trunk and canopy, plants at the right edge; dialog text also differs by frame). Cost at 4K in the same yard (3 runs queued one after another with other workers' runs going, so indicative only): original 21.7 ms/present (presents 6000-9000), `SNAP_LOD_DIST=4` 24.6 ms (+13%), LOD 8 + force0 + draw 8 25.6 ms (+18%). Scoring (florio_eval, 3 runs, `SNAP_LOD_DIST=8 SNAP_LOD_FORCE0=1` run `1-20261112_231306`; plus `SNAP_DRAW_DIST=8` run `2-20261112_223109`; default rerun `0-20261112_232118`; the first default run `0-20261112_223105` crashed at 17 s in a host null dereference from guest `main+0x904304`, not in lodanim): both modded runs reach photo select with scored photos and no crash: LOD run Dodrio photo with distant Vivillon (Pose 500, Size 127, Direction 866, Placement 799, Other Pokemon 54, total 2,346, `lod_score_dodrio_lod8_force0.png`), LOD+draw run Vivillon 1,552 (Pose 500, Size 33, Direction 143, Placement 789, Other 88). Same ranges as earlier default runs (Dodrio Pose 500, Size 142, Direction 851), but the default rerun reached the professor with no chosen photo (+0 points), so an exact same-photo score comparison is NOT done: the route's photos differ per run. Spawns not compared. Keep everything off until a same-photo comparison exists.
- **LOD follow-up (2026-11-13):** (1) Stack slot checked by disassembly: both hook sites load the LOD table pointer from `[sp, #0x28]` (`0x337cac` main path, `0x337ab8` sub-model path, one function frame, stored once at `0x337754`), so the shared offset is right. (2) The F1 key `gfx_draw_distance` (old env `SNAP_DRAW_DISTANCE`, LOD and cull together) is replaced by `gfx_lod_dist` + `gfx_draw_dist` (env `SNAP_DRAW_DIST`); `runtime/hle/settings.cpp` `read_file` migrates an old saved value (clamped to 8) into both new keys and erases the old one (hle test added). (3) Same-photo score check NOT achieved: 2 default `florio_eval` reruns (`1-20261113_084654`, `1-20261113_085648`, 100 shots each) take different photos (Dodrio vs Emolga in the first opened subject) and mostly show the photo viewer without a score panel; the route's A-mash selection depends on load timing, so the same photo cannot be chosen deterministically from the route, and the modded pair could not be queued (4 run slots held by other workers). Conclusion: the Maximum/Ultra presets do NOT get Detail distance, Always full detail, Draw distance or Full-rate animation until a same-photo comparison exists (an in-game score log or a frame-deterministic photo route is the missing piece). **Known issue:** a default (no mod) `florio_eval` run, `0-20261112_223105`, crashed at 17 s: host null dereference (`0xc0000005`, address 0x10, host rip offset 0x113997) on a guest thread from `main+0x904304` (an NVN host entry), not from lodanim; not reproduced in my later runs.
- **Photo scoring:** scoring must not change. Draw-distance and LOD changes need verification that photo evaluation, visibility tests and spawns behave as on the original path.

### High frame rates

- Stabilize original 60 FPS behavior first, then test true 120/144/240 simulation and rendering.
- If a subsystem must remain at 60 Hz, use explicit render interpolation while reporting its simulation rate separately.
- Input sampling and camera control should run at presentation rate.
- Mod scripts receive delta time in seconds and must not depend on frame counts.
- Lower-rate distant Pokémon animation is a separate optional LOD improvement, not something FPS unlocking fixes automatically.

## Modding plan

### Content loader and packages

- Use layered overlays with per-pack enable state, priority, dependencies, target-version declarations, per-pack settings, and conflict reporting.
- Support existing LayeredFS-style replacement layouts where practical.
- **Entry-level DRP mods (2026-11-11; `docs/mods.md`, `runtime/mods/`, `scripts/mods/make_override.py`):** packs under `%APPDATA%\SnapRecomp\mods\<pack>\<archive>.drp\<entry>.<ext>` replace single DRP entries without repacking, any size. The hook is `MAIN_INLINE_HOOKS` in `recomp/snap_gen.py` (before `main+0x5e3a58`, in the entry worker `0x5e38b0`); changing it needs `main` regenerated.
- Keep original game data out of mod packages. Validate assets and fail with actionable messages.
- Support hot reload for textures, materials, text, and shaders where safe. Models/courses may initially require a course reload.
- Version modded saves, record pack versions, preserve unknown IDs, and provide profiles and automatic backups.

### Asset tooling

- `kwsch/NewSnap` is ISC-licensed and useful for DRP archives, Oodle entries, saves, and MSBT-related handling. Its changer replaces existing entries; it is not a complete new-content system. Do not source the proprietary Oodle DLL from unofficial downloads.
- Existing NUSRCMDLB MaxScript is an importer, not a writer. Build a model exporter with skeleton, material, mesh-group, skin-weight, and LOD validation.
- Build NUTEXB import/export with mip generation, block-linear layout, ASTC/BC formats, and GPU-readback verification.
- Extend DRP handling to add new entries and validate indexes/checksums.
- Add Wwise event/bank mapping and UI format editing only after the exact RomFS structures are confirmed.
- Every writer needs decode -> edit -> encode -> in-game reload validation.

### New Pokémon and courses

- Start by cloning an existing species/course into a new ID and prove the complete path before attempting fully original registries.
- A species pack may require species/form IDs, names, models, animations, sounds, spawns, behaviors, photo scoring, research entries, thumbnails, and save identity.
- A course pack may require geometry, lighting, collision, camera-rail data, spawns, scripts, registration, unlock rules, localization, map/loading assets, scoring, and save handling.
- Decompile the corresponding registries and subsystems rather than assuming filenames alone define content.

### Mod API

- Expose build-ID-guarded semantic hooks, not public raw-address APIs.
- Provide versioned native C ABI events for course load, spawn, photo capture, scoring, save, and UI creation.
- Use a separate host Lua VM for data-driven mod scripts; never execute untrusted mod scripts in the game's own Lua state.
- Native DLL mods require explicit user opt-in because they have full process privileges.

## Settings and accessibility UX

- Use a game-themed layout inspired by the reviewed tabbed settings screenshot: top categories, options on the left, contextual explanations on the right, version/FPS at the edges, and input hints at the bottom.
- Derive typography, icons, shapes, and palette from Snap's own lab/NEO-ONE interface assets loaded locally. Do not copy Hookshot's theme or ship game assets.
- **Owner request (2026-11-11): the F1 menu, profile picker and shader screens must look like they belong in the game.**
  - **Approach:** restyle the ImGui overlay from a measured style reference (`analysis\ui\style_ref.md`). The game's font and UI textures are loaded at run time from `extracted\`, with a plain fallback if they are missing.
  - **Audio:** an Audio tab drives `snap_audio_set_volume`.
  - **Later:** adding an entry to the game's own pause or options menu is only a feasibility check for now.
- **Native PC options in the game's Settings screen (2026-11-13, owner: "native, in game menu for options, not an F1 menu"):** the Settings screen (`option.drp`: `option.lm` layout, `option.lmb` FlatBuffers behavior file, text `Option_UI.msbt`) is data driven. States are tabs (Game, Camera, Button, Sound, Others plus popup states), each with elements (focusable buttons, named events), focus groups (up/down links tried in order) and enter/focus/decide actions (goto frame label, set text, play sound) that use `{Var}` variables the C++ handler (`main+0x728e10`, a std::function: w1 = event, 8 focus, 10 decide, x3 state, x4 element) puts in a state descriptor before SetState (`player->vtable[0x140]`). Row slots `selector_01..06_mc` take widget labels `lb_common` (2 to 4 choices), `lb_pulldown`, `lb_number` (0..10 dots), `lb_play` (button), `lb_hide`. Route chosen: patch `option.lmb` as a local mod pack (`scripts/ui/make_native_options.py`, reader/patcher `scripts/ui/lmb.py`; it only prepends new objects) and connect it with two hooks in `host/mods/nativeopt.cpp`. Values live in `settings.cpp` keys, never the game save. The cursor reaches only elements in the descriptor's element list (+0x90, 0x130-byte entries), so the hook lists the PC elements there. Tab switches are the Lumen player's own (element f2 = target state with f6 = 1; f6 = 4 = back to the previous state; L/R open the state named at +0x30 of the page's Prev/Next element entries); after a switch the player sends event 5 and the handler answers with BuildPage (`main+0x737360`) + SetState, which the hook does for PC states (SetState alone never switches). Working now (2026-11-13): ten PC tabs after "Other" in two sets of five (Quality, Textures, Effects, Output, View | Display, Controller, Mouse, Audio, Photos) with the game's two-choice rows and pulldown popups (a popup is the game's own `PulldownMenu` list element, items registered on the row's decide with `player->vtable[0x148]` as `main+0x776c80` does; the cursor starts on the list header, since `vtable[0x1f0]` (the game's move to the current value, `0x776bb0`) is overridden by the player's first focus; Sharpening and Master volume are pulldowns too: the game's 0..10 slider knob is moved by the game's own tab handler, so it never moves on a PC page), the visual extras at the original look by default (owner 2026-11-13: Anti-aliasing Original/SMAA/SMAA + supersampling (1.5x at 4K), Sharpening Off/Low/Medium, Texture filtering Original/16x, Sharper menu text, Save PNG copies; defaults read from `runtime\hle\visual_defaults.h` at pack build; explicit values, restart), help lines ("Applies after restart." where true), the quality presets, and Restore Default Settings resetting only the open tab (PC tabs: our defaults; game tabs: PC settings untouched); checked by `host\routes\native_options_tabs.txt` (crops `analysis\ui\native_options_tab_*.png`, local). The pack is built from the user's own `option.lmb` by `host\play.ps1` (`--if-stale`; `-NoNativeOptions` skips it). F1 only: PNG folder path, lighting preset, stick dead zones, mouse smoothing, F1 menu scale, bindings, mods, saves, test input. Next: open popups on the current value; drive the slider knob on PC pages; ship the pack step in the installer flow.
- **Option pages (2026-11-12):** tabs Graphics, Display, Photos, Mods and the Audio output mode are table-driven in `runtime\ui\ui_options.cpp`; settings keys map to env names in `kEnvKeys` (`runtime\hle\settings.cpp`), env stays the override. Upscaler and upscaler quality are live restart rows (native, quality, balanced, performance; not in the presets); lighting preset is a disabled "coming soon" row (flip `kSoon` when code lands). "Apply and restart" uses `restart_now`. Tests: `tests\hle\run_options_test.ps1` (details in `host\README.md`).
- **Render pass toggles (2026-11-12, `host/mods/gamemods.cpp` `rt_gm_pass`, `runtime/hle/settings.cpp` `kPassKeys`, F1 Graphics rows Bloom / Depth of field / Film grain / Chromatic aberration, `host/README.md` "Render pass toggles"):** pass objects (42 in the loop, vtable `0xcc4058`) hold their name as a libc++ string at `+0x40` and the enable byte at `+0xf0`; `SNAP_PASS_DUMP=1` + `SNAP_GM_TRACE=1` lists them. `SNAP_PASS_OFF=<names>` zeroes `+0xf0` before the loop reads it, so the pass is not recorded (output targets keep their earlier contents; frames with bloom off were checked valid, no black or garbage). Allowed by default: BloomCreate, BloomDraw, DOFBlurX, DOFBlurY, DOF, FilmGrain, ChromaticAberration. Evaluation, PhotoEditing, PhotoEditingFrame, Capture3D, CaptureCompress, Report, ResizeTexture, Final, UI, Fade, DownsizeTarget, CompositeBlendBuffer are always refused with a log line; other names (SSAO*, Monotone, Gaussian*, Mipmap*, shadow, scene) are refused unless `SNAP_PASS_FORCE=1` (unverified, test only). `SNAP_PASS_AB=<P>` alternates the listed passes every P presents (test aid). The game sets the byte only on scene changes: in the Florio course Bloom is on all the time, DOF is on for a few presents at load, FilmGrain and ChromaticAberration are never on, so those three toggles only matter where the game turns them on (not seen in the course or photo select). **Not verified:** a same-view A/B image of any pass (the camera is never still in the routes; consecutive-present pairs are dominated by motion and jitter), the effect of DOF/grain/aberration when the game does turn them on, SSAO off. florio_eval with all seven passes off still reaches the professor's score (photo 2,430, total 2,375, run `0-20261112_225706`). Very Low: Bloom and DOF off.
- **Quality presets (2026-11-12, `runtime/ui/ui_options.cpp` `kPresets`):** F1 Graphics "Quality preset" row (Very Low, Low, Normal, High, Ultra, Maximum, Custom). The preset is derived from nine rows (render scale, AA, sharpen, aniso, LOD bias, shadow res, SSAO quality, `gfx_ssao_samples`, `gfx_ssao_hbao`), never stored; Normal = all defaults. Sub-native render scale works since 2026-11-12 (below): Very Low = scale 0.5 and the slider starts at 0.5; scale 6 and 8 crash at boot, 4 is the max tested. `SNAP_SHADOW_RES=512` added. Very Low now also sets Bloom and Depth of field to Off (11 preset rows; see the pass toggles note). Details and numbers in `host/README.md`.
- Default categories: Graphics, Audio, Controls, Gameplay, Mods, Accessibility, System. Keep Debug behind an advanced toggle.
- Graphics options include output/render resolution, upscaler, DLSS model, frame cap, pacing, Reflex, HDR, and renderer diagnostics where appropriate.
- Mods UI includes enabled packs, content browser, load order, profiles, dependencies, conflicts, pack settings, hot-reload/restart status, and safe removal.
- Explain every option in plain language and mark immediate versus restart-required changes. Unsupported options must explain themselves rather than silently fail.
- Distinguish simulation FPS, rendered FPS, and generated FPS.
- Include independent UI/text scaling, high contrast, redundant non-color cues, full remapping, toggle/hold options, reduced motion, independent audio categories, subtitle customization, and clear error/apply feedback.

## Validation strategy

- Differential-test AArch64 instructions, SIMD/FP, atomics, jump tables, and whole functions against Unicorn, QEMU, or real ARM64 as appropriate.
- Record interpreted/unresolved targets and feed them into later AOT builds.
- Track import/SVC/IPC/ioctl/shader coverage and fail loudly on unknown behavior during development.
- Build a complete shader census with translation and SPIR-V validation.
- Provide SwitchRECOMP-style frame traces, per-draw inputs/results, watchdogs, and offline draw replay.
- Compare screenshots and render targets against the original path or an external reference.
- Create scripted course replays covering movement, Pokémon behavior, photo capture, scoring, album/editing, saving, and UI.
- Benchmark held-out scenes after correctness, including shader-cold and shader-warm runs. Do not present other projects' performance claims as Snap benchmarks.

HD textures, material swaps, long LOD, NEO-ONE speed, skips, pass toggles, upscaler modes and the score overlay are parked (all off by default; the score overlay is in `analysis\parked\`). Core results go in `analysis\core\`.

PC options move into the game's own options screens, with the game's widgets, font and controller navigation, and are stored through `runtime\hle\settings.cpp`. The F1 overlay stays as a fallback until every row is native.

1. Done 2026-11-11: revision audit, target lock, validated import path, deterministic maps (see Current verified state).
2. Done 2026-11-11: authoritative function list, classes, static render-graph trace, CPU backend evaluation, and the patched RomFS census.
3. DRP unpack and first format pass done. Next: decode the SSBH shader layout into a full shader census (stages, resource bindings, SASS sizes). Recover the FlatBuffers registry schemas from their reader functions in `main`.
4. Try the validated ELF in REA, and compare its function set against `analysis/maps/functions_final.tsv`.
5. Prototype the selected CPU backend and differential tests before building game-dependent runtime code.
6. Follow the playable milestone order: startup -> title -> complete course with photo scoring -> stable 60 -> native 4K/DLAA -> DLSS -> real 120+ FPS and advanced content mods.
- **Perf pass 1 (2026-11-11; `analysis\perf\{baseline,results,proposals,shader_precompile_api}.md`):** the lab intro went from 32.1 to 57.5 fps average.
  - **Pacing:** `Pace()` added a full extra period to every slow frame. Fixed.
  - **Buffer sync:** bound buffers were synced per draw, about 128 MB per frame. They are now synced once per submit.
  - **Pipelines:** an async pipeline service with a persistent `VkPipelineCache` and key list in `%APPDATA%\SnapRecomp\shadercache`. Startup precompile goes through `runtime\nvn\shaderprecompile.h`.
  - **Open risks:**
    - A cold cache skips about 1.4 draws per new pipeline. A photo taken in that window could miss objects, so photo frames must never skip draws.
    - Texture-upload bursts (320-440 ms at scene changes) set the worst lows.
    - The first course was not measured.
  - **Pass 2 design** (`analysis\perf\pass2_design.md`): implement it after the photo worker releases `runtime\nvn`.
    - **Order:** instrumentation, then dirty-page tracking with `GetWriteWatch` (poolsync copies 44-52 MB per frame, about 3 ms), then off-thread texture uploads, then a fast pipeline link with GPL (the RTX 4090 supports it). `present_wait` pacing comes after that.
    - **Finding:** most frames over 50 ms are guest-side stalls (replay under 3 ms). The 1% lows need a CPU-side investigation (game thread, `nn::os`, file I/O), not more renderer work.
- **Perf pass 3 (2026-11-12, CPU side, Florio course; `analysis\perf\results.md` "Scene 2 ... pass 3", `stall_report.py`):** no proven gain.
  - **Numbers:** exclusive benches, course presents 6000-11400. Core release off: 50.9 fps, 1% low 16.8, 134 frames over 33 ms, 28 over 50 ms. Core release on, two runs: 49.3/11.3/211/70 and 56.0/24.1/45/8. The PC was shared with another project's game and tests, so same-config runs differ more than the configs do.
  - **Cause found:** on a quiet run, `nn::os` waits are small in slow course frames (core waits 1-4 ms, file reads and sleeps 0). The frame is a job graph; the presenting `JobWorker`'s NVN replay grows (10-15 ms, up to 45). On a saturated PC, pinned loader threads (`ResourceUncompress` p31) starve for virtual cores held by JobWorkers during replay or GPU waits.
  - **Switches (default off):** `SNAP_NVN_RELEASE_CORE=1` (bridge releases the virtual core in submit/present/finish/SyncWait/acquire; `host\gen_nvn_bridge.py`), `SNAP_OS_CORES`, `SNAP_OS_OVERCOMMIT_US`, `SNAP_OS_RR_US`, `SNAP_PERF_WAIT_MS`. New `SNAP_PERF` output: per-cause blocked time (`gt_*`/`mt_*`/`oth_*` columns, `<base>_waits.csv`, long-wait events naming the waker or the core holders).
  - **HD mods:** the owner's `%APPDATA%\SnapRecomp\mods` slowed hidden-run loading about 15x (present #300 at 131 s vs #4,950 at 145 s with `SNAP_MODS_DIR` empty). Loader threads wait on one lock. Not fixed (`runtime\mods`). Benches use an empty `SNAP_MODS_DIR`.
  - **Next:** the requested NVN changes are in `pass2_design.md` "Pass 3 note" (dirty pages first, then replay sub-scopes).
- **Perf pass 4 (2026-11-13, NVN replay + mods loader; `analysis\perf\results.md` "Florio course, pass 4", `p4_report.py`; switches in `host\README.md` "Performance switches"):** Florio course with owner mods, shared PC, A (old paths) vs B (new) alternated: course 57.2/56.8 fps, 1% low 14.2/24.7, >50 ms 23/7 (A) vs 59.1/58.4 fps, 1% low 28.8/18.4, >50 ms 5/13 (B); native 4K (`SNAP_RENDER_SCALE=2`) 59.3 fps, 1% low 28.9. Pre-course (title, hub, loading) 47-53 fps to 57-58, present 6000 reached 20-50 s sooner.
  - **Changes (default on):** dirty-page buffer sync with `MEM_WRITE_WATCH` + `GetWriteWatch` (`SNAP_SYNC_FULL=1` restores; poolsync 33-37 MB/2.4 ms to 0.6 MB/0.6 ms per course frame, hub 61-66 MB/6-10 ms to 0.7 ms). Texture upload prefetch (deswizzle on workers at `TextureInitialize`, hash-checked at upload; `SNAP_UPLOAD_PREFETCH_MB=0`; upload time per run 1.4-2.1 s to 0.7-0.9 s). Scratch buffer recycling incl. readbacks (`SNAP_SCRATCH_POOL_MB=0`). Mods built-chunk cache (`SNAP_MODS_CHUNK_CACHE=0`). Binary view key. Course replay 5.7-6.1 ms to 3.6-4.5 ms.
  - **Instrumentation:** `SNAP_PERF_SHARED` (perf CSVs on a shared, non-exclusive run), sub-scopes `ensureimg_ms`, `view_ms`, `rendbegin_ms`, `upload_pref`.
  - **Mods 15x:** not reproduced; loader lock waits are small. The earlier read-once file cache had fixed it. Pacing (`present_wait`) not needed: steady course p99 22.6 ms.
  - **Scoring:** a photo still scores (run `1-20261113_112612`, Vivillon, +1,728).
- **Perf pass 5 (2026-11-13 afternoon; `analysis\perf\results.md` "Pass 5"; PC very busy, so only alternating pairs count):**
  - **Integration:** pass 4 + the crash worker's SlotTable/BufferInitialize/watchdog (`build\w\perf5`, owner mods): course 58.0 fps, hub 59.2, no crash. Sound.
  - **`florio_eval.txt` fixed:** f12000-f20000 only A then B (never selects), then pick + Plus from f20000. Repeated picks toggle check marks off, and the old cycle could open photo select right before Plus. Scored with it: Dodrio Total 2,364 (`1-20261113_121414`). It needs about 50 fps to reach the f20000 picks within 590 s (the perf8 check at 30 fps timed out waiting).
  - **Lental loading hang:** not reproduced in 4 eval runs. New `SNAP_DUMP_EVERY=<s>` dumps all guest threads every s seconds (a hang that keeps presenting never trips the 8 s watchdog); run evals with `SNAP_DUMP_EVERY=30` until it recurs.
  - **Upload bursts:** image creation on the prefetch workers (`SNAP_UPLOAD_PREFETCH_IMAGE=1`) and replay-thread queue helping (`SNAP_UPLOAD_PREFETCH_HELP=1`) are both OFF by default. Image creation cut `ensureimg` but doubled the hub burst in two pairs; helping showed no change. New `pref_miss_*` columns show all burst misses are textures never queued or dropped from the budget (none late, failed or changed). Next: split those into "not eligible at TextureInitialize" vs "evicted".
  - **Review fixes:**
    - The write-watch test showed buffered ReadFile is never missed, but unbuffered reads racing a reset are. The fs read path now marks the filled pages.
    - `boot.cpp` checks for an x86-64-v3 CPU at start.
    - Scratch and prefetch env values are clamped, and both pools are drained before `vkDestroyDevice`.
- **Perf pass 6 (2026-11-13 evening; `analysis\perf\results.md` "Pass 6"):**
  - **Miss split:** new `pref_miss_drop` (queued, then evicted by the staging budget) vs `pref_miss_none` (never queued). All burst misses were drops; none were never-queued.

## Visual defaults and bug-hunt fixes (2026-11-13, worker "defaults")

- **Owner chose original-look defaults on 2026-11-13.** With no env var and no saved setting: AA is the game's own FXAA (`SNAP_AA=original`), CAS 0, no forced anisotropy, no UI font supersampling, no PNG photo export. `SNAP_PROFILE=enhanced` turns the old extras back on at once (ssaa2+smaa, CAS 0.30, 16x, font auto, PNG export). Every extra still works alone through its own env name (`SNAP_AA`, `SNAP_SHARPEN`, `SNAP_ANISO`, `SNAP_UI_FONT_SCALE`, `SNAP_PHOTO_EXPORT`; names unchanged) and beats the profile. One table: `runtime/hle/visual_defaults.h` (`snapdef::`, flip `kDefaultEnhanced` to change the default); the F1 menu labels, the preset rows and `nvn_aa.cpp`, `nvn_entry.cpp`, `gamemods.cpp`, `photoexport.cpp` read it. Table in `host/README.md` ("Visual defaults and SNAP_PROFILE"). LOD bias is not a row (automatic is a no-op at 1x). The Quality presets High/Ultra/Maximum now set aniso 16 explicitly.
- **Fixes from `analysis/core/review_extra.md`:** ssaa2 scale capped at 3.0 and 8192 px (a 2160p window used 4.0 = 7680x4320; log `aa: ssaa2 scale capped`); a failed AA setup resets `g_scale.scale` to 1 (only new textures see it, existing targets keep their size); one `HostWindowHeight()` (SNAP_WINDOW_H, window.json, else 720) shared with the upscaler (it used 1080); CAS is off with an upscaler unless `SNAP_SHARPEN` is set; AA UNORM view cache keyed by (image, level, layer) and freed in `DestroyTexture` (graveyard); no `mods.json` = no pack enabled except `native-options` (loader and F1 Mods tab agree); `SaveCache` unique tmp + atomic rename; `PatchTmplEft` publishes a patched copy of the stage (`Tmpl::cur`) instead of editing it in place, fragMods start empty; `pipeline_keys.bin` is validated per record and cut at the first bad one; `Ent::pipe` is atomic; the boot stall watchdog reads guest pointers with `ReadProcessMemory`.
- **Deferred:** async pipeline draw-drops, frame pacing, ExitProcess on close, services_sys items (other workers); native-options pack stays built by `play.ps1` and on by default (owner call if it should be opt-in). Open risk: AaFail lowers the scale after targets exist, so a failure after boot can leave scaled and unscaled targets mixed.

## Repository hygiene

- **Git:** the repo is public on GitHub at `finalpantasy/new-pokemon-snap-recomp` (created 2026-11-11, made public by the owner the same day), with code and two README screenshots only.
  - The local git identity is `finalpantasy` with its noreply email. Never use the global identity.
  - Only the coordinator commits and pushes. Before every push, check that `git grep -i` finds no owner name or email and that `git ls-files` contains no game formats or images.
  - Push using the finalpantasy token (`gh auth token -u finalpantasy`) through a per-command credential helper. The active gh account is a different one.

- `work/`, `extracted/`, `analysis/`, and `tools/` are generated/local and ignored.
- Never commit `.nsp`, `.xci`, `.nca`, `.nso`, `.keys`, extracted RomFS, generated C from the game, NVIDIA binaries, or proprietary SDK files.
- Keep research/source code separate from game-derived artifacts and record tool versions and input hashes for reproducibility.
- **Window options (2026-11-12, code written, NOT yet linked or run):** host/window_opts.cpp (F11/Alt+Enter borderless, monitor, remembered rect, pause + mute on focus loss via host tick freeze and present-hook block because the game imports no focus query, window.json, C API; docs in host/README.md), os_time_pause in runtime/os/os_kernel.cpp, hle::oe_post_message in runtime/hle/services_sys.cpp; frame-cap line for nvn Pace() is request #3 in analysis/mods/nvn_hook_requests.md (applied). Linked and run 2026-11-12: the focus test (`SNAP_WINDOW_TEST=blur@70,focus@90`) shows presents and guest time frozen for the blur, audio output 0, all resumed on focus; F11, monitor moves and a real alt-tab are untested.
- **HDR10 output (2026-11-12, `runtime/nvn/nvn_hdr.{h,cpp}`, `runtime/nvn/shaders/hdr.{vert,frag}`, `nvn_hdr_spv.h` made by `shaders/make_spv.py`; small edits in `nvn_vk.cpp`: extension lists, format pick in `WindowImpl::Recreate`, a branch in `PresentWindowOnce`; `WindowImpl::hdr`):** off by default. `SNAP_HDR=1` enables `VK_EXT_swapchain_colorspace` and `VK_EXT_hdr_metadata`, creates an A2B10G10R10 + HDR10_ST2084 swapchain, sets the static metadata, and replaces the present blit with a PQ pass (sRGB decode, inverse tone map that lifts only the top quarter of the range, Rec.709 to Rec.2020, PQ). `SNAP_HDR_PEAK` (nits, default 1000), `SNAP_HDR_PAPER` (default 200). If the display or driver lacks the format the log says `hdr: A2B10G10R10 + HDR10_ST2084 not offered ... falling back to SDR` and the SDR path runs; a failed pass setup also falls back. Debug: with `NVN_FRAME_DUMP`, `NVN_FRAME_DUMP_POST=1` and `SNAP_HDR=1`, each dump is the raw PQ swapchain image written as `<name>.bmp` (SDR preview with a soft shoulder above paper white) plus `<name>_nits.bmp` (grey to paper white, then blue to red up to peak) and a `hdr: dump ... mean/max nits` log line. Photo capture, thumbnails and scoring read the game's own targets and never see this pass.
  - **Verified:** the hidden desktop DOES create the HDR10 swapchain (`hdr: swapchain 1280x720 fmt=64 colorspace=1000104008 HDR10 ST2084 active`, runs `4-20261112_094357` and `4-20261112_100111`). Opened previews: loading screen, course frames, professor dialogue, photo select; course frames average 100 to 130 nits with a 400 nit maximum (itm only lifts near-white). Validation run (florio_eval, `4-20261112_100111`): 1 error, a `vkCreateGraphicsPipelines` with a BC1 colour attachment at startup, logged before the first present (existing pipeline service, not the HDR pass); the HDR pass gave none. The ImGui overlay and `SNAP_LOOK` problem is fixed (see the HDR overlay entry below).
  - **Scene-tap mode (option a) NOT built, findings:** the scene HDR target is RGBA16F 1920x1080 (NVN format 0x29). The tonemap plus FXAA draw (prog 411 in boot runs, fragment key `724587eedba6`, one sampler) writes straight into the RGBA8 SRGB window texture (0x38, 3 rotating slots), and a later draw (key `0b6e3cad047c`) also writes the window texture. But the loading and menu UI is drawn into the HDR scene target BEFORE the tonemap (many draws with rt0 = the 0x29 target plus a depth buffer), so UI cannot go on top at paper white without replacing the game's tonemap (bloom blend, LUT, exposure, FXAA). That needs its own pass fed with the game's constants; not attempted.
  - **scRGB mode (2026-11-12, owner request):** `SNAP_HDR=off|hdr10|scrgb` (`1` = hdr10). `scrgb` = R16G16B16A16_SFLOAT + EXTENDED_SRGB_LINEAR swapchain, linear Rec.709, 1.0 = 80 nits; fallback chain scrgb -> hdr10 -> SDR with a log line at each step. Both modes: `SNAP_HDR_PEAK_NITS` (default the DXGI_OUTPUT_DESC1 MaxLuminance of the window's output, else 1000; 775 on this PC, also works on the hidden desktop; the old `SNAP_HDR_PEAK`/`SNAP_HDR_PAPER` still work), `SNAP_HDR_PAPER_NITS` (200), `SNAP_HDR_EXPAND` (0..1, default 0.3, how far near-white is lifted: a plain SDR frame cannot separate UI white from a highlight, so the UI is at paper white only for expand 0) and an exponential roll-off above 75% of peak so highlights approach the peak instead of clipping. Verified (runs `1-20261112_105753` scrgb with validation, `1-20261112_114517` hdr10; opened a scRGB title frame): both swapchains active at 775 nits; scRGB run had only the same startup BC1 pipeline validation error as above and no HDR error. Banding probe (`hdr: dump ... sky strip` line: distinct green codes and one code step in the top quarter of the frame, title screen): hdr10 one code = 0.96 to 1.7% of luminance, scRGB one code = 0.05 to 0.08% (fp16). The overlay and `SNAP_LOOK` are handled in both modes (next entry). Photo scoring was re-checked only in hdr10 mode (florio_eval run `3-20261112_101335`: the score screen shows 2,376 for a Vivillon photo); scRGB uses the same untouched game targets. One hdr10 run crashed in a guest thread right after the swapchain was created (`1-20261112_111536`, host rip in the `std::unordered_map<int, TexSlot>` emplace of the texture pool code, other workers were editing `runtime/nvn`); the rerun was fine; triaged 2026-11-12: a null-object dereference in a host NVN entry reached from guest `main+0x91044c` before the first present, not the swapchain path, never reproduced (noted in `analysis/qa/bugs.md`).
  - **Overlay and SNAP_LOOK under HDR (2026-11-12):** with HDR active `PresentWindowOnce` blits the scene into an RGBA8 sRGB scratch image (`snap_hdr::PrepScratch`), runs `snap_look_present` on that scratch, and runs `snap_ui_present` on a second RGBA8 UNORM layer cleared to transparent (the overlay code is unchanged; it only sees a different image and format). `hdr.frag` then composes in linear light: scene gets the inverse tone map and roll-off, the layer (premultiplied, sRGB encoded) is decoded and blended at `SNAP_HDR_PAPER_NITS` after the roll-off, so UI is never lifted; output is PQ (hdr10) or nits/80 (scRGB). Verified with `SNAP_UI_TEST` (F1 at 56 s) and `NVN_FRAME_DUMP_POST`: the open F1 menu is a clean white panel at paper white (hdr10 mean 144 nits, max 199.2; scRGB max 200.0; previews `analysis/hdr/f1_hdr10_menu.png`, `f1_scrgb_menu.png`, opened); validation showed only the old startup BC1 pipeline error. `SNAP_LOOK` was not run under HDR (code path shared with the SDR scratch, untested). Test notes: hidden runs take about 45 s of wall time before the scene appears (black frames before that, not a bug), and the ui-test `key F1 0` posts a second toggle that closes the menu. `SNAP_HDR_DBG=1` clears the scratch red and skips the scene blit.
- **Fast boot (2026-11-12):** `SNAP_FAST_BOOT=1` drops the frame limiter for the first 3200 presents (`SNAP_FAST_BOOT_FRAMES`). Present #3030 (title logo up) at 58.8 s average over 3 exclusive runs before, 42.4 s after. The first ~2070 frames are a black, frame-count-bound load phase that A presses do not skip.
- **Skip dialogue, #18 partial / #17 not done (2026-11-13, `host/mods/skips.cpp`, `SNAP_SKIP_CUTSCENES=1`, F1 Photos tab row "Skip dialogue", off by default):** inline hook `rt_gm_skip_wait` at main+0x676630 (MAIN_INLINE_HOOKS), the cutscene/skit dialogue window's per-present predicate (called every present while the box waits for A, every 3rd present while text types; vtable main+0xc8aff8). While it is active the host holds A for 3 presents every 12 (`hle::input::g_inject_buttons/_until_ns`, ORed in `Hub::poll`), `SNAP_SKIP_DELAY` (6), `SNAP_SKIPS_LOG=1`. The lab cutscene advances with no scripted input (route `skips_dialogue.txt`); no measurable per-present cost (46.7 vs 46.9 presents/s, loaded PC). **Known risk:** the predicate also ran in a Yes/No style pause-menu dialog in one florio_eval run (6 fires, route also pressed A), so choices are NOT proven safe. Non-dialogue cutscenes (course intro, portal) and #17 fast evaluation were NOT implemented: no skip button exists in the lab cutscene (Plus/X/Y do nothing), and the post_tutorial florio_eval route never reached the evaluation in the last run. Discovery tool: `SNAP_SKIPS_REC=<from>,<len>,<out>,<bucket>` (per-bucket function-entry histogram; forces g_fnprof, discovery only).
- **Photo export, gallery, album limit (2026-11-12, album worker; `host/mods/photoexport.cpp`, `tools-src/gallery/`, rows 22 and "Full-res photo export" of `docs/mod-ideas.md`):**
  - **Export (done, verified):** every photo the game JPEG-encodes for the album is also written as a lossless PNG plus a `.json` sidecar (size, JPEG byte size, CRC) to `%APPDATA%\SnapRecomp\photos\`. Two host overrides wrap the lifted `nn::image::JpegEncoder::SetPixelData` and `Encode` (the original still runs, so the saved JPEG is unchanged); a worker thread writes the PNG through WIC. The game passes pixel format 14 (RGBA bytes) at **1080x720**; thumbnails are 240x200 and 204x136 and are skipped (`SNAP_PHOTO_MIN_W`, default 640). 1080x720 is the game's own capture size (its Capture3D target), so this is the full resolution of a photo; it does not follow `SNAP_RENDER_SCALE`. `SNAP_PHOTO_EXPORT=0` disables, `SNAP_PHOTO_DIR` moves the folder, `SNAP_PHOTO_LOG=1` logs each encode. Test runs (`SNAP_SAVE_DIR` set, no `SNAP_PHOTO_DIR`) export nothing, so they never fill the player's folder. Each distinct JPEG is written once per session (the game encodes some photos twice). Checked: a florio_eval run (build\album_test\photos) wrote 15 PNGs; opened `photo_20261112_112222_001.png` (a real Dodrio and Vivillon scene); `analysis/mods/compare/gallery_page.png` shows the gallery with real photos.
  - **Encoder detail:** the first `Encode` calls on a photo return 0xffffffbf (buffer too small) and the game retries with a bigger buffer; only a result of 0 is exported.
  - **Gallery (done for export, partly for album):** `tools-src/gallery` lists the PNG exports (with date from the file name) plus the save's album, Source filter, thumbnails with Pillow if present. An export is joined to its album entry by equal JPEG byte size, confirmed by a 24x16 grey-thumbnail comparison (the CRC cannot be used: the game edits the JPEG after the encoder). Course, species and score are NOT shown: `META_LAYOUT` (file 6, 0x148 bytes) is still undecoded, because no run has left more than one album record in a save (the route never ends a course, and the album is written then). So the album-to-export join was not seen to succeed on real data.
  - **Unlimited photos (#3): decision, PNG export is the unlimited store.** The 1200 limit is the entry count in the headers of save files 6, 7 and 10; the code that sets it was not found (`analysis/save/album.md`), the game makes those files itself with fixed sizes, and 1200 x 0x70840 bytes is already 82 MB. Raising it would mean patching lifted code plus migrating saves, with no way to check the album UI, so `SNAP_ALBUM_LIMIT` is NOT implemented. The export folder has no limit.
  - **Not done:** #4 photo-score overlay; settings-menu toggle for the export (env only); decoding file 6.

```

`README.md`:

```md
<div align="center">

# New Pokémon Snap PC Recomp

**A native Windows static recompilation of New Pokémon Snap (Switch).**
The game's AArch64 code is lifted to C, built with clang, and run on a hand-written Horizon OS and NVN-to-Vulkan runtime.

![Platform: Windows x64](https://img.shields.io/badge/platform-Windows%2010%2F11%20x64-0078D6)
![Graphics: Vulkan](https://img.shields.io/badge/graphics-Vulkan-AC162C)
![Game version: 2.0.1](https://img.shields.io/badge/game%20version-2.0.1-informational)
![Status: early playable](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-early%20playable-yellow)
![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue)

</div>

> **This repository contains source code only. It includes no game files, keys, extracted assets or generated game code. You must supply your own legally dumped copy of v2.0.1 (version 262144, title update 2.0.1) of the game.**

## Contents

- [Status](#status)
- [Features](#features)
- [Screenshots](#screenshots)
- [Building](#building)
- [Running and settings](#running-and-settings)
- [Testing](#testing)
- [Project layout](#project-layout)
- [Roadmap](#roadmap)
- [FAQ](#faq)
- [License and credits](#license-and-credits)

## Status

Early playable. The game boots to the title screen, the lab hub and the courses, and photos can be taken, scored, saved and reloaded. Checks so far are scripted runs on a hidden desktop with a null audio backend. No full human play-through has been done.

| Area | State |
| --- | --- |
| Boot, title, lab hub, map | Works |
| Florio Park ride, photo select, scoring | Works. Photos sort by subject, thumbnails show, and the professor scores them |
| Progression | Points registration, save and reload, level 2 unlock (Florio Night) and Photodex persistence pass from a real save. Professor requests were not reached |
| Story | Events 1, 2, 27 and 33 start and play, with cutscenes, dialogue, credits and the post-credits talk. The save after event 2 is verified. The save after credits and events 8 and 35 are not confirmed |
| Secrets | Scan pulses, Level 3 spawns and Night spawns pass. Florio Side Path, Mew, targeted orb, melody and fluffruit reactions, and special-pose photos were not triggered |
| Saves | Written atomically with generations and backups. Every crash stage tested left the old or the new save, never a torn one |
| Audio, video, text | Title, hub, map, Florio ride and photo select have music, shutter and ambience with no clipping. Cutscenes are in-engine, so there are no video files. English text and score numbers read correctly |
| Input | Keyboard, mouse and controllers (XInput, plus SDL3 when built with it). Rumble: the host side works with scripted test values, but no game action was seen producing vibration yet. Gyro was tested only with a scripted route, because no test pad reports a gyro |
| Frame rate | Capped at 60 fps, like the original. A Florio ride held 60.0 fps on an RTX 4090. Frame rate drops when several test instances share one PC; that case has no clean benchmark yet |
| Vulkan validation | Title, hub, one Florio ride and photo select gave no synchronization hazards and no other validation errors after one startup pipeline error was fixed |

Known problems:

- Wurmple photos stay unselectable ("subject is not clearly visible"). The cause is unknown; it may be normal game behavior, since the subject is whatever the reticle center points at.
- A loading hang on Lental was seen once and did not come back in four later runs.
- Draw distance and full-rate distant animation are experimental and may change photo scores.
- A Vulkan warning remains about the BC1 thumbnail encoder drawing a float format into an RGBA16UI stand-in. The spec calls it undefined, but it works on NVIDIA.
- On a 144 Hz display a 60 FPS cadence judders. Present pacing needs VRR or frame-pacing work.
- Rumble in the game itself, evaluation score screen audio, the album viewer, the pause menu and the Sound tab volume were not checked.

## Features

**Look and graphics**

- Default look is original: the game's own FXAA, with no sharpening and no forced anisotropic filtering.
- The enhanced look turns on with one setting (see [Running and settings](#running-and-settings)): 2x supersampling plus SMAA, CAS sharpening, 16x anisotropic filtering, automatic UI font supersampling and PNG photo export (lossless, with a JSON sidecar).
- Quality presets: Very Low, Low, Normal, High, Ultra, Maximum and Custom. Normal leaves the visual defaults alone.
- Upscalers: NVIDIA DLSS and DLAA, AMD FSR and Intel XeSS, each with quality modes. The vendor SDK files are not in this repo. Photos and scoring never use jittered or upscaled output.
- HDR output (HDR10 and scRGB, with fallback to SDR), peak and paper-white settings.
- Render scale from 0.5x to 4x, shadow resolution up to 8192, ambient occlusion options.
- Optional color looks (Neutral, Vivid, Warm, Cool) and per-pass switches for bloom, depth of field, film grain and chromatic aberration.

**Menus and controls**

- Ten PC settings tabs inside the game's own Settings screen: Quality, Textures, Effects, Output, View, Display, Controller, Mouse, Audio and Photos. They use the game's own widgets and its Restore Default Settings. They need a local pack built from your own game files (see [Running and settings](#running-and-settings)).
- An F1 overlay (or hold Back/View + Start on a controller for half a second) with the same options, button remapping, mods and save management.
- Rumble, plus gyro aim on controllers that report a gyro. Gyro drives the right stick because the game never reads motion.
- Keyboard and mouse, including mouse look and click-to-touch.

**Window, saves and tools**

- Borderless fullscreen (F11 or Alt+Enter), monitor choice, remembered window position and size, pause and mute when unfocused, and a fast-boot mode that skips the frame limiter during loading.
- Save profiles with a picker, duplicate, import and restore from trash. Each commit is an immutable generation, and the current and 5 earlier generations are kept as backups.
- One running copy per save folder, so two instances cannot corrupt a save.
- A mod loader for loose-file packs that replace single game archive entries, including HD texture packs. See [docs/mods.md](docs/mods.md). The repo holds only the loader, never pack contents made from game data.
- Options that go beyond the original game: draw distance, detail distance, full-rate distant animation, photos per expedition (72 original, up to 500), NEO-ONE speed and dialogue skipping.

## Screenshots

![Professor Mirror and Rita at the lab, rendered by the PC port](docs/screenshots/lab.webp)

![Photographing Vivillon in the first course. The black box at bottom left is the old broken photo thumbnail, fixed since.](docs/screenshots/course.webp)

Both are older captures of the native build running on Windows, scaled to 1280x720.

## Building

You need your own dump of the game. Nothing here downloads it, and no committed script extracts it.

Windows 10 or 11 x64. Local tools go under `tools/`, which is git-ignored, and the scripts look for them at these paths.

| Tool | Path | Used for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| LLVM, clang and lld 23 | `tools/llvm` | Building the lifted C and the host |
| Visual Studio 2022 Build Tools | `C:\Program Files (x86)\Microsoft Visual Studio\2022\BuildTools` | Windows SDK and `vcvars64.bat` |
| Vulkan SDK | `tools/vulkan_sdk` | `vulkan-1.lib`, `glslangValidator` |
| SDL3 (optional) | `tools/dl_sdl3` | Gamepads. XInput is the fallback |
| Python 3 | `tools/venv-recomp` | Lifter and build scripts. Needs `capstone`, `pyelftools`, `numpy`, `lz4` (NSO conversion). `unicorn` for the instruction tests |
| Python 3 | `tools/venv-oodle` | DRP unpacking. Needs `unicorn` for the in-engine Oodle decoder |
| Rust | none | Building the XOR helper: `rustc -O --crate-type cdylib -o tools/oodle_build/drp_xor.dll scripts/drp_xor/drp_xor.rs` |
| NSTool | `tools/nstool` | NCA and RomFS extraction |
| Ghidra 12.1.2 with the Switch loader extension, JDK 21 | `tools/ghidra_*`, `tools/jdk-*` | Function discovery |
| .NET 10 SDK | none | `scripts/shader_harness`, which the host build needs. It references a manually cloned checkout of the Ryubing Ryujinx shader translator at `tools/ref/ryubing-ryujinx` |

`scripts/audit_revisions.py` is the only script that reads `SNAP_DUMPS_DIR` (default `./dumps`): set it to the folder holding your XCI/NSP files and `prod.keys`. NSTool needs `prod.keys` in one of its documented key locations.

Run from the repo root.

1. **Extract.** Use NSTool on the base XCI plus the 2.0.1 update NSP to get the program NCA and the patched RomFS (into `extracted/`). `scripts/pfs0.py` lists and extracts PFS0/NSP members.
2. **Convert modules.** `python -I scripts/nso2elf.py <main.nso> <main.elf>`, then the same for `sdk`.
3. **Unpack archives.**
   ```powershell
   tools\venv-oodle\Scripts\python -I scripts\drp_unpack.py --set priority
   ```
   It is resumable and writes only to `extracted/`.
4. **Discover functions.**
   ```powershell
   scripts\ghidra_import.ps1 -InputFile <main.elf> -Project snap-v262144
   scripts\ghidra_analyze.ps1 -Stage All
   ```
   `-Stage All` runs Analyze, Export and Reconcile. Reconcile writes `functions_final.tsv` and `jump_tables.tsv`, which the lifter needs.
5. **Lift and compile.**
   ```powershell
   tools/venv-recomp/Scripts/python -I recomp/snap_gen.py --module main
   tools/venv-recomp/Scripts/python -I recomp/snap_gen.py --module sdk
   tools/venv-recomp/Scripts/python -I recomp/snap_build.py
   ```
   Generated C goes under `generated/`, which is never committed.
6. **Build the shader harness.**
   ```powershell
   dotnet build scripts/shader_harness/ShaderHarness.csproj -c Release
   ```
   `scripts/xlate_build.ps1` does the same build. The output goes to `tools/shader_harness/bin`, and the host build bakes in the DLL path.
7. **Build the host.**
   ```powershell
   tools/venv-recomp/Scripts/python -I host/build_snap.py
   ```
   `build_snap.py` also runs `host/gen_nvn_bridge.py` and `runtime/hle/gen_hle_stubs.py` to produce the NVN bridge and the unimplemented-function stubs. It produces `build/snap/snap_boot.exe`. A cold host build takes about 90 seconds, and a relink 5 to 10 seconds.
8. **Run.** See the next section.

`AGENTS.md` and `host/README.md` hold the detailed flags and the current state of each step.

## Running and settings

```powershell
powershell -File host\play.ps1                 # normal play, no timeout
powershell -File host\play.ps1 -SkipIntro      # feeds a script through the intro (about 3 to 4 minutes), then hands control back
powershell -File host\play.ps1 -ListPads       # list detected controllers
powershell -File host\run_boot.ps1 -Timeout 100 run   # timed, hidden run with a trace log
```

`play.ps1` also takes `-Profile`, `-PickProfile` and `-NoNativeOptions`. The game window needs one click for focus. Saves are under `%APPDATA%\SnapRecomp\`.

**Native settings tabs.** `play.ps1` builds a local `native-options` pack from your own extracted `option.lmb` before each start (`python -I scripts/ui/make_native_options.py`). The pack is game-derived and is never committed. If the build fails, the PC tabs do not appear. In the game, open the Settings screen from the lab hub gear and press R past the last tab, "Other".

**Environment variables.** A value set by hand always wins over a menu choice and over the look profile.

| Variable | Values | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `SNAP_PROFILE` | `original` (default), `enhanced` | Switches the five visual defaults together. See `host/README.md` for the table |
| `SNAP_AA` | `original` (default), `fxaa`, `off`, `smaa`, `ssaa2`, joined with `+` or `,` | Anti-aliasing, for example `ssaa2+smaa` |
| `SNAP_RENDER_SCALE` | number | Explicit render scale, never capped |
| `SNAP_SHARPEN` | 0 to 1 | CAS sharpening strength |
| `SNAP_ANISO` | `0` (default, the game's own) or `1` to `16` | Anisotropic filtering |
| `SNAP_UPSCALER` | `off`, `dlss`, `dlaa`, `fsr`, `xess` | Upscaler backend. Falls back through DLSS, FSR and XeSS |
| `SNAP_UPSCALE_QUALITY` | `native`, `quality`, `balanced`, `performance` | Upscaler quality |
| `SNAP_HDR` | `off`, `hdr10`, `scrgb` | HDR output. Peak and paper white (in nits) use `SNAP_HDR_PEAK_NITS` and `SNAP_HDR_PAPER_NITS` |
| `SNAP_PHOTO_EXPORT` | 0, 1 | PNG copies of photos. The folder is `SNAP_PHOTO_DIR` |
| `SNAP_UI_FONT_SCALE` | `off`, `auto`, 1 to 4 | Sharper menu text. `auto` gives 2x at 1440p and above |
| `SNAP_FAST_BOOT` | 1 | Turns the frame limiter off during loading (about 28% faster to the title logo) |
| `SNAP_MODS_DIR` | path | Mod pack folder |
| `SNAP_CONFIG_DIR` | path | Where `input.json` and `window.json` live |

`SNAP_PROFILE` is also read as a save profile name, so any value other than `original` or `enhanced` selects a save profile. To pick a save profile, use `play.ps1 -Profile "<name>"`.

## Testing

- `tests\hle\run_tests.ps1`: HLE host-side tests (build and run).
- `tests\mods\run_tests.ps1`: mod loader tests.
- `tests\os\build.bat`, `tests\audio\build.bat`, `tests\nvn\build.bat`: OS, audio and NVN tests.
- `tests/insn/`: instruction-level differential tests against a Unicorn reference.
- `tests\hle\run_ui_test.ps1`, `run_options_test.ps1`, `run_profiles_test.ps1`, `run_switch_test.ps1`: tests that boot the game.

Game-level checks use scripted routes: `powershell -File host\run_boot.ps1 -Route <name>` feeds `host\routes\<name>.txt` as input and saves checkpoint screenshots. Scripts can wait on game state with `wait <condition>` and `end` lines (conditions such as `ui=<scene>`, `dialog`, `ride`, `ride_end` and `film<=<n>`), so a route does not depend on fixed timing. A timeout exits with code 3 and logs the UI state. Up to 4 hidden runs at a time. See `host/README.md` for details.

## Project layout

| Path | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| `recomp/` | Python lifter and C emitter. Reads the game's `main` and `sdk` modules as ELF files and writes C, one function per guest function |
| `runtime/` | Guest CPU model and SIMD helpers, Horizon OS layer (`os/`), HLE services (`hle/`), audio (`audio/`, WASAPI), NVN-to-Vulkan graphics (`nvn/`), mod loader (`mods/`) |
| `host/` | Loader, boot driver, `build_snap.py`, `play.ps1`, `run_boot.ps1`, scripted routes and in-game mods |
| `scripts/` | Extraction, unpacking and analysis tools: NSO to ELF, PFS0, DRP archives, shader and format parsers, Ghidra scripts, an offline Maxwell-to-SPIR-V harness |
| `tests/` | Instruction differential, HLE, mods, audio, NVN and OS tests |
| `docs/` | Design notes, `mods.md` and screenshots |
| `AGENTS.md` | The project's decisions and current state |

Game shaders are translated offline (Ryujinx shader translator to SPIR-V) and loaded at run time from your own extracted files. Nothing derived from the game is stored in the repo.

## Roadmap

Unpushed work in progress: save hardening and the profile changes it needs; load-time and scheduler fixes; NVN object lifetime fixes and audits.

Planned:

- Wider scripted course coverage.
- A human play-through. Professor requests, the album viewer and several secrets are unchecked.
- The cause of the Wurmple photo problem.
- Present pacing for high-refresh displays.

## FAQ

**Is this an emulator?**
No. The game's code is translated ahead of time into C and compiled into a Windows executable. The Switch OS and GPU interfaces are re-implemented natively (Horizon OS services, and NVN on top of Vulkan). There is no CPU emulation loop at run time.

**Where are the game files?**
The repo has no game files, so you dump your own copy of v2.0.1 and run the pipeline above. Generated code, extracted assets, keys and vendor SDK binaries are git-ignored and must never be committed or shared.

**Does it change photo scoring?**
Not by default. The defaults aim for the original look and behavior. Photos and scoring never use jittered or upscaled output. The View options (draw distance, detail distance, full-rate animation) can change which Pokémon are in a photo and so the score, which is why they are marked experimental.

**Why does the first launch build something with my game files?**
The native settings tabs are patched into a copy of the game's own settings UI file, built on your PC. That file is never committed.
