`docs/audio.md`:

```md
# Audio

Code: `runtime/audio/`, test: `tests/audio/`. Proof: `analysis/audio/sink_test.wav` (10 s sweep) and the `.log` files.

## Surface the game uses

**AudioOut only. No `nn::audio` AudioRenderer.** `main` imports exactly 16 `nn::audio` functions
(`analysis/runtime/imports_usage.tsv`), all AudioOut or device queries: `InitializeAudioOutParameter`,
`OpenDefaultAudioOut`, `GetAudioOutChannelCount`, `SetAudioOutBufferInfo`, `GetAudioOutBufferDataPointer`,
`AppendAudioOutBuffer`, `GetReleasedAudioOutBuffer`, `StartAudioOut`, `StopAudioOut`, `GetAudioOutState`,
`CloseAudioOut`, `GetActiveAudioDeviceName`, `GetActiveAudioDeviceChannelCountForOutput`,
`AcquireAudioDeviceNotificationForOutput`, `ListAudioDeviceName`, `SetAudioDeviceOutputVolume`. There is no
`OpenAudioRenderer`, voice, mix, effect or sink call and no `WaitAudioOutBufferEvent`: Wwise mixes everything itself
(statically linked, lifted) and the game only hands finished PCM to the OS. The 1,410 `nn::audio` exports in `sdk`
(renderer, Opus decoder, etc.) are never reached from `main`.

Call-site evidence (module offsets, v262144 `main`). The sink is a Wwise platform sink with vtable `0xc68b20`:

| Offset | Role |
|---|---|
| `0x124640` | ctor: 0x1f8-byte object, `numBuffers = AkPlatformInitSettings+0xac (u16)`, `sampleRate = +0xa8 (u32)`, memset of the 0x168-byte `AudioOut`, `nn::mem::StandardAllocator` over 128 KiB |
| `0x1231e0` | default platform settings: `0x0004'0000'BB80` stored at +0xa8: **sample rate 48000, 4 buffers** (`0xa9d94` forces 4 if the field is 0) |
| `0x124780` | Open: `InitializeAudioOutParameter`, sets `sampleRate`, `channelCount` (2, or 6 when the speaker config asks for surround), `OpenDefaultAudioOut`, `GetAudioOutChannelCount`, then per buffer `StandardAllocator::Allocate(size, 0x1000)` and `SetAudioOutBufferInfo(buf, mem, cap, dataSize)`, then 4 silent prefill submits through vtable slot 15 (`0x124c30`) |
| `0x124b10` | submit: converts Wwise's interleaved float mix to s16 (`fcvtzs #15` + saturating narrow) into the next free `AudioOutBuffer` and calls `AppendAudioOutBuffer`; ring index modulo `numBuffers` |
| `0x124ce0` | poll: drains `GetReleasedAudioOutBuffer` until null (non-blocking), reports `numBuffers - pending` free slots |
| `0x124d60` / `0x124a10` | Start / (state check, Stop, Close, free buffers) |
| `0x123480`, `0x1232e0` | device notification: `TryWaitSystemEvent` on the acquired event, re-query channel count, reopen the sink if it changed |
| `0x67ffa0` | settings path: `ListAudioDeviceName` + `SetAudioDeviceOutputVolume` (per-device volume) |

Format: **48000 Hz, signed 16-bit PCM, interleaved, 2 channels (6 if the device query says surround)**.
Frames per buffer: `uNumSamplesPerFrame` global at `0xc66388` = **0x400 = 1024 frames** (21.3 ms), so a buffer is
4096 bytes (stereo) or 12288 bytes (5.1, 0x3000, 4 KiB aligned capacity). Queue depth 4 buffers = 85.3 ms.
`AudioOutBuffer` is 0x28 bytes (`next, buffer, capacity, dataSize, offset`), `AudioOut` storage is 0x168 bytes.
Device names compared in `0x1235xx`: `AudioStereoJackOutput`, `AudioBuiltInSpeakerOutput`, `AudioTvOutput`,
`AudioUsbOutput` (the `strcmp` table at GOT `0xcc8340`; the exact mapping to indices is unverified).

## Boundary decision: override at the `nn::audio` API

Override the 16 imports by mangled name; do not lift sdk's audio client. Reasons: (1) the surface is small and
fully visible at call sites; (2) lifting sdk's AudioOut would run the guest side of the `audout:u` IPC and need a
fake audio service, which is the pure-HLE route that `runtime-boundary.md` rejects; (3) there is no renderer, so the
"hard" rating (voices, mempools, effects, mixing) does not apply. Ryujinx's AudioRenderer is therefore not needed;
only its AudioOut semantics were used as a reference (buffers queue FIFO, are released when consumed, release is
polled).

## Design

```
Wwise sink thread (guest)            device thread (host)
  Append ----> SPSC submit ring ---->  core_mix(): pop, s16->float, remap, master gain, clip
  GetReleased <- SPSC released ring <-  buffer released once fully consumed
                                        -> WASAPI event buffer / timer
                                        -> optional tap ring (tests)
```

- **Zero copy until the device:** guest memory is host memory, so the submit ring carries `AudioOutBuffer*` and the
  device thread reads PCM in place. A buffer belongs to the host from Append until it comes out of GetReleased, as on
  hardware.
- **Rings:** both are wait-free SPSC rings (`spsc_ring.h`, 64 entries). The device thread takes no lock. A buffer
  is released after the device pulled its last frame (device latency is the only difference from hardware).
- **Close safety:** Close clears `alive`, then spins until the device thread leaves the slot (`inUse` handshake,
  Dekker-style, seq_cst) so the guest can free the buffers right after.
- **Up to 4 AudioOuts** are mixed additively; the game uses one. Rate must match the device rate (48000).
- **Channel mapping:** same count: copy. Mono: to L/R. Stereo into a 5.1 device: FL/FR. 5.1 into stereo:
  `L = (FL + 0.707 FC + 0.707 BL) / 1.707` (LFE dropped).
- **Underruns:** a pull where a started AudioOut had less than the requested frames counts as an underrun (counter,
  missing frames, stderr log). The device is fed silence for the gap.
- **Stats/latency:** `snap_audio_get_stats`: frames mixed, appended, released, underruns, WASAPI buffer, latency.

### Backend: WASAPI shared mode (SDL3 is not vendored)

`runtime/hle` does not exist yet and no SDL3 is vendored anywhere in the repo, so WASAPI is used directly rather than
adding a dependency (SDL3 can replace `audio_wasapi.cpp` behind the same `Backend` interface if the HLE layer
vendors it). Event-driven, float32 stream at the guest rate and channel count with `AUTOCONVERTPCM |
SRC_DEFAULT_QUALITY` (Windows converts to the endpoint). It tries `IAudioClient3::InitializeSharedAudioStream` at the
engine's minimum period first, then falls back to `IAudioClient::Initialize` (default period). Measured here
(`sink_test`): **1056-frame engine buffer (22.0 ms), reported stream latency 22.0 ms**, plus up to 85 ms of guest
queue (4 x 1024 frames), so worst-case game-to-speaker delay is about 107 ms; the typical figure is about 22 ms plus
about 43 ms. The device thread uses MMCSS "Pro Audio".

**Device changes:** `IMMNotificationClient` watches the default render endpoint. On a default-device change, or on
`DEVICE_INVALIDATED`, unplug or a failed `GetBuffer`, the stream is rebuilt on the new default endpoint, and the guest
notification event is signaled (`core_notify_device_change` -> `snap_audio_set_os_hooks`), which makes the game
re-query the channel count. While there is no endpoint, a 10 ms timer keeps consuming at stream rate so the game
never stalls, and the stream is retried every 500 ms. This path was written but not exercised: the test machine had
one endpoint and the test did not switch devices (see Risks).

A `null` backend (`SNAP_AUDIO_BACKEND=null` or `cfg.backend`) consumes on a real-time timer and is what the unit test
uses for exact comparison.

### Volume

Findings (names and IDs only; the soundbank data stays local). `Init.bnk` (Wwise bank version 134, 40 buses) has this
bus tree; IDs are the FNV-1 32-bit hash of the lower-case name and the three category names were confirmed by hash:

| Bus | ID | Parent |
|---|---|---|
| `Master Audio Bus` | 3803692087 | none |
| (unnamed mixer under master) | 508372457 | 3803692087 |
| `bgm` | 412724365 | 508372457 (6 child buses) |
| `se` | 1584861537 | 508372457 (about 25 child buses) |
| `voice` | 3170124113 | 508372457 (4 child buses) |
| (second root, unnamed) | 985987111 | none |

`Init.bnk` has no game parameters bound to bus volume, so there is no RTPC to set. The game does it with events: its
own options menu has BGM/SE/voice levels 0..10, and `BANK_MAIN.bnk` holds 33 events `Set_volume_bgm_NN`,
`Set_volume_se_NN`, `Set_volume_voice_NN` (NN = 00..10, e.g. `Set_volume_bgm_00` = 129505574, `_10` = 146283161,
`Set_volume_se_00` = 1152448242, `Set_volume_voice_00` = 2616401070) that set the matching bus volume.
We do not call `AK::SoundEngine` (stripped, no symbol) and do not add our own events; we drive the game's setter.

How the calls are made:

- Game setter: `main+0x67c610(AudioManager* this, int cat, uint8 level)`, `cat` 0 = bgm, 1 = se, 2 = voice. It builds
  `Set_volume_<cat>_<2-digit level>` and posts it by name (`this->[8]` vtable +0x78). Its callers are the game's startup
  apply (`0x444498`) and the options-menu setter (`0x737090`).
- Guest objects: audio manager pointer at `main+0x12fef28`; the game's saved levels are bytes `+0x6f` (bgm), `+0x70` (se),
  `+0x71` (voice) of the settings object whose address sits in GOT slot `main+0xcfab68`; manager `+0x128` = 2 forces
  voice to 0.
- `host/abi_audio.cpp` `apply_category_volumes()` runs from the `GetReleasedAudioOutBuffer` bridge, so it executes on
  the Wwise sink thread (a guest thread with its own `Cpu`) and uses `loader::call_guest_nested`. Level posted =
  `round(gameLevel * userVolume)`, so 1.0 is exactly the original mix. It re-posts when the user volume changes, when the
  game writes its own level (that post would override ours), and once a second while a volume is below 1.0. A category never
  moved off 1.0 is never touched.
- Resolution is the game's 11 steps (0.1 each); a user volume of 0 is silence for that bus. Master is applied in the host
  mixer (continuous, ramped per block) times the per-device volume.

Debug aids: `SNAP_AUDIO_LEVELS=1` prints `[audio-level] t=Ns rms= peak=` of the final mix each second;
`SNAP_AUDIO_DUMP=<file>` writes the final mix as raw s16 (device rate and channels); `SNAP_AUDIO_TRACE=1` logs the
game levels and each category post.

### Volume API for UI

```c
#include "audio/audio_out.h"
enum { SNAP_VOL_MASTER = 0, SNAP_VOL_BGM = 1, SNAP_VOL_SE = 2, SNAP_VOL_VOICE = 3 };
void  snap_audio_set_volume(int category, float v);  // v clamped to 0..1; applies live and persists
float snap_audio_get_volume(int category);           // current value, 1.0 default
```

- Callable from any thread, at any time (before or after boot). Setting is lock-free for the audio path; persisting
  writes a small file, so call it when a slider is released (or at most a few times per second), not per frame.
- Persistence: `audio.json` (`{"master":..,"bgm":..,"se":..,"voice":..}`) in `%SNAP_CONFIG_DIR%`, else
  `%APPDATA%\SnapRecomp`. Loaded when the audio layer starts; defaults to 1.0 everywhere (original mix). It is a
  separate file, not `hle.json`, so the UI needs no config plumbing: just call `snap_audio_set_volume`.
- Env overrides, not persisted (tests/scripts): `SNAP_VOL_MASTER`, `SNAP_VOL_BGM`, `SNAP_VOL_SE`, `SNAP_VOL_VOICE`.
- BGM/SE/VOICE take effect within about a second at most, in 0.1 steps, and only once the game's audio manager exists.
  The game's own BGM/SE/voice options still work; the user volume scales them.

## Surround and spatial output

**The switch.** Wwise's Switch sink asks `nn::audio::GetActiveAudioDeviceChannelCountForOutput` (callers `0x1232e0`,
`0x123480`, `0x123510`) and opens `AudioOut` with 2 or 6 channels (`0x124780`). The host answers with the "game
channels" value below, so the game itself switches Wwise to 5.1 (no patching). `SNAP_AUDIO_TRACE=1` logs the query and the
Open (`[audio-trace] ...`). The game never reads `nn::settings` or `nn::oe` for audio.

**Guest layout:** 48 kHz s16 interleaved, 6 channels in the Switch and Wwise order FL FR FC LFE BL BR (the downmix and
mapping are in `runtime/audio/audio_mix.h`, tested by `tests/audio/mix_test.cpp`; whether the lab and course scenes
really put content in the rear and center channels is in the evidence section below).

**Output modes** (env `SNAP_AUDIO_OUTPUT`, or `audio.json` key `output`; restart required, the game opens its sink once):

| Mode | Device stream | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `stereo` (default) | 2 ch float | 5.1 is downmixed `L = (FL + .707 FC + .707 BL) / 1.707`, LFE dropped. Game channels default to 2. |
| `speakers` | WASAPI 5.1 (mask 0x3F) or 7.1 (0x63F) | `speakers` key / `SNAP_AUDIO_SPEAKERS` = 6, 8, or 0 = 8 if the device mix format has 8 or more channels, else 6. On 7.1 the surrounds feed the SIDE speakers, the back pair stays empty. Windows converts if the device has fewer. |
| `spatial` | `ISpatialAudioClient`, 6 static bed objects | FL FR FC LFE and the surrounds on SideLeft/SideRight, rendered by Windows Sonic, Dolby Atmos for Headphones or DTS. Needs the spatial format enabled on the default device. If not available it logs why and falls back to 5.1 speakers, then stereo. |

Game channels: env `SNAP_AUDIO_CHANNELS` (2 or 6) > `audio.json` `channels` (0 = auto) > auto (6 for speakers and spatial, 2 for
stereo). Debug and tests: `SNAP_AUDIO_CAPTURE=<dir>` writes `guest_<n>ch.wav` (what Wwise produced) and
`device_<mode>_<n>ch.wav` (final mix) starting at the first non-silent frame, `SNAP_AUDIO_CAPTURE_SECS` (default 30), and
logs `[audio-ch] guest|device ... rms: FL=.. FR=..` every 5 s.

`audio.json` keys: `"output": "stereo"|"speakers"|"spatial"`, `"channels": 0|2|6`, `"speakers": 0|6|8`, next to the
volume keys (the volume writer preserves them).

### Output API for the UI

```c
void snap_audio_set_output(int mode /*0 stereo,1 speakers,2 spatial; -1 keep*/, int gameChannels /*0,2,6; -1 keep*/,
                           int speakerChannels /*0,6,8; -1 keep*/);   // persists to audio.json; applies on next start
int  snap_audio_get_output_mode(void);      // configured (env wins)
int  snap_audio_active_output_mode(void);   // running, after fallbacks (also SnapAudioStats.outputModeActive)
int  snap_audio_spatial_available(void);    // 1 if the default device can render the bed (probe, starts nothing)
```

The UI should say "restart required" next to the control, and may grey out Spatial when
`snap_audio_spatial_available()` is 0 (tell the user to enable Windows Sonic or Dolby Atmos for Headphones in Sound settings).

### Resampler

There is none: the stream is opened at 48 kHz float with `AUTOCONVERTPCM | SRC_DEFAULT_QUALITY`, so Windows resamples
when the device runs at 44.1 or 96 kHz (spatial streams are 48 kHz and Windows handles the device side). Not replaced:
it is a quality choice only and nothing measured is wrong.

### Getting real 5.1 out of Wwise (2026-11-12)

Three things stack, all needed:

1. **Settings word:** the game builds its `AkOutputSettings` in `main+0x67ffa0` with channel config `0x3102` (stereo). `host/abi_audio.cpp`
   rewrites it to `0x60f106` (5.1) at the `ListAudioDeviceName` call (`main+0x680270`) and again at the sink Open
   (`main+0x1247d8`), when the host wants 6 channels. The sink then opens 6 channels.
2. **Bank:** `Init.bnk` fixes the mixer bus under the Master Audio Bus (id 508372457, parent of bgm/se/voice) at stereo
   (channel config field `0x3102`; the other 39 buses are 0 = inherit). Without a change Wwise mixes stereo no matter what the
   sink is. `python -I scriptsudio_make_surround_pack.py` writes the local mod pack `surround-bus` (config 0 = same as
   parent) to `%APPDATA%\SnapRecomp\mods`; with it the sink buffers carry a real 5.1 mix. Stereo output is unaffected (the
   bus follows the 2-channel device). Never commit the pack (it is game data).
3. **Upmixer:** the game's content is stereo-authored, so even on a 5.1 bus FC, LFE and the surrounds stay near 0 (RMS
   0.0000 to 0.0001 for 130 s of the lab). The host upmixer (`Upmixer` in `audio_mix.h`) fills them from FL/FR when a block
   has no real surround content: center 0.354 (L+R), LFE 0.5 x lowpass 120 Hz (L+R), surrounds (7.1: sides) 0.4 x the fronts
   delayed 15 ms. FL/FR are unchanged. `SNAP_AUDIO_UPMIX=0` turns it off.

Lab capture (`florio_photos`, 130 s, speakers, per-channel RMS FL FR FC LFE BL BR): game mix
0.021 0.021 0.0000 0.0000 0.0001 0.0001; device mix after the upmixer 0.021 0.021 0.014 0.009 0.008 0.008.

**Course capture (2026-11-12, `florio_photos`, post_tutorial fixture, `SNAP_AUDIO_OUTPUT=speakers`, `surround-bus` pack installed, 450 s run `1-20261112_074123`, WASAPI backend (started before the muted-by-default change), `SNAP_AUDIO_CAPTURE_SECS=400`, files in `buildudio_capslorio\`).**
RMS per 20 s window of `device_speakers_6ch.wav` (FL FR FC LFE BL BR); the wav starts at the first non-silent frame, about 45 s into the run, so the ride (presents 3300 to 14300, about 60 to 270 s) is roughly wav t=15 to 225 s (alignment estimated, the log has no wav timestamps):

| wav t (s) | scene | FL | FR | FC | LFE | BL | BR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0-20 | title, map, ride start | 0.026 | 0.026 | 0.016 | 0.009 | 0.010 | 0.010 |
| 40-60 | ride | 0.018 | 0.020 | 0.0003 | 0.0002 | 0.002 | 0.003 |
| 60-200 | ride | 0.014-0.029 | 0.017-0.029 | 0.0000 (0.0007 at 120) | 0.0000 (0.0005 at 120) | 0.003-0.010 | 0.005-0.009 |
| 220-380 | professor, photo select, album | 0.023-0.030 | 0.023-0.029 | 0.011-0.018 | 0.004-0.013 | 0.008-0.012 | 0.008-0.012 |

Result: **during the ride FC and LFE are about 0 and the surrounds (BL/BR) are non-zero (0.003 to 0.010)**. The surrounds are real game content: the guest mix itself has BL/BR 0.006 to 0.010 in the ride (guest wav, the Wwise 5.1 bus carries course ambience), so the course is not purely stereo. Because the upmixer gate (`audio_mix.h`, `surroundPresent` over FC+LFE+BL+BR together, threshold 1e-6) sees that surround energy, it closes and does not fill FC and LFE either. FC and LFE come back only in menus and the evaluation (no surround in the guest mix, gate open). So the "non-zero on all channels in the ride" target is met for BL/BR only. Fix (needs a build, not done): gate per channel pair (FC+LFE separate from BL/BR) so a mix with real surrounds but no center still gets the phantom center and bass. FL/FR 0.014 to 0.03 throughout.

**Per-channel upmixer gate (2026-11-12, `runtime/audio/audio_mix.h`, `tests/audio/mix_test.cpp` 'ambient surrounds' check, all pass):** the Upmixer now has two gates: FC and LFE are filled from the stereo content whenever the game's own FC+LFE are silent, and BL/BR (7.1: sides) are filled whenever the game's own surrounds are silent; each gate closes only on its own channels, so real ambience in BL/BR no longer blocks the center and bass fill, and the game's own surround content is never touched. Florio capture after the change (run `2-20261112_084938`, null backend, `SNAP_AUDIO_OUTPUT=speakers`, `buildudio_capslorio2\`, 20 s windows, FL FR FC LFE BL BR): ride windows t=40 to 220 s give FC 0.009 to 0.019 and LFE 0.003 to 0.008 (before: 0.0000), BL/BR unchanged at 0.002 to 0.009; menus and the evaluation FC 0.016 to 0.018, LFE 0.0075 to 0.013.

**Spatial (2026-11-12, `SNAP_AUDIO_OUTPUT=spatial SNAP_AUDIO_BACKEND=wasapi SNAP_VOL_MASTER=0 SNAP_AUDIO_TRACE=1`, 80 s, run `0-20261112_075033`):** opens. Log: `[audio] output=spatial, game channels=6, device mix channels=6`, `[audio] spatial audio stream: 6 static bed objects (FL FR FC LFE SL SR)`, sink opened with 6 channels (config word `0x0060f106`); no fallback to speakers or stereo. Not heard (master volume 0, hidden run).

## Listening checklist (owner; the output could not be heard while building this)

1. `stereo` mode, play a course: sound is unchanged from before, no new hiss or clipping in busy scenes (the 5.1 downmix only runs if you force 6 channels).
2. `speakers` on 5.1 speakers: each speaker works; in a course, turning the camera or a Pokemon flying past moves effects between front and rear; voices and menu sounds sit in the center speaker; the subwoofer carries bass hits only.
3. `speakers` on 7.1: the rear (back) pair is silent by design, the sides carry the surrounds.
4. `spatial` with Windows Sonic or Dolby Atmos for Headphones on headphones: the sound is outside the head and wider than stereo; the log says `spatial audio stream: 6 static bed objects`. If it says "unavailable" it fell back to 5.1 speakers.
5. Volume sliders (master, BGM, SE, voice) still work in every mode, and unplugging or switching the default device recovers without a freeze.

## Threading

- Guest side: the Wwise sink thread (created via `nn::os::CreateThread`, name not in the 5 known `AK::` threads, so
  it is probably the sound-engine audio thread) is the only caller of Append/GetReleased. Both are single-thread-safe
  and wait-free. Open/Close/queries take one init mutex.
- Host side: one device thread (WASAPI or timer). It never blocks on the guest and the guest never blocks on it,
  except Close waiting for `inUse` (one device period at worst, a few ms).
- `nn::os` interplay: only the notification event needs `nn::os` (hook, `PROPOSED_SHARED_CHANGES.md` item 2). The
  `runtime\os` docs did not exist when this was written, so that is not yet coordinated.

## Test (`tests/audio/sink_test.cpp`, `tests/audio/build.bat`)

Drives the API in the sink's order (query device, Open with rate 48000, `numBuffers = 4` x 1024 frames, 4 silent
prefill buffers, Start, then poll/submit loop with the same float->s16 conversion, Close) with a 10 s log sweep
(100 Hz to 6 kHz plus 440 Hz), then reopens as 5.1 and checks the downmix. Checks: no underruns while feeding,
every buffer accounted for, the captured final mix equals the submitted PCM sample for sample (null: max error 0;
WASAPI at volume 0.05: 1e-9), downmix level, slot reuse. Result at the time of writing: null and WASAPI both pass
(483,328 frames in, 0 underruns while feeding, 472 buffers appended and released). Capture: `analysis/audio/sink_test.wav`.

Note: a normal-priority sink thread inside a BelowNormal process underran heavily when the machine was at 77% CPU;
the test raises its own thread to HIGHEST (the process stays BelowNormal). The real sink thread needs the same care.

## Risks

1. **Struct layouts are inferred** (`AudioOutParameter`, `AudioOutBuffer`, `AudioDeviceName`) from call-site offsets and
   the public SDK shape; sizes match (0x28 stride) but the field order of `AudioOutBuffer` past `buffer` is by
   convention. Only `buffer`, `dataSize` and `dataOffset` are read by the host, and `SetAudioOutBufferInfo` writes
   them, so a different order would still work as long as the game never reads them directly (it uses the getter).
2. **Device switching is untested** (no second endpoint here). The rebuild path is straightforward but unproven.
3. **Wwise sink thread priority/cadence**: if lifted `nn::os` thread priorities map low, 85 ms of queue is thin.
   Raising `numBuffers` is a one-line settings change (`AkPlatformInitSettings+0xac`) if needed.
4. **Category volumes** use the game's 11-step events (no finer than 0.1) and are posted from the sink thread.
5. **Device-name semantics** (which of the 4 names selects which game behavior) unverified; the host reports
   `AudioTvOutput` and 2 channels by default (`cfg.channelMode` can report 5.1 or follow the device mix format).
6. **Release timing:** buffers are released when consumed by the device thread, not when heard (up to one WASAPI
   period early), which only makes the game's queue accounting slightly optimistic.
7. **Mixed-rate AudioOuts** are rejected (only 48000 is used by the game).

### Volume verification (hidden run, `-SaveFixture post_tutorial`, 100 s, `SNAP_AUDIO_LEVELS=<file>`)

Mean final-mix RMS over seconds 20..90 (71 one-second samples): normal run 0.0139, `SNAP_VOL_BGM=0` run 0.0072
(about 48% lower; peak 0.756 -> 0.595). The trace shows the setter posting level 0 for category 0 (BGM) with the game's
own level at 10; SE and voice stayed untouched. Only one run of each, and the two runs are not frame-aligned, so the
ratio is indicative, not exact. Not yet checked: SE and voice at 0, and live changes from the UI.

```

`docs/cpu-backend-eval.md`:

```md
# CPU backend evaluation: Kirikae vs LAS/TotK-style AArch64-to-C

Status: read-only source study, 2026-11-11. No project was built or run (reason in section 6). No game data in this file.
All numbers labeled "claim" are the projects' own statements, not measurements of ours.

Sources (shallow clones under `tools\ref\`, ignored by VCS):

| backend | repo | newest commit read | license | commits (GitHub API) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Kirikae | `Cor3Duo/kirikae` (`tools\ref\kirikae`) | 2026-11-07 (repo created 2026-10-23; v0.1.0-v0.1.2 released 2026-10-23..24) | MIT or Apache-2.0 | 133 |
| TotK Recomp | `valentderah/totk-pc-recomp` (`tools\ref\totk`) | 2026-11-10 | MIT | 1006 |
| LAS Recomp (canonical) | `peiikai/LASRecomp` (`tools\ref\las`), linked from `totk\README.md:74` and `totk\THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md:8` (pinned at `da35b83`) | 2026-11-06 (579fdad) | MIT | 950 |

TotK's CPU half is a derivative of LAS (lifter, NEON lowering, CPU headers, differential tests), rewritten for scale
(`totk\docs\architecture.md:17,33-46`). Below, "LAS/TotK" means the TotK generator unless stated; LAS-only facts are marked.
LAS and TotK are Python generators emitting C; Kirikae is a Rust workspace (`crates\a64` 11.2K lines, `recomp` 3.0K,
`rt` 31.6K, `loader` 2.1K).

## 1. Inputs and ingestion

**Kirikae**
- Takes a whole dump: NSP/XCI/ExeFS folder/NSO/NRO (`crates\loader\src\package.rs:225-275`, `nso.rs:55`). Modules are
  laid out at `LOAD_BASE = 0x0800_0000` (`loader\src\lib.rs:17`, `package.rs:43`), not at the Switch base.
- Function discovery is its own and runs at build time: seeds = each module entry + `dynamic::code_pointers`
  (RELATIVE/ABS64/GLOB_DAT/JUMP_SLOT to defined targets, plus defined FUNC dynsyms; `loader\src\dynamic.rs:94-150`,
  `recomp\src\project.rs:152-159`), then a worklist over BL targets, ADR, and ADRP+ADD (`recomp\src\discover.rs:224-262`).
  No `.eh_frame` reader (grep for `eh_frame` in `loader` and `recomp`: no hits). Only RELA tables are read (no DT_RELR; Snap
  uses RELA per our `relocations.tsv`, so this is not a blocker).
- There is no way to feed an external function list. Extra entries come only from a profile file of addresses the
  interpreter had to run (`project.rs:191-264,313-320`, header `# kirikae:`, tagged to the dump via `.guest`).
- Adapter for us: (a) a small patch to `discover::find_entries` seeds (`project.rs:313`) to also read `functions_final.tsv`
  (FDE starts, Ghidra starts, address_taken) or, with no code change, write our list as a `.profile` file (format at
  `project.rs:191-218`; needs the `.guest` hash tag); (b) feed the loader the NSO directly (it LZ4-decompresses; our
  `main.uncompressed.nso` is probably accepted, to be verified at first build); (c) map our module-relative offsets by
  adding `LOAD_BASE`.

**LAS/TotK**
- Python generator over raw NSO files: `recomp\nso.py` (LZ4, MOD0, DT_RELA/JMPREL/RELR, `.eh_frame_hdr` bounds),
  `recomp\module.py:1-112`. Function starts = `.eh_frame_hdr` FDEs + exported FUNC symbols + RELATIVE targets + every BL
  target + ADR/ADRP+ADD materialized code addresses, then a fixpoint that promotes out-of-function branch targets to new
  starts (`recomp\gen.py:18-24,83-170`). LAS does the same (`las\tools\gen.py:20,74,550`, uses `eh_frame_functions`).
  This is almost exactly our own map method (FDE seeds, address_taken), so our TSV is a cross-check, not new information.
- Adapter for us: small. Replace `Module.seeds()` (`module.py`) with a loader of `functions_final.tsv`, and diff the
  generator's `manifest.json` function list against it; or leave it alone and treat the generator's list as the
  independent cross-check AGENTS.md asks for. Guest base is configurable (`gen.py <name> <nso> <base> <outdir>` in LAS,
  `--version`/layout in TotK `recomp\layout.py`).
- Our relocations are consumed at runtime by the host loader (`totk\runtime\loader.c`, 737 lines) rather than by the lifter,
  except RELATIVE targets as seeds.

## 2. Instruction coverage

**Kirikae** (`crates\a64`)
- One IR per instruction (`ir.rs:40-75`, `lift.rs` 861 lines, `lift_fp.rs` 976, `simd\*` ~3.4K incl. `neon.rs`,
  `crypto.rs`, `fp.rs`). The same IR drives the interpreter and Cranelift; `ops.rs` is the single semantic source.
- Integer/branch/load-store: native Cranelift lowering. FP scalar partly lowered; NEON/other FP are `Stmt::Simd(word)` helper
  calls into Rust semantics (`clif.rs:1252-1259`, `simd.rs`): correct by construction but slower than inlined vector code.
- System registers: `lift.rs:186-196` lists TPIDR_EL0, TPIDRRO_EL0, CNTVCT_EL0, CNTPCT_EL0, CNTFRQ_EL0, FPCR, FPSR,
  DCZID_EL0, CTR_EL0 (MRS), writes via `SetSysReg` (`lift.rs:285-298`).
- Exclusives: LDXR/LDAXR/STXR/STLXR/LDXP/STXP lowered to `Monitor`/`StoreExclusive` (`lift.rs:380-411`, state in
  `rt\src\cpu.rs:22-24,103-132` using `compare_exchange` SeqCst). No ARMv8.1 LSE (CAS/SWP/LDADD): grep finds none; harmless
  for a Switch A57 title but unverified for Snap until a coverage scan.
- Unimplemented: anything not lifted becomes `Stmt::Undefined(word)` (`lift.rs:6`) which the generated code reports through
  `kirikae_undefined` (`clif.rs:1275-1283`, `rt\src\abi.rs:49`). `kirikae info <dump>` prints decoder coverage (README).

**LAS/TotK** (`recomp\lifter.py` 805 lines, `simd_c.py` 1157, `runtime\cpu.h` 361, `simd.h`, `simd_fp.h`)
- Integer, branches, load/store, pairs, bitfields, CRC32, FP/NEON lowered to C (clang auto-vectorizes; AVX2/FMA build
  default, x86-64-v2 fallback with software fma, `totk\docs\building.md:95-101`). LAS can alternatively emit AArch64 inline asm on
  ARM hosts (`las\tools\gen.py:1-6`).
- Sysregs: MRS of TPIDRRO_EL0, TPIDR_EL0, CNTFRQ (hard-coded 19.2 MHz), CNTVCT/CNTPCT (`rt_ticks()`), NZCV, FPCR, FPSR, DCZID, CTR;
  MSR of TPIDR_EL0, NZCV, FPCR, FPSR (`lifter.py:318-362`). Anything else raises `Unsupported`.
- Atomics: exclusive monitor emulated by compare-and-swap (`cpu.h:86-125`, incl. 128-bit LDXP/STXP via cmpxchg16b, added in TotK),
  plus ARMv8.1 atomics tested in `tests\diff\atomic.py` (`building.md:233`). DMB/DSB/ISB/CLREX handled (`lifter.py:324-329`).
- Unimplemented: `Unsupported` becomes `rt_udf(c, pc)` (noreturn trap) in generated code (`module.py:73-80`, `runtime\main.c:169`).
  `tests\diff\lift.py --coverage` lists every rejected word (`building.md:233`). TotK reports covering all 68,968 OS-touching sites of 1.4.3 `main`
  (`architecture.md:36`); that is a claim about TotK, the Snap NSO still needs its own scan.

## 3. Control flow

| topic | Kirikae | LAS/TotK |
|---|---|---|
| Direct branches | per-function blocks; branch out of function becomes a call/tail via entries (`discover.rs:271-333`) | `goto` inside the function; out-of-function target is `musttail` call to its function, or via `rt_dispatch` if not a known start (`gen.py:381-388`) |
| Indirect `br` / jump tables | own symbolic `jump_table()` (`discover.rs:136-176`), compact; unresolved falls to dispatcher | `recomp\jumptables.py` (1,345 lines): symbolic walk with a fixpoint, rejects what it cannot prove; checked against a Unicorn oracle with "0 disagreements" required (`tests\jumptables_check.py`, `building.md:236`); unresolved `br` re-enters via `fb_<entry>` switch on `c->pc` then `rt_dispatch` (`gen.py:390-403`) |
| Tail calls | same IR `Jump` to another entry; the entry set controls it (`discover.rs:271-290`) | `musttail` C tail calls (`gen.py:55,386`), so no stack growth |
| Noreturn | no explicit model; `Undefined` and `Return` end blocks; SVC halts via `cpu.halted` (`clif.rs:1260-1273`) | `rt_udf`/break are `noreturn` (`cpu.h:39`); no noreturn inference |
| `blr` through vtables | `call_indirect` -> `run_until` lookup (`process.rs:414-460`) | `rt_dispatch`: O(1) flat table, 4 bytes per guest instruction, sealed read-only (`dispatch.c:1-13,163-196`) |
| Unresolved target | falls back to the **interpreter** (`process.rs:431-446`); records the address (`coverage.rs`, `interp.rs:73`) in a `.profile` consumed by the next build | **fatal**: `dispatch_fail` prints pc, lr and reason, exit 70 (`dispatch.c:176-186`); no interpreter |

For Snap, TotK's fatal-unknown matches AGENTS.md "unresolved targets remain explicit"; Kirikae's interpreter-plus-profile loop
matches "record interpreted/unresolved targets and feed them into later AOT builds" directly (AGENTS.md Validation strategy). Both
satisfy it in different ways. Note AGENTS.md says "Do not link an emulator": Kirikae's interpreter is its own IR evaluator (`interp.rs`,
109 lines), not a third-party emulator, but it is a second execution engine in the product; a TotK-style build has none.

## 4. Memory model

- **Kirikae: translated.** Reserves the 39-bit guest space once and emits `host = base + (addr & ADDR_MASK)` for every guest
  access (`rt\src\mem.rs:7-11,88`, `clif.rs:631-634`). Guest pointer != host pointer. Safe (bad pointer page-faults inside the
  reservation) but costs an AND+ADD per access and conflicts with AGENTS.md "preserve guest pointers as host pointers where
  practical" (NVN/Vulkan imports, host-visible buffers, mirrored pools would need translation at the boundary).
  Stack and TLS are allocated inside it (`process.rs:18-19,189`). Exclusive monitor lives in the per-thread `Cpu` (`cpu.rs:22-24`).
- **LAS/TotK: identity.** Guest address equals host address, all below 2^39 (`totk\docs\architecture.md:37`; the `Cpu` carries
  `tpidr`/`tpidrro`/`excl_addr`/`excl_val`/`excl_val_hi`, `cpu.h:13-20`). Heap/stack/alias are reserved with `MEM_WRITE_WATCH`
  so the graphics layer can ask for CPU-written pages. This is the AGENTS.md preference, and it simplifies NVN memory-pool
  imports. Cost: the host must be able to reserve the same virtual addresses on Windows (TotK does, `runtime\memory.c`).
- Register state: both keep a `Cpu` struct; TotK keeps NZCV and six hot registers in C locals (`flags.py`, `regs.py`); Kirikae has a
  `fast_regs` cache planner (`clif.rs:401-475`, test `recomp\tests\fast_regs.rs`).

## 5. Runtime boundary (SVC / SDK imports / HLE)

- **Kirikae**: emulates the console: Horizon kernel SVC table (`rt\src\horizon.rs`), IPC/CMIF sessions and services (`services\*`),
  an `nvdrv` GPU command processor with a Maxwell translator and Vulkan renderer (31.6K lines in `rt`). `hle.rs:1-40` places host
  functions at synthetic guest addresses (`BASE 0x7f_ff00_0000`) that the dispatcher recognizes; `Table::replace(addr, f)` can
  replace a guest function by address, which is the SDK-import HLE hook we need. NVN is wrapped, not replaced: `KIRIKAE_NVN=trace|shadow|exec`
  (`ARCHITECTURE.md`, NVN section), with shadow-vs-command-processor comparison already present (AGENTS.md wants this concept).
  Per AGENTS.md we do not want the guest NVN driver or `sdk`/`rtld` lifted in production; Kirikae recompiles every module it is given,
  so for Snap we would feed only `main` and implement `nn::*` through `hle.replace` by address from our maps. The IPC/service half
  would then be dead weight we would either drop or reuse.
- **TotK/LAS**: SDK boundary is by symbol/function: `HOST_OVERRIDE` / `HOST_OBSERVER` linker-section tables (`runtime\hostfn.c:1-40`),
  ~163 `nn::*` functions replaced by name in TotK (`architecture.md:13`), 38 SVCs (`runtime\svc.c`, 21 listed as fatal-unimplemented,
  `svc.c:29-36`), only `audren:u` and `sm:` as real IPC (`architecture.md:41`). `rtld` is dropped and linking is done by the host
  loader. This is the AGENTS.md "replace SDK imports at a high-level host boundary" design.
  Snap fit: our `imports.tsv` (731 undefined symbols, 413 `nn`) maps one-to-one to `hostfn` overrides; our PLT/GOT stubs
  need the host loader to bind them (TotK `loader.c`).

## 6. Build and runtime performance

No build was run. `cargo` is installed here, but Kirikae's workspace pulls a large dependency tree (Vulkan, egui, audio) over the
network, no C toolchain (`clang`) is on PATH for the TotK path (it targets MSYS2 UCRT64 clang/lld 23.1.3 and ninja,
`building.md:17`), and other workers hold heavy jobs. Both would exceed the "light work only" bar. Evidence below is documentary.

| item | Kirikae | LAS/TotK |
|---|---|---|
| Output form | Cranelift `.obj`, 1024 functions per object, parallel (`README.md` "How it works", `clif.rs`) plus a generated Cargo project (`project.rs`); needs rustc+MSVC at the user's machine | chunked C (LAS `--chunk` default 1500 functions per file, `gen.py:521`; TotK size-estimated chunks, `gen.py:189`) compiled by clang |
| Build time claim | "whole game in well under a minute on a desktop CPU" (README, claim); the final `cargo build` link is separate | TotK 1.4.3: lifting about 15 s, clean compile about 200 s on 24 threads (`building.md:103-105`, claim); sccache supported; later builds recompile only changed chunks |
| Scale evidence | commercial games run at 30 fps "on a modest GPU" (README "Status", claim); no function counts published in the repo | TotK is far larger than Snap (68,968 OS sites in `main` alone); Snap's ~24.6K functions are well within what it handles |
| Runtime numbers | none published as a benchmark; `KIRIKAE_STATS=1` reports fps and native-vs-interpreted counts | PGO: trained fight 12% faster per frame, untrained about 6%, on 1.4.3 (`docs\pgo.md:1-6`, claim); AGENTS.md already notes this is a reference, not a promise. `docs\agents` / pr-review kit show perf work is ongoing |
| Codegen quality note | Cranelift optimizes less than LLVM (no loop vectorization, weaker inlining); NEON through helper calls | clang -O1/-O2 with PGO and `-march=x86-64-v3`; NEON lowered to vector C |
| Compile-time risk | none known | a pathological function once cost "tens of seconds" in clang loop passes (`gen.py:391-393` comment) |

## 7. Differential testing

- **Kirikae**: Cranelift backend vs the IR semantics (`ops.rs`) on random inputs (`recomp\tests\clif_ops.rs`, `fast_regs.rs`, 244 lines);
  decode/SIMD unit tests; optional Unicorn oracle for SIMD against a Cortex-A57 model (`tools\simd_oracle.py`, `a64\src\simd\oracle.rs`);
  testkit end-to-end synthetic NROs (`crates\testkit`); CI runs `cargo test --release --workspace`. Whole-function and whole-binary differential
  testing is not provided. Runtime tracing: `KIRIKAE_STATS`, coverage JSON of used SVC/IPC/ioctl/shader, per-event PNG and backtrace.
- **LAS/TotK**: the most complete harness of the two: `tests\diff\lift.py` (instructions sampled from the real modules, Unicorn),
  `simd.py` (whole FP/SIMD encoding space), `atomic.py` (exclusives plus LSE), `func.py` (whole generated functions incl. loops, jump tables,
  calls checked at the stub), `jumptables_check.py` vs Unicorn, `excl_mt.py` (monitor under contention), `flags_check.py`
  (`building.md:229-239`). LAS uses Unicorn at generation time for jump tables (`las\tools\gen.py:17`); TotK removed that to keep GPL out of
  the shipped generator (`architecture.md:34`). Unicorn is test-only in TotK, consistent with AGENTS.md.
  Runtime probes: `--probe-kernel`, `--probe-vkexec`, `--probe-nvn-tex`, `--probe-shader`; TOTK_TRACE, flight recorder, perf overlay.
- The `tests\diff` harness needs the Snap modules only for `lift.py`/`func.py`; the others are game-independent.

## 8. Maturity

| | Kirikae | LAS Recomp | TotK Recomp |
|---|---|---|---|
| Age / activity | 16 days, 133 commits, 96 stars, v0.1.2 | about 5 weeks, 950 commits, 2.3K stars | 13 days at read time, 1006 commits, 6.6K stars |
| Games shown | "complete commercial 3D games" (names not given in the README); "tested on a handful" | Link's Awakening (beta, Win/macOS/Linux) | Tears of the Kingdom (playable, 3 game versions) |
| Self-described state | "Early preview", expect crashes and missing services | Beta | "Early development", crashes expected |
| Notable gaps | no updates/DLC; NVN-on-host in progress; interpreter fallback needs profile loop | AI-authored by its own disclosure (README header); LAS-specific host | Python 3.14 pipeline, 60 GB working space, MSYS2 clang; TotK specifics throughout runtime |
| Fit to Snap | recompiles whole dumps incl. `sdk`/`rtld`; host != guest pointers | per-game host layer | closest precedent: large Switch engine game, SDK replaced, NVN to Vulkan |

Caveat: all three projects are weeks old and largely AI-assisted (LAS says so; the other two show it in `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md`). Treat
every "works" claim as unverified for Snap until our own differential tests pass.

## Recommendation

**Prototype the LAS/TotK-style C generator first, taking TotK's `recomp\` and `runtime\cpu.h` as the base, and use Kirikae as a
differential reference and a bake-off candidate on a fixed function subset.** Do not maintain both as production lifters (AGENTS.md).

Top 3 reasons:
1. Memory and boundary match AGENTS.md: identity guest==host pointers and a symbol-level `HOST_OVERRIDE` SDK boundary with `main` only; Kirikae
   translates every access (`mem.rs`, `clif.rs:631`) and ships a whole-console runtime we would mostly not use.
2. Same discovery inputs as our maps (`.eh_frame_hdr` FDEs, dynsym, RELATIVE, BL, ADRP+ADD, fixpoint) and the strongest test kit
   (whole-function and whole-encoding-space Unicorn diffs, jump-table oracle); the adapter is a seed-list swap.
3. Scale and speed evidence is for a bigger title (about 200 s clean compile, PGO gains claimed); Kirikae's build and run numbers are only claims
   with no data in the repo, and NEON goes through helper calls.

Key risks:
- LAS/TotK: Python generator at 24.6K functions needs memory (TotK pool restarts with fewer workers on OOM, `building.md:103`); unresolved indirect
  target is fatal (needs our trace-and-feed loop, which we build); clang toolchain and size of generated C; per-function code size inflates with `Cpu`
  spills; Windows reservation of identical guest addresses; heavy cooperative-scheduling hooks (`rt_spin_gate`, preemption in `dispatch.c`).
- Kirikae: 2 weeks old, single maintainer (not verified beyond the commit log); Rust/Cranelift plus MSVC toolchain at runtime; per-access masking; Cranelift code quality and
  NEON helper calls; second execution engine (interpreter) in the product; discovery has no `.eh_frame` and no external function list (patch or profile
  trick); would need a fork or plugin hooks to drop `sdk`/`rtld` and replace NVN.

## Bake-off criteria (same inputs, same function set, same machine, BelowNormal priority)

1. **Correctness**: pass rate on a differential set vs Unicorn (an external, test-only dependency): (a) 20K instruction words sampled from `main`
   .text by class (integer, FP, NEON, exclusives, sysregs), (b) 300 whole functions (loops, jump tables, vtable calls, leaf FP) with identical
   input registers and memory, comparing all X/V/NZCV/FPSR and memory writes, (c) any word either backend rejects (coverage list). Target: 0 mismatches,
   rejected words listed with counts.
2. **Compile time for the full `main`**: wall time and peak RSS of lift/codegen, then compile/link of all ~24.6K functions; cold and warm cache; output
   size on disk. Target set by measurement: any build under 10 minutes fits our rules.
3. **Hot-function runtime**: 20 hot functions chosen from the maps (render-pass setup `0x5bd940`, tonemap `0x59ab20`, vtable-heavy, a NEON skinning loop once identified),
   microbenchmarked with fixed inputs, median and p99 per call, both backends against each other. Report ratios, not absolute claims.
4. **Integration cost**: engineer-hours and lines changed to (a) ingest `functions_final.tsv`, (b) bind our PLT/GOT imports, (c) override 10 `nn::`/libc
   functions, (d) keep guest==host pointers for NVN pools, (e) record and feed back unresolved targets. Also: build-toolchain footprint on the user's PC.
5. **Diagnosability**: cost to get a guest backtrace and unresolved-target log on a crash.

## 1-2 week prototype plan (against our maps)

Day 0: record the pinned commits (`da35b83` LAS; Kirikae and TotK commits from `tools\ref`); stage one NSO copy in a scratch folder (read only, no changes to `extracted\`).

1. **Days 1-2, function-list cross-check (no execution of game code).** Run TotK's `discover()` (`gen.py:83`) on `main.uncompressed.nso` with Snap's base and diff its
   starts against `functions_final.tsv` (FDE, ghidra, address_taken tags). Do the same with Kirikae `kirikae info` / `find_entries`. Write the two disagreement
   lists. This validates our maps and measures how many starts each backend finds without Ghidra.
2. **Days 2-4, instruction coverage scan.** `tests\diff\lift.py --coverage` equivalent for Snap's `main` and Kirikae's decode coverage. Output: rejected-word counts per class (NEON, LSE, sysreg, crypto, exclusives), a ranked list.
3. **Days 3-6, differential set.** Build the 20K-word and 300-function sets from `main` (indexed by `functions_final.tsv` so selection is reproducible), run Unicorn once, store golden
   register/memory results as data files (not code), then run each backend's lifted output against them. Needs a one-time Unicorn install in a venv; Unicorn is test-only.
4. **Days 5-8, full-binary build.** Generate the whole `main` with the TotK generator (cold, then warm) and with Kirikae, record time/RSS/size. If a toolchain is missing, install it in
   a scratch location, never touching `extracted\` or `analysis\ghidra\`.
5. **Days 7-10, hot function microbench** using the twenty functions above in a stub harness with fixed memory; no game boot.
6. **Days 9-12, integration spike.** Bind five imports from `imports.tsv` (`nvnBootstrapLoader`, one libc, one libc++, two `nn`) through `HOST_OVERRIDE` (TotK) and `hle.replace` (Kirikae) and call `FUN_7100910270` (NVN bootstrap, `analysis\maps\README.md`) with a mocked `getProcAddress`; record how each backend handles the unresolved indirect call (fatal vs interpreter).
7. **Day 12-14**: score with the criteria above, write a decision note, delete the losing backend's scratch build. If Kirikae loses on pointer model or toolchain but wins on speed, record a follow-up: lift only its `a64` crate and Cranelift emit as a library, not the runtime.

Assumptions and open questions for the first day: (1) Kirikae's loader accepts the uncompressed NSO as-is; (2) Snap `main` uses no LSE atomics (coverage scan answers it); (3) Snap's relocations are plain RELA (our `relocations.tsv` shows RELATIVE/ABS64/GLOB_DAT/JUMP_SLOT only);
(4) the Windows host can reserve the guest range at identical addresses without clashing with the process, which TotK's `runtime\memory.c` shows is workable.

```

`docs/hd-assets.md`:

```md
# HD assets: preview pipeline and viewer

Goal: preview higher-resolution textures, and later better models, outside the game, with before/after comparison. Then pack the good ones as a mod that the game loads through the RomFS overlay.

Everything produced from game data stays local, under `build/hd/`, which is git-ignored. The repo holds only code.

## Phase 1: textures and preview (now)

There are two parts, joined by the cache layout below.

1. **Pipeline:** `scripts/hd/`, Python, run with `-I` or `-E -P`.
   - It finds an asset's model and textures in `extracted/drp-v262144/`.
   - It converts the SSBH model (numdlb/numshb/numatb/nusktb) to glTF 2.0, mesh and skeleton only, with no textures embedded.
   - It decodes the textures to PNG.
   - It runs local AI upscalers on them.
2. **Viewer:** `tools-src/asset_viewer/`, a static web app (three.js) plus a tiny localhost server. It reads the cache and shows the assets before and after.

### Cache layout (the contract)

```
build/hd/cache/
  manifest.json
  <asset_id>/
    model.gltf (+ .bin)          mesh, skeleton, UVs, material slots; textures referenced by name only
    textures/<tex>.orig.png      decoded original (RGBA8, all mips dropped)
    textures/<tex>.<variant>.png upscaled variants, e.g. x4_realesrgan, x4_anime
    info.json                    per-asset details (LODs, material -> texture map)
```

`manifest.json`:

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "variants": [{"id": "x4_realesrgan", "label": "Real-ESRGAN x4plus", "scale": 4}],
  "assets": [{
    "id": "pm0025_00",
    "name": "Pikachu",
    "category": "pokemon|course|character|prop|ui",
    "model": "pm0025_00/model.gltf",
    "lods": ["pm0025_00/model.gltf", "pm0025_00/model_lod1.gltf"],
    "materials": [{"name": "body", "albedo": "tex_a", "normal": "tex_n", "mask": "tex_m", "emissive": null}],
    "textures": [{
      "name": "tex_a",
      "role": "albedo|normal|mask|emissive|other",
      "orig": "pm0025_00/textures/tex_a.orig.png",
      "w": 512, "h": 512, "format": "BC7",
      "variants": {"x4_realesrgan": "pm0025_00/textures/tex_a.x4_realesrgan.png"}
    }]
  }]
}
```

### Viewer features

- An asset list with search and category filter.
- **3D view:** orbit and zoom, a variant toggle (original or any upscale), a split-screen A/B mode, wireframe, LOD switch, and a neutral studio light plus an HDRI-free sky.
- **Texture view:** a before/after slider at 1:1 and zoomed, pixel-peeping with nearest filtering, and per-channel display (RGB, A).

## Phase 2: in-game test (after phase 1 looks good)

1. Re-encode the chosen upscales to nutexb, in the same format as the originals (BC7/BC1/BC5, mips, block-linear).
2. Place them in a mod folder that the HLE `rom` overlay mounts over RomFS.
3. Compare screenshots in game.

## Phase 3: better models (later)

- A numshb/numdlb writer.
- Retargeting the existing skeletons and rigs onto higher-detail meshes.
- Sources can be the owner's own game data, models we make ourselves (subdivision and sculpting, or local generation), or third-party model files the owner chooses for personal use.
- Third-party files live only in `build/hd/external/` with a local `SOURCES.md` provenance list, and are never committed or distributed. Only model and texture formats are allowed, never executables.

## AI re-texture (SD1.5 + tile ControlNet, 2026-11-12)

Local only. Models in `tools/sd/` (see `tools/sd/SOURCES.md`), venv `tools/venv-sd`. Script: `scripts/hd/retexture_sd.py` (run with `tools\venv-sd\Scripts\python.exe -I`), contact sheets: `scripts/hd/sd_sheet.py` -> `analysis/hd/sd_<tex>.png`.

- Method: wrap-pad (if the source tiles), Lanczos 4x, 512 px tiles with 128 px feathered overlap, img2img strength 0.4 plus tile ControlNet, per-channel histogram match back to the source, alpha resampled only. Output `<tex>.x4_sd.png`, variant `x4_sd` in the manifest. `--max-seconds N` pauses and resumes (the 2048 ground = 8192 px takes about 7.5 min on a shared 4090; other textures 10 s to 2 min).
- Verified: mean RGB within 0.6 of the source on groundB, groundC and bark; edge wrap difference no worse than the source on those three.
- Verdict from contact sheets: the flower, bark and groundB variants are visibly different at a glance and faithful. It adds legible structure (pebbles, bark plates, petal veins), but it is smoother and more painterly than the original grain. At strength 0.4 and above SD invents content: rockK (terraced cracks, dark holes) and rockD (moss turned to straw) drift, so rocks are not ready. Lower strength (0.25-0.3) trades detail for faithfulness.
- Not run on normal or mask maps.

### groundB round 2 (owner: round-1 SD "a bit smooth")

Sheet: `analysis/hd/groundB_round2.png` (1:1 crop and 4x zoom per column; test crop = 256 px source centre). Seam check: `analysis/hd/groundB_scan_seams.png`.
- A (SD retuned: sharper prompt/negatives, cn 1.3, 40 steps, DPM++ 2M Karras, strength 0.4, unsharp) and B (ESRGAN low + SD high, gain 1.0/1.5): still soft; SD at 512 px tiles cannot invent sharp grain from a blurry 4x input. Not worth shipping over round 1.
- C (`scripts/hd/detail_scan.py`, variant `x4_scan`): ESRGAN x4 base + high-pass (sigma 3, gain 0.5) of an ambientCG CC0 dirt scan (Ground111, `build/hd/external/`), histogram-matched to the source. Crisp, photo-like grain, layout and colors unchanged; mean RGB within 0.43 of the source (full 8192 px). Caveat: fine speckle also lands on smooth stones.
- Tileability: the source groundB itself is not seamless (edge wrap difference 8.8 vs neighbor 2.1); x4_scan adds only about 1.3 to it (the 1024 px scan tile divides 8192).
- D (SDXL + tile ControlNet) not installed: A to C did not need it.

### x4_blend (owner pick, 2026-11-12)

The owner rejected x4_scan (grain) on groundB and prefers Real-ESRGAN and SD, or a blend. `scripts/hd/blend_variants.py` writes `<tex>.x4_blend.png` = 50/50 RGB blend of x4_realesrgan and x4_sd (alpha from Real-ESRGAN), then an additive per-channel mean lock to the source (mean diff at most 0.25 on all). Made for flower, grassB, bark, groundB (8192), groundC, groundD, rockF; not rockD or rockK (SD drift). Every variant is at most 8192 px. Real-ESRGAN dif variants were created for these textures with the existing ncnn tool (`-n realesrgan-x4plus`). Seen on a groundC crop: the SD half adds a hatched pattern and shifts the leaf layout, and the blend keeps a faint trace of it.

## Phase 2 result (2026-11-12)

- **Tools:** `scripts/hd/detail_boost.py` makes `<tex>.x2_detail.png` for tiling environment textures: Lanczos 2x, plus the texture's own finest band-pass detail re-used one octave finer (tiled with a shift, zero mean, so colors do not move), a mild unsharp, and a bump term from that band added to the normal map. Mask and emissive maps get a plain 2x. `scripts/hd/make_hd_pack.py` writes a pack from the cache in the original nutexb format (BC1/BC3/BC5 as the source, full mip chain, block-linear, capped at 4096). Choice order for albedo: x4_blend (not groundC), x4_sd (bark, flower), x2_detail. Emissive (BC6H) is not encoded.
- **In game:** pack `build/mods_hd_florio/hd-florio` (28 Florio textures) loaded with 28 `[mods] hit` lines and no crash. Size 2x and 4x of the original works. Crops in `analysis/mods/compare/hd_ground_*` and `hd_path_*`: finer grain, crisper pebbles and grass, same colors. The gain is modest, and the ground is still magnified at 1080p.
- **Magenta wash:** not caused by larger textures. With only `hud-00024/25` (960x540) replaced at 1x, the same full-screen wash shows at the same fade (`analysis/mods/compare/magenta_wash_1x_hud2425.png`). Those two are a full-screen overlay used in fades. The text "Y" is the first typed letter of the text box.
- **Loader check:** a replacement nutexb with a bad footer, size or mip table is skipped with `[mods] skipped ...: invalid nutexb (reason)` and the original loads (`nutexb_problem`, `runtime/mods/mods.cpp`). All 28,369 original nutexb files and the packs pass the same rules in Python; the C++ was syntax-checked with clang only.
- **4K check (2026-11-12):** `hd-florio` at `SNAP_RENDER_SCALE=2` (3840x2160, groundB 8192) loaded 28 of 28 and did not crash. The pack is copied to `%APPDATA%\SnapRecomp\mods\hd-florio`. Cross-run frame pairing at 4K failed (image difference too high), so only unpaired crops exist in `analysis\mods\compare\4k\`.
- **Pikachu pack and the hub crash (QA bug B1), result 2026-11-13: NOT size related, no pool sizing exists.** Texture pools are made per texture by the game from the data size (`MemoryPoolInitialize size=0x556000` for a 2048 body_nor, 0x2ac000 for a 2048 BC1, 22 MB at 4096), so a larger replacement just gets a larger pool. Clean runs with `hd_pikachu` (9 `[mods] hit` lines each, hub route `qa_hub1`, `SNAP_FAST_BOOT=1`, build `build\w1`): 1024 `2-20261113_085345`, `0-20261113_091651` (plus `1-20261112_223017` with `SNAP_MODS_DELAY_MS=3000`); 2048 `1-20261112_213201`, `2-20261112_215952`; 4096 `2-20261112_213825`, `1-20261112_222748`, and 4096 at `SNAP_RENDER_SCALE=2` `2-20261112_230507`. Across all archived runs: 222 clean runs with the 22 MB textures vs 3 crashes (about 1%), and a run with no mods at all (`2-20261112_170915`, slow, 447 s) crashed with the identical stack, so the crash is a rare guest-side race that the mods only make a little more likely (slower loads). Signature: host null read in a guest variant visitor at `main+0x95d500` (the crash is the return after `main+0x95d548 bl 0x346de0`, a generation-checked handle lock that returns null), called from `0x95e14c`/`0x95ed48`/`0x345c24` (model instance setup `0x32e3c0`); just before it, three `BufferInitialize: builder has no memory pool (pool=0, off=0, size=0x26640...)` errors: the game passed a null pool for the model's mesh buffers, i.e. a stale resource handle in the guest, not our allocator. Not fixed (no reproducer: about 1 in 100 runs; the guest chain at the null-pool call is not logged). `make_pikachu_packs.py --max-edge` defaults to 4096 again. Pikachu was not shown on screen: no test route reaches a scene with it. `runtime/os/os_memory.cpp` now logs `[os-mem]` lines when the guest's heap or page allocation fails (none seen).
- **Loader cost:** replacement files are now read and validated once and shared (before, each hit re-read the file from disk). Present count at 125 s on `qa_lab1` with other workers running: no mods 6090, owner set plus hd-florio 5550, old loader with the same set 6330. The reported 15x slowdown did not reproduce with the current owner set.

## Same-frame before/after: `SNAP_MODS_AB=<P>` (test aid, 2026-11-12)

Cross-run pairs of the HD packs failed (route timing shifts with PC load), so the packs can be toggled inside one run. Off when unset, no effect on normal play.

- Set `SNAP_MODS_AB=<P>` and a mods folder (`SNAP_MODS_DIR`). While (present count / P) is odd the draws sample the ORIGINAL texture, otherwise the replacement. With `P=1` and `NVN_FRAME_DUMP_AT=N,N+1` the two dumps are consecutive presents (same pose, only the texture differs). In the dumps the odd-numbered present showed the replacement (the dump at present N shows the frame drawn under count N-1), so check which of the pair is sharper before labelling.
- How: when a replaced nutexb is served (`runtime/mods/mods.cpp`, `ab_register`) the host also reads the original file from `SNAP_MODS_AB_ORIG` (default `extracted/drp-v262144`, same relative path as in the pack). On the first draw that samples a texture (`runtime/nvn/nvn_draw.cpp`, `AbSubstitute`, called from `ResolveHandle`), `snap_mods_ab_original` finds the pair by comparing the first 4096 bytes of the guest's texture with the replacement (same width, height and mip count), and a second `TextureImpl` is built from the original data (its own width, height and mips, `packaged` data, uploaded once like any static texture). The descriptor then picks one of the two images per draw. Both stay resident; nothing is re-uploaded. `TextureImpl::abAlt/abTried` in `nvn_internal.h`.
- Limits: 2D textures only; a replacement whose format differs from the original is skipped; the original files must exist under `SNAP_MODS_AB_ORIG`. `SNAP_MODS_AB_LOG=1` logs each registration and near-miss.
- Dump 4K frames with `SNAP_WINDOW_W=3840 SNAP_WINDOW_H=2160 SNAP_RENDER_SCALE=2` (the scale is relative to 1080p) and `NVN_FRAME_DUMP_FULL=1` (the default dump is half size).

## Material re-texture: authoring rules (owner feedback 2026-11-12)

Owner on the first pass: "Magicarp texture/relief kinda creepy. You need to be more bespoke and really make it fit rather than just slathering weird scales over it everywhere." Cause: one dense hex-cell pattern over the whole body (lips and fin edges included), cells far smaller than the scales the artist painted. Rules for every material texture from now on:

1. **Refine what the artist painted.** Find each texture's own motifs (painted scale outlines, fur strokes, seams, cracks, rib lines, markings) and add detail at their scale and direction, so the HD texture is the same design seen closer. Do not introduce a pattern the original does not suggest.
2. **Bespoke per species.** One spec per species, `scripts/hd/species/<species>.json`, with hand-placed regions (UV island ids, Lab colour ranges, UV polygons, distance to the island edge), each with its own treatment, detail size in texels at 1024, amplitude, direction, and explicit exclusions (lips, mouth, eyes, fin borders, claws, cheeks, markings). First match wins, so exclusions come first. No global pattern.
3. **Real-world logic per region.** Fish: large overlapping scales following the painted ones, rear edge slightly raised, smooth glossy lips, fins with ribs only on the painted rib lines. Fur: soft, short, flow from the painted strokes, longer and softer at ear edges, cheeks untouched. Rock: segments with a bevel and sparse chips at edges, not brushed metal. Shell: scutes with grooved seams and faint growth lines. Silhouette and colours must read exactly like the original; detail shows only up close (Detective Pikachu style).
4. **Restraint.** Low amplitude by default. Nothing that reads as holes, cells or bumps clustered densely on skin (trypophobia). Large forms first, then subtle micro detail.
5. **Judge every output** with the sheet against the original; if a region looks worse or uncanny, turn it down or off.

### Second pass (2026-11-12/13): `species_author.py`

`scripts/hd/species_author.py author <species> [--debug DIR]` reads the spec and writes `x4_mat` (4096 master) and `x1_mat` (the master area-downsampled to the original size, normals renormalised; the detail now sits at the painted scale, so it survives at 1024 without the old "3x coarser" trick) into `build/hd/cache/<asset>/textures`, registered in the manifest. `pack <species> --root DIR --pack NAME` packs only the maps the material binds (`in_game` in the spec). `scripts/hd/mat_preview.py <species>` writes `analysis/hd/mat_<species>.png`: two angles and a close-up, each as original | **new, in game today** (only the maps the shader binds) | new, full (adds cache-only maps such as a normal for a body without a normal sampler; needs the material-swap work), plus 1:1 crops at 4096 of the original (Lanczos), the new `_dif` and `_nor`. The lit render is an approximation of the game shader.

Treatments (all read the painted feature first): `scales_lattice` (Voronoi of the staggered lattice that reproduces the painted scale column; height rises toward each scale's rear edge), `fin_membrane` (black-hat rib lines -> raised ribs, slight sag and lighter membrane between), `fur` (strand direction from the structure tensor of the painted strokes, gravity guess only where the paint has no direction; half the strand field is the painted stroke sharpened along the flow; optional longer/softer band at the island edge), `skin` (the painted grain only), `plates` (painted seams -> groove, bevel, dome; optional growth lines, sparse edge chips, painted-mottling grain; seam specks shorter than `min_area` texels are dropped, because a speck turned into a ring of growth lines on Squirtle and into round pits on Steelix), `none`. Any region can add `crisp_lines` (the painted line kept, its profile narrowed at 4096) and `par` targets. Bodies whose normal does not load get a faint baked cavity in `_dif` (`bake_ao`) and the cavity in `_par` G.
