Verdict: at 1:1 it reads as a butterfly wing; at pack size it is the painted powder with faint rows; the CPU preview (no mipmaps) shows the 4096 scales as twill/moire, which mipmapping should remove (not checked in game) | `_dif` + `_par` (512); `Body_nor` cache-only (Body and Wing share one set) |
| Dodrio (first courses) | Down on body and heads and the black lower body (short fur along the painted strokes); tail plumes and crest as long thin barbs along the painted streaks; legs and necks: their painted reticulation as the only micro relief (no new cells); beaks smooth, glossier; claws, tongues, mouth parts untouched. Verdict: faithful and subtle; the body highlight is a little softer | `_dif` + `_par`; `Body_nor` cache-only |
| Grookey (first courses) | Short fur along the painted strokes on green, brown and orange fur (four materials share the set); face patch shorter fur; muzzle is bare skin (grain only, gloss kept); head leaf: grain only, crisp midrib, waxier; stick, mouth, tooth untouched (no wood grain was painted, none added). Verdict: good, visibly furrier up close, colours unchanged | `_dif` + `_par`; `Body_nor` cache-only (Body binds the dummy normal) |
| Scorbunny (first courses) | Short fur along the painted strokes, longer at ear tips and tufts; on the white the albedo strands are capped at 1% and the baked cavity at 0.12 (a first try at 2% made the white look grey); yellow ear marks, nose, band, mouth untouched; toe and finger lines crisp. Verdict: clean white, fur only up close; ears improved most | `_dif` + `_par`; flocky shader keeps `dummy_flocky_texture` as normal, `Body_nor` cache-only |
| Wurmple (first courses) | Red skin: the painted wrinkle crackle as the only micro relief, artist roughness kept (a rougher `_par` spread the highlight over the painted sparkle and read as speckles); belly: soft grooves exactly on the painted fold lines; spikes glossier keratin; prolegs untouched. Verdict: faithful; change is small (crisper folds) | `_dif` + `_par`; `Body_nor` cache-only |
| Pinsir (first courses) | Body and legs: chitin plates split on the painted segment grooves (narrow groove, soft bevel, gentle dome), painted mottling as fine grain, satin; limbs grain only; horns, spikes, claws smooth glossier keratin, the painted horn pores stay paint (no pits); teeth, mouth untouched. Verdict: faithful; in game nearly identical (crisper grooves), the relief is in the cache-only normal | `_dif` + `_par`; `Body_nor` cache-only |
| Wingull (first courses) | Wing and tail: long thin barbs along the painted streaks, low relief; head and body: smooth contour feathers, long soft strands, albedo change under 1% (a first try made the white look hairy); beak glossier; feet grain only; mouth untouched. Verdict: clean, subtle | `_dif` + `_par`; `Body_nor` cache-only |
| Crabrawler (first courses) | Shell: groove and soft bevel only on the painted panel outlines, gentle dome, painted mottling as faint grain, satin; cream crest and joints glossier; claw opening and dark patch untouched; no granules (none painted). Verdict: faithful; in game nearly identical (crisper outlines) | `_dif` + `_par`; `Body_nor` cache-only |
| Bounsweet (first courses) | Rind: painted grain only, a little glossier; white body matte grain; sepals waxy grain with a faint undulation; no pores (none painted; the dotted look in the preview highlight is the artist's own `_par` sparkle); nub and feet untouched. Verdict: faithful; small change | `_dif` + `_par`; `Body_nor` cache-only |

First-course batch (2026-11-13): species from Florio Nature Park, Lental Beach and Lental Jungle (course map from the `LV_MAP_*.levelb` string tables, local note `analysis/hd/course_species.md`), added with `build_cache.py --variants none`, authored with `scripts/hd/species_author_ext2.py` (species_author + `species_author_ext.py` multi-material sets + the new `wing_scales` treatment in `species_ext_wing.py`). Every body lacks a usable normal slot, so in game today only `_dif` and `_par` change; fur and plate relief stay faint until the material-swap work. `mat_preview.py` samples the 4096 maps without mipmaps, so very fine detail (wing scales, `_par` sparkle) aliases in the panels; compare at `--variant x1_mat` for the pack-size look.

Batch 3 (2026-11-13, owner asked for metal, plastic-like and organic): species picked from courses outside Florio and the other texture workers' lists, added to the cache with `build_cache.py --variants none`. A spec set can now cover several materials that share one texture set (`"mat": ["Body", "wing", "wingB"]`); island ids follow mesh order. Every batch-3 body again lacks a normal sampler, so the visible in-game change is `_par` roughness and spec mask (gloss) plus the faint cavity in `_dif`. Metallic: only Skarmory and Carbink have BC3 `_par` (alpha kept as authored); BC1 bodies get roughness/spec only.

Batch 2 lesson: every batch-2 body lacks a normal sampler, so in game only the albedo strands/cavity and the `_par` roughness change; skins (Charizard, Bulbasaur, Machamp, Gengar) will look almost unchanged until the material-swap work lets a normal load. Painted vein or crackle lines fainter than about 5 L do not trace as lines; use the paint-proportional `skin` high-pass on them instead of `fin_membrane`.

Not done: in-game check of any of these; the normal sign is still assumed OpenGL; the first-pass `material_author.py` stays for its helpers and the old species table only.

## Material re-texture (pilot, 2026-11-12; superseded by the rules and second pass above)

Script `scripts/hd/material_author.py` (`author <asset> --scale 4|1`, `pack <asset> --root DIR --pack NAME`), preview `scripts/hd/mat_preview.py` (offline lit CPU render + sheet `analysis/hd/mat_<species>.png`). Variant `x4_mat` = 4096 master from the 1024 originals (Cheek 512 -> 2048); `x1_mat` = same pipeline at original size with 3x coarser features so the detail survives at 1024 (this is what packs use until B1 is fixed). Both are in `build/hd/cache/<asset>/textures` and registered in the manifest. Eye and Mouth: upscale only (Lanczos on straight RGBA, alpha untouched), never in the pack.

Method:
1. **Islands and flow.** UV islands from `model.gltf` (triangles joined by shared UV points), rasterized at 2048 and extended to the gutter by nearest island, so strands/streaks stop at island borders and the padding carries the island's own pattern (no bleed over seams). Some meshes sit outside 0..1 (material repeat/offset, e.g. Cheek); the UV is wrapped per triangle. Fur flow = gravity + backward (-Y, -Z) projected on each triangle's tangent plane into UV space, smoothed per island with doubled-angle averaging, with a low-frequency angle jitter; where the flow is unsure (flat top of the head) strand strength is lowered.
2. **Regions.** k-means (6) in Lab on the albedo; each cluster centroid goes through a per-species colour rule (`SPECIES` in the script) to a class (Pichu black = smooth_skin per catalog, rest fur; Magikarp orange = scales, cream/white = smooth_skin; Steelix = metal, near-black = none). Class masks are blurred 1 px so blends do not hard-edge.
3. **Per class.** fur: two-scale line-integral-convolution strands (fine + clump) along the flow; albedo gets multiplicative luminance variation (about 4%) plus root darkening/saturation (gamma > 1 in crevices), colors locked to the original low-frequency (Gaussian sigma 2.5 px at 1024, ratio clamped 0.8..1.25); normal = original XY + strand gradient XY (std 0.08), clamped to length 0.9; _par R pulled 40% toward 0.72 with strand variation, G times (1 - 0.2 cavity), B slightly lowered in crevices. smooth_skin: pores plus two-octave noise, normal std 0.035, R toward 0.62, B x0.65 (it removed plastic gloss on the black ears). scales: jittered hex-row cells (36 px at 4096), dome + border groove, per-cell tint, G cavity 0.3 at borders, R toward 0.34, B domed. metal: brushed LIC streaks (random +-20 degree angle per island) + hammered blotches, R toward 0.2, B pulled toward 1; A = metal only where the _par format has alpha (BC3/BC7), else untouched.
4. **Channel convention written.** `_dif` sRGB, alpha kept; `_nor` in the original's format: BC5 XY (Pichu), BC7 XYZ with B copied as the original's constant 255 (Pikachu), OpenGL (+Y up) assumed for G (the originals are pure noise, so the sign could not be read from them; if lit micro-relief looks inverted in game, flip G); `_par` R/G/B linear.
5. Albedo is procedural, not SD: SD tile ControlNet re-draws pixels and risks marking drift, and the fur/scale detail needed to be strand-aligned. Mean RGB of the albedo stays within about 0.5/255 (Pichu body 3/255 in B from the crevice gamma).

Species, results (sheets `analysis/hd/mat_pichu.png`, `mat_pikachu.png`, `mat_magikarp.png`, `mat_steelix.png`; the lit render is my approximation of the shader, not the game's):
- Pichu (fur; Body dif/nor/par, Cheek dif/par): clearly furrier, colors and ear/collar markings unchanged. Seams between islands show as a change of strand direction in the flat texture, not in the lit render.
- Pikachu (fur; Body dif/nor, Cheek dif): same. The body has no `_par` slot (the fur shader `12075339` binds none), so `Body_par.x4_mat.png` is a cache-only new file for a future material change.
- Magikarp (scales): scales read as scales on the lit render, but the Body material has no normal sampler: only `_dif` and `_par` can load, so in game the relief is just the albedo shading plus AO (G) and roughness (R). `Body_nor.x4_mat.png` is cache-only.
- Steelix (metal): subtle (brushed streaks, lower roughness). Body `_par` is BC1 (no A) and the body shader `3452202033` has no normal sampler, so no metallic and no relief can load; Body_emi, flb, flc, flp untouched.
- Squirtle, rock, feather, plant, slime classes: not done.

Not done: in-game check of normal sign and strength on more than Pichu; 4096 in game (waits for B1); fur on shells/eyes; a per-region flow better than the gravity guess; SD or Real-ESRGAN base under the procedural detail; a viewer toggle beyond the manifest entry.

```

`docs/hle-services.md`:

```md
# Horizon service HLE (runtime/hle)

Host overrides for every non-os, non-audio, non-NVN `nn::` service that New Pokemon Snap reaches. Each override is a
plain `void(Cpu*)` function keyed by its mangled symbol (TotK `HOST_OVERRIDE` convention): arguments come from the
AAPCS64 registers in `Cpu`, guest pointers are host pointers. Nothing here depends on the lifted game, so `tests/hle`
runs without it.

Layout (all under `runtime/hle/`):

| File | Content |
| --- | --- |
| `hle.h`, `overrides.cpp` | `Entry` registry, `HLE_IMPL` / `HLE_NOOP`, `bind_all`, logging, `unimplemented()` backstop, `fatal()` |
| `hle_config.*`, `json_lite.h` | Config file (`hle.json`), minimal JSON reader/writer with `//` comments |
| `fs_core.*`, `fs.cpp` | Host file system (rom, save, host mounts) and the `nn::fs` shims |
| `input_core.*`, `input_backends.cpp`, `hid.cpp` | Mapping table, Win32 and SDL3 backends, `nn::hid` shims |
| `services_sys.cpp` | oe, pctl, settings, time, account, err, diag, album, ngc, swkbd, vi, crypto, friends, codec |
| `services_net.cpp` | nifm, nsd, prepo, socket, ssl (offline) |
| `reg_sys.inc`, `reg_net.inc` | One registration per line, generated from `analysis/runtime/imports_usage.tsv` |
| `gen_hle_stubs.py` | Writes `analysis/runtime/hle_coverage.tsv` and `generated/hle_unimplemented.cpp` |
| `PROPOSED_SHARED_CHANGES.md` | What the loader, `runtime/os` and `runtime/nvn` need to do |

## Coverage

`analysis/runtime/hle_coverage.tsv` has one row per import of `main` (731) plus 14 rows for overrides of symbols that are
not `main` imports. Totals for the 731:

| Status | Count | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| implemented | 153 | Real behavior in `runtime/hle` |
| stub-noop | 67 | Registered, does nothing on purpose (prepo, nv, init/finalize calls) |
| lifted-pure-software | 408 | Runs as lifted guest code: libc, libc++, libc++abi, nn::util, fontll, image (JPEG), mem, crypto AES/MD5/SHA1, swkbd arg builders, nn::result, weak data symbols |
| todo | 103 | os 86 (`runtime/os`), audio 16 (`runtime/audio`), nvn 1 (`runtime/nvn`). Zero are owned by `runtime/hle` |

`nn::` imports owned here that have no override log their name, caller (x30), sp and x0-x7 (plus readable C-string
arguments) and abort: `hle::unimplemented()`. `gen_hle_stubs.py` creates one such stub per leftover import
(`generated/hle_unimplemented.cpp`); today that list is empty. `--all` also stubs os, audio and nvn imports.

Regenerate after any registration change: `python runtime/hle/gen_hle_stubs.py`.

## nn::fs

### Mounts and boot path (evidence in `main`, module offsets)

- `nnMain` builds the strings "rom", "save", "sdmc" (0x4e3f70..0x4e4138). Only `MountRom("rom", cache, size)` runs
  (0x4e4138), after `QueryMountRomCacheSize` (0x4e410c). Paths are built as `rom:/...` (prefix at 0x4e4150-0x4e41cc).
  `rom:` maps to `extracted/romfs-v262144/` (config `romfs_root`), read-only.
- Save init is one function (0x4d5300-0x4d9cf4): `account::Initialize` (0x4d7a0c), `GetUserCount` (0x4d7a14),
  `TryOpenPreselectedUser` (0x4d7a30), `GetUserId` (0x4d7a44), `GetNickname` (0x4d7a60),
  `fs::GetSaveDataSize(&size, &journal, uid)` (0x4d7b00), `MountSaveData("savedata", uid)` (0x4d7b10, string at 0xb0aad6).
- Save file names use the format `savedata:/%08x%08x` (0xaf02b0). `Unmount("savedata")` at 0x4e146c.
  `Commit("savedata")` at 0x6072f4, 0x60744c, 0x607564, 0x607678, 0x607790, 0x6078ac, 0x609710.
- `GetFreeSpaceSize` at 0x609a30 requires 100 MiB or more (`>> 0x16 >= 0x19`) and at 0x6107c8; on shortage the game calls
  `ExtendSaveData(uid, size + need, journal)` (0x610800). The host reports at least 4 GiB free so that path never runs.
  `GetSaveDataSize` reports `save_data_size` (128 MiB) and `save_journal_size` (32 MiB): the NACP values were not found,
  these are assumptions.
- The SDK libc inside `sdk` reaches `CreateFile`, `GetFileSize`, `SetFileSize`, `GetEntryType`, `OpenDirectory`,
  `ReadDirectory`, `CloseDirectory`, `GetDirectoryEntryCount`, `OpenFile`, `CloseFile`, `WriteFile`: all overridden.

### Result codes

`nn::Result` = module in bits 0-8, description in bits 9-21. The game classifies fs failures at 0x602c90: module must be
2 (`w & 0x1ff`), description is `w & 0x3ffe00`.

| Result | Value | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| PathNotFound | 2-1 (0x202) | description 1 (0x200) maps to game error 0xd |
| PathAlreadyExists | 2-2 (0x402) | `CreateFile` compares `& 0x3fffff == 0x402` at 0x602f0c; maps to game error 0xf |
| TargetLocked | 2-7 (0xe02) | description 7 (0xe00) maps to game error 0x11 (0x60362c) |
| UsableSpaceNotEnough | 2-31 | `ubfx w9,w0,#9,#0xd; sub #0x1e; cmp #0x10` at 0x603614: descriptions 30..45 map to game error 0x10 |
| DirectoryNotEmpty | 2-8 | SDK value, not seen in the game |
| OutOfRange | 2-3005 | SDK value for a short strict read |
| InvalidArgument, NotMounted, WriteNotPermitted | 2-6001, 2-6002, 2-6003 | host-chosen; the game treats any other nonzero as a generic failure |

Other facts the shims follow: `GetEntryType` gives 0 = directory, 1 = file (0x8bd348); `OpenDirectory` mode 1 is used
(0x8bd38c); the 4-argument `ReadFile` is strict (the generic reader at 0x8d9840 treats nonzero as failure), so a read past
the end returns OutOfRange; `WriteFile` honors the WriteOption flush bit (bit 0).

### Layered overlay (mod-loader hook)

`Fs::set_rom_layers({dirA, dirB, ...})` or config `rom_layers`: an ordered list, first match wins, `romfs_root` is
always last. File lookup, entry types and directory listings merge all layers (a name present in two layers is listed
once, the first layer's file wins). Layers are read-only; `extracted/` is never written.

### Save data design

Goal: the save on disk is always one complete committed state, even if the process dies at any instruction.

```
<save_root>\<uid>\            default %APPDATA%\SnapRecomp\save\<32 hex digits of the uid>\
  CURRENT                     "SNAPSAVE1\n<n>\n<check>\n"  pointer to the live generation
  gens\<n>\                   complete state of generation n, immutable once committed
  gens\<n>.ok                 marker, written after generation n is complete
  working\                    copy-on-write scratch for the mounted session (wiped at mount)
```

- Writes after `MountSaveData` go to `working/` (files are copied on first write). Nothing is visible to the next mount
  until `Commit`.
- `Commit` builds generation n+1: unchanged files are hard-linked (copied if linking fails), dirty files are copied, then
  the marker is written, then `CURRENT.tmp` is written and moved over `CURRENT` with
  `MoveFileEx(REPLACE_EXISTING | WRITE_THROUGH)` (rename on POSIX). The pointer replace is the single commit point.
- Recovery at mount: read `CURRENT`; if it is missing or invalid use a valid `CURRENT.tmp`; otherwise scan for the newest
  `.ok`. Generations newer than the pointer (a crashed commit) are deleted.
- Automatic backups: the newest `save_backups` (default 5) older generations are kept next to the current one, older ones
  are pruned. `Fs::list_generations` and `Fs::restore_generation` expose them; restore commits a copy of the chosen
  generation as a new one, so it is atomic too.
- Test fault hook stages: `commit:begin`, `commit:carried`, `commit:file`, `commit:files-done`, `commit:marker`,
  `commit:pointer-tmp`, `commit:pointer-done`. Crash at any stage before `pointer-done` leaves the old save; at
  `pointer-done` the new save (tested).
- `Unmount` without `Commit` discards the working copy, like the console.

## nn::hid

Pipeline: backend (Win32 XInput + keyboard + mouse, or SDL3) fills `RawInput` -> mapping table -> `PadSample` /
`TouchSample` -> the shims fill `NpadState` (0x28 bytes: `{s64 seq; u64 buttons; s32 lx, ly, rx, ry; u32 attrs}`).

- Npad: `controller_style` 0 (default) = Pro Controller style (FullKey, id No1); 1 = Handheld (id 0x20, attributes 0x3f).
  The game lists No1 and 0x20 (0x9258f4, 0x925944) and sets styles 3 = FullKey | Handheld (0x925948), so both work.
  All four `GetNpadState` variants exist; other ids and styles read as empty. `ShowControllerSupport` reports one player.
- Touch: the left mouse button is one finger on the 1280x720 panel (`TouchScreenState<6>`, 0x100 bytes, 0x28-byte touches).
  Gestures report none.
- Six-axis: one handle per npad (a 4-byte word; 0x7fffffff means none, 0x4c1514-0x4c152c), at rest, identity matrix
  (`GetSixAxisSensorStates` stride 0x60, angular velocity at +0x1c, 0x4c15ec). The game never calls them (trace verified), so gyro
  aim is a host feature: SDL3 gyro (or `SNAP_GYRO_FAKE`) is added to the right stick; the six-axis state also carries the rate
  (1.0 = 360 deg/s) when gyro aim is on, UNTESTED against the game. Switches in `host\README.md`.
- Vibration: `SendVibrationValue` (floats ampLow, freqLow, ampHigh, freqHigh; amplitudes become the low/high motors) goes to
  `SDL_RumbleGamepad` on every rumble-capable pad, XInput as fallback, scaled by `SNAP_RUMBLE` (0 off .. 1.5) or the profile.
  `SNAP_RUMBLE_LOG=1` logs each game request and host call (`rumble:` lines).
- Focus: when the window is not in the foreground all input reads as released (env `SNAP_INPUT_BACKGROUND=1` disables).
- Default mapping (by position, A = east button). Stored in `%APPDATA%\SnapRecomp\input.json` (format version 2; `SNAP_CONFIG_DIR` overrides the folder; the version 1 `config\input_map.json` is migrated). Edited live by the F1 controls menu (`runtime/ui`); schema in `Mapping::to_json`. Menu open: the npad reads idle.

| Switch | Gamepad | Keyboard / mouse |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A / B / X / Y | east / south / north / west | L / K / I / J |
| L / R | left / right shoulder | Q / E |
| ZL / ZR | left / right trigger (threshold 0.5) | Left Shift / Space |
| Plus / Minus | start / back | Enter / Backspace |
| D-pad | d-pad | T / F / G / H (up / left / down / right) |
| Left stick | left stick, radial dead zone 0.15 | W A S D |
| Right stick | right stick | arrow keys |
| Touch | | left mouse button |

Schema (JSON, `//` comments allowed, every key optional, missing keys keep the default; an invalid file is rejected as
a whole with a message and the old table stays):

```json
{ "version": 1,
  "trigger_threshold": 0.5,
  "mouse": { "touch": true, "look_sensitivity": 0 },
  "buttons": { "A": ["pad:east", "key:L"], "ZR": ["pad:rtrigger", "key:Space"] },
  "left_stick":  { "analog": "left",  "deadzone": 0.15, "up": ["key:W"], "down": ["key:S"], "left": ["key:A"], "right": ["key:D"] },
  "right_stick": { "analog": "right", "deadzone": 0.15, "up": ["key:Up"], "down": ["key:Down"], "left": ["key:Left"], "right": ["key:Right"] } }
```

Sources: `pad:<south|east|west|north|back|guide|start|lstick|rstick|lshoulder|rshoulder|dpad_up|dpad_down|dpad_left|dpad_right|ltrigger|rtrigger>`,
`key:<name>` (A-Z, 0-9, F1-F12, Up/Down/Left/Right, Space, Enter, Escape, Tab, Backspace, LShift ..., Numpad0-9),
`mouse:<left|right|middle>`. Button names: A B X Y StickL StickR L R ZL ZR Plus Minus Left Up Right Down. Positional
pad names follow SDL3, so one table serves XInput and SDL (south = Xbox A). `look_sensitivity` above 0 lets mouse
movement drive the right stick.

## nn::oe, nn::applet

`GetOperationMode` returns Console (docked) unless config `docked` is false. Focus state stays in-focus:
`TryPopNotificationMessage` never returns a message. `SetPerformanceConfiguration(mode, config)` (called at
`main 0x638a84` with `0, 0x20004`) is accepted and logged under `SNAP_HLE_TRACE=svc`. `GetDesiredLanguage` returns the
language code for config `language`. `GetProgramTotalActiveTime` returns process uptime. The imports do not include a
display-version or performance-mode query, so `display_version` is stored but nothing reads it.

## Other services

| Service | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| time | `GetCurrentTime` / `now()` from the host clock (UTC posix). `ToCalendarTime` returns the calendar in the host's local zone (Windows setting through the CRT, DST by date; fills dayOfWeek, dayOfYear, abbreviation, isDst and utcOffset in CalendarAdditionalInfo); `SNAP_TIME_ZONE=utc` forces UTC, env `TZ` overrides the zone (tests). `ToPosixTimeFromUtc` real; `GetDeviceLocationName` still reports "UTC" (the game does not branch on it) |
| settings | `LanguageCode::Make`, `operator==` with the 18-entry Language table (1 = en-US default); `region` is stored, not read by any import |
| account | One local user, name from `user_name` ("Default"), uid from config `uid` (default `534e415052454331` `0000000000000001`). Network service account calls fail with the offline result |
| err | `ApplicationErrorArg` constructor fills the real layout (error at 0, language at 8, dialog at 16, fullscreen at 2064); `ShowApplicationError` and `ShowError` log and show a message box unless `headless` |
| diag | `AbortImpl` and `DiagAbortFormat` log expr, function, file, line and abort |
| album | `SaveScreenshot` writes an RGBA8 PNG to `screenshot_dir` (default `%APPDATA%\SnapRecomp\screenshots`) and returns success |
| swkbd | `ShowKeyboard` returns a canceled result (no on-screen keyboard) |
| ngc | Profanity filter initializes; `CountNumbers` counts digits |
| vi | Only what NVN needs: tokens for display, layer and native window; vsync event at 60 Hz via the os hooks |
| nifm, nsd, prepo | Offline: `IsNetworkAvailable` false, requests fail, `nsd::ResolveEx` echoes the name, prepo calls succeed and store nothing |
| socket | Every call fails with -1 and errno ENETDOWN (50, FreeBSD numbering), `Close` with EBADF; byte-order and inet helpers are real; `GetAddrInfo` returns EAI_NONAME |
| ssl | Contexts and connections fail with an offline result; destroy calls succeed |
| friends, pctl, codec, nv | No-ops (`pctl::TryBeginFreeCommunication` and `IsFreeCommunicationAvailable` return true) |
| crypto | `GenerateCryptographicallyRandomBytes` uses a host RNG; the AES/MD5/SHA1 code is lifted |
| mem, util, fontll, image | Pure software, lifted, no override |

Host-chosen result codes (the game only tests success versus failure, 25 call sites): nifm 110-300, ssl 123-1,
account 124-5, swkbd 101-1.

## Config

`%APPDATA%\SnapRecomp\config\hle.json` (env `SNAP_HLE_CONFIG` overrides the path). All keys optional.

| Key | Default |
| --- | --- |
| `romfs_root` | `extracted/romfs-v262144` (env `SNAP_ROMFS`) |
| `rom_layers` | `[]` (mod directories, first match wins) |
| `data_root` | `%APPDATA%\SnapRecomp` |
| `save_root` | `<data_root>\save` (env `SNAP_SAVE_ROOT`) |
| `save_backups` | 5 |
| `save_data_size`, `save_journal_size` | 128 MiB, 32 MiB (assumed) |
| `user_name`, `uid` | "Default", 32 hex digits |
| `language`, `region` | 1 (en-US), "US". Language numbers: 0 ja, 1 en-US, 2 fr, 3 de, 4 it, 5 es, 6 zh-CN, 7 ko, 8 nl, 9 pt, 10 ru, 11 zh-TW, 12 en-GB, 13 fr-CA, 14 es-419, 15 zh-Hans-CN, 16 zh-Hant-TW, 17 pt-BR |
| `docked` | true |
| `controller_style` | 0 (Pro Controller); `"handheld"` or 1 for Handheld |
| `input_map` | `%SNAP_CONFIG_DIR%` or `<data_root>`, file `input.json` |
| `screenshot_dir` | `<data_root>\screenshots` |
| `headless` | false (env `SNAP_HLE_HEADLESS=1`): error dialogs only log |

Trace: `SNAP_HLE_TRACE=fs,hid,svc` or `all`.

## Not verified (assumptions)

- `save_data_size` / `save_journal_size` values (NACP not seen); only that `GetSaveDataSize` succeeds matters.
- `album::SaveScreenshot` `ImageSize` call site was not found; 0 = 1280x720, 1 = 1920x1080, anything else is derived from
  the data size.
- Result values other than the four in the table above are SDK recollection or host-chosen.
- `vi` vsync and `account` async events need the os hooks (PROPOSED_SHARED_CHANGES.md); until `runtime/os` provides them
  the events never fire.
- Windows only in practice: the Win32 backend and `MoveFileEx` commit are tested; the POSIX branches compile paths exist
  but were not run.

`docs/horizon-os.md`:

```md
# Horizon nn::os on the host (runtime/os)

`runtime/os` replaces the sdk's `nn::os` layer with host code. It covers threads, scheduling, synchronization, fibers, time, TLS slots, and memory (VAMM and heap). Each function is a host override keyed by mangled symbol. The calling convention follows TotK's `HOST_OVERRIDE`: arguments arrive in guest x0-x7 and the result goes back in x0.

- **Table:** `os_override_table()` holds 197 entries, listed in `runtime/os/overrides.tsv`. Every name was checked against sdk's dynsym.
- **Tests:** `tests/os/os_test.cpp` has 145 host-only checks and uses no game data. Build it with `tests/os/build.bat`.
- **Integration:** the remaining loader work is in `runtime/os/PROPOSED_SHARED_CHANGES.md`.

Addresses below are sdk module offsets (`analysis/import/v262144-sdk.elf`) unless they say `main+`.

## 1. Design

| piece | file | model |
|---|---|---|
| scheduler, arbitration, SVC backstop | `os_kernel.cpp` | one global lock `G`; one host condition variable per guest thread; keyed wait queues (wake order: lower priority value first, then first come) |
| threads, TLS, fibers, time | `os_thread.cpp` | one Win32 thread per guest thread; one Win32 fiber per guest fiber |
| sync objects, MultiWait | `os_sync.cpp` | guest-layout objects; host state keyed by guest address |
| VAMM, heap | `os_memory.cpp` | VirtualAlloc reserve and commit |
| table | `os_overrides.cpp` | merged name to function map |

The scheduler shape (one lock, a condition variable per thread, priority-then-FIFO order) follows TotK Recomp `runtime/kernel.c` (MIT). No code was copied from it.

**Two override levels.**

- The public `nn::os` API is replaced, for example `LockMutex` and `WaitEvent`.
- The sdk-internal primitives under it are replaced too: `InternalCriticalSectionImplByHorizon`, `InternalConditionVariableImplByHorizon`, `SdkMutexType`, `SdkRecursiveMutexType`, `SdkConditionVariableType`, and the `ThreadManager`/`TlsManager`/`VammManager` members.

sdk calls its own exports through its PLT, so internal callers reach the host versions as well.

**Lock words keep Horizon's encoding.** A lock word holds the owner thread handle, OR'd with 0x40000000 when there are waiters. A condition-variable key is a u32 that is 1 while it has waiters. Because of this, sdk code that is still lifted and touches these words inline agrees with the host. Examples are the arbitration in `ReaderWriterLockImpl`, `IsLockedByCurrentThread`, and libc++'s pthread condvar, which reaches SVC 0x1d directly.

**SVC backstop.** `os_svc` handles these SVCs on the same queues:

- thread SVCs: 0x0b-0x10 and 0x25;
- arbitration SVCs: 0x1a ArbitrateLock, 0x1b ArbitrateUnlock, 0x1c WaitProcessWideKeyAtomic, 0x1d SignalProcessWideKey;
- 0x1e GetSystemTick.

**No OsResourceManager.** sdk keeps all `nn::os` state in `OsResourceManager` (GOT sdk+0xc88838). The host never constructs it.

- **Overridden:** every function on the boot path that dereferences it. The full xref list has 66 functions; it was made with a scratch ADRP/LDR scanner.
- **Still lifted:** the functions listed in `PROPOSED_SHARED_CHANGES.md` section 6. They would crash on the null singleton if reached.

This fixes boot blocker 1 in `analysis/recomp/sdk_and_boot.md`: `ThreadManager::SetZeroToAllThreadsTlsSafe` (sdk+0x344af0) on a null `this`.

## 2. Guest layouts and evidence

All offsets are in `runtime/os/os_layout.h`, with the instruction that proves each one. Summary:

| object | size | key fields (offset: meaning) | evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| TLR (tpidrro_el0) | 0x200 | 0x0 IPC buffer, 0x100 disable count, 0x1d8 errno, 0x1f0 ELF thread pointer, 0x1f8 ThreadType* | trampoline sdk+0x348e80 |
| ThreadType | 0x1c0 | see the ThreadType rows below | sdk+0x344480 (CreateThread), sdk+0x3446a0 (InvokeThread) |
| FiberType | 0x58 | 0x20 state (1 ready, 2 running), 0x28 func, 0x30 arg, 0x38 original stack, 0x40 stack, 0x48 size, 0x50 saved context | sdk+0x33f6b0..0x33f860 |
| MutexType | 0x20 | 0 state, 1 recursive, 4 lock level, 8 nest count, 0x10 owner ThreadType*, 0x18 CS word | sdk+0x340ff0..0x341160 |
| ConditionVariableType | 8 | 0 state, 4 key | sdk+0x33e9e0 |
| EventType | 0x28 | 0 holder list, 0x10 signaled, 0x11 initially signaled, 0x12 clear mode, 0x13 state, 0x14 broadcast counter u64, 0x1c CS, 0x20 CV | sdk+0x33ed20 |
| SystemEventType | 0x30 | EventType plus 0x28 state (1 intra-process, 2 inter-process) | sdk+0x33ffd8 |
| LightEventType | 0xc | 0 word (2 = signaled), 4 autoclear, 5 state | sdk+0x33f040 |
| SemaphoreType | 0x28 | 0x14 count, 0x18 max, 0x1c CS, 0x20 CV | sdk+0x3417e0 |
| BarrierType | 0x14 | 0 max u16, 2 arrived u16, 4 generation u64, 0xc CS, 0x10 CV | sdk+0x33e6e0 |
| ReaderWriterLockType | 0x2c+ | 0 CS, 0x10 state, 0x18 write owner, 0x24/0x28 CVs (0x4-0xf are host counters) | sdk+0x3411f0, +0x3412e4 |
| TimerEventType | 0x40 | 0x13 timer state (0 stop, 1 one-shot, 2 periodic), 0x20 next expiry, 0x28 first, 0x30 interval | sdk+0x33f8d0, +0x33f9c0 |
| MessageQueueType | 0x48 | 0x20 buffer, 0x28 max, 0x2c count, 0x30 offset, 0x38 CS, 0x3c/0x40 CVs | sdk+0x3402f0 |
| MultiWaitHolderType | 0x40 | 0x28 owning MultiWait, 0x30 object, 0x38 user data (0 = host kind tag instead of the vtable) | sdk+0x340e8c, +0x340fb0 |

ThreadType fields:

| offset | meaning |
|---|---|
| 0x40 | state: 0 not initialized, 1 initialized, 2 destroyed before start, 3 started, 4 terminated |
| 0x44 | base priority (s16) |
| 0x48 / 0x50 / 0x58 | original stack, stack, stack size |
| 0x60 / 0x68 | argument, function |
| 0x70 / 0x78 | current fiber, the thread's own fiber |
| 0x80 | 32 TLS values |
| 0x180 / 0x1a0 | name buffer, name pointer |
| 0x1a8 / 0x1ac | CS, CV |
| 0x1b0 / 0x1b8 | handle, thread id |

**Confidence.**

- **High:** ThreadType, TLR, Mutex, Event, Semaphore, MessageQueue, TimerEvent and FiberType. Each offset was read from at least one load or store in the functions named above. The fiber and TLS offsets are also exercised by the tests.
- **Medium:** ReaderWriterLock counters (host-defined) and MultiWait list internals. The guest never reads those through anything other than the overridden API.

**Priorities.** nn::os priorities run 0..31, and kernel priority = nn::os priority + 28 (sdk+0x348d20). The main thread is kernel 44, from `main.npdm`, which is nn::os 16. The game's wrapper at main+0x8dea70 uses 31, 23, 16, 8 and 1.

**Thread creation.** As in svcCreateThread, a new thread is pinned to its ideal core (mask = 1 << ideal) until `SetThreadCoreMask` is called. The default ideal core is the npdm default core 0. The default name is `Thread_0x<entry hex>` (sdk+0x3445c0).

**Time.** `GetSystemTick` is 19.2 MHz counts. `ConvertToTimeSpan` and `ConvertToTick` are exact replicas of TickManager sdk+0x3451e0 and sdk+0x345270, including their clamps and round-up.

## 3. Scheduler model and how it approximates Horizon

- **Cores and stacks.** Every guest thread is a host thread with its own `Cpu`, a 256 MiB reserved host stack (every guest BL is a host call), the guest stack it was given, and a TLR. A guest thread runs guest code only while it holds one of three virtual cores, subject to its core mask.
- **Blocking.** A thread releases its core whenever it blocks: in a mutex, condvar, event, sleep, MultiWait, or `os_host_block_begin`. It takes a core back before returning to guest code.
- **Free core.** A free core goes to the best waiter whose mask allows it: lowest effective priority value first, then longest ready.
- **Core handoff (fixed 2026-11-12).** A waiter takes a free core only if it is that core's best waiter, so the best waiter of every free core must be woken after any change (core freed, waiter leaves the wait list, waiter priority or mask changes); `kick_free_cores` does this. Before the fix, a waiter that took one of two freed cores still counted as waiting while it handed on the other core's wakeup, so it woke itself and a core-pinned waiter slept forever with all cores free. That was the intermittent lab-intro hang (main thread 65, timer thread and audio thread in `run` with `waiting_core=1`, cores free). An untimed core wait now rechecks every `core_rescue_ms` (20 ms) as a safety net; any wait it ends is a missed handoff and is logged and counted in `OsStats::core_wake_rescues`, which should stay 0. The watchdog dump prints the core wait list and the waiter each free core is reserved for.
- **Preemption** is cooperative.
  - **Request:** a ready thread that outranks a core holder sets the holder's preempt flag. So does an equal-priority thread at priority 31 once the holder has run longer than the 10 ms round-robin slice (Horizon round-robins only kernel priority 59).
  - **Where the holder yields:** at its next poll point. Poll points are `GetSystemTick`, `UnlockMutex`, `SignalEvent`, `SleepThread(0)`, `YieldThread`, every blocking call, and `os_spin_gate`/`os_poll`.
  - **Overflow core:** if the holder does not yield within `overcommit_us` (2 ms), the waiter runs on an overflow core, so a non-polling spin loop cannot deadlock the game. This is counted in `overflow_grants`. The deadline restarts when the holder asked to yield changes (2026-11-13).
  - **Migration (2026-11-13, review finding 1):** a waiter that outranks no holder, but whose core is held by a thread that may run on a free core, asks that holder to move (Horizon's idle core pulls a suggested thread whose core has a next thread). At its poll point the holder moves straight to the free core and keeps running; the waiter takes the vacated core. A holder that does not poll gives the waiter an overflow core after 2 ms. A freed core that no waiter may use wakes the waiters that have such a migration. Before this, a pinned loader (p31, core 2) waited behind a JobWorker on core 2 for as long as the job ran, with core 0 idle.
  - **Priority drops (2026-11-13, finding 3):** when a holder's priority gets worse (end of a priority-inheritance boost or ChangeThreadPriority), the core waiters it no longer outranks are woken and the holder is asked to yield. Before, they noticed only at their 20 ms safety-net recheck.
  - **Yield to any (2026-11-13, finding 2):** `svcSleepThread(-2)` and a spin gate after 4,096 consecutive passes hand the core straight to its best waiter of any priority; the yielder does not preempt that thread for `yield_any_us` (1 ms). `svcSleepThread(0/-1)` and `YieldThread` still yield only to equal or better waiters.
  - **Blocking host work (2026-11-13, finding 9):** `Fs::read_file` and the VAMM retry backoff release the virtual core (`os_io_begin`/`os_io_end`), like a Horizon IPC wait.
  - All four are switchable back with `SNAP_SCHED_LEGACY` (`host\README.md` "Scheduler switches").
- **Priority inheritance.**
  - A thread waiting in ArbitrateLock is recorded on the lock owner. The owner's effective priority becomes the minimum of its base priority and its waiters' priorities. The boost propagates along chains (owner waiting on another lock) up to depth 64.
  - Unlocking hands the lock directly to the best waiter, like KConditionVariable::SignalToAddress.
  - A condvar waiter that is signalled while its mutex is held moves to that mutex's waiter list.
- **Wake order.** All waits wake in priority order, then FIFO. This covers condvar, LightEvent, timer, ReaderWriterLock, join and MultiWait queues. `test_wake_order` checks order 1, 8, 16, 23, 31.

**Where it differs from Horizon.**

- **Per-core run queues:** there are none. Horizon keeps per-core run queues and migrates threads; here a thread may take any free core its mask allows.
- **Preemption:** it happens at poll points, not at any instruction.
- **Time quanta:** the host OS decides time slicing between the host threads that hold cores.
- **Core numbers:** `GetCurrentCoreNumber` returns the virtual core held, so code that indexes per-core data stays consistent while a thread holds its core.

## 4. Spin loops and the lifter's back-edge poll

The lifter turns marked spin back-edges into `rt_spin_gate(c, head)`. The loader forwards that to `os_spin_gate`, which does the following:

- every pass runs `_mm_pause`;
- every 64 passes it yields to an equal or better waiter, and after 4,096 consecutive passes (no gap of about 3 ms) it yields to any waiter of its core;
- it always honors a pending preemption.

Spin loops that need the gate (see `PROPOSED_SHARED_CHANGES.md` section 4):

- `nn::os::BusyMutex`. It is deliberately left lifted; its word is touched inline.
- The job scheduler at main+0x548000..0x54f000.
- LL/SC retry loops in libc++ (`call_once`, atomic waits).

Without a gate, such a loop still makes progress: a thread Horizon would run gets an overflow core after 2 ms. The spinning thread still burns its core, though.

## 5. Fibers

The job scheduler switches fibers. Each guest fiber gets its own `Cpu` and a Win32 fiber with a 64 MiB reserved stack, because lifted code keeps its frames on the host stack. The fiber's guest stack is still the one the game passed to `InitializeFiber`.

**What is saved per fiber.** Horizon's DispatchFiberContext (sdk+0x3483ec) saves only x19-x30, sp and q8-q15. So tpidr, tpidrro, FPCR and FPSR follow the thread: the switch copies them into the target fiber's `Cpu`.

**Sdk semantics kept:**

- target 0 means the thread's own context;
- a fiber function returns the next fiber, and 0 returns to the thread;
- ThreadType+0x70 and +0x78 are cleared when the thread context resumes.

**Migration.** A fiber can migrate between threads. It is claimed with an atomic `running` flag, and the context that was switched away from is released only after the next context runs. That way a fiber is never resumed on two threads at once.

**Tests:** 2,000-round ping-pong between two fibers, and one fiber resumed by three different threads.

## 6. Memory

- **VAMM.**
  - `AllocateAddressRegion` reserves with `VirtualAlloc(MEM_RESERVE)`.
  - `AllocateMemoryPages` commits read/write pages inside a reserved region.
  - `FreeMemoryPages` decommits, and `FreeAddressRegion` releases.
  - `AllocateMemory` does reserve plus commit.
  - Result codes are the sdk's own: 0x1003 out of memory, 0x1803 out of address space, 0xe03 range not inside a region (VammManager sdk+0x346f00, +0x347630).
  - This fixes boot blockers 3-5. main's first request is a 0x200000-byte region.
- **Heap.**
  - `SetMemoryHeapSize` uses one 16 GiB reservation and commits up to the requested size, in 2 MiB units.
  - `AllocateMemoryBlock` is first fit and page aligned; `FreeMemoryBlock` returns a block.

## 7. Deviations from Horizon (deliberate)

- **SystemEvents** are always intra-process (state byte 1).
  - `AttachSystemEvent(handle)` binds the guest event to a host handle from `os_handle_alloc`. HLE services signal it with `os_handle_signal`.
  - `InitializeMultiWaitHolder(holder, handle)` resolves to the first event attached to that handle.
- **MultiWaitHolder.** The guest vtable slot at +0 holds a host kind tag. The holder lists live in a host registry, not in the guest intrusive lists.
- **Not supported:** `SuspendThread`, `ResumeThread`, `GetThreadContext`, InterProcessEvent and InterruptEvent waits, and shared or transfer memory mapping. They are not on the boot path.
- **QuickExit and ExitProcess** terminate the host process.
- **`GetIdleTickCount`** returns 0.
- **Alias stacks** are not created. `stack aliased` stays 0, and the guest stack address is used directly.

## 8. Tests (`tests/os/os_test.cpp`)

The harness's `rt_dispatch` calls `c->pc` as a host function. Thread entries and fiber functions in the test are therefore plain C++ functions, and every `nn::os` call goes through `os_override_find(mangled)`.

| case | what it checks |
|---|---|
| time+layout | tick frequency, ConvertToTimeSpan/ConvertToTick values and clamps, a 20 ms sleep, main ThreadType state, name, TLR+0x1f8 and priority 16 |
| threads+tls | state transitions, default name, pinning to the ideal core, running on core 2, TLS value and destructor |
| producer/consumer | 4 producers and 4 consumers at priorities 31/23/16/8/1 over an 8-slot MessageQueue, 20,000 items; exact count and sum; Jam/Peek order |
| priority inversion | low-priority L holds a mutex, high-priority H waits, medium M spins 600 ms on L's core; L's current priority is 1 while H waits, and H gets the lock about 0.2-3 ms after L is released (before M finishes) |
| fibers | ping-pong alternation and fiber field reset; migration across 3 threads |
| multiwait | timed WaitAny timeout, WaitAny on 3 events, link order, thread holder |
| wake order | 5 condvar waiters woken one at a time, in priority order |
| memory+boot | VAMM, heap, TlsManager/ThreadManager members with a null `this`, available core mask |
| core handoff | 300 rounds: cores 0 and 2 freed back to back while a better unpinned waiter sleeps; the core-0-pinned waiter must still run (hung on round 0-2 before the fix) and no wait may end by the safety net |
| sched migrate | 2 x 250 rounds: a p16 JobWorker-like thread (mask 7) on core 2 spins (no poll, then through the gate) on a flag that a p31 thread pinned to core 2 sets; core 0 is then freed. The p31 thread must run within 50 ms (before the fix: 300 ms, the spinner's own timeout; after: median 3 ms no poll, 0.01 ms gated) |
| sched yield any | 300 rounds: p23 holds a busy lock and is preempted at GetSystemTick by a p16 thread on the same core that spins on the lock through the gate; the spinner must get the lock (before: 276 of 300 stuck) |
| sched unboost | 60 rounds: a p31 holder boosted to p1 unlocks; the p8 core waiter must run within 3 ms median (before: 21 ms) |
| sched mw race / time mono / cv far / destroy race / event pulse / link wake / vamm block | findings 4, 5, 6, 8, 11, 13, 9 of `analysis\core\review_os.md` (vamm block needs `SNAP_FAULT_VAMM=0:7 OS_TEST_ONLY=vamm`; destroy race shows the old use-after-free only under `-fsanitize=address`) |
| stress 10K | mutex 6x10K, Event and LightEvent ping-pong 10K, Semaphore 10K, condvar 10K, RW lock, Barrier 3x1000, Sdk* types, periodic timer |

**Result:** 145 checks, 0 failed, on 7 consecutive runs. One run takes about 4 s on a loaded PC.

**Sanitizers:** TSan is not available for clang on Windows, so the stress test relies on assertions over non-atomic shared data protected by the primitives under test. The stress test found one real bug, now fixed: a condvar waiter published its key word after releasing the mutex, which lost wakeups.

## 9. Risks

1. **Poll coverage.** A tight loop with no poll point holds a core until the 2 ms overflow. Frame pacing may need more gates in the job scheduler.
2. **Lifted nn::os code that reads OsResourceManager** (section 1) crashes if reached. The probe run will show which, if any, are on the game's path.
3. **Thread-pointer hooks.** Until the loader passes `nnmuslThreadPointerInitializer` and `nnmuslThreadPointerDestroyer` to `OsConfig`, new guest threads start with tpidr 0, which breaks musl TLS.
4. **Host stack size.** 256 MiB is reserved per thread and 64 MiB per fiber. Deep guest recursion is a host stack overflow. The job scheduler may create many fibers; each reserves address space but commits only what it uses.
5. **Inter-process events, interrupt events and shared memory** are unimplemented. HLE services must use `os_system_event_*` or `os_handle_*`.
6. **Timer precision** is the Windows high-resolution timer, about 0.5-1 ms. A periodic 60 Hz TimerEvent can drift by up to one period under load. Expiry catches up and never accumulates.
7. **Scheduling is not cycle accurate.** Races that happen to be benign on Switch timing may show up. The `SNAP_OS_TRACE` log and the `OsStats` counters are the first diagnostic.

```

## Top 8, implementation sketches

Ordered by score; ties go to the lower-risk idea. #12 (free camera) has the highest impact but is TRACE-gated, so it is a stretch goal rather than an overnight item.

### 1. Anisotropy 16x and LOD bias (rows 1 and 3)

- **Files:** `runtime/nvn/nvn_entry.cpp` (SamplerInitialize path that already applies `nvnHostSetAnisotropyOverride`), `runtime/nvn/nvn_host.h` (add `nvnHostSetSamplerLodBias(float)`), the F1 Graphics tab in `runtime/ui` or `host`.
- **Where in the game:** all samplers come from `0x9216d0` (cache `0x3206d0`, 27 call sites). Aniso is 1 and bias about 0 today. The override applies to mipmapped, non-comparison samplers only, which matches the game's rule that aniso applies when mip mode is 2.
- **Steps:** (1) set 16 before the game creates samplers (start-up config, restart to apply); (2) add the bias hook next to it, applied as `lodBias += setting` at SamplerInitialize; (3) F1 dropdown 1x/2x/4x/8x/16x and a bias slider; cap at the device limit.
- **Test:** `tests/nvn` run with 16 and 0; log the created `VkSamplerCreateInfo`; boot the lab scene with `SNAP_SAVE_DIR=build\testsave`, compare a floor or wall screenshot at the same camera. Validation errors stay 0. Then a mip-bias run at render scale 2 with bias -0.5 to -1.

### 2. Unlock all courses and time-of-day variants (row 2)

- **Files:** `scripts/snap_save.py` (`unlock`, `unlock_routes`; existing), `build\fixtures\saves\unlock_all` and `unlock_routes`, F1 Saves tab "Import test save" (exists in `host/README.md`).
- **Fields:** course status = save file 11, byte at `route-1`, 0 locked / 1 unlocked / 2 entered (`analysis/save/fields.md`, read side High). All 30 `RouteData` rows already cover the A/B/C time-of-day packs (`time_of_day` 1/2/3), so unlocking all 30 gives time of day on every course with no data edit.
- **Steps:** (1) import `unlock_routes` into a new profile (no points, so the research log cannot hit an invalid entry id); (2) enter each course in game; (3) only then try `unlock_all` (level 4) and watch the research log.
- **Test:** the map select screen shows all 30 routes, each course loads, and the save survives quit and reload (checksums verified by `snap_save.py dump`). Risk: the `+4` field and entry id 1 are Low confidence, so keep a backup profile.

### 3. Render scale and 4K (row 4)

- **Files:** `runtime/nvn/nvn_entry.cpp` and `nvn_host.h` (existing hooks), a config read at start-up, F1 Graphics tab.
- **Where in the game:** fixed immediates (scene and SSAO 1920x1080 in `0x5bd940`, 960x540 chain, bloom 192x108 at `0x5c23a0`). The host scales plain render targets and keeps the guest's view of sizes, so no guest patch is needed. The built-in exemption keeps the Evaluation depth target (1920 wide, `0x5c3d38`) at 1.0.
- **Steps:** (1) test scale 1.0 vs 1.5 and 2.0 with zero validation errors; (2) add tag-based exemptions for `Capture3D`, `CaptureCompress`, `ResizeTexture` (sizes in `0x5c7f70`, `0x5c8028`, `0x5c8ab4`) so saved photos and scoring inputs stay original; (3) pair with idea 1's LOD bias.
- **Test:** (a) screenshot at 2.0 shows finer edges; (b) take a photo at scale 1.0 and 2.0 of the same scene and compare the saved JPEG and the score (identical expected); (c) FXAA output not blurred. Not done yet: the open question that the game reads GPU-written memory without a sync, and the 15,000 render-target-also-sampled skips per minute (AGENTS.md) that scaled targets could change.

### 4. Pass toggles and clean-photo HUD (rows 6 and 7)

- **Files:** `host/hooks.cpp` (add a host override for the pass enable setters or the execute loop `0x988fe0`), the F1 overlay.
- **Where in the game:** 37 pass nodes built in `0x5bd940` (names and create sites in `analysis/maps/render_passes_final.tsv`); the loop `0x988fe0` calls the per-pass Execute (`0x982210`, slot 5) only on enabled passes; setters `0x5cc0a0`, `0x5cd4a0`, `0x5cd5c0`, `0x5cd6e0` flip enables per `[ctx+0xcec]`.
- **TRACE first (short):** one NVN trace of a frame with draw-call tagging per pass to learn the enable flag offset in the 0xf8-byte pass object, and to confirm that the viewfinder and film counter draw in `UI`.
- **Steps:** (1) map pass name to object; (2) skip Execute for a chosen set; (3) expose FilmGrain, ChromaticAberration, Monotone, DOF, bloom and `UI` as toggles; (4) a "photo clean" hotkey that hides `UI` only.
- **Test:** each toggle changes the screenshot as expected; `Capture3D`, `CaptureCompress`, `Evaluation`, `Report` are not togglable; take a photo with `UI` hidden and confirm the saved photo and score match the normal path.

### 5. Texture pack path: HD upscales (row 5)

- **Files:** `scripts/hd/` (upscaler outputs in `build/hd/cache/`), a new nutexb encoder, the loose-file loader, a pack folder under `build/hd/` per `docs/hd-assets.md` phase 2.
- **Where in the game:** `nutexb` is loaded whole, no streaming (wrappers `0x8f86e8`, `0x8f87e8`), so a replaced entry takes effect without engine changes. Owner direction: modest detail only, textured same-camera comparisons, no model work.
- **Steps:** (1) encoder round trip first (decode -> re-encode -> bit compare, same format, mips, block-linear); (2) one species end to end (Pikachu `CH_025`); (3) A/B screenshot in game against the original.
- **Test:** the encoded file decodes identical to the PNG; the game loads it; no validation errors; frame time not worse than baseline. Open item: the match for dimension changes (the engine reads mip levels from the nutexb header, so larger sizes should work, unconfirmed).

### 6. Golden Pikachu and recolors (row 8)

- **Files:** the same encoder and loader as #5; `CH_025_00_0_A00_Body_dif.nutexb` (and `_par`, `_Eye_dif` if needed) from `extracted\drp-v262144\nx\Pack\Characters\master\CH_025.drp\`.
- **Steps:** (1) hue-shift the body texture only (small Python script, `-I`); (2) override the entry; (3) run the first course with Pikachu. This also serves as the first end-to-end proof for #5.
- **Test:** Pikachu shows gold in game, other species unchanged. Zero scoring effect expected because no geometry or registry changes; check one photo of Pikachu scores like the stock texture on a fixed replay.

### 7. Shadow map size (row 9)

- **Files:** `runtime/nvn/nvn_entry.cpp` (texture creation hook, like render scale), config and F1.
- **Where in the game:** dynamic shadow depth target 1024x1024, format id `0x144` (`0x5b8b10` call at `0x5bdd34`); static 3 x 1024x1024 (`0x4d12a8`, loop `0x4d1310`). Match by signature (1024x1024, depth, that format) and allocate larger, reporting the original size to the guest as the render-scale hook does.
- **Risk to check:** the shadow cbuffer texel size must match. If the shader reads a constant texel size from the game, upscaled maps sample only part of the map unless the host also rescales the viewport (the render-scale code already scales viewports, scissors and clears). Compare with the baked 4,578 `Shadow.nutexb`, which stay as is.
- **Test:** screenshot a character shadow edge at 1024, 2048, 4096; no light leaking; zero validation errors; scoring unchanged (the Evaluation pass uses its own targets).

### 8. Fog and atmosphere distance, plus research thresholds as the cheap data mods (rows 10 and 11)

- **Files:** loose-file overrides of `LV_ENV_*.levelb` (33 on disk) and `Resident.drp/ResearchPoint.mdrp`; `scripts/fb_roundtrip.py` and `scripts/fb_walk.py` as the writer.
- **Where in the data:**
  - ENV levelb keys (crc32 of name) for `atmosphericStartingDistance`, `horizontalAtmosphericDistance`, `verticalAtmosphericDistance`, `fogUnevenness`; CRC32 bytes found in 33 of 33 files. The matching consumer reads are at `0x5d93bc`, `0x5d9450`, `0x5d96c4` (loader compares at `0x2c8538..0x2c85a8`).
  - `ResearchPoint.mdrp` `thresholds` (`mdrp.fbs`, M confidence for the struct meaning; threshold use at `0x5e0b10`, High).
- **Steps:** (1) use the walker to print the value slot next to each key for one `LV_ENV`; (2) scale the start distance and see the effect; (3) for thresholds, lower the three non-zero values per route and confirm the level-up in game after one photo.
- **Test:** re-encoded files are identical when unchanged (335/335 round trip), then edited values show in game; photo evaluation depends on what is visible, so run the same replay on stock and edited fog (S risk low-medium); thresholds do not touch saved scores (the level is derived at read time).

`docs/mods.md`:

```md
# Mods: loose-file DRP entry replacement

A mod replaces single entries inside the game's DRP archives (textures, models, FlatBuffers registries, Lua, UI, text) by
dropping the decompressed file into a pack folder. No archive is repacked. Everything is local: the repo holds the loader,
never game data or mod payloads made from it.

## Folder layout

Mods root: `%APPDATA%\SnapRecomp\mods\`, or the folder named by the `SNAP_MODS_DIR` environment variable.

```
mods\
  mods.json                      priority order and enabled flags (optional)
  my-hd-pack\
    pack.json                    name, version, author, description
    common\UI\master\Foo.drp\    <- the archive path, exactly as under rom:/ (the folder name ends in .drp)
      icon_a.nutexb              <- one decompressed entry, named like the extracted file
```

The path below the pack folder is `<archive path>/<entry file>`, the same layout as
`extracted\drp-v262144\` (written by `scripts\drp_unpack.py`). The first folder whose name ends in `.drp` is the
archive; the file inside it is the entry. Files elsewhere in a pack (`pack.json`, readme, screenshots) are ignored.

How an entry is matched (case-insensitive):

- **Archive**: the path up to and including the `.drp` folder.
- **Name**: the file name without its last extension (`icon_a`). A name the game stores with its extension
  (`foo.nutexb`) is matched either way.
- **Type**: the extension, mapped to the game's extension id (crc32 of the lowercase extension; `nutexb` -> `5C156DBC`).
  An 8-digit hex extension (the unpacker's name for types it does not know, e.g. `DC4A8177`) is used as the id directly.

Limit: the unpacker names an entry whose name repeats inside one archive `name__<index>.ext`. The loader cannot tell such
entries apart, so that file overrides every entry with the same name and type in that archive.

## pack.json

```json
{ "name": "Magenta UI test", "version": "1.0.0", "author": "you", "description": "What it changes." }
```

All fields are optional text. The folder name is the pack id used in `mods.json` and in the log.

## mods.json and priority

```json
{ "packs": [
    { "id": "my-hd-pack", "enabled": true },
    { "id": "ui-tweaks",  "enabled": false },
    "older-pack"
] }
```

- The list is in priority order: the first pack wins when two packs replace the same entry. The loser is named in the log
  (`[mods] conflict: ...`).
- A plain string means enabled. A pack that is listed but missing, or on disk but not listed, is skipped (a warning is
  logged for the first case).
- Without a `mods.json`, every folder that contains a `pack.json` is enabled, in name order.
- Changes apply at the next game start. There is no hot reload.

## Making an override

1. Find the entry under `extracted\drp-v262144\` (the manifest `analysis\romfs\drp_unpacked.tsv` lists every entry).
2. Make your replacement in the same format as the original. For a texture, a `nutexb` with the same BC/ASTC format, or
   any new size you like (below).
3. Place it:

   ```
   python -I scripts\mods\make_override.py extracted\drp-v262144\common\UI\master\Foo.drp\icon_a.nutexb my_icon.nutexb --pack my-hd-pack
   ```

   This writes `%APPDATA%\SnapRecomp\mods\my-hd-pack\common\UI\master\Foo.drp\icon_a.nutexb` (and a starter `pack.json`).
   `--mods-root` and `--dry-run` are available.
4. Start the game and read the log (stderr, or the trace of `host\run_boot.ps1`).

Log lines:

```
[mods] root C:\Users\...\SnapRecomp\mods: 1 overrides
[mods] common/ui/master/foo.drp/icon_a <- my-hd-pack            (every override, once, at startup)
[mods] hit common/ui/master/foo.drp/icon_a <- my-hd-pack (4096 bytes)   (first load of each entry)
[mods] summary: 1 replacements served, 0 failed, 1 overrides installed  (at exit)
```

## Larger or smaller replacements

The replacement may be any size. The loader's output buffer is allocated from the entry's size field after the hook runs,
and the game then checks the data against a CRC32 that the hook recomputes, so an HD texture 4x the original just
allocates 4x the memory. Whether the rest of the game copes is a content question: a `nutexb` carries its own width,
height and mip sizes, so a self-consistent bigger texture works. Data whose size is fixed elsewhere (tables that other
code indexes by the original length) must keep its size.

## How it works (for developers)

- `recomp/snap_gen.py` `MAIN_INLINE_HOOKS` makes the generated code call `rt_mod_entry(Cpu*)` just before `main+0x5e3a58`,
  inside the DRP entry worker (`main+0x5e38b0`, the only caller of `OodleLZ_Decompress`). Regenerating `main` is needed
  once after pulling this change (`recomp/snap_gen.py --module main`, then `recomp/snap_build.py`).
- The hook (`runtime/mods/mods.cpp`) finds the archive and entry name, looks them up in a hash set built at startup
  (`runtime/mods/mods_core.cpp`), and on a hit points the worker at a host-built chunk: the original header with csize =
  dsize = file size, the file's CRC32, and the file as an uncompressed payload. With no packs installed the hook is one
  atomic load and a return.
- Tests: `tests\mods\run_tests.ps1` (path mapping, index priority, size override) and
  `python -I tests\mods\test_make_override.py`.

```

`docs/motion-vectors.md`:

```md
# Motion vectors for DLAA / DLSS (design study)

Read-only study, 2026-11-12. Static analysis plus reads of the shipped shader reflection. No code was changed and the game was not run. Addresses are module offsets of `main` (build `DDB900FF...`) unless noted.
Confidence: H = several independent facts agree, M = one solid fact plus inference, L = guess that needs a run.

Overlap note: another worker is writing the upscaler front end in `runtime/nvn/upscale/` (`upscaler.h`, `upscale_nvn.h`, `upscale_dlss.cpp`, `shaders/upscale_mv.comp`) while this study was done. It already does tier 0 below (camera-only vectors from depth, jitter through viewports). Section 6 says what this study adds and what to check against that code.

## 1. Findings

1. The game has no velocity target, no TAA and no history buffer. FXAA is spatial. (H)
2. The camera matrices are in one constant buffer, `PerViewCBuffer`, with the current frame only. There is no previous-frame matrix anywhere in the buffers, so the host must keep last frame's copy. (H)
3. Every moving object is a `CharacterShader` draw. Its vertices come out of GPU skinning compute, so previous positions exist only if the host keeps last frame's skinned buffer. (H for the shader split, M for the buffer reuse)
4. Cheapest correct route: camera-only reprojection from depth (tier 0), then a velocity write for `CharacterShader` draws only (tier 1). Skip a full velocity pass for the world. (M)

## 2. Does the game already have a velocity target? No.

Evidence:

- `work/v262144-main.strings.txt` has no hit for velocity, motion vector, TAA, temporal, jitter, reproject, prev view or last frame. The only matches are `Wwise_Motion`, `ScenarioEmotion_Lines` and NEX packet history. (H)
- The 278 shader base names in `analysis/shaders/census.tsv` have no velocity, motion, temporal or history entry. The only anti-aliasing shaders are `FXAAOnlyPS`, `TonemappingFXAAPS`, `TonemappingLutFXAAPS`, `TonemappingLutFXAADistortionPS`. (H)
- Reflection of the three per-draw constant buffers (section 3) lists no previous-frame member. The 37 pass names (`render_graph.md` section 4) include ZPrepass, Opaque, Effect, BlendBuffer, Bloom, DOF, Final, UI, Fade and none for velocity. (H)
- The only render targets with a fixed size are the 1920x1080 scene targets, the 960x540 chain and the 192x108 bloom target (`analysis/enhancements/knobs.md`). No RG16F target was found by name. Formats were not decoded from the allocation sites, so a hidden RG16F target is excluded only by the three points above. (M)

## 3. Matrices and constant buffers

The shader reflection (`scripts/nushdb_parse.py`, 497 of the Resident programs sampled, all consistent) gives these layouts. NVN slot = reflection binding + 3 (`docs/nvn-vulkan-design.md`, "Binding model"). The layer maps them to Vulkan set 0 (design doc, "Binding model").

| Buffer | Reflection binding | NVN slot (`c[n]`) | Size | Stage | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `PerViewCBuffer` | 0 | c3 | 752 (0x2f0) | VS and PS | H |
| `PerWorldCBuffer` | 1 | c4 | 352 (0x160) | VS | H |
| `UpdatePerObject` | 3 | c6 | 128 (0x80) | VS and PS | H |

`PerViewCBuffer` members (offsets in bytes, each matrix is four vec4 = 64 bytes):

| Offset | Member |
|---|---|
| 0x000 / 0x040 | `viewMatrix` / `viewInverseMatrix` |
| 0x080 / 0x0c0 | `projectionMatrix` / `projectionInverseMatrix` |
| 0x100 / 0x140 | `viewProjectionMatrix` / `viewProjectionInverseMatrix` |
| 0x240 / 0x250 | `cameraPosition` / `cameraDirection` |
| 0x2a0 | `screenSize` (vec2) |
| 0x2a8, 0x2ac, 0x2b0 | game timer, absolute timer, cut-scene timer (seconds) |
| 0x2b4, 0x2c4, 0x2c8 | `exposureReciprocal`, `currentEV`, `currentExposure` |
| 0x200 | `preComputedWindDirection` (foliage wind) |
| 0x2e0, 0x2e4 | `dynamicShadowFarClip`, `dynamicShadowFadeLength` |

`PerWorldCBuffer` members: `worldMatrix` +0x00, `worldInverseTranspose` +0x40, `worldViewProjectionMatrix` +0x80, `billboardWorldMatrix` +0xc0, then padding.

Facts that matter for vectors:

- Matrices are stored column-major as four column vec4s. The shipped GLSL of `NormalTangentTexcoordPositionWorldSpaceVS` does `gl_Position = x*m[0] + y*m[1] + z*m[2] + m[3]`. (H)
- Objects are drawn with the baked `worldViewProjectionMatrix`, not with `viewProjection * world`. So changing `PerViewCBuffer` does not move objects. This is why jitter must go through the viewport (section 5). (H)
- There is no previous-frame member in any of the three buffers. (H)
- Depth is near-is-zero 0..1 (host layer, design doc). The projection matrix gives near, far and field of view at run time: `P[2][2]`, `P[3][2]`, `P[1][1]`. (M)
- Scene views other than the main camera also bind c3: shadow maps (1024x1024), evaluation spheres, photo passes. Tell the main view apart by its depth target (the other worker does this in `UpscaleOnSceneDraw`). (H)

Who writes `PerViewCBuffer`: not found statically. The layout string `ConstantBufferLayoutPerView` is referenced only from the pass-graph builder `0x5bd940` (at `0x5bde90`, `0x5be4e0`), which creates the layout; the fill code is behind a plug object (`Ccc4208` family, `0x5b8340` ctor). Camera globals found by the LOD work (`host/mods/lodanim.cpp`): camera object `main+0xcfb480`, vertical fov `main+0xcfb4c8`, aspect `main+0xcfb4cc`; perspective builder `0x38b710` (call site `0x38cdbc`, gameplay camera, fov 33 deg in the yard). (M, from that worker's static and dynamic notes)
Cheapest way to find the writer: guard-page the bound c3 range (the layer already has `NVN_WB_WATCH` machinery) and log the writer's stack. Not needed for tiers 0 and 1, because the layer reads the buffer at draw time.

## 4. The skinning compute (character vertex output)

The skinning programs are not in the nushdb files. They are plaintext NV_gpu_program5 compute programs inside GLSLC binaries in `main` rodata, each with `GROUP_SIZE 256`. Reflection names: `ForGPUSkinning`, `SkinningParam`, `PoseMatrix[0]`, `sourceStruct`, `influenceStruct`, `nearestBonesStruct`, `destinationStruct`, `dataPerBone[].dualQuaternion`, `enableBulgeCorrection`.

| Binary (module offset, size) | What it is | SSBOs | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| `0xca2780` (0x5600) | matrix-palette skinning, `PoseMatrix` cbuffer | 0 source, 1 influence, 2 destination | H |
| `0xca7d80` (0x54c8) | same, no source struct | 1 influence, 2 source and destination | M |
| `0xcad248` (0x7168) | dual-quaternion with bulge correction | 0 source, 1 influence, 2 destination, 3 nearest bones | M |
| `0xcb43b0` (0x7038) | same, no source struct | 1 influence, 2 in and out, 3 nearest bones | M |
| `0xcbb3e8` (0x7af8) | morph or blend-shape: base, deltas, weights | 0 base, 8 deltas, 2 destination; cbuffers 2 and 3 | M |

How they are used:

- The five programs are created in `0x95f210` (stored at object offsets +0x40, +0x60, +0x80, +0xa0, +0xc0). It sits in vtable slot `0xcc2f10`. (H)
- There are exactly two `DispatchCompute` call sites in the game: `0x95be00` and `0x960a30` (`analysis/runtime/nvn_usage.tsv`). Both group count = `(numberOfVertices >> 8) + 1`. `0x960a30` copies 0x200 bytes of pose matrices and 0x20 bytes of `SkinningParam`; `0x95be00` copies 0x50 bytes of params into a per-frame constant ring (256-byte aligned, ring object at data `0x71012febc8`). (H for the sites, M for which program each one drives)
- The call goes through the loader-filled pointer `main+0x1489a98` (`nvnCommandBufferDispatchCompute`). (H)
- About 20 dispatches per frame in the lab and yard (design doc, "Characters and Pokemon invisible"). The destination SSBO is the same pool range later bound as the character vertex buffer. The layer marks it GPU-written (`MarkGpuWritten`, `nvn_draw.cpp` line 770) and never copies it back. (H)
- Character vertex shaders (`CharacterShader_*VS`) take only `in_POSITION0`, `in_NORMAL0`, `in_TANGENT0`, `in_TEXCOORD0`. No bone indices. So skinning is finished before the draw and the vertex positions are final model-space positions. (H)
- The in-place variants (`0xca7d80`, `0xcb43b0`) read and write the same SSBO. If the game relies on the CPU re-uploading bind-pose data each frame, the GPU-owned rule would skip that upload. Character screenshots look right, so these variants are either unused or use ranges the CPU never rewrites. Unverified; check with `NVN_DRAW_LOG` before building tier 1. (L)

Shader families (counts from `census.tsv`):

- `CharacterShader`: 1,369 programs per stage, 96 unique VS and 714 unique PS code bodies. All Pokemon and characters. (H)
- `StageShader`: 1,010 programs per stage, 134 unique VS and 463 unique PS. All static world meshes. (H)
- `SkyShader` (44), `Constant` (7), `vdkEfx*` (particles and effects), `nuPreZ`.
- This split (moving versus static) is the cheapest handle for deciding which draws need object motion.

## 5. Hooks DLSS needs

Jitter:

- Use the viewport. Add a sub-pixel offset to every viewport emitted for scene targets (x right, y down). It moves every draw with no shader change and needs no edit of `PerViewCBuffer`. Scissor is left alone. The other worker's `UpscaleViewportJitter` already does this. (H)
- Never jitter: the 1024x1024 shadow maps, SSAO and bloom targets, the Evaluation depth target (width 1920, `0x5c3d38`), photo capture and thumbnail passes. Photo frames must be rendered unjittered and not upscaled. (H, matches `AGENTS.md` scoring rule)
- Sequence: 8 or 16 phase Halton. Send the same jitter to the vector pass so vectors are jitter-free, as DLSS expects.

Mip bias:

- Sampler choke point `0x9216d0` (cache `0x3206d0`); LOD bias is read at `0x921858` (desc+0x30). The host override already exists (`SNAP_LOD_BIAS=<f>|auto`, `runtime/nvn/nvn_entry.cpp`). (H)
- NVIDIA's guidance is `log2(renderWidth / displayWidth) - 1` for DLSS. The existing `auto` is `-log2(scale)`, where scale is relative to the game's 1080p targets, which is a different quantity. Reconcile before shipping. For DLAA the first value to try is the native-4K one (`-1`), to match the original texture sharpness at 1080p. (M)

Depth and exposure:

- ~~Depth is 0..1, near-is-zero, not inverted.~~ Corrected 2026-11-12 by a runtime probe of `PerViewCBuffer` (upscaler worker, `SNAP_UPSCALE_PROBE`): the projection is reversed infinite Z. P row 2 = (0, 0, 0, 0.01), row 3 = (0, 0, -1, 0), so depth 1 = near plane (0.01) and 0 = infinity. Pass `DepthInverted` (DLSS), `DEPTH_INVERTED | DEPTH_INFINITE` (FSR) and `INVERTED_DEPTH` (XeSS); `runtime/nvn/upscale/upscale.cpp` `TakeCamera` reads this from the matrix every frame. (H)
- Exposure: `currentExposure` / `exposureReciprocal` at `PerViewCBuffer+0x2c8` / `+0x2b4` can feed `pInExposureTexture` or `InPreExposure`. Scene color format was not decoded; if it is already tonemapped 0..1, run DLSS as LDR (`hdr = false` in `Eval`). (L)

Where DLSS goes and where UI stays:

- The UI is composited in the pass named `UI`, then `Fade`, into the window (DISPLAY) textures. The layer already never scales window textures and treats the present blit as the single scene-to-window mapping (design doc, "Window and present"). So UI naturally stays at output size, after upscaling. (H)
- Upscale the scene color before the game's post chain if the post targets can read the output-size image: SSAO, bloom (192x108) and DOF (960x540 chain) are small fixed targets and only need a bigger source. `Final` (tonemap and FXAA) must then draw at output size. If that is too invasive, upscale the tonemapped image instead and treat it as LDR. (M; the pass order edges were never decoded, `render_graph.md` section 8)
- Turn the game's FXAA off while DLSS or DLAA runs (`AaPatchFragment`, `SNAP_AA=off` in `runtime/nvn/nvn_aa.cpp`). Two anti-aliasing steps would blur the result. (H)
- Photo capture (`Capture3D`, `CaptureCompress`, `Evaluation`, `PhotoEditing`) must read pre-upscale, pre-UI images. `AGENTS.md` and the design doc already require this.

## 6. Design: cheapest correct route

Tier 0, camera-only reprojection from depth (small, mostly done):

1. At the first scene draw of a frame, copy `PerViewCBuffer` (c3, 752 bytes) from the bound range. Keep two frames.
2. Compute `prevViewProj * viewProjectionInverse` in double precision, run one compute pass over the depth target. Output RG16F pixel-space vectors (previous minus current), render size, jitter removed. This is `upscale_mv.comp`.
3. Wrong for: moving Pokemon and the player vehicle, foliage wind, water, particles. Right for the whole static world and for camera cuts handled by `reset`.

Tier 1, object and skinned motion (characters only):

1. Keep last frame's per-object world-view-projection. The per-draw cbuffer lives in a per-frame ring (the same ring pattern as the skin params), so its address cannot be the key. Key by vertex buffer address of attribute 0 plus first index; for characters the skinned destination range is the stable identity. Validate in a run that the destination ranges do not move between frames. (L)
2. Keep last frame's skinned positions. In the compute dispatch hook (`nvn_draw.cpp` near line 770), before the dispatch, copy the destination SSBO range into a shadow buffer of the same pool offset (about 20 characters per frame, a few MB, one `vkCmdCopyBuffer` and a barrier). Bind that shadow as an extra vertex stream when drawing the character. (M)
3. Patch only the `CharacterShader` family at translation time (96 VS, 714 PS bodies, reusing the `PatchFragmentOutputs` approach): the VS adds an output `prevClip = prevWVP * prevPosition`; the PS writes `prevWindow - (gl_FragCoord.xy - jitter)` to a second color attachment. Add that attachment to the scene pass only (the pipeline variant key already carries attachment count).
4. Make the second attachment RGBA16F, cleared to alpha 0. Character draws write alpha 1. The tier 0 compute pass keeps pixels with alpha 1 and fills the rest from depth, then writes the final RG16F image for NGX. This avoids a second geometry pass and keeps depth testing correct, because the vector comes from the same fragment that won the depth test.
5. Dither-faded and alpha-tested character pixels (`DitherRatio`, `AlphaTestRef` in `UpdatePerObject`) discard in the same shader, so they drop their vector too.
6. Skip alpha-blended character draws, particles (`vdkEfx*`), sea and the sky. Give them zero vectors and mark them in the reactive mask (`pInBiasCurrentColorMask`).

Not worth doing first:

- A separate velocity pass for all `StageShader` draws (1,010 programs, 134 unique VS). The static world is already right in tier 0.
- Foliage wind vectors. They need the previous time in the VS (`preComputedWindDirection`, timers in `PerViewCBuffer`). Revisit if ghosting on grass is visible.
- Transform-feedback geometry replay (the ScarletNX method). It costs more than tier 1 here because the skinning output is already a buffer.

Edge cases:

- Camera cuts and scene loads: call `reset` when the camera position jumps, a fade is above a threshold, or the scene targets are recreated.
- Newly spawned objects have no history: use their own current world matrix for the previous one (camera-only motion).
- The Evaluation passes and photo frames bypass all of this.

## 7. NVIDIA SDK status and integration points

- `tools/nvidia/` exists (created 2026-11-12). It holds `dlss_v310.9.16/` with the NGX headers (`nvsdk_ngx*.h`, including `nvsdk_ngx_helpers_vk.h` and the frame-generation headers), `lib/nvsdk_ngx_{d,s}.lib`, `bin/nvngx_dlss.dll`, `LICENSE.txt`, and `SOURCES.md` (tag v310.9.16, local use only, git-ignored). Contents of `SOURCES.md` agree with the folder. (H)
- Not present: the Streamline SDK (`sl.interposer.dll`, `sl.*.dll`) and a separate frame-generation runtime. So Reflex and DLSS-G through Streamline are not available yet. DLSS-G headers are in the NGX include folder only.
- `runtime/nvn/upscale/upscale_dlss.cpp` does not compile SDK code. It declares the NGX ABI itself and loads the driver's `_nvngx.dll`, with `nvngx_dlss.dll` copied beside the exe. That keeps the public build free of NVIDIA binaries.
- NGX call sites in our layer:
  - Instance and device creation: `NVSDK_NGX_VULKAN_RequiredExtensions` result must be added to `Host::Init` in `runtime/nvn/nvn_vk.cpp` (`snap_upscale::AddInstanceExtensions` / `AddDeviceExtensions`).
  - After device creation: `NVSDK_NGX_VULKAN_Init`, then `GetCapabilityParameters`, `CreateFeature(DLSS)` on a command buffer.
  - Per frame: `EvaluateFeature` recorded into the replay command buffer when the scene pass ends (`UpscaleOnSetRenderTargets` in `upscale_nvn.h`). Inputs: color, depth, vectors (RG16F), exposure, jitter, `InMVScaleX/Y = 1`, `InReset`, `InFrameTimeDeltaInMsec`, optional reactive mask. Output image needs storage usage.
  - Teardown: `ReleaseFeature`, `NVSDK_NGX_VULKAN_Shutdown1` in `Shutdown()`.
- Public builds: no DLSS binaries. Fall back to FSR, XeSS or plain render scale (already the order in `upscaler.h`).
- Streamline, if ever wanted for Reflex or frame generation: hook the swapchain and present in `PresentWindowOnce`. It requires the Streamline interposer to own the Vulkan loader, a larger change. Frame generation never counts toward real 60 or 120 FPS (`AGENTS.md`).

## 8. Order of work and effort

1. Verify tier 0 against the front end already written (matrix source, sign, jitter): 1 to 2 days of checking, not new code.
2. Dynamic check (needs a run, not done here): dump c3 and c4 of one character draw over three frames. Confirm the matrices, ring behavior, and that skinned ranges are stable. 1 day.
3. Tier 1 skinned shadow buffer and `CharacterShader` patch: about 1 to 2 weeks including photo-safety checks.
4. Reactive mask for particles and water, then wind: later.

- Which dispatch site drives which of the five skinning programs.
