`runtime/audio/audio_wasapi.cpp`:

```cpp
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// WASAPI shared-mode, event-driven render backend (Windows). Follows the default render endpoint: when the default
// device changes, or the current one is invalidated or unplugged, the stream is rebuilt on the new default device;
// while no endpoint exists a timer keeps consuming at stream rate so the guest never stalls.
#if defined(_WIN32)
#include "audio_internal.h"

#define WIN32_LEAN_AND_MEAN
#define NOMINMAX
#include <windows.h>
#include <audioclient.h>
#include <avrt.h>
#include <mmdeviceapi.h>
#include <ks.h>
#include <ksmedia.h>
#include <functiondiscoverykeys_devpkey.h>
#include <SpatialAudioClient.h>
#include <propidl.h>
#include "audio_mix.h"

#include <algorithm>
#include <atomic>
#include <new>
#include <chrono>
#include <cstdio>
#include <cstdlib>
#include <mutex>
#include <string>
#include <thread>
#include <vector>

#pragma comment(lib, "avrt.lib")
#pragma comment(lib, "ole32.lib")

namespace snap_audio {
namespace {

template <class T> void safe_release(T*& p) { if (p) { p->Release(); p = nullptr; } }

class Notify : public IMMNotificationClient {
 public:
  explicit Notify(HANDLE ev) : ev_(ev) {}
  ULONG STDMETHODCALLTYPE AddRef() override { return ++ref_; }
  ULONG STDMETHODCALLTYPE Release() override { ULONG r = --ref_; if (!r) delete this; return r; }
  HRESULT STDMETHODCALLTYPE QueryInterface(REFIID id, void** o) override {
    if (id == __uuidof(IUnknown) || id == __uuidof(IMMNotificationClient)) { *o = this; AddRef(); return S_OK; }
    *o = nullptr; return E_NOINTERFACE;
  }
  HRESULT STDMETHODCALLTYPE OnDefaultDeviceChanged(EDataFlow flow, ERole role, LPCWSTR) override {
    if (flow == eRender && role == eConsole) SetEvent(ev_);
    return S_OK;
  }
  HRESULT STDMETHODCALLTYPE OnDeviceAdded(LPCWSTR) override { return S_OK; }
  HRESULT STDMETHODCALLTYPE OnDeviceRemoved(LPCWSTR) override { return S_OK; }
  // Only the render endpoint in use matters (a USB mic, a headset's capture side or an idle second card must not rebuild the stream and
  // signal the game). With no endpoint open (cur_ empty) any render device becoming active is worth a retry.
  HRESULT STDMETHODCALLTYPE OnDeviceStateChanged(LPCWSTR id, DWORD state) override {
    std::lock_guard<std::mutex> g(mu_);
    if (!id) return S_OK;
    if (!cur_.empty()) { if (cur_ == id) SetEvent(ev_); }
    else if (state == DEVICE_STATE_ACTIVE) SetEvent(ev_);
    return S_OK;
  }
  void set_current(const wchar_t* id) { std::lock_guard<std::mutex> g(mu_); cur_ = id ? id : L""; }
  HRESULT STDMETHODCALLTYPE OnPropertyValueChanged(LPCWSTR, const PROPERTYKEY) override { return S_OK; }
 private:
  std::atomic<ULONG> ref_{1};
  HANDLE ev_;
  std::mutex mu_;
  std::wstring cur_;   // id of the render endpoint the stream is built on
};

void make_format(WAVEFORMATEXTENSIBLE& w, uint32_t rate, uint32_t ch) {
  ZeroMemory(&w, sizeof(w));
  w.Format.wFormatTag = WAVE_FORMAT_EXTENSIBLE;
  w.Format.nChannels = (WORD)ch;
  w.Format.nSamplesPerSec = rate;
  w.Format.wBitsPerSample = 32;
  w.Format.nBlockAlign = (WORD)(ch * 4);
  w.Format.nAvgBytesPerSec = rate * ch * 4;
  w.Format.cbSize = 22;
  w.Samples.wValidBitsPerSample = 32;
  w.dwChannelMask = ch == 8 ? (SPEAKER_FRONT_LEFT | SPEAKER_FRONT_RIGHT | SPEAKER_FRONT_CENTER | SPEAKER_LOW_FREQUENCY |
                               SPEAKER_BACK_LEFT | SPEAKER_BACK_RIGHT | SPEAKER_SIDE_LEFT | SPEAKER_SIDE_RIGHT)
          : ch == 6 ? (SPEAKER_FRONT_LEFT | SPEAKER_FRONT_RIGHT | SPEAKER_FRONT_CENTER | SPEAKER_LOW_FREQUENCY |
                               SPEAKER_BACK_LEFT | SPEAKER_BACK_RIGHT)
                            : (ch == 1 ? SPEAKER_FRONT_CENTER : (SPEAKER_FRONT_LEFT | SPEAKER_FRONT_RIGHT));
  w.SubFormat = KSDATAFORMAT_SUBTYPE_IEEE_FLOAT;
}

class WasapiBackend : public Backend {
 public:
  bool start(const DeviceFormat& f) override {
    fmt_ = f;
    // Probe once so a machine with no usable COM or enumerator falls back to the timer backend.
    IMMDeviceEnumerator* e = nullptr;
    HRESULT hr = CoCreateInstance(__uuidof(MMDeviceEnumerator), nullptr, CLSCTX_ALL, IID_PPV_ARGS(&e));
    if (FAILED(hr)) {
      if (hr == CO_E_NOTINITIALIZED) {
        CoInitializeEx(nullptr, COINIT_MULTITHREADED);
        hr = CoCreateInstance(__uuidof(MMDeviceEnumerator), nullptr, CLSCTX_ALL, IID_PPV_ARGS(&e));
      }
      if (FAILED(hr)) return false;
    }
    e->Release();
    stopEv_ = CreateEventW(nullptr, TRUE, FALSE, nullptr);
    run_.store(true);
    th_ = std::thread([this] { thread_main(); });
    return true;
  }
  void stop() override {
    run_.store(false);
    if (stopEv_) SetEvent(stopEv_);
    if (th_.joinable()) th_.join();
    if (stopEv_) { CloseHandle(stopEv_); stopEv_ = nullptr; }
  }
  int kind() const override { return SNAP_AUDIO_BACKEND_WASAPI; }
  int spatial_available() override {
    HRESULT hi = CoInitializeEx(nullptr, COINIT_MULTITHREADED);
    int ok = 0;
    IMMDeviceEnumerator* en = nullptr;
    IMMDevice* dev = nullptr;
    if (SUCCEEDED(CoCreateInstance(__uuidof(MMDeviceEnumerator), nullptr, CLSCTX_ALL, IID_PPV_ARGS(&en))) &&
        SUCCEEDED(en->GetDefaultAudioEndpoint(eRender, eConsole, &dev))) {
      ok = probe_spatial(dev, 48000, nullptr) ? 1 : 0;
    }
    safe_release(dev); safe_release(en);
    if (SUCCEEDED(hi)) CoUninitialize();
    return ok;
  }
  uint32_t native_channels() override {
    HRESULT hi = CoInitializeEx(nullptr, COINIT_MULTITHREADED);
    uint32_t ch = 2;
    IMMDeviceEnumerator* en = nullptr;
    IMMDevice* dev = nullptr;
    IAudioClient* ac = nullptr;
    WAVEFORMATEX* mf = nullptr;
    if (SUCCEEDED(CoCreateInstance(__uuidof(MMDeviceEnumerator), nullptr, CLSCTX_ALL, IID_PPV_ARGS(&en))) &&
        SUCCEEDED(en->GetDefaultAudioEndpoint(eRender, eConsole, &dev)) &&
        SUCCEEDED(dev->Activate(__uuidof(IAudioClient), CLSCTX_ALL, nullptr, (void**)&ac)) && SUCCEEDED(ac->GetMixFormat(&mf))) {
      ch = mf->nChannels;
    }
    if (mf) CoTaskMemFree(mf);
    safe_release(ac); safe_release(dev); safe_release(en);
    if (SUCCEEDED(hi)) CoUninitialize();
    return ch;
  }

 private:
  struct Stream {
    IAudioClient* ac = nullptr;
    IAudioRenderClient* rc = nullptr;
    HANDLE ev = nullptr;
    UINT32 frames = 0;
    ~Stream() {
      if (ac) ac->Stop();
      safe_release(rc); safe_release(ac);
      if (ev) CloseHandle(ev);
    }
  };


  // ---- Windows spatial audio: static bed objects (Windows Sonic, Dolby Atmos for Headphones, DTS) ---------------------
  struct Spatial {
    ISpatialAudioClient* sac = nullptr;
    ISpatialAudioObjectRenderStream* st = nullptr;
    ISpatialAudioObject* obj[6] = {};
    HANDLE ev = nullptr;
    bool started = false;
    ~Spatial() {
      if (st && started) st->Stop();
      for (auto& o : obj) safe_release(o);
      safe_release(st); safe_release(sac);
      if (ev) CloseHandle(ev);
    }
  };

  static AudioObjectType bed_type(mix::BedObject b) {
    switch (b) {
      case mix::BedObject::FrontLeft: return AudioObjectType_FrontLeft;
      case mix::BedObject::FrontRight: return AudioObjectType_FrontRight;
      case mix::BedObject::FrontCenter: return AudioObjectType_FrontCenter;
      case mix::BedObject::LowFrequency: return AudioObjectType_LowFrequency;
      case mix::BedObject::SideLeft: return AudioObjectType_SideLeft;
      default: return AudioObjectType_SideRight;
    }
  }

  static void spatial_format(WAVEFORMATEX& f, uint32_t rate) {
    ZeroMemory(&f, sizeof(f));
    f.wFormatTag = WAVE_FORMAT_IEEE_FLOAT; f.nChannels = 1; f.nSamplesPerSec = rate; f.wBitsPerSample = 32;
    f.nBlockAlign = 4; f.nAvgBytesPerSec = rate * 4; f.cbSize = 0;
  }

  static AudioObjectType bed_mask() {
    unsigned m = 0;
    for (auto b : mix::kBed51) m |= (unsigned)bed_type(b);
    return (AudioObjectType)m;
  }

  // Probe: activate the client and ask whether the 6 bed objects are available. Nothing is started.
  static bool probe_spatial(IMMDevice* dev, uint32_t rate, ISpatialAudioClient** out) {
    ISpatialAudioClient* sac = nullptr;
    if (FAILED(dev->Activate(__uuidof(ISpatialAudioClient), CLSCTX_INPROC_SERVER, nullptr, (void**)&sac)) || !sac) return false;
    WAVEFORMATEX f; spatial_format(f, rate);
    bool ok = SUCCEEDED(sac->IsAudioObjectFormatSupported(&f));
    AudioObjectType native = AudioObjectType_None;
    if (ok) ok = SUCCEEDED(sac->GetNativeStaticObjectTypeMask(&native));
    if (ok) ok = (native & bed_mask()) == bed_mask();
    if (ok && out) { *out = sac; return true; }
    sac->Release();
    return ok;
  }

  bool open_spatial(IMMDeviceEnumerator* en, Spatial& sp) {
    IMMDevice* dev = nullptr;
    if (FAILED(en->GetDefaultAudioEndpoint(eRender, eConsole, &dev))) return false;
    bool ok = probe_spatial(dev, fmt_.rate, &sp.sac);
    safe_release(dev);
    if (!ok) return false;
    WAVEFORMATEX f; spatial_format(f, fmt_.rate);
    sp.ev = CreateEventW(nullptr, FALSE, FALSE, nullptr);
    SpatialAudioObjectRenderStreamActivationParams ap = {};
    ap.ObjectFormat = &f;
    ap.StaticObjectTypeMask = bed_mask();
    ap.MinDynamicObjectCount = 0;
    ap.MaxDynamicObjectCount = 0;
    ap.Category = AudioCategory_GameMedia;
    ap.EventHandle = sp.ev;
    ap.NotifyObject = nullptr;
    PROPVARIANT pv; PropVariantInit(&pv);
    pv.vt = VT_BLOB; pv.blob.cbSize = sizeof(ap); pv.blob.pBlobData = (BYTE*)&ap;
    HRESULT hr = sp.sac->ActivateSpatialAudioStream(&pv, IID_PPV_ARGS(&sp.st));
    if (FAILED(hr) || !sp.st) { std::fprintf(stderr, "[audio] spatial stream activation failed 0x%08lx\n", (unsigned long)hr); return false; }
    for (int i = 0; i < 6; ++i)
      if (FAILED(sp.st->ActivateSpatialAudioObject(bed_type(mix::kBed51[i]), &sp.obj[i]))) return false;
    if (FAILED(sp.st->Start())) return false;
    sp.started = true;
    return true;
  }

  // Returns false if the stream broke (rebuild), true if stopped.
  bool run_spatial(Spatial& sp, HANDLE changeEv) {
    HANDLE h[3] = {sp.ev, changeEv, stopEv_};
    std::vector<float> mixbuf;
    bool first = true;
    while (run_.load()) {
      DWORD w = WaitForMultipleObjects(3, h, FALSE, 250);
      if (w == WAIT_OBJECT_0 + 2) return true;
      if (w == WAIT_OBJECT_0 + 1) return false;
      if (w == WAIT_TIMEOUT) continue;
      UINT32 dyn = 0, frames = 0;
      HRESULT hr = sp.st->BeginUpdatingAudioObjects(&dyn, &frames);
      if (FAILED(hr)) return false;
      mixbuf.resize((size_t)frames * 6);
      core_mix(mixbuf.data(), frames);
      for (int c = 0; c < 6; ++c) {
        BYTE* buf = nullptr; UINT32 bytes = 0;
        if (SUCCEEDED(sp.obj[c]->GetBuffer(&buf, &bytes)) && buf) {
          float* o = reinterpret_cast<float*>(buf);
          const UINT32 n = std::min<UINT32>(frames, bytes / 4);
          for (UINT32 i = 0; i < n; ++i) o[i] = mixbuf[(size_t)i * 6 + c];
        }
      }
      hr = sp.st->EndUpdatingAudioObjects();
      if (FAILED(hr)) return false;
      if (first) { first = false; core_set_device_info(true, frames, 1000.0 * frames / fmt_.rate * 2.0, 6, fmt_.rate, SNAP_AUDIO_OUT_SPATIAL); }
    }
    return true;
  }

  bool open_stream(IMMDeviceEnumerator* en, Stream& s, uint32_t ch) {
    IMMDevice* dev = nullptr;
    if (FAILED(en->GetDefaultAudioEndpoint(eRender, eConsole, &dev))) return false;
    HRESULT hr = dev->Activate(__uuidof(IAudioClient), CLSCTX_ALL, nullptr, (void**)&s.ac);
    safe_release(dev);
    if (FAILED(hr)) return false;
    WAVEFORMATEXTENSIBLE wf;
    make_format(wf, fmt_.rate, ch);
    s.ev = CreateEventW(nullptr, FALSE, FALSE, nullptr);
    const DWORD flags = AUDCLNT_STREAMFLAGS_EVENTCALLBACK | AUDCLNT_STREAMFLAGS_AUTOCONVERTPCM | AUDCLNT_STREAMFLAGS_SRC_DEFAULT_QUALITY;
    bool done = false, triedLowLat = false;
    lowLat_ = false;
    if (!std::getenv("SNAP_AUDIO_NO_LOWLAT") && fmt_.bufferMs == 0) {
      IAudioClient3* a3 = nullptr;
      if (SUCCEEDED(s.ac->QueryInterface(IID_PPV_ARGS(&a3)))) {
        triedLowLat = true;
        UINT32 defP = 0, fund = 0, minP = 0, maxP = 0;
        if (SUCCEEDED(a3->GetSharedModeEnginePeriod(&wf.Format, &defP, &fund, &minP, &maxP)) &&
            SUCCEEDED(a3->InitializeSharedAudioStream(flags, minP, &wf.Format, nullptr))) {
          done = true; lowLat_ = true;
        }
        a3->Release();
      }
    }
    if (!done) {
      if (triedLowLat) {   // a client whose InitializeSharedAudioStream failed cannot be initialized again: take a fresh one
        safe_release(s.ac);
        IMMDevice* d2 = nullptr;
        if (FAILED(en->GetDefaultAudioEndpoint(eRender, eConsole, &d2))) return false;
        hr = d2->Activate(__uuidof(IAudioClient), CLSCTX_ALL, nullptr, (void**)&s.ac);
        safe_release(d2);
        if (FAILED(hr)) return false;
      }
      const REFERENCE_TIME dur = fmt_.bufferMs ? (REFERENCE_TIME)fmt_.bufferMs * 10000 : 0;
      hr = s.ac->Initialize(AUDCLNT_SHAREMODE_SHARED, flags, dur, 0, &wf.Format, nullptr);
      if (FAILED(hr)) {
        std::fprintf(stderr, "[audio] WASAPI Initialize failed 0x%08lx\n", (unsigned long)hr);
        return false;
      }
    }
    if (FAILED(s.ac->SetEventHandle(s.ev)) || FAILED(s.ac->GetBufferSize(&s.frames)) ||
        FAILED(s.ac->GetService(IID_PPV_ARGS(&s.rc))))
      return false;
    // prefill with silence, then start
    BYTE* p = nullptr;
    if (SUCCEEDED(s.rc->GetBuffer(s.frames, &p))) s.rc->ReleaseBuffer(s.frames, AUDCLNT_BUFFERFLAGS_SILENT);
    REFERENCE_TIME lat = 0;
    s.ac->GetStreamLatency(&lat);
    const double bufMs = 1000.0 * s.frames / fmt_.rate;
    core_set_device_info(true, s.frames, lat / 10000.0 + bufMs, ch, fmt_.rate, ch == 2 ? SNAP_AUDIO_OUT_STEREO : SNAP_AUDIO_OUT_SPEAKERS);
    return SUCCEEDED(s.ac->Start());
  }

  void timer_wait(std::chrono::milliseconds total) {  // consume at stream rate while there is no device
    using clk = std::chrono::steady_clock;
    const uint32_t block = fmt_.rate / 100;
    std::vector<float> buf((size_t)block * 8);
    const auto period = std::chrono::nanoseconds(1000000000ll * block / fmt_.rate);
    auto next = clk::now() + period;
    const auto end = clk::now() + total;
    while (run_.load() && clk::now() < end) {
      core_mix(buf.data(), block);   // the core's current channel count never exceeds 8
      std::this_thread::sleep_until(next);
      next += period;
    }
  }

  void thread_main() {
    CoInitializeEx(nullptr, COINIT_MULTITHREADED);
    DWORD task = 0;
    HANDLE mm = AvSetMmThreadCharacteristicsW(L"Pro Audio", &task);
    HANDLE changeEv = CreateEventW(nullptr, FALSE, FALSE, nullptr);
    IMMDeviceEnumerator* en = nullptr;
    CoCreateInstance(__uuidof(MMDeviceEnumerator), nullptr, CLSCTX_ALL, IID_PPV_ARGS(&en));
    Notify* nc = new Notify(changeEv);
    if (en) en->RegisterEndpointNotificationCallback(nc);
    bool first = true;
    while (run_.load()) {
      Stream s;
      Spatial sp;
      // Mode ladder: the configured mode first, then speakers 5.1, then stereo. Re-tried from the top on every rebuild.
      int mode = fmt_.mode;
      uint32_t ch = fmt_.channels;
      bool ok = false, spatialOpen = false;
      {  // remember which endpoint this build uses (device-state notifications for other endpoints are ignored)
        IMMDevice* cd = nullptr; LPWSTR cid = nullptr;
        if (en && SUCCEEDED(en->GetDefaultAudioEndpoint(eRender, eConsole, &cd)) && SUCCEEDED(cd->GetId(&cid))) nc->set_current(cid);
        else nc->set_current(nullptr);
        if (cid) CoTaskMemFree(cid);
        safe_release(cd);
      }
      if (en && mode == SNAP_AUDIO_OUT_SPATIAL) {
        if (open_spatial(en, sp)) { ok = true; spatialOpen = true; }
        else {
          std::fprintf(stderr, "[audio] spatial audio unavailable on the default device (enable Windows Sonic or Dolby Atmos for it), falling back to 5.1 speakers\n");
          sp.~Spatial(); new (&sp) Spatial();
          mode = SNAP_AUDIO_OUT_SPEAKERS; ch = 6;
        }
      }
      if (en && !ok && mode == SNAP_AUDIO_OUT_SPEAKERS) {
        if (open_stream(en, s, ch)) ok = true;
        else { std::fprintf(stderr, "[audio] %u-channel stream failed, falling back to stereo\n", ch); s.~Stream(); new (&s) Stream(); mode = SNAP_AUDIO_OUT_STEREO; ch = 2; }
      }
      if (en && !ok) { ok = open_stream(en, s, 2); ch = 2; mode = SNAP_AUDIO_OUT_STEREO; }
      if (!ok) {
        core_set_device_info(false, 0, 0.0, 0, fmt_.rate, mode);
        timer_wait(std::chrono::milliseconds(500));  // no endpoint: keep time, retry
        continue;
      }
      if (!first) core_notify_device_change();
      first = false;
      if (spatialOpen) {
        std::fprintf(stderr, "[audio] spatial audio stream: 6 static bed objects (FL FR FC LFE SL SR)\n");
        core_set_device_info(true, 480, 20.0, 6, fmt_.rate, SNAP_AUDIO_OUT_SPATIAL);
        if (!run_spatial(sp, changeEv)) core_set_device_info(false, 0, 0.0, 0, fmt_.rate, SNAP_AUDIO_OUT_SPATIAL);
        continue;
      }
      std::fprintf(stderr, "[audio] WASAPI stream: %u ch, %u frames (%.1f ms)%s\n", ch, s.frames, 1000.0 * s.frames / fmt_.rate,
                   lowLat_ ? " low-latency" : "");
      HANDLE h[3] = {s.ev, changeEv, stopEv_};
      bool rebuild = false;
      while (run_.load() && !rebuild) {
        DWORD w = WaitForMultipleObjects(3, h, FALSE, 250);
        if (w == WAIT_OBJECT_0 + 2) break;
        if (w == WAIT_OBJECT_0 + 1) { rebuild = true; break; }
        UINT32 pad = 0;
        HRESULT hr = s.ac->GetCurrentPadding(&pad);
        if (FAILED(hr)) { rebuild = true; break; }
        const UINT32 avail = s.frames - pad;
        if (!avail) continue;
        BYTE* p = nullptr;
        hr = s.rc->GetBuffer(avail, &p);
        if (FAILED(hr)) { rebuild = true; break; }  // AUDCLNT_E_DEVICE_INVALIDATED etc.
        core_mix(reinterpret_cast<float*>(p), avail);
        s.rc->ReleaseBuffer(avail, 0);
      }
      if (rebuild) core_set_device_info(false, 0, 0.0, 0, fmt_.rate, mode);
    }
    if (en) { en->UnregisterEndpointNotificationCallback(nc); en->Release(); }
    nc->Release();
    CloseHandle(changeEv);
    if (mm) AvRevertMmThreadCharacteristics(mm);
    CoUninitialize();
  }

  DeviceFormat fmt_{};
  bool lowLat_ = false;
  std::atomic<bool> run_{false};
  HANDLE stopEv_ = nullptr;
  std::thread th_;
};

}  // namespace

Backend* make_wasapi_backend() { return new WasapiBackend(); }

}  // namespace snap_audio
#endif

```

`runtime/audio/spsc_ring.h`:

```h
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Lock-free single-producer single-consumer rings (power-of-two capacity). Wait-free on both sides.
#pragma once
#include <atomic>
#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>

namespace snap_audio {

template <typename T, size_t N>
class SpscRing {
  static_assert((N & (N - 1)) == 0 && N >= 2, "N must be a power of two");
 public:
  // Producer side. Returns false when full.
  bool push(const T& v) {
    const size_t h = head_.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
    if (h - tail_.load(std::memory_order_acquire) == N) return false;
    buf_[h & (N - 1)] = v;
    head_.store(h + 1, std::memory_order_release);
    return true;
  }
  // Consumer side. Returns false when empty.
  bool pop(T& v) {
    const size_t t = tail_.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
    if (t == head_.load(std::memory_order_acquire)) return false;
    v = buf_[t & (N - 1)];
    tail_.store(t + 1, std::memory_order_release);
    return true;
  }
  size_t size() const { return head_.load(std::memory_order_acquire) - tail_.load(std::memory_order_acquire); }
  // Only safe while neither side is running.
  void reset() { head_.store(0); tail_.store(0); }
 private:
  alignas(64) std::atomic<size_t> head_{0};
  alignas(64) std::atomic<size_t> tail_{0};
  T buf_[N];
};

// SPSC ring of float samples with bulk transfer (the capture tap).
template <size_t N>
class SampleRing {
  static_assert((N & (N - 1)) == 0, "N must be a power of two");
 public:
  size_t write(const float* src, size_t n) {  // returns samples written (drops the rest)
    const size_t h = head_.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
    const size_t room = N - (h - tail_.load(std::memory_order_acquire));
    if (n > room) n = room;
    for (size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) buf_[(h + i) & (N - 1)] = src[i];
    head_.store(h + n, std::memory_order_release);
    return n;
  }
  size_t read(float* dst, size_t n) {
    const size_t t = tail_.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
    const size_t avail = head_.load(std::memory_order_acquire) - t;
    if (n > avail) n = avail;
    for (size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) dst[i] = buf_[(t + i) & (N - 1)];
    tail_.store(t + n, std::memory_order_release);
    return n;
  }
  void reset() { head_.store(0); tail_.store(0); }
 private:
  alignas(64) std::atomic<size_t> head_{0};
  alignas(64) std::atomic<size_t> tail_{0};
  float buf_[N];
};

}  // namespace snap_audio

// Via TotK Recomp @ 7a37fc3 (MIT, Copyright (c) 2026 Valiantsin Dzerakh); modified for the Snap prototype where noted.
// Adapted from LAS Recomp runtime/cpu.h @ da35b83 (MIT, Copyright (c) 2026 Peiikai).
// Guest CPU state and helpers used by recompiled code.
#pragma once
#include <stddef.h>
#include <stdint.h>
#include <string.h>

typedef struct __attribute__((aligned(16))) Cpu {
    uint64_t x[32];          // x0-x30 (x[31] unused; sp is separate)
    uint64_t sp;             // 256
    uint64_t pc;             // 264: target for indirect dispatch
    uint64_t nzcv;           // 272: flags in bits 31..28
    uint64_t tpidr;          // 280
    uint64_t tpidrro;        // 288
    uint64_t excl_addr;      // 296
    uint64_t excl_val;       // 304
    void *thread;            // 312: runtime thread object
    uint64_t fpcr;           // 320: guest FPCR/FPSR (portable FP/SIMD lowering only; the asm path uses the host's)
    uint64_t fpsr;           // 328
    uint64_t excl_val_hi;    // 336: upper half of a 128-bit exclusive pair (LDXP/LDAXP of two X registers)
    uint64_t resuming;       // 344: exception / longjmp in flight (docs/runtime-boundary.md section 2); c->pc and c->sp name the
                             //      frame to resume. Lifted call sites test it after every call.
    uint8_t _pad[512 - 352];
    __uint128_t v[32];       // 512
} Cpu;

_Static_assert(offsetof(Cpu, sp) == 256, "sp");
_Static_assert(offsetof(Cpu, pc) == 264, "pc");
_Static_assert(offsetof(Cpu, nzcv) == 272, "nzcv");
_Static_assert(offsetof(Cpu, fpcr) == 320, "fpcr");
_Static_assert(offsetof(Cpu, fpsr) == 328, "fpsr");
_Static_assert(offsetof(Cpu, resuming) == 344, "resuming");
_Static_assert(offsetof(Cpu, v) == 512, "v");

// Test after every lifted call (generated code, recomp/gen.py). Off by one load, test and not-taken branch per call site.
#define RESUMING(c) __builtin_expect((c)->resuming != 0, 0)

typedef void (*GuestFn)(Cpu *);

// ---- runtime services (runtime/*.c)
void rt_dispatch(Cpu *c);                 // call function at c->pc
void rt_unresolved(Cpu *c, uint64_t addr, const char *what);   // log and abort (host)
void rt_import_call(Cpu *c, uint32_t idx);  // main's PLT stub #idx: call the loader-resolved target (host)
void rt_spin_gate(Cpu *c, uint64_t head);  // a pass of a spin wait loop (kernel.c, recomp/patches.py `spin`)

void rt_brk(Cpu *c, uint32_t imm, uint64_t pc) __attribute__((noreturn));
void rt_udf(Cpu *c, uint64_t pc) __attribute__((noreturn));
uint64_t rt_ticks(void);

#if defined(__aarch64__)
static inline uint64_t rt_get_fpcr(void) { uint64_t v; __asm__ volatile("mrs %0, fpcr" : "=r"(v)); return v; }
static inline uint64_t rt_get_fpsr(void) { uint64_t v; __asm__ volatile("mrs %0, fpsr" : "=r"(v)); return v; }
static inline void rt_set_fpcr(uint64_t v) { __asm__ volatile("msr fpcr, %0" :: "r"(v)); }
static inline void rt_set_fpsr(uint64_t v) { __asm__ volatile("msr fpsr, %0" :: "r"(v)); }
static inline void rt_fpcr_sync(const Cpu *c) { (void)c; }
#else
// Host FP state is not the guest's here: code lifted with --simd=c keeps FPCR/FPSR in Cpu (c->fpcr, zeroed
// with the Cpu), so the host-side reset in thread start-up has nothing to do.
static inline uint64_t rt_get_fpcr(void) { return 0; }
static inline uint64_t rt_get_fpsr(void) { return 0; }
static inline void rt_set_fpcr(uint64_t v) { (void)v; }
static inline void rt_set_fpsr(uint64_t v) { (void)v; }
// The MXCSR of a host thread running guest code mirrors c->fpcr: FTZ|DAZ = FPCR.FZ, RC = nearest (FPCR.RMode takes
// the slow paths of runtime/simd.h, which switch RC around one operation). The FP helpers rely on it without checking,
// so it is set wherever FPCR or the host FP context changes: MSR FPCR (recomp/lifter.py), rt_call (thread and fiber
// entry, host code calling guest code), fiber resume (runtime/kernel.c fiber_resumed; fibers keep their own MXCSR).
static inline void rt_fpcr_sync(const Cpu *c) {
    unsigned cur = __builtin_ia32_stmxcsr();
    unsigned want = (cur & ~0xE040u) | (c->fpcr & (1u << 24) ? 0x8040u : 0);   // FTZ 0x8000, DAZ 0x40, RC 0x6000
    if (cur != want) __builtin_ia32_ldmxcsr(want);
}
#endif

// ---- memory: guest addresses are host addresses
typedef uint16_t __attribute__((aligned(1), may_alias)) u16u;
typedef uint32_t __attribute__((aligned(1), may_alias)) u32u;
typedef uint64_t __attribute__((aligned(1), may_alias)) u64u;
typedef uint8_t __attribute__((may_alias)) u8a;

// Function-entry profiler (runtime/fnprof.c, LARECOMP_FNPROF): one predictable branch per call when off.
extern volatile int g_fnprof;
void fnprof_hit(uint64_t addr, uint64_t lr, uint64_t x0);
#define FN_ENTER(a) do { if (__builtin_expect(g_fnprof, 0)) fnprof_hit(a, c->x[30], c->x[0]); } while (0)

#define LD8(a)  (*(const u8a *)(uintptr_t)(a))
#define LD16(a) (*(const u16u *)(uintptr_t)(a))
#define LD32(a) (*(const u32u *)(uintptr_t)(a))
#define LD64(a) (*(const u64u *)(uintptr_t)(a))
#define ST8(a, v)  (*(u8a *)(uintptr_t)(a) = (uint8_t)(v))

#define ST32(a, v) (*(u32u *)(uintptr_t)(a) = (uint32_t)(v))
#define ST64(a, v) (*(u64u *)(uintptr_t)(a) = (uint64_t)(v))

// ---- exclusive monitor (emulated with compare-and-swap)
#define EXCL(N, T)                                                                         \
    static inline uint64_t ldx##N(Cpu *c, uint64_t a) {                                    \
        T v = __atomic_load_n((T *)(uintptr_t)a, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE);                        \
        c->excl_addr = a;                                                                  \
        c->excl_val = v;                                                                   \
        return v;                                                                          \
    }                                                                                      \
    static inline uint32_t stx##N(Cpu *c, uint64_t a, uint64_t v) {                        \
        if (c->excl_addr != a) return 1;                                                   \
        c->excl_addr = ~0ull;                                                              \
        T expected = (T)c->excl_val;                                                       \
        return !__atomic_compare_exchange_n((T *)(uintptr_t)a, &expected, (T)v, 0,         \
                                            __ATOMIC_SEQ_CST, __ATOMIC_SEQ_CST);           \
    }                                                                                      \
    static inline uint64_t lda##N(uint64_t a) {                                            \
        return __atomic_load_n((T *)(uintptr_t)a, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE);                       \
    }                                                                                      \
    static inline void stl##N(uint64_t a, uint64_t v) {                                    \
        __atomic_store_n((T *)(uintptr_t)a, (T)v, __ATOMIC_RELEASE);                       \
    }
EXCL(8, uint8_t)
EXCL(16, uint16_t)
EXCL(32, uint32_t)
EXCL(64, uint64_t)

// Exclusive pair of two X registers: one 16-byte-aligned 128-bit access (cmpxchg16b; x86-64-v2 has CX16).
// A pair of two W registers is a 64-bit exclusive and uses ldx64/stx64.
static inline __uint128_t ldxp128(Cpu *c, uint64_t a) {
    __uint128_t v = __atomic_load_n((__uint128_t *)(uintptr_t)a, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE);
    c->excl_addr = a;
    c->excl_val = (uint64_t)v;
    c->excl_val_hi = (uint64_t)(v >> 64);
    return v;
}
static inline uint32_t stxp128(Cpu *c, uint64_t a, uint64_t lo, uint64_t hi) {
    if (c->excl_addr != a) return 1;
    c->excl_addr = ~0ull;
    __uint128_t expected = ((__uint128_t)c->excl_val_hi << 64) | c->excl_val;
    __uint128_t v = ((__uint128_t)hi << 64) | lo;
    return !__atomic_compare_exchange_n((__uint128_t *)(uintptr_t)a, &expected, v, 0, __ATOMIC_SEQ_CST,
                                        __ATOMIC_SEQ_CST);
}

// ---- LSE atomics (ARMv8.1; the A57 lacks them, the SDK carries them behind a CPU feature check).
// Add, clear, xor, set and swap map to __atomic builtins in the lifter; min/max need a CAS loop. Return the old value.
#define ATOMIC_MINMAX(N, T, S)                                                             \
    static inline T atomic_smax##N(uint64_t a, T v) {                                      \
        T o = __atomic_load_n((T *)(uintptr_t)a, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);                        \
        while (!__atomic_compare_exchange_n((T *)(uintptr_t)a, &o, (S)o > (S)v ? o : v, 1, \
                                            __ATOMIC_SEQ_CST, __ATOMIC_RELAXED)) {}        \
        return o;                                                                          \
    }                                                                                      \
    static inline T atomic_smin##N(uint64_t a, T v) {                                      \
        T o = __atomic_load_n((T *)(uintptr_t)a, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);                        \
        while (!__atomic_compare_exchange_n((T *)(uintptr_t)a, &o, (S)o < (S)v ? o : v, 1, \
                                            __ATOMIC_SEQ_CST, __ATOMIC_RELAXED)) {}        \
        return o;                                                                          \
    }                                                                                      \
    static inline T atomic_umax##N(uint64_t a, T v) {                                      \
        T o = __atomic_load_n((T *)(uintptr_t)a, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);                        \
        while (!__atomic_compare_exchange_n((T *)(uintptr_t)a, &o, o > v ? o : v, 1,       \
                                            __ATOMIC_SEQ_CST, __ATOMIC_RELAXED)) {}        \
        return o;                                                                          \
    }                                                                                      \
    static inline T atomic_umin##N(uint64_t a, T v) {                                      \
        T o = __atomic_load_n((T *)(uintptr_t)a, __ATOMIC_RELAXED);                        \
        while (!__atomic_compare_exchange_n((T *)(uintptr_t)a, &o, o < v ? o : v, 1,       \
                                            __ATOMIC_SEQ_CST, __ATOMIC_RELAXED)) {}        \
        return o;                                                                          \
    }
ATOMIC_MINMAX(8, uint8_t, int8_t)
ATOMIC_MINMAX(16, uint16_t, int16_t)
ATOMIC_MINMAX(32, uint32_t, int32_t)

// ---- flags (packed NZCV in bits 31..28)
#define FLAG_N(c) (((c)->nzcv >> 31) & 1)
#define FLAG_Z(c) (((c)->nzcv >> 30) & 1)
#define FLAG_C(c) (((c)->nzcv >> 29) & 1)
#define FLAG_V(c) (((c)->nzcv >> 28) & 1)
#define COND_EQ(c) (FLAG_Z(c))
#define COND_NE(c) (!FLAG_Z(c))
#define COND_CS(c) (FLAG_C(c))
#define COND_CC(c) (!FLAG_C(c))
#define COND_MI(c) (FLAG_N(c))
#define COND_PL(c) (!FLAG_N(c))
#define COND_VS(c) (FLAG_V(c))
#define COND_VC(c) (!FLAG_V(c))
#define COND_HI(c) (FLAG_C(c) && !FLAG_Z(c))
#define COND_LS(c) (!(FLAG_C(c) && !FLAG_Z(c)))
#define COND_GE(c) (FLAG_N(c) == FLAG_V(c))
#define COND_LT(c) (FLAG_N(c) != FLAG_V(c))
#define COND_GT(c) (!FLAG_Z(c) && FLAG_N(c) == FLAG_V(c))
#define COND_LE(c) (!(!FLAG_Z(c) && FLAG_N(c) == FLAG_V(c)))

#define MKFLAGS(n, z, cy, v) \
    (((uint64_t)(n) << 31) | ((uint64_t)(z) << 30) | ((uint64_t)(cy) << 29) | ((uint64_t)(v) << 28))

static inline uint64_t adds64(Cpu *c, uint64_t a, uint64_t b) {
    uint64_t r = a + b;
    c->nzcv = MKFLAGS(r >> 63, r == 0, r < a, ((a ^ r) & (b ^ r)) >> 63);
    return r;
}
static inline uint64_t subs64(Cpu *c, uint64_t a, uint64_t b) {
    uint64_t r = a - b;
    c->nzcv = MKFLAGS(r >> 63, r == 0, a >= b, ((a ^ b) & (a ^ r)) >> 63);
    return r;
}
static inline uint32_t adds32(Cpu *c, uint32_t a, uint32_t b) {
    uint32_t r = a + b;
    c->nzcv = MKFLAGS(r >> 31, r == 0, r < a, ((a ^ r) & (b ^ r)) >> 31);
    return r;
}
static inline uint32_t subs32(Cpu *c, uint32_t a, uint32_t b) {
    uint32_t r = a - b;
    c->nzcv = MKFLAGS(r >> 31, r == 0, a >= b, ((a ^ b) & (a ^ r)) >> 31);
    return r;
}
static inline uint64_t logic64(Cpu *c, uint64_t r) { c->nzcv = MKFLAGS(r >> 63, r == 0, 0, 0); return r; }
static inline uint32_t logic32(Cpu *c, uint32_t r) { c->nzcv = MKFLAGS(r >> 31, r == 0, 0, 0); return r; }

#define ADC_IMPL(N, S)                                                                     \
    static inline uint##N##_t adc##N(Cpu *c, uint##N##_t a, uint##N##_t b) {               \
        return a + b + (uint##N##_t)FLAG_C(c);                                             \
    }                                                                                      \
    static inline uint##N##_t sbc##N(Cpu *c, uint##N##_t a, uint##N##_t b) {               \
        return a - b - 1 + (uint##N##_t)FLAG_C(c);                                         \
    }                                                                                      \
    static inline uint##N##_t adcs##N(Cpu *c, uint##N##_t a, uint##N##_t b) {              \
        uint##N##_t cin = FLAG_C(c), r = a + b + cin;                                      \
        int carry = cin ? r <= a : r < a;                                                  \
        c->nzcv = MKFLAGS(r >> (N - 1), r == 0, carry, ((a ^ r) & (b ^ r)) >> (N - 1));    \
        return r;                                                                          \
    }                                                                                      \
    static inline uint##N##_t sbcs##N(Cpu *c, uint##N##_t a, uint##N##_t b) {              \
        return adcs##N(c, a, (uint##N##_t)~b);                                             \
    }
ADC_IMPL(64, )
ADC_IMPL(32, )

// ---- function-local flags (recomp/flags.py)
// Generated functions keep NZCV in a local Flags F, never in c->nzcv. A definition of a known kind stores its
// operands (a - b, a + b, or a logic result in a); fc_<kind>(&F, CC_xx) computes a condition from them, so a compare
// and its branch become one host compare. F.nz holds the packed form for definitions only known packed (CCMP, FCMP,
// MSR, ADCS) and for readers that several kinds of definition reach. Every helper is always inlined with a constant
// condition, so F stays in registers and only the condition's own arithmetic remains.
typedef struct { uint64_t a, b, nz; } Flags;
enum { CC_EQ, CC_NE, CC_CS, CC_CC, CC_MI, CC_PL, CC_VS, CC_VC, CC_HI, CC_LS, CC_GE, CC_LT, CC_GT, CC_LE };
#define CPU_FL static inline __attribute__((always_inline))

CPU_FL int fl_cond(int cc, int n, int z, int cy, int v) {
    switch (cc) {
    case CC_EQ: return z;
    case CC_NE: return !z;
    case CC_CS: return cy;
    case CC_CC: return !cy;
    case CC_MI: return n;
    case CC_PL: return !n;
    case CC_VS: return v;
    case CC_VC: return !v;
    case CC_HI: return cy && !z;
    case CC_LS: return !cy || z;
    case CC_GE: return n == v;
    case CC_LT: return n != v;
    case CC_GT: return !z && n == v;
    default: return z || n != v;
    }
}

// Subtract (SUBS, CMP): conditions as host compares of the operands.
#define FL_SUB(N, U, S)                                                                    \
    CPU_FL U fsub##N(Flags *f, U a, U b) { f->a = a; f->b = b; return (U)(a - b); }            \
    CPU_FL int fc_sub##N(const Flags *f, int cc) {                                             \
        U a = (U)f->a, b = (U)f->b, r = (U)(a - b);                                        \
        switch (cc) {                                                                      \
        case CC_EQ: return a == b;                                                         \
        case CC_NE: return a != b;                                                         \
        case CC_CS: return a >= b;                                                         \
        case CC_CC: return a < b;                                                          \
        case CC_MI: return (S)r < 0;                                                       \
        case CC_PL: return (S)r >= 0;                                                      \
        case CC_VS: return (S)((a ^ b) & (a ^ r)) < 0;                                     \
        case CC_VC: return (S)((a ^ b) & (a ^ r)) >= 0;                                    \
        case CC_HI: return a > b;                                                          \
        case CC_LS: return a <= b;                                                         \
        case CC_GE: return (S)a >= (S)b;                                                   \
        case CC_LT: return (S)a < (S)b;                                                    \
        case CC_GT: return (S)a > (S)b;                                                    \
        default: return (S)a <= (S)b;                                                      \
        }                                                                                  \
    }                                                                                      \
    CPU_FL uint64_t nz_sub##N(U a, U b) {                                                      \
        U r = (U)(a - b);                                                                  \
        return MKFLAGS((S)r < 0, r == 0, a >= b, (S)((a ^ b) & (a ^ r)) < 0);              \
    }                                                                                      \
    CPU_FL uint64_t fnz_sub##N(const Flags *f) { return nz_sub##N((U)f->a, (U)f->b); }
FL_SUB(64, uint64_t, int64_t)
FL_SUB(32, uint32_t, int32_t)

// Add (ADDS, CMN) and logic results (ANDS, TST, BICS): conditions from N, Z, C, V.
#define FL_ADD(N, U, S)                                                                    \
    CPU_FL U fadd##N(Flags *f, U a, U b) { f->a = a; f->b = b; return (U)(a + b); }            \
    CPU_FL uint64_t nz_add##N(U a, U b) {                                                      \
        U r = (U)(a + b);                                                                  \
        return MKFLAGS((S)r < 0, r == 0, r < a, (S)((a ^ r) & (b ^ r)) < 0);               \
    }                                                                                      \
    CPU_FL int fc_add##N(const Flags *f, int cc) {                                             \
        U a = (U)f->a, b = (U)f->b, r = (U)(a + b);                                        \
        return fl_cond(cc, (S)r < 0, r == 0, r < a, (S)((a ^ r) & (b ^ r)) < 0);           \
    }                                                                                      \
    CPU_FL uint64_t fnz_add##N(const Flags *f) { return nz_add##N((U)f->a, (U)f->b); }         \
    CPU_FL U flogic##N(Flags *f, U r) { f->a = r; return r; }                                  \
    CPU_FL int fc_logic##N(const Flags *f, int cc) {                                           \
        U r = (U)f->a;                                                                     \
        return fl_cond(cc, (S)r < 0, r == 0, 0, 0);                                        \
    }                                                                                      \
    CPU_FL uint64_t fnz_logic##N(const Flags *f) { return MKFLAGS((S)f->a < 0, (U)f->a == 0, 0, 0); }
FL_ADD(64, uint64_t, int64_t)
FL_ADD(32, uint32_t, int32_t)

// Packed flags.
CPU_FL int fc_nz(const Flags *f, int cc) {
    return fl_cond(cc, f->nz >> 31 & 1, f->nz >> 30 & 1, f->nz >> 29 & 1, f->nz >> 28 & 1);
}
CPU_FL uint64_t fnz_nz(const Flags *f) { return f->nz; }

// ADC, SBC, ADCS, SBCS with the carry in from F.
#define FL_ADC(N, U)                                                                       \
    CPU_FL U adc##N##f(int cin, U a, U b) { return (U)(a + b + (U)cin); }                      \
    CPU_FL U sbc##N##f(int cin, U a, U b) { return (U)(a - b - 1 + (U)cin); }                  \
    CPU_FL U adcs##N##f(Flags *f, int cin, U a, U b) {                                         \
        U r = (U)(a + b + (U)cin);                                                         \
        int carry = cin ? r <= a : r < a;                                                  \
        f->nz = MKFLAGS(r >> (N - 1), r == 0, carry, ((a ^ r) & (b ^ r)) >> (N - 1));      \
        return r;                                                                          \
    }                                                                                      \
    CPU_FL U sbcs##N##f(Flags *f, int cin, U a, U b) { return adcs##N##f(f, cin, a, (U)~b); }
FL_ADC(64, uint64_t)
FL_ADC(32, uint32_t)
#undef CPU_FL

// ---- bit ops
#define ROR64(v, r) ((uint64_t)(v) >> ((r) & 63) | (uint64_t)(v) << ((64 - ((r) & 63)) & 63))
#define ROR32(v, r) ((uint32_t)(v) >> ((r) & 31) | (uint32_t)(v) << ((32 - ((r) & 31)) & 31))
static inline uint64_t clz64(uint64_t v) { return v ? __builtin_clzll(v) : 64; }
static inline uint32_t clz32(uint32_t v) { return v ? __builtin_clz(v) : 32; }
static inline uint64_t cls64(uint64_t v) { return clz64(v ^ (uint64_t)((int64_t)v >> 1)) - 1; }
static inline uint32_t cls32(uint32_t v) { return clz32(v ^ (uint32_t)((int32_t)v >> 1)) - 1; }
static inline uint64_t rbit64(uint64_t v) { return __builtin_bitreverse64(v); }
static inline uint32_t rbit32(uint32_t v) { return __builtin_bitreverse32(v); }
static inline uint32_t rev16_32(uint32_t v) { return ((v & 0x00ff00ffu) << 8) | ((v >> 8) & 0x00ff00ffu); }
static inline uint64_t rev16_64(uint64_t v) {
    return ((v & 0x00ff00ff00ff00ffull) << 8) | ((v >> 8) & 0x00ff00ff00ff00ffull);
}
static inline uint64_t rev32_64(uint64_t v) {
    return ((uint64_t)__builtin_bswap32((uint32_t)v)) | ((uint64_t)__builtin_bswap32((uint32_t)(v >> 32)) << 32);
}
static inline uint64_t udiv64(uint64_t a, uint64_t b) { return b ? a / b : 0; }
static inline uint32_t udiv32(uint32_t a, uint32_t b) { return b ? a / b : 0; }
static inline uint64_t sdiv64(uint64_t a, uint64_t b) {
    if (!b) return 0;
    if ((int64_t)a == INT64_MIN && (int64_t)b == -1) return a;
    return (uint64_t)((int64_t)a / (int64_t)b);
}
static inline uint32_t sdiv32(uint32_t a, uint32_t b) {
    if (!b) return 0;
    if ((int32_t)a == INT32_MIN && (int32_t)b == -1) return a;
    return (uint32_t)((int32_t)a / (int32_t)b);
}

// Portable FP/SIMD helpers for code lifted with --simd=c (default off AArch64; gen.py includes simd.h itself
// in that mode, so AArch64 hosts can build it too).
#if !defined(__cplusplus) && !defined(__aarch64__)
#include "simd.h"
#endif

```

`runtime/fma.c`:

```c
// Via TotK Recomp @ 7a37fc3 (MIT, Copyright (c) 2026 Valiantsin Dzerakh).
// Correctly rounded fma/fmaf for x86-64 builds without FMA3: the -march=x86-64-v2 build (docs/building.md).
//
// runtime/simd.h lowers AArch64 FMADD/FMSUB and the RECPS/RSQRTS helpers to __builtin_elementwise_fma, which clang
// turns into a call to fma/fmaf when the target has no FMA instruction. The C runtime is not a substitute: on CPUs
// without FMA3 the UCRT's software fallback is documented as rounding incorrectly by up to half an ulp, while the FP
// lowering needs the single rounding the ARM instruction gives. This file supplies it.
//
// Adapted from musl src/math/fma.c and src/math/fmaf.c (MIT, Copyright (c) 2005-2020 Rich Felker and contributors).
// The result is rounded in the MXCSR rounding mode the caller set (simd.h simd_rm_enter), and MXCSR FTZ and DAZ are
// honoured as the hardware FMA would, so runtime/simd.h's fast paths keep their assumptions: denormal inputs read as
// zero and denormal results as zero under FPCR.FZ, without a trip through the slow path.
//
// The definitions exist only where the compiler would emit the calls. A -march=x86-64-v3 build defines __FMA__ and
// emits vfmadd instead, so this file contributes nothing there.
#include <stdint.h>

#if defined(__x86_64__) && !defined(__FMA__)

#include <float.h>
#include <immintrin.h>

#define MXCSR_DAZ 0x0040u
#define MXCSR_FTZ 0x8000u

static double fma_flush_d(double x) {
    union { double f; uint64_t i; } u = {x};
    if (!(u.i & 0x7ff0000000000000ull) && (u.i & 0x000fffffffffffffull)) u.i &= 0x8000000000000000ull;
    return u.f;
}

static float fma_flush_f(float x) {
    union { float f; uint32_t i; } u = {x};
    if (!(u.i & 0x7f800000u) && (u.i & 0x007fffffu)) u.i &= 0x80000000u;
    return u.f;
}

// ---- float: the exact product fits in a double, so one extra term and a round-to-odd step decide the float
// rounding. Halfway and tiny results are the only ones where rounding the double first can change the float result.
float fmaf(float x, float y, float z) {
    unsigned csr = _mm_getcsr();
    if (csr & MXCSR_DAZ) x = fma_flush_f(x), y = fma_flush_f(y), z = fma_flush_f(z);
    double xy = (double)x * y;   // exact
    union { double r; uint64_t i; } u = {xy + z};
    int e = u.i >> 52 & 0x7ff;
    int halfway = (u.i & 0x1fffffff) == 0x10000000;
    int tiny = e <= 0x3ff - 126 && e >= 0x3ff - 149;
    if (halfway || tiny) {
        if (e != 0x7ff) {
            // r+t is the exact sum in nearest rounding; otherwise t keeps its sign and whether it is zero, which
            // is all the round-to-odd step needs. An odd sticky bit makes the final conversion round once, in
            // whichever mode MXCSR asks for.
            int s = u.i >> 63;
            double t = s == (xy < z) ? xy - u.r + z : z - u.r + xy;
            if (t) {
                u.i -= s ^ (t < 0);
                u.i |= 1;
            }
        }
    }
    float r = (float)u.r;
    if (csr & MXCSR_FTZ) r = fma_flush_f(r);
    return r;
}

// ---- double: the significands are multiplied and aligned as integers, then converted back with one rounding.
#define ASUINT64(x) ((union { double f; uint64_t i; }){x}).i
#define ZEROINFNAN (0x7ff - 0x3ff - 52 - 1)

struct fma_num { uint64_t m; int e; int sign; };

static struct fma_num fma_normalize(double x) {
    uint64_t ix = ASUINT64(x);
    int e = ix >> 52;
    int sign = e & 0x800;
    e &= 0x7ff;
    if (!e) {
        ix = ASUINT64(x * 0x1p63);
        e = ix >> 52 & 0x7ff;
        e = e ? e - 63 : 0x800;
    }
    ix &= (1ull << 52) - 1;
    ix |= 1ull << 52;
    ix <<= 1;
    e -= 0x3ff + 52 + 1;
    return (struct fma_num){ix, e, sign};
}

static void fma_mul(uint64_t *hi, uint64_t *lo, uint64_t x, uint64_t y) {
    uint64_t xlo = (uint32_t)x, xhi = x >> 32;
    uint64_t ylo = (uint32_t)y, yhi = y >> 32;
    uint64_t t1 = xlo * ylo;
    uint64_t t2 = xlo * yhi + xhi * ylo;
    uint64_t t3 = xhi * yhi;
    *lo = t1 + (t2 << 32);
    *hi = t3 + (t2 >> 32) + (t1 > *lo);
}

// scalbn from musl src/math/scalbn.c (MIT): the fma's final scaling, kept here so the result does not depend on the
// C runtime's version. Its multiplications honour MXCSR like any other host FP operation.
static double fma_scalbn(double x, int n) {
    union { double f; uint64_t i; } u;
    double y = x;
    if (n > 1023) {
        y *= 0x1p1023;
        n -= 1023;
        if (n > 1023) {
            y *= 0x1p1023;
            n -= 1023;
            if (n > 1023) n = 1023;
        }
    } else if (n < -1022) {
        // Make sure the final n < -53, so the subnormal range rounds only once.
        y *= 0x1p-1022 * 0x1p53;
        n += 1022 - 53;
        if (n < -1022) {
            y *= 0x1p-1022 * 0x1p53;
            n += 1022 - 53;
            if (n < -1022) n = -1022;
        }
    }
    u.i = (uint64_t)(0x3ff + n) << 52;
    return y * u.f;
}

double fma(double x, double y, double z) {
#pragma STDC FENV_ACCESS ON
    unsigned csr = _mm_getcsr();
    if (csr & MXCSR_DAZ) x = fma_flush_d(x), y = fma_flush_d(y), z = fma_flush_d(z);

    struct fma_num nx = fma_normalize(x), ny = fma_normalize(y), nz = fma_normalize(z);
    if (nx.e >= ZEROINFNAN || ny.e >= ZEROINFNAN) return x * y + z;
    if (nz.e >= ZEROINFNAN) {
        if (nz.e > ZEROINFNAN) return x * y;   // z == 0
        return z;
    }

    uint64_t rhi, rlo, zhi, zlo;
    fma_mul(&rhi, &rlo, nx.m, ny.m);

    // Align the exponents: shift z left by kz and r right by kr with kz + kr == d.
    int e = nx.e + ny.e;
    int d = nz.e - e;
    if (d > 0) {
        if (d < 64) {
            zlo = nz.m << d;
            zhi = nz.m >> (64 - d);
        } else {
            zlo = 0;
            zhi = nz.m;
            e = nz.e - 64;
            d -= 64;
            if (d == 0) {
            } else if (d < 64) {
                rlo = rhi << (64 - d) | rlo >> d | !!(rlo << (64 - d));
                rhi = rhi >> d;
            } else {
                rlo = 1;
                rhi = 0;
            }
        }
    } else {
        zhi = 0;
        d = -d;
        if (d == 0) {
            zlo = nz.m;
        } else if (d < 64) {
            zlo = nz.m >> d | !!(nz.m << (64 - d));
        } else {
            zlo = 1;
        }
    }

    int sign = nx.sign ^ ny.sign;
    int samesign = !(sign ^ nz.sign);
    int nonzero = 1;
    if (samesign) {
        rlo += zlo;
        rhi += zhi + (rlo < zlo);
    } else {
        uint64_t t = rlo;
        rlo -= zlo;
        rhi = rhi - zhi - (t < rlo);
        if (rhi >> 63) {
            rlo = -rlo;
            rhi = -rhi - !!rlo;
            sign = !sign;
        }
        nonzero = !!rhi;
    }

    // Keep the top 63 bits in rhi; the last bit is sticky.
    if (nonzero) {
        e += 64;
        d = __builtin_clzll(rhi) - 1;
        rhi = rhi << d | rlo >> (64 - d) | !!(rlo << d);
    } else if (rlo) {
        d = __builtin_clzll(rlo) - 1;
        if (d < 0)
            rhi = rlo >> 1 | (rlo & 1);
        else
            rhi = rlo << d;
    } else {
        return x * y + z;   // exact +-0
    }
    e -= d;

    int64_t i = rhi;
    if (sign) i = -i;
    double r = i;   // |r| is in [0x1p62, 0x1p63]

    if (e < -1022 - 62) {
        // The result is subnormal before rounding.
        if (e == -1022 - 63) {
            double c = 0x1p63;
            if (sign) c = -c;
            if (r == c) {
                // The smallest normal after rounding: whether it underflows depends on the architecture. A double
                // to float conversion imitates the before-rounding rule the guest has.
                float fltmin = 0x0.ffffff8p-63 * FLT_MIN * r;
                r = DBL_MIN / FLT_MIN * fltmin;
                return (csr & MXCSR_FTZ) ? fma_flush_d(r) : r;
            }
            // One bit is lost when scaled: add another top bit so the conversion rounds only once if inexact.
            if (rhi << 53) {
                i = rhi >> 1 | (rhi & 1) | 1ull << 62;
                if (sign) i = -i;
                r = i;
                r = 2 * r - c;
                // Raise underflow portably, so the compiler cannot optimize the expression away.
                double tiny = DBL_MIN / FLT_MIN * r;
                r += (double)(tiny * tiny) * (r - r);
            }
        } else {
            // Only round once when scaled.
            d = 10;
            i = (rhi >> d | !!(rhi << (64 - d))) << d;
            if (sign) i = -i;
            r = i;
        }
    }
    r = fma_scalbn(r, e);
    if (csr & MXCSR_FTZ) r = fma_flush_d(r);
    return r;
}

#endif

```

`runtime/hle/PROPOSED_SHARED_CHANGES.md`:

```md
# Proposed shared changes (runtime/hle)

`runtime/hle` did not edit any shared header. Each item below is what the HLE layer needs from the loader, `runtime/os`
or `runtime/nvn`, with the smallest change that works.

## 1. Bind the overrides in the loader (needed)

`hle::bind_all(BindFn bind, void* user)` calls `bind(symbol, fn, user)` for every override (about 220 symbols) and for
the generated "not implemented" stubs. Wire it where the loader applies overrides (TotK name: `hostfn_add_override`):

```cpp
hle::init_trace_from_env();
hle::load_config("");                       // before the first fs call: fs::instance() reads the config once
hle::bind_all([](const char* sym, GuestFn fn, void* u) { hostfn_add_override(*(Module*)u, sym, fn); }, &module);
```

Both `main` and `sdk` get the same binder: 725 of the 731 imports resolve into `sdk`, so an override must replace the
symbol in every module that defines or imports it. The `sdk`-internal overrides (the 14 rows in `hle_coverage.tsv` with
`boot = n/a`, for example `nn::socket::Write`, `nn::socket::Read`, the `nn::err` constructor) only match inside `sdk`.

## 2. Two os hooks (needed for vsync and account async)

`hle::os_hooks()` has two function pointers that `runtime/os` should fill once its event type exists:

```cpp
hle::os_hooks().init_system_event   = [](void* ev, bool manual_clear) { /* nn::os::InitializeSystemEvent-like, in place */ };
hle::os_hooks().signal_system_event = [](void* ev) { /* nn::os::SignalSystemEvent-like, callable from any host thread */ };
```

Users: `nn::vi::GetDisplayVsyncEvent` starts a 60 Hz thread that signals the event, and
`nn::account::AsyncContext::GetSystemEvent` signals an already-done event. Without the hooks both log one line and return
success; the game then waits on an event that never fires. Call `hle::vi_stop_vsync()` at shutdown.

## 3. nn::vi native window token for NVN (needed by runtime/nvn)

`nn::vi::OpenDefaultDisplay`, `CreateLayer` and `GetNativeWindow` return opaque tokens. `hle::vi_native_window()` is the
`nn::vi::NativeWindowHandle` the game then hands to the NVN window builder. `runtime/nvn` should accept exactly that
pointer (or ignore the argument) and create the host swapchain itself. HLE does not touch NVN.

## 4. Mouse position from the NVN window (optional)

`input::RawInput::mouse_x/mouse_y` are 0..1 over the game's client area. The Win32 backend uses the foreground window of
the process. When `runtime/nvn` owns an SDL/GLFW window it can call a future `input::set_window_provider()`; until then the
SDL3 backend reads the focused SDL window and the Win32 backend needs nothing.

## 5. Symbols registered here that another layer might also register

- `nv::SetGraphicsAllocator` and `nv::InitializeGraphics` are no-ops here (service `nv`). `runtime/nvn` should not
  register them again; if it needs them, delete the two `HLE_NOOP("nv", ...)` lines in `reg_sys.inc` and rerun `gen_hle_stubs.py`.
- `nn::diag::detail::AbortImpl` and `nndetailDiagAbortFormatImpl` log the expression, function, file and line and then
  call `hle::fatal()`. If `runtime/os` wants a guest crash dump it can set `hle::fatal_hook`.
- No `nn::os` or `nn::audio` symbol is overridden here. Those 102 imports are `todo` with owner `runtime/os` and
  `runtime/audio` in `hle_coverage.tsv`.

## 6. Link the generated backstop (optional)

`generated/hle_unimplemented.cpp` (from `gen_hle_stubs.py`) registers a logging abort stub for each `nn::` import this layer
owns but has no override for. It is empty today (every owned import has an override). Run `gen_hle_stubs.py --all` to also
stub the os, audio and nvn imports while those layers are unfinished; `bind_all` never lets a stub replace a real override
from this layer, but the loader must bind other layers' overrides after `bind_all`.

## 7. Build flags

- C++20, add `runtime/` to the include path. Windows needs `-luser32` (message box, `GetAsyncKeyState`).
- Default input backend: Win32 (XInput loaded at run time, `GetAsyncKeyState`, cursor). For SDL3 gamepads (PS4/PS5,
  Switch Pro, generic) add `-DHLE_WITH_SDL3`, `-Itools/dl_sdl3/x/SDL3-3.4.20/include` and link SDL3. Both compile clean.
- Define `_CRT_SECURE_NO_WARNINGS` with clang-cl/clang on MSVC headers or the `getenv`/`sscanf` deprecation warnings appear.

## 8. Config must be loaded before the first fs call

`hle::fs::instance()` snapshots `rom_layers`, `romfs_root`, `save_root` and `save_backups` on first use. Call
`hle::load_config()` first, or call `set_rom_layers()` / `set_save_root()` afterwards.

```

`runtime/hle/fs.cpp`:

```cpp
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// nn::fs host overrides. Mount names and call shapes come from `main`:
//   nnMain 0x4e3f70..0x4e4138: builds the string "rom", calls QueryMountRomCacheSize(&n) (0x4e410c), allocates n bytes and
//     calls MountRom("rom", cache, n) (0x4e4138). Paths are then built as "rom:/" + name (0x4e4150..0x4e41cc).
//   save init 0x4d5300..0x4d9cf4: account::Initialize/GetUserCount/TryOpenPreselectedUser/GetUserId/GetNickname, then
//     GetSaveDataSize(&size,&journal,uid) (0x4d7b00) and MountSaveData("savedata", uid) (0x4d7b10); files are named
//     "savedata:/%08x%08x" (format string at 0xaf02b0). Unmount("savedata") at 0x4e146c.
//   Commit("savedata") at 0x6072f4, 0x60744c, 0x607564, 0x607678, 0x607790, 0x6078ac, 0x609710.
//   GetFreeSpaceSize(&n,"savedata") at 0x609a30 (needs n >> 22 >= 0x19, i.e. 100 MiB) and 0x6107c8, then
//   ExtendSaveData(uid, saveSize + need, journal) at 0x610800 when it is short: the host reports plenty so that
//   path never runs.
#include <algorithm>
#include <cstdio>
#include <cstring>
#ifdef _WIN32
#define NOMINMAX
#define WIN32_LEAN_AND_MEAN
#include <windows.h>
#endif

#include "fs_core.h"
#include "hle.h"
#include "hle_config.h"

// Taps for the DRP entry mod loader (runtime/mods/mods.cpp installs them only when mod packs exist): it learns which archive
// a read buffer came from. Null otherwise.
void (*g_snap_fs_tap_open)(uint64_t id, const char* path) = nullptr;
void (*g_snap_fs_tap_close)(uint64_t id) = nullptr;
void (*g_snap_fs_tap_read)(uint64_t id, const void* buf, size_t n) = nullptr;

namespace hle {
namespace {

using fs::instance;

std::string cstr(uint64_t a) { return a ? std::string(ptr<const char>(a)) : std::string(); }

// ---- mounting
void fs_set_allocator(Cpu* c) { (void)c; ret(c, 0); }  // game allocator for the SDK's internal buffers: not needed

void fs_query_mount_rom_cache_size(Cpu* c) {  // Result QueryMountRomCacheSize(size_t*)
  store<uint64_t>(ptr<void>(arg(c, 0)), 0x10000);
  ret(c, kSuccess);
}

void fs_mount_rom(Cpu* c) {  // Result MountRom(const char* name, void* cache, size_t size)
  ret(c, instance().mount_rom(cstr(arg(c, 0))));
}

void fs_get_save_data_size(Cpu* c) {  // Result GetSaveDataSize(long* size, long* journal, const Uid&)
  store<int64_t>(ptr<void>(arg(c, 0)), config().save_data_size);
  store<int64_t>(ptr<void>(arg(c, 1)), config().save_journal_size);
  ret(c, kSuccess);
}

void fs_mount_save_data(Cpu* c) {  // Result MountSaveData(const char* name, const Uid& uid)
  uint64_t uid[2];
  std::memcpy(uid, ptr<void>(arg(c, 1)), sizeof uid);
  uint32_t rc = instance().mount_save(cstr(arg(c, 0)), uid);
#ifdef _WIN32
  if (rc == fs::kResultTargetLocked) {   // another copy of the game owns this save folder: say so and stop, never touch its files
    const char* msg = "Another copy of New Pokemon Snap is already running with this save folder. Close it, or start this copy with a different profile or save folder (SNAP_SAVE_DIR). This copy will now close without changing any save.";
    log("fs: %s", msg);
    if (!config().headless) MessageBoxA(nullptr, msg, "Pokemon Snap", MB_OK | MB_ICONERROR | MB_TOPMOST | MB_SETFOREGROUND);
    std::fflush(nullptr);
    ExitProcess(3);
  }
#endif
  ret(c, rc);
}

void fs_extend_save_data(Cpu* c) { ret(c, kSuccess); }  // Result ExtendSaveData(const Uid&, long, long): host space is not limited

void fs_unmount(Cpu* c) { instance().unmount(cstr(arg(c, 0))); ret(c, 0); }  // void Unmount(const char*)

void fs_commit(Cpu* c) { ret(c, instance().commit(cstr(arg(c, 0)))); }  // Result Commit(const char* mount) / CommitSaveData

void fs_get_free_space_size(Cpu* c) {  // Result GetFreeSpaceSize(long* out, const char* path)
  std::string path = cstr(arg(c, 1));
  size_t colon = path.find(':');
  int64_t v = 0;
  uint32_t rc = instance().get_free_space(&v, colon == std::string::npos ? path : path.substr(0, colon));
  if (!rc) store<int64_t>(ptr<void>(arg(c, 0)), v);
  ret(c, rc);
}

void fs_set_priority(Cpu* c) { (void)c; }  // void SetPriorityOnCurrentThread(Priority)

// ---- files
void fs_create_file(Cpu* c) { ret(c, instance().create_file(cstr(arg(c, 0)), (int64_t)arg(c, 1))); }  // (path, size[, option])
void fs_delete_file(Cpu* c) { ret(c, instance().delete_file(cstr(arg(c, 0)))); }

void fs_open_file(Cpu* c) {  // Result OpenFile(FileHandle* out, const char* path, int mode)
  fs::FileId id = 0;

  uint32_t rc = instance().open_file(&id, path, (int)arg32(c, 2));
  if (!rc) { store<uint64_t>(ptr<void>(arg(c, 0)), id); if (g_snap_fs_tap_open) g_snap_fs_tap_open(id, path.c_str()); }
  ret(c, rc);
}

  if (g_snap_fs_tap_read) g_snap_fs_tap_read(arg(c, 0), ptr<void>(arg(c, 2)), arg(c, 3));
  ret(c, instance().read_file(arg(c, 0), (int64_t)arg(c, 1), ptr<void>(arg(c, 2)), arg(c, 3), nullptr));
}
void fs_read_file_opt(Cpu* c) {  // Result ReadFile(FileHandle, long, void*, size_t, const ReadOption&)
  if (g_snap_fs_tap_read) g_snap_fs_tap_read(arg(c, 0), ptr<void>(arg(c, 2)), arg(c, 3));
  ret(c, instance().read_file(arg(c, 0), (int64_t)arg(c, 1), ptr<void>(arg(c, 2)), arg(c, 3), nullptr));

void fs_read_file_out(Cpu* c) {  // Result ReadFile(size_t* out, FileHandle, long, void*, size_t)
  size_t got = 0;

  uint32_t rc = instance().read_file(arg(c, 1), (int64_t)arg(c, 2), ptr<void>(arg(c, 3)), arg(c, 4), &got);
  if (!rc && arg(c, 0)) store<uint64_t>(ptr<void>(arg(c, 0)), got);

}
void fs_write_file(Cpu* c) {  // Result WriteFile(FileHandle, long, const void*, size_t, const WriteOption&)

  ret(c, instance().write_file(arg(c, 0), (int64_t)arg(c, 1), ptr<void>(arg(c, 2)), arg(c, 3), (flags & 1) != 0));
}
void fs_flush_file(Cpu* c) { ret(c, instance().flush_file(arg(c, 0))); }

  ret(c, rc);
}
void fs_set_file_size(Cpu* c) { ret(c, instance().set_file_size(arg(c, 0), (int64_t)arg(c, 1))); }

// ---- directories
void fs_get_entry_type(Cpu* c) {  // Result GetEntryType(DirectoryEntryType*, const char*)
  int t = 0;
  uint32_t rc = instance().get_entry_type(&t, cstr(arg(c, 1)));
  if (!rc) store<int32_t>(ptr<void>(arg(c, 0)), t);
  ret(c, rc);
}
void fs_create_directory(Cpu* c) { ret(c, instance().create_directory(cstr(arg(c, 0)))); }
void fs_delete_directory(Cpu* c) { ret(c, instance().delete_directory(cstr(arg(c, 0)), false)); }
void fs_delete_directory_rec(Cpu* c) { ret(c, instance().delete_directory(cstr(arg(c, 0)), true)); }
void fs_rename_file(Cpu* c) { ret(c, instance().rename_file(cstr(arg(c, 0)), cstr(arg(c, 1)))); }
void fs_open_directory(Cpu* c) {  // Result OpenDirectory(DirectoryHandle*, const char*, int mode)
  fs::DirId id = 0;
  uint32_t rc = instance().open_directory(&id, cstr(arg(c, 1)), (int)arg32(c, 2));
  if (!rc) store<uint64_t>(ptr<void>(arg(c, 0)), id);
  ret(c, rc);
}
void fs_close_directory(Cpu* c) { instance().close_directory(arg(c, 0)); ret(c, 0); }
void fs_get_directory_entry_count(Cpu* c) {  // Result (long* out, DirectoryHandle)
  int64_t n = 0;
  uint32_t rc = instance().get_directory_entry_count(arg(c, 1), &n);
  if (!rc) store<int64_t>(ptr<void>(arg(c, 0)), n);
  ret(c, rc);
}
// nn::fs::DirectoryEntry: char name[0x301]; pad[3]; s8 type @0x304; pad[3]; s64 size @0x308; sizeof 0x310
constexpr size_t kDirEntrySize = 0x310;
void fs_read_directory(Cpu* c) {  // Result ReadDirectory(long* outCount, DirectoryEntry* out, DirectoryHandle, long max)
  int64_t max = (int64_t)arg(c, 3);
  max = std::min<int64_t>(max, 1 << 16);   // a guest-controlled count must not size a host allocation (no game directory is near this)
  std::vector<fs::DirEntry> tmp((size_t)(max > 0 ? max : 0));
  int64_t n = 0;
  uint32_t rc = instance().read_directory(arg(c, 2), tmp.data(), max, &n);
  if (!rc) {
    uint8_t* out = ptr<uint8_t>(arg(c, 1));
    for (int64_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
      uint8_t* e = out + (size_t)i * kDirEntrySize;
      std::memset(e, 0, kDirEntrySize);
      std::snprintf(reinterpret_cast<char*>(e), 0x301, "%s", tmp[(size_t)i].name.c_str());
      e[0x304] = (uint8_t)tmp[(size_t)i].type;
      store<int64_t>(e + 0x308, tmp[(size_t)i].size);
    }
    store<int64_t>(ptr<void>(arg(c, 0)), n);
  }
  ret(c, rc);
}

}  // namespace
