```cpp
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
#include "fs_core.h"
#include "os/perf.h"

#include <algorithm>
#include <atomic>
#include <cctype>
#include <cstdio>
#include <filesystem>
#include <fstream>
#include <map>
#include <set>
#include <sstream>
#include <unordered_map>

#include "hle_config.h"

// runtime/os releases the caller's virtual core around blocking reads. These no-op weak defaults keep builds without
// runtime/os (tests/hle) linking; snap_boot links the real ones from os_kernel.cpp.
extern "C" __attribute__((weak)) void os_io_begin(void) {}
extern "C" __attribute__((weak)) void os_io_end(void) {}

#ifdef _WIN32
#define NOMINMAX
#define WIN32_LEAN_AND_MEAN
#include <windows.h>
#else
#include <fcntl.h>
#include <unistd.h>
#endif

#pragma clang diagnostic ignored "-Wdeprecated-declarations"

namespace hle::fs {

namespace stdfs = std::filesystem;

static stdfs::path to_path(const std::string& s) { return stdfs::u8path(s); }
static std::string from_path(const stdfs::path& p) {
  auto u = p.u8string();
  return std::string(u.begin(), u.end());
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
// host file with positioned I/O
class HostFile {
 public:
  ~HostFile() { close(); }
  bool open(const stdfs::path& p, bool write) {
#ifdef _WIN32
    DWORD access = GENERIC_READ | (write ? GENERIC_WRITE : 0);
    h_ = CreateFileW(p.c_str(), access, FILE_SHARE_READ | FILE_SHARE_WRITE | FILE_SHARE_DELETE, nullptr, OPEN_EXISTING,
                     FILE_ATTRIBUTE_NORMAL | FILE_FLAG_RANDOM_ACCESS, nullptr);
    return h_ != INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE;
#else
    fd_ = ::open(p.c_str(), write ? O_RDWR : O_RDONLY);
    return fd_ >= 0;
#endif
  }
  void close() {
#ifdef _WIN32
    if (h_ != INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE) { CloseHandle(h_); h_ = INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE; }
#else
    if (fd_ >= 0) { ::close(fd_); fd_ = -1; }
#endif
  }
  int64_t size() {
#ifdef _WIN32
    LARGE_INTEGER s;
    return GetFileSizeEx(h_, &s) ? s.QuadPart : -1;
#else
    off_t cur = lseek(fd_, 0, SEEK_CUR); (void)cur;
    return lseek(fd_, 0, SEEK_END);
#endif
  }
  // returns bytes read, -1 on error
  int64_t read_at(int64_t off, void* buf, size_t n) {
    size_t done = 0;
    char* b = static_cast<char*>(buf);
    while (done < n) {
#ifdef _WIN32
      DWORD chunk = (DWORD)std::min<size_t>(n - done, 1u << 30), got = 0;
      OVERLAPPED ov{};
      ov.Offset = (DWORD)((off + (int64_t)done) & 0xffffffff);
      ov.OffsetHigh = (DWORD)((off + (int64_t)done) >> 32);
      if (!ReadFile(h_, b + done, chunk, &got, &ov)) {
        if (GetLastError() == ERROR_HANDLE_EOF) break;
        return -1;
      }
      if (got == 0) break;
      // [perf] pass 5: mark the filled pages written from user mode, so GetWriteWatch (dirty-page buffer sync, runtime\nvn\nvn_vk.cpp)
      // reports them after the data is final. A test (perf pass 5, results.md) showed buffered reads are seen anyway but
      // unbuffered/DMA reads racing a watch reset leave pages stale; an atomic OR with 0 per page changes no byte.
      for (uintptr_t p = (uintptr_t)(b + done) & ~(uintptr_t)3, e = (uintptr_t)(b + done + got); p < e; p = (p | 4095) + 1)   // one aligned dword per page (same page as the buffer bytes)
        InterlockedOr((volatile LONG*)p, 0);
      done += got;
#else
      ssize_t got = pread(fd_, b + done, n - done, off + (off_t)done);
      if (got < 0) return -1;
      if (got == 0) break;
      done += (size_t)got;
#endif
    }
    return (int64_t)done;
  }
  bool write_at(int64_t off, const void* buf, size_t n) {
    const char* b = static_cast<const char*>(buf);
    size_t done = 0;
    while (done < n) {
#ifdef _WIN32
      DWORD chunk = (DWORD)std::min<size_t>(n - done, 1u << 30), got = 0;
      OVERLAPPED ov{};
      ov.Offset = (DWORD)((off + (int64_t)done) & 0xffffffff);
      ov.OffsetHigh = (DWORD)((off + (int64_t)done) >> 32);
      if (!WriteFile(h_, b + done, chunk, &got, &ov)) return false;
      done += got;
#else
      ssize_t got = pwrite(fd_, b + done, n - done, off + (off_t)done);
      if (got <= 0) return false;
      done += (size_t)got;
#endif
    }
    return true;
  }
  bool set_size(int64_t size) {
#ifdef _WIN32
    LARGE_INTEGER li;
    li.QuadPart = size;
    return SetFilePointerEx(h_, li, nullptr, FILE_BEGIN) && SetEndOfFile(h_);
#else
    return ftruncate(fd_, size) == 0;
#endif
  }
  bool flush() {
#ifdef _WIN32
    return FlushFileBuffers(h_) != 0;
#else
    return fsync(fd_) == 0;
#endif
  }

 private:
#ifdef _WIN32
  HANDLE h_ = INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE;
#else
  int fd_ = -1;
#endif
};

// Flushes a file to disk by path (used for commit durability). Best effort.
static void flush_path(const stdfs::path& p) {
  HostFile f;
  if (f.open(p, true)) { f.flush(); }
}

// Atomically replaces `to` with `from` (same directory/volume), writing through.
static bool replace_file(const stdfs::path& from, const stdfs::path& to) {
#ifdef _WIN32
  return MoveFileExW(from.c_str(), to.c_str(), MOVEFILE_REPLACE_EXISTING | MOVEFILE_WRITE_THROUGH) != 0;
#else
  std::error_code ec;
  stdfs::rename(from, to, ec);
  return !ec;
#endif
}

bool split_path(const std::string& path, std::string* mount, std::string* rel) {
  size_t c = path.find(':');
  if (c == std::string::npos || c == 0 || c > 32) return false;
  *mount = path.substr(0, c);
  std::string r = path.substr(c + 1);
  if (r.empty() || (r[0] != '/' && r[0] != '\\')) return false;
  std::string out, comp;
  auto flush_comp = [&]() -> bool {
    if (comp.empty() || comp == ".") { comp.clear(); return true; }
    if (comp == "..") return false;
    if (!out.empty()) out += '/';
    out += comp;
    comp.clear();
    return true;
  };
  for (char ch : r) {
    if (ch == '/' || ch == '\\') { if (!flush_comp()) return false; }
    else comp += ch;
  }
  if (!flush_comp()) return false;
  *rel = out;
  return true;
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
namespace {

struct OpenFile {
  HostFile hf;
  bool writable = false;
  std::string mount;
  std::string rel;          // save mounts: path inside the mount, so a write after a commit re-marks the file dirty
  struct Save* save = nullptr;  // owned by the mount; kept alive by keep below
  std::shared_ptr<void> keep;   // the owning Mount: a write that outlives unmount/remount still has a valid save for mark_dirty
  std::mutex mu;  // serializes write / resize on this handle
};
struct OpenDir {
  std::vector<DirEntry> entries;
  size_t cursor = 0;
};

constexpr const char* kPointerName = "CURRENT";

// The save mount: committed generations on disk plus a working directory for the uncommitted changes.
//   <root>/gens/<n>/      complete state of generation n (immutable once committed)
//   <root>/gens/<n>.ok    written after generation n is complete
//   <root>/CURRENT        "SNAPSAVE1\n<n>\n<check>\n", replaced atomically at commit
//   <root>/working/       copy-on-write scratch of the running session; wiped at every mount
struct Save {
  stdfs::path root;
  uint64_t cur = 0;
  int keep = 5;
  std::string lock_key;  // key of the folder lock in Fs::Impl::locks (empty: none)
  std::set<std::string> dirty, deleted, dirs;  // dirs: directories created since the last commit

  stdfs::path gens() const { return root / "gens"; }
  stdfs::path gen_dir(uint64_t n) const { return gens() / std::to_string(n); }
  stdfs::path gen_ok(uint64_t n) const { return gens() / (std::to_string(n) + ".ok"); }
  stdfs::path working() const { return root / "working"; }
  stdfs::path committed() const { return gen_dir(cur); }

  static uint32_t check_of(uint64_t n) { return (uint32_t)(n * 2654435761u) ^ 0x534e4150u; }

  bool read_pointer(uint64_t* n) const {
    std::ifstream f(root / kPointerName, std::ios::binary);
    if (!f) return false;
    std::string magic;
    unsigned long long g = 0, chk = 0;
    if (!(f >> magic >> g >> chk) || magic != "SNAPSAVE1") return false;
    if ((uint32_t)chk != check_of(g)) return false;
    *n = g;
    return true;
  }
  bool write_pointer(uint64_t n, const std::function<void(const char*)>& hook) const {
    stdfs::path tmp = root / "CURRENT.tmp";
    {
      std::ofstream f(tmp, std::ios::binary | std::ios::trunc);
      if (!f) return false;
      f << "SNAPSAVE1\n" << n << "\n" << check_of(n) << "\n";
    }
    flush_path(tmp);
    if (hook) hook("commit:pointer-tmp");
    if (!replace_file(tmp, root / kPointerName)) return false;
    if (hook) hook("commit:pointer-done");
    return true;
  }
  bool gen_valid(uint64_t n) const {
    std::error_code ec;
    return stdfs::exists(gen_ok(n), ec) && stdfs::is_directory(gen_dir(n), ec);
  }

  // Finds the newest complete generation at or below `limit` (no limit: any).
  bool scan(uint64_t* out) const {
    std::error_code ec;
    bool found = false;
    uint64_t best = 0;
    for (auto& e : stdfs::directory_iterator(gens(), ec)) {
      if (e.path().extension() != ".ok") continue;
      uint64_t n = std::strtoull(e.path().stem().string().c_str(), nullptr, 10);
      if (gen_valid(n) && (!found || n > best)) { best = n; found = true; }
    }
    if (found) *out = best;
    return found;
  }

  // Opens the save: finds the committed generation, drops every uncommitted or half-built leftover.
  bool open(int keep_gens) {
    keep = keep_gens;
    std::error_code ec;
    stdfs::create_directories(gens(), ec);
    uint64_t n = 0;
    bool have = read_pointer(&n) && gen_valid(n);
    if (!have) {
      // the pointer is missing or torn: a CURRENT.tmp that is valid and complete is the interrupted replace
      stdfs::path tmp = root / "CURRENT.tmp";
      if (stdfs::exists(tmp, ec)) {
        std::ifstream f(tmp, std::ios::binary);
        std::string magic; unsigned long long g = 0, chk = 0;
        if (f && (f >> magic >> g >> chk) && magic == "SNAPSAVE1" && (uint32_t)chk == check_of(g) && gen_valid(g)) {
          n = g; have = true;
        }
      }
    }
    if (!have) have = scan(&n);
    if (!have) {
      n = 0;
      stdfs::create_directories(gen_dir(0), ec);
      std::ofstream(gen_ok(0)) << "ok\n";
    }
    cur = n;
    // leftovers newer than the committed generation never became current: an interrupted commit
    for (auto& e : stdfs::directory_iterator(gens(), ec)) {
      uint64_t g = std::strtoull(e.path().stem().string().c_str(), nullptr, 10);
      if (g > cur) stdfs::remove_all(e.path(), ec);
    }
    stdfs::remove(root / "CURRENT.tmp", ec);
    std::error_code ec2;
    if (!read_pointer(&n) || n != cur) {
      std::function<void(const char*)> none;
      write_pointer(cur, none);
    }
    stdfs::remove_all(working(), ec);
    stdfs::create_directories(working(), ec);
    dirty.clear(); deleted.clear(); dirs.clear();
    return true;
  }

  // 0 none, 1 directory, 2 file
  int kind(const std::string& rel) const {
    if (rel.empty()) return 1;
    if (deleted.count(rel)) return 0;
    std::error_code ec;
    stdfs::path w = working() / to_path(rel);
    if (stdfs::exists(w, ec)) return stdfs::is_directory(w, ec) ? 1 : 2;
    stdfs::path c = committed() / to_path(rel);
    if (stdfs::exists(c, ec)) return stdfs::is_directory(c, ec) ? 1 : 2;
    return 0;
  }
  // The host path to read `rel` from (working copy if there is one).
  stdfs::path read_path(const std::string& rel) const {
    std::error_code ec;
    stdfs::path w = working() / to_path(rel);
    if (stdfs::exists(w, ec)) return w;
    return committed() / to_path(rel);
  }
  // Makes sure the file has a working copy and returns it.
  bool ensure_working(const std::string& rel, stdfs::path* out) {
    std::error_code ec;
    stdfs::path w = working() / to_path(rel);
    stdfs::create_directories(w.parent_path(), ec);
    if (!stdfs::exists(w, ec)) {
      stdfs::path c = committed() / to_path(rel);
      if (!deleted.count(rel) && stdfs::exists(c, ec) && stdfs::is_regular_file(c, ec)) {
        stdfs::copy_file(c, w, stdfs::copy_options::overwrite_existing, ec);
        if (ec) return false;
      }
    }
    dirty.insert(rel);
    *out = w;
    return true;
  }

  std::vector<DirEntry> list(const std::string& rel) const {
    std::map<std::string, DirEntry> m;
    std::error_code ec;
    auto add = [&](const stdfs::path& dir) {
      for (auto& e : stdfs::directory_iterator(dir, ec)) {
        std::string name = from_path(e.path().filename());
        std::string child = rel.empty() ? name : rel + "/" + name;
        if (deleted.count(child)) continue;
        DirEntry d;
        d.name = name;
        std::error_code e2;
        d.type = e.is_directory(e2) ? kDirectory : kFile;
        d.size = d.type == kFile ? (int64_t)e.file_size(e2) : 0;
        m[name] = d;  // working (added second) overrides committed
      }
    };
    stdfs::path c = committed() / to_path(rel), w = working() / to_path(rel);
    if (stdfs::is_directory(c, ec)) add(c);
    if (stdfs::is_directory(w, ec)) add(w);
    std::vector<DirEntry> out;
    for (auto& kv : m) out.push_back(kv.second);
    return out;
  }

  void carry(const stdfs::path& from, const stdfs::path& to, const std::string& rel) {
    std::error_code ec;
    for (auto& e : stdfs::directory_iterator(from, ec)) {
      std::string name = from_path(e.path().filename());
      std::string child = rel.empty() ? name : rel + "/" + name;
      if (deleted.count(child)) continue;
      if (e.is_directory(ec)) {
        stdfs::create_directories(to / name, ec);
        carry(e.path(), to / name, child);
      } else if (!dirty.count(child)) {
        stdfs::create_hard_link(e.path(), to / name, ec);
        if (ec) { ec.clear(); stdfs::copy_file(e.path(), to / name, stdfs::copy_options::overwrite_existing, ec); }
      }
    }
  }

  uint32_t do_commit(const std::function<void(const char*)>& hook) {
    auto stage = [&](const char* s) { if (hook) hook(s); };
    std::error_code ec;
    stage("commit:begin");
    uint64_t n = cur + 1;
    stdfs::path ng = gen_dir(n);
    stdfs::remove_all(ng, ec);
    stdfs::remove(gen_ok(n), ec);
    stdfs::create_directories(ng, ec);
    if (ec) return result(2, 6010);
    carry(committed(), ng, "");
    stage("commit:carried");
    for (const std::string& rel : dirty) {
      stdfs::path src = working() / to_path(rel), dst = ng / to_path(rel);
      if (!stdfs::exists(src, ec)) continue;  // created then deleted in the same session
      stdfs::create_directories(dst.parent_path(), ec);
      stdfs::copy_file(src, dst, stdfs::copy_options::overwrite_existing, ec);
      if (ec) return kResultUsableSpaceNotEnough;
      flush_path(dst);
      stage("commit:file");
    }
    for (const std::string& rel : dirs) stdfs::create_directories(ng / to_path(rel), ec);
    stage("commit:files-done");
    { std::ofstream f(gen_ok(n), std::ios::binary); f << "ok\n"; }
    flush_path(gen_ok(n));
    stage("commit:marker");
    if (!write_pointer(n, hook)) return kResultUsableSpaceNotEnough;
    cur = n;
    dirty.clear(); deleted.clear(); dirs.clear();
    // automatic backups: keep the current generation and `keep` before it
    if (keep >= 0 && cur > (uint64_t)keep) {
      for (auto& e : stdfs::directory_iterator(gens(), ec)) {
        uint64_t g = std::strtoull(e.path().stem().string().c_str(), nullptr, 10);
        if (g + (uint64_t)keep < cur) stdfs::remove_all(e.path(), ec);
      }
    }
    return kSuccess;
  }
};

struct Mount {
  enum Kind { Rom, SaveData, Host } kind = Host;
  bool writable = false;
  std::vector<stdfs::path> layers;  // rom/host
  std::unique_ptr<Save> save;
};

}  // namespace

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
struct Fs::Impl {
  std::mutex mu;  // mounts and tables
  std::map<std::string, std::shared_ptr<Mount>> mounts;
  std::unordered_map<uint64_t, std::shared_ptr<OpenFile>> files;
  std::unordered_map<uint64_t, std::shared_ptr<OpenDir>> dirs;
  std::atomic<uint64_t> next{0x1000};
  std::vector<std::string> rom_layers;
  std::string save_root;
  int save_backups = 5;
  std::function<void(const char*)> hook;
  std::map<std::string, void*> locks;  // save root -> open ".snap.lock" handle holding an exclusive byte lock (one running game per save folder)

  ~Impl() {
#ifdef _WIN32
    for (auto& kv : locks) CloseHandle((HANDLE)kv.second);
#endif
  }
  // Drops the folder lock once no save mount uses it any more (unmount, remount).
  void release_lock(const std::string& key) {
#ifdef _WIN32
    if (key.empty()) return;
    for (auto& kv : mounts) if (kv.second->save && kv.second->save->lock_key == key) return;
    if (auto it = locks.find(key); it != locks.end()) { CloseHandle((HANDLE)it->second); locks.erase(it); }
#else
    (void)key;
#endif
  }
  std::shared_ptr<Mount> find_mount(const std::string& name) {
    auto it = mounts.find(name);
    return it == mounts.end() ? nullptr : it->second;
  }
  uint64_t token() { return next.fetch_add(0x10); }
};

Fs::Fs() : p_(new Impl) {
  Config& c = config();
  p_->save_root = c.save_root;
  p_->save_backups = c.save_backups;
  std::vector<std::string> l = c.rom_layers;
  l.push_back(c.romfs_root);
  p_->rom_layers = std::move(l);
}
Fs::~Fs() = default;

void Fs::set_rom_layers(std::vector<std::string> dirs) {
  std::lock_guard<std::mutex> g(p_->mu);
  p_->rom_layers = std::move(dirs);
}
std::vector<std::string> Fs::rom_layers() const {
  std::lock_guard<std::mutex> g(p_->mu);
  return p_->rom_layers;
}
void Fs::set_save_root(const std::string& dir) { std::lock_guard<std::mutex> g(p_->mu); p_->save_root = dir; }
void Fs::set_save_backups(int n) { std::lock_guard<std::mutex> g(p_->mu); p_->save_backups = n; }
void Fs::set_fault_hook(std::function<void(const char*)> hook) { std::lock_guard<std::mutex> g(p_->mu); p_->hook = std::move(hook); }

uint32_t Fs::mount_rom(const std::string& name) {
  std::lock_guard<std::mutex> g(p_->mu);
  auto m = std::make_shared<Mount>();
  m->kind = Mount::Rom;
  std::error_code ec;
  for (auto& d : p_->rom_layers) {
    stdfs::path p = to_path(d);
    if (stdfs::is_directory(p, ec)) m->layers.push_back(p);
    else log("fs: rom layer %s does not exist; skipped", d.c_str());
  }
  if (m->layers.empty()) { log("fs: no rom layer exists; MountRom(%s) fails", name.c_str()); return kResultPathNotFound; }
  p_->mounts[name] = m;
  if (trace_flags & kTraceFs) log("fs: mounted %s: with %zu layer(s), first %s", name.c_str(), m->layers.size(), from_path(m->layers[0]).c_str());
  return kSuccess;
}

uint32_t Fs::mount_host(const std::string& name, const std::string& dir, bool writable) {
  std::lock_guard<std::mutex> g(p_->mu);
  auto m = std::make_shared<Mount>();
  m->kind = Mount::Host;
  m->writable = writable;
  std::error_code ec;
  stdfs::path p = to_path(dir);
  if (writable) stdfs::create_directories(p, ec);
  if (!stdfs::is_directory(p, ec)) return kResultPathNotFound;
  m->layers.push_back(p);
  p_->mounts[name] = m;
  return kSuccess;
}

uint32_t Fs::mount_save(const std::string& name, const uint64_t uid[2]) {
  std::lock_guard<std::mutex> g(p_->mu);
  auto m = std::make_shared<Mount>();
  m->kind = Mount::SaveData;
  m->writable = true;
  m->save = std::make_unique<Save>();
  m->save->root = to_path(p_->save_root) / to_path(uid_dir_name(uid));
  std::error_code ec;
  // Same name mounted again: the old mount stays untouched until the new one can no longer fail (lock, directory); only then is it
  // dropped (its open handles die with it; Save::open wipes working/ anyway). The new mount takes over the same folder lock.
#ifdef _WIN32
  // One running game per save folder. Save::open deletes working/ and every newer generation, which would wreck a second live
  // process on the same folder, so refuse before touching anything. Per save root (parallel test runs use their own roots);
  // the lock dies with the process, so a crash never leaves a stale one.
  {
    stdfs::path root = to_path(p_->save_root);
    stdfs::create_directories(root, ec);
    const std::string key = from_path(root);
    m->save->lock_key = key;
    if (!p_->locks.count(key)) {
      HANDLE h = CreateFileW((root / ".snap.lock").c_str(), GENERIC_READ | GENERIC_WRITE, FILE_SHARE_READ | FILE_SHARE_WRITE | FILE_SHARE_DELETE,
                             nullptr, OPEN_ALWAYS, FILE_ATTRIBUTE_NORMAL, nullptr);
      OVERLAPPED ov{};
      if (h == INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE) {
        log("fs: cannot open the save lock file in %s (error %lu); continuing without the single-instance guard", key.c_str(), GetLastError());
      } else if (!LockFileEx(h, LOCKFILE_EXCLUSIVE_LOCK | LOCKFILE_FAIL_IMMEDIATELY, 0, 1, 0, &ov)) {
        DWORD e = GetLastError();
        CloseHandle(h);
        log("fs: save folder %s is in use by another running copy of the game (lock error %lu); not mounting it", key.c_str(), e);
        return e == ERROR_LOCK_VIOLATION ? kResultTargetLocked : kResultUsableSpaceNotEnough;
      } else {
        p_->locks[key] = h;
      }
    }
  }
#endif
  stdfs::create_directories(m->save->root, ec);
  if (ec) { log("fs: cannot create save directory %s: %s", from_path(m->save->root).c_str(), ec.message().c_str()); return kResultUsableSpaceNotEnough; }
  if (auto old = p_->mounts.find(name); old != p_->mounts.end()) {
    for (auto f = p_->files.begin(); f != p_->files.end();) { if (f->second->mount == name) f = p_->files.erase(f); else ++f; }
    p_->mounts.erase(old);   // OpenFile::keep holds the Save of a handle a writer still has in flight
  }
  m->save->open(p_->save_backups);
  p_->mounts[name] = m;
  if (trace_flags & kTraceFs) log("fs: mounted %s: save %s generation %llu", name.c_str(), from_path(m->save->root).c_str(), (unsigned long long)m->save->cur);
  return kSuccess;
}

uint32_t Fs::unmount(const std::string& name) {
  std::lock_guard<std::mutex> g(p_->mu);
  auto it = p_->mounts.find(name);
  if (it == p_->mounts.end()) return kResultNotMounted;
  for (auto f = p_->files.begin(); f != p_->files.end();) {
    if (f->second->mount == name) f = p_->files.erase(f); else ++f;
  }
  const std::string lock_key = it->second->save ? it->second->save->lock_key : std::string();
  p_->mounts.erase(it);  // uncommitted save changes are dropped, as on hardware
  p_->release_lock(lock_key);
  return kSuccess;
}

bool Fs::is_mounted(const std::string& name) {
  std::lock_guard<std::mutex> g(p_->mu);
  return p_->mounts.count(name) != 0;
}

// ---- path resolution helpers (caller holds the lock)
namespace {
struct Resolved {
  std::shared_ptr<Mount> m;
  std::string rel;
  stdfs::path host;  // for layered mounts: first layer holding rel (or the first layer if none)
  int kind = 0;      // 0 none, 1 dir, 2 file
};
}  // namespace

static uint32_t resolve(Fs::Impl* p, const std::string& path, Resolved* r) {
  std::string mount;
  if (!split_path(path, &mount, &r->rel)) return kResultInvalidArgument;
  r->m = p->find_mount(mount);
  if (!r->m) return kResultNotMounted;
  std::error_code ec;
  if (r->m->kind == Mount::SaveData) {
    r->kind = r->m->save->kind(r->rel);
    r->host = r->m->save->read_path(r->rel);
    return kSuccess;
  }
  r->host = r->m->layers[0] / to_path(r->rel);
  r->kind = 0;
  for (auto& layer : r->m->layers) {
    stdfs::path h = layer / to_path(r->rel);
    if (stdfs::exists(h, ec)) {
      r->host = h;
      r->kind = stdfs::is_directory(h, ec) ? 1 : 2;
      break;
    }
  }
  if (r->rel.empty()) r->kind = 1;
  return kSuccess;
}

uint32_t Fs::open_file(FileId* out, const std::string& path, int mode) {
  std::lock_guard<std::mutex> g(p_->mu);
  Resolved r;
  uint32_t rc = resolve(p_.get(), path, &r);
  if (rc) return rc;
  bool want_write = (mode & (kModeWrite | kModeAppend)) != 0;
  if (want_write && !r.m->writable) return kResultWriteNotPermitted;
  if (r.kind != 2) return kResultPathNotFound;
  auto of = std::make_shared<OpenFile>();
  of->writable = want_write;
  std::string mount, rel;
  split_path(path, &mount, &rel);
  of->mount = mount;
  if (want_write && r.m->kind == Mount::SaveData) { of->rel = r.rel; of->save = r.m->save.get(); of->keep = r.m; }
  stdfs::path host = r.host;
  if (want_write) {
    if (r.m->kind == Mount::SaveData) {
      if (!r.m->save->ensure_working(r.rel, &host)) return kResultUsableSpaceNotEnough;
    }
  }
  if (!of->hf.open(host, want_write)) return kResultTargetLocked;
  uint64_t t = p_->token();
  p_->files[t] = of;
  *out = t;
  if (trace_flags & (kTraceFs | kTraceOpen)) log("fs: open %s mode %d -> %s (file %llu)", path.c_str(), mode, from_path(host).c_str(), (unsigned long long)t);
  return kSuccess;
}

uint32_t Fs::close_file(FileId f) {
  std::lock_guard<std::mutex> g(p_->mu);
  auto it = p_->files.find(f);
  if (it == p_->files.end()) return kResultInvalidArgument;
  p_->files.erase(it);
  if (trace_flags & kTraceFs) log("fs: close file %llu", (unsigned long long)f);
  return kSuccess;
}

static std::shared_ptr<OpenFile> get_file(Fs::Impl* p, FileId f) {
  std::lock_guard<std::mutex> g(p->mu);
  auto it = p->files.find(f);
  return it == p->files.end() ? nullptr : it->second;
}

uint32_t Fs::read_file(FileId f, int64_t off, void* buf, size_t n, size_t* out) {
  auto of = get_file(p_.get(), f);
  if (!of) return kResultInvalidArgument;
  if (off < 0) return kResultOutOfRange;
  if (n == 0) { if (out) *out = 0; return kSuccess; }
  int64_t got;
  os_io_begin();   // the read releases the caller's virtual core (os review finding 9; SNAP_SCHED_LEGACY=hostblock keeps it)
  if (snap_perf::on) {   // perf pass 3: time file reads
    const uint64_t t0 = snap_perf::now_ns();
    got = of->hf.read_at(off, buf, n);
    snap_perf::wait_add(snap_perf::WT_FS, snap_perf::now_ns() - t0);
    if (got > 0) snap_perf::g_fs_bytes.fetch_add((uint64_t)got, std::memory_order_relaxed);
  } else {
    got = of->hf.read_at(off, buf, n);
  }
  os_io_end();
  if (trace_flags & kTraceFs) log("fs: read file %llu off %lld n %zu -> %lld", (unsigned long long)f, (long long)off, n, (long long)got);
  if (got < 0) return kResultTargetLocked;
  if (out) { *out = (size_t)got; return kSuccess; }
  return (size_t)got == n ? kSuccess : kResultOutOfRange;
}

// A handle that stays open across Commit keeps writing to the working copy; do_commit cleared the dirty set, so every write
// re-marks its file (after the write, so a commit that runs in between still sees the file dirty next time). Lock order: of->mu, then p->mu
// (commit holds p->mu and never takes of->mu).
static void mark_dirty(Fs::Impl* p, OpenFile& of) {
  if (!of.save) return;
  std::lock_guard<std::mutex> g(p->mu);
  of.save->dirty.insert(of.rel);
}

uint32_t Fs::write_file(FileId f, int64_t off, const void* buf, size_t n, bool flush) {
  auto of = get_file(p_.get(), f);
  if (!of) return kResultInvalidArgument;
  if (!of->writable) return kResultWriteNotPermitted;
  if (off < 0) return kResultOutOfRange;
  std::lock_guard<std::mutex> g(of->mu);
  // Horizon needs the file to be created with its final size (WriteFile does not grow it unless OpenMode_AllowAppend).
  // The host grows it either way: the game only ever writes inside the size it created.
  if (n && !of->hf.write_at(off, buf, n)) return kResultUsableSpaceNotEnough;
  if (flush) of->hf.flush();
  mark_dirty(p_.get(), *of);
  if (trace_flags & kTraceFs) log("fs: write file %llu off %lld n %zu", (unsigned long long)f, (long long)off, n);
  return kSuccess;
}

uint32_t Fs::flush_file(FileId f) {
  auto of = get_file(p_.get(), f);
  if (!of) return kResultInvalidArgument;
  if (of->writable) { std::lock_guard<std::mutex> g(of->mu); of->hf.flush(); }
  return kSuccess;
}

uint32_t Fs::get_file_size(FileId f, int64_t* out) {
  auto of = get_file(p_.get(), f);
  if (!of) return kResultInvalidArgument;
  int64_t s = of->hf.size();
  if (s < 0) return kResultTargetLocked;
  *out = s;
  return kSuccess;
}

uint32_t Fs::set_file_size(FileId f, int64_t size) {
  auto of = get_file(p_.get(), f);
  if (!of) return kResultInvalidArgument;
  if (!of->writable) return kResultWriteNotPermitted;
  if (size < 0) return kResultOutOfRange;
  std::lock_guard<std::mutex> g(of->mu);
  if (!of->hf.set_size(size)) return kResultUsableSpaceNotEnough;
  mark_dirty(p_.get(), *of);
  return kSuccess;
}

uint32_t Fs::get_entry_type(int* out, const std::string& path) {
  std::lock_guard<std::mutex> g(p_->mu);
  Resolved r;
  uint32_t rc = resolve(p_.get(), path, &r);
  if (rc) return rc;
  if (r.kind == 0) return kResultPathNotFound;
  *out = r.kind == 1 ? kDirectory : kFile;
  return kSuccess;
}

uint32_t Fs::create_file(const std::string& path, int64_t size) {
  std::lock_guard<std::mutex> g(p_->mu);
  Resolved r;
  uint32_t rc = resolve(p_.get(), path, &r);
  if (rc) return rc;
  if (!r.m->writable) return kResultWriteNotPermitted;
  if (r.rel.empty()) return kResultInvalidArgument;
  if (r.kind != 0) return kResultPathAlreadyExists;
  std::error_code ec;
  stdfs::path host;
  if (r.m->kind == Mount::SaveData) {
    std::string parent = r.rel.find('/') == std::string::npos ? "" : r.rel.substr(0, r.rel.rfind('/'));
    if (r.m->save->kind(parent) != 1) return kResultPathNotFound;
    r.m->save->deleted.erase(r.rel);
    r.m->save->dirty.insert(r.rel);
    host = r.m->save->working() / to_path(r.rel);
    stdfs::create_directories(host.parent_path(), ec);
  } else {
    host = r.m->layers[0] / to_path(r.rel);
    if (!stdfs::is_directory(host.parent_path(), ec)) return kResultPathNotFound;
  }
  HostFile tmp;
  {
    std::ofstream f(host, std::ios::binary | std::ios::trunc);
    if (!f) return kResultPathNotFound;
  }
  if (size > 0) {
    if (!tmp.open(host, true) || !tmp.set_size(size)) return kResultUsableSpaceNotEnough;
  }
  if (trace_flags & kTraceFs) log("fs: create %s size %lld", path.c_str(), (long long)size);
  return kSuccess;
}

uint32_t Fs::delete_file(const std::string& path) {
  std::lock_guard<std::mutex> g(p_->mu);
  Resolved r;
  uint32_t rc = resolve(p_.get(), path, &r);
  if (rc) return rc;
  if (!r.m->writable) return kResultWriteNotPermitted;
  if (r.kind != 2) return kResultPathNotFound;
  std::error_code ec;
  if (r.m->kind == Mount::SaveData) {
    Save& s = *r.m->save;
    stdfs::remove(s.working() / to_path(r.rel), ec);
    s.dirty.erase(r.rel);
    if (stdfs::exists(s.committed() / to_path(r.rel), ec)) s.deleted.insert(r.rel);
  } else {
    stdfs::remove(r.m->layers[0] / to_path(r.rel), ec);
    if (ec) return kResultTargetLocked;
  }
  return kSuccess;
}

uint32_t Fs::create_directory(const std::string& path) {
  std::lock_guard<std::mutex> g(p_->mu);
  Resolved r;
  uint32_t rc = resolve(p_.get(), path, &r);
  if (rc) return rc;
  if (!r.m->writable) return kResultWriteNotPermitted;
  if (r.kind != 0) return kResultPathAlreadyExists;
  std::error_code ec;
  if (r.m->kind == Mount::SaveData) {
    Save& s = *r.m->save;
    std::string parent = r.rel.find('/') == std::string::npos ? "" : r.rel.substr(0, r.rel.rfind('/'));
    if (s.kind(parent) != 1) return kResultPathNotFound;
    s.deleted.erase(r.rel);
    stdfs::create_directories(s.working() / to_path(r.rel), ec);
    s.dirs.insert(r.rel);
  } else {
    stdfs::path h = r.m->layers[0] / to_path(r.rel);
    if (!stdfs::is_directory(h.parent_path(), ec)) return kResultPathNotFound;
    stdfs::create_directory(h, ec);
    if (ec) return kResultPathNotFound;
  }
  return kSuccess;
}

uint32_t Fs::delete_directory(const std::string& path, bool recursive) {
  std::unique_lock<std::mutex> g(p_->mu);
  Resolved r;
  uint32_t rc = resolve(p_.get(), path, &r);
  if (rc) return rc;
  if (!r.m->writable) return kResultWriteNotPermitted;
  if (r.kind != 1 || r.rel.empty()) return kResultPathNotFound;
  std::error_code ec;
  if (r.m->kind == Mount::SaveData) {
    Save& s = *r.m->save;
    std::function<uint32_t(const std::string&)> rm = [&](const std::string& rel) -> uint32_t {
      for (auto& e : s.list(rel)) {
        std::string child = rel + "/" + e.name;
        if (!recursive) return kResultDirectoryNotEmpty;
        if (e.type == kDirectory) { uint32_t x = rm(child); if (x) return x; }
        else {
          stdfs::remove(s.working() / to_path(child), ec);
          s.dirty.erase(child);
          if (stdfs::exists(s.committed() / to_path(child), ec)) s.deleted.insert(child);
        }
      }
      stdfs::remove(s.working() / to_path(rel), ec);
      s.dirs.erase(rel);
      if (stdfs::exists(s.committed() / to_path(rel), ec)) s.deleted.insert(rel);
      return kSuccess;
    };
    return rm(r.rel);
  }
  stdfs::path h = r.m->layers[0] / to_path(r.rel);
  if (recursive) stdfs::remove_all(h, ec);
  else {
    if (!stdfs::is_empty(h, ec)) return kResultDirectoryNotEmpty;
    stdfs::remove(h, ec);
  }
  return ec ? kResultTargetLocked : kSuccess;
}

uint32_t Fs::rename_file(const std::string& from, const std::string& to) {
  std::lock_guard<std::mutex> g(p_->mu);
  Resolved a, b;
  uint32_t rc = resolve(p_.get(), from, &a);
  if (rc) return rc;
  rc = resolve(p_.get(), to, &b);
  if (rc) return rc;
  if (a.m != b.m) return kResultInvalidArgument;
  if (!a.m->writable) return kResultWriteNotPermitted;
  if (a.kind != 2) return kResultPathNotFound;
  if (b.kind != 0) return kResultPathAlreadyExists;
  std::error_code ec;
  if (a.m->kind == Mount::SaveData) {
    Save& s = *a.m->save;
    stdfs::path src;
    if (!s.ensure_working(a.rel, &src)) return kResultUsableSpaceNotEnough;
    stdfs::path dst = s.working() / to_path(b.rel);
    stdfs::create_directories(dst.parent_path(), ec);
    stdfs::rename(src, dst, ec);
    if (ec) return kResultTargetLocked;
    s.dirty.erase(a.rel);
    if (stdfs::exists(s.committed() / to_path(a.rel), ec)) s.deleted.insert(a.rel);
    s.deleted.erase(b.rel);
    s.dirty.insert(b.rel);
  } else {
    stdfs::rename(a.m->layers[0] / to_path(a.rel), a.m->layers[0] / to_path(b.rel), ec);
    if (ec) return kResultTargetLocked;
  }
  return kSuccess;
}

uint32_t Fs::open_directory(DirId* out, const std::string& path, int mode) {
  std::lock_guard<std::mutex> g(p_->mu);
  Resolved r;
  uint32_t rc = resolve(p_.get(), path, &r);
  if (rc) return rc;
  if (r.kind != 1) return kResultPathNotFound;
  auto od = std::make_shared<OpenDir>();
  std::map<std::string, DirEntry> merged;
  std::error_code ec;
  if (r.m->kind == Mount::SaveData) {
    for (auto& e : r.m->save->list(r.rel)) merged[e.name] = e;
  } else {
    // layered union: the first layer that has the name decides its type and size
    for (auto it = r.m->layers.rbegin(); it != r.m->layers.rend(); ++it) {
      stdfs::path d = *it / to_path(r.rel);
      if (!stdfs::is_directory(d, ec)) continue;
      for (auto& e : stdfs::directory_iterator(d, ec)) {
        DirEntry de;
        de.name = from_path(e.path().filename());
        std::error_code e2;
        de.type = e.is_directory(e2) ? kDirectory : kFile;
        de.size = de.type == kFile ? (int64_t)e.file_size(e2) : 0;
        merged[de.name] = de;
      }
    }
  }
  for (auto& kv : merged) {
    bool is_dir = kv.second.type == kDirectory;
    if ((is_dir && (mode & kOpenDirs)) || (!is_dir && (mode & kOpenFiles))) od->entries.push_back(kv.second);
  }
  uint64_t t = p_->token();
  p_->dirs[t] = od;
  *out = t;
  return kSuccess;
}

uint32_t Fs::read_directory(DirId d, DirEntry* out, int64_t max, int64_t* count) {
  std::lock_guard<std::mutex> g(p_->mu);
  auto it = p_->dirs.find(d);
  if (it == p_->dirs.end()) return kResultInvalidArgument;
  OpenDir& od = *it->second;
  int64_t n = 0;
  while (n < max && od.cursor < od.entries.size()) out[n++] = od.entries[od.cursor++];
  *count = n;
  return kSuccess;
}

uint32_t Fs::get_directory_entry_count(DirId d, int64_t* out) {
  std::lock_guard<std::mutex> g(p_->mu);
  auto it = p_->dirs.find(d);
  if (it == p_->dirs.end()) return kResultInvalidArgument;
  *out = (int64_t)it->second->entries.size();
  return kSuccess;
}

uint32_t Fs::close_directory(DirId d) {
  std::lock_guard<std::mutex> g(p_->mu);
  return p_->dirs.erase(d) ? kSuccess : kResultInvalidArgument;
}

uint32_t Fs::commit(const std::string& mount) {
  std::vector<std::shared_ptr<OpenFile>> to_flush;
  std::unique_lock<std::mutex> g(p_->mu);
  auto m = p_->find_mount(mount);
  if (!m) return kResultNotMounted;
  if (m->kind != Mount::SaveData) return kSuccess;  // nothing to commit on other mounts
  for (auto& kv : p_->files) if (kv.second->mount == mount && kv.second->writable) to_flush.push_back(kv.second);
  for (auto& f : to_flush) f->hf.flush();
  auto hook = p_->hook;
  uint32_t rc = m->save->do_commit(hook);
  if (trace_flags & kTraceFs) log("fs: commit %s -> generation %llu (result %#x)", mount.c_str(), (unsigned long long)m->save->cur, rc);
  return rc;
}

bool Fs::drain_for_exit(int ms) {
#ifdef _WIN32
  const ULONGLONG end = GetTickCount64() + (ULONGLONG)(ms > 0 ? ms : 0);
  while (!p_->mu.try_lock()) {
    if (GetTickCount64() >= end) return false;
    Sleep(5);
  }
  return true;
#else
  (void)ms;
  return true;
#endif
}

uint32_t Fs::get_free_space(int64_t* out, const std::string& mount) {
  std::lock_guard<std::mutex> g(p_->mu);
  auto m = p_->find_mount(mount);
  if (!m) return kResultNotMounted;
  std::error_code ec;
  stdfs::path where = m->kind == Mount::SaveData ? m->save->root : m->layers[0];
  auto sp = stdfs::space(where, ec);
  int64_t avail = ec ? (int64_t)1 << 40 : (int64_t)sp.available;
  // the game extends the save when it sees under 100 MiB free (main 0x609a3c); report at least 4 GiB
  *out = std::clamp<int64_t>(avail, (int64_t)4 << 30, (int64_t)1 << 40);
  return kSuccess;
}

std::vector<SaveGeneration> Fs::list_generations(const std::string& mount) {
  std::lock_guard<std::mutex> g(p_->mu);
  std::vector<SaveGeneration> v;
  auto m = p_->find_mount(mount);
  if (!m || m->kind != Mount::SaveData) return v;
  std::error_code ec;
  for (auto& e : stdfs::directory_iterator(m->save->gens(), ec)) {
    if (e.path().extension() != ".ok") continue;
    uint64_t n = std::strtoull(e.path().stem().string().c_str(), nullptr, 10);
    if (m->save->gen_valid(n)) v.push_back({n, n == m->save->cur});
  }
  std::sort(v.begin(), v.end(), [](auto& a, auto& b) { return a.gen < b.gen; });
  return v;
}

uint32_t Fs::restore_generation(const std::string& mount, uint64_t gen) {
  std::lock_guard<std::mutex> g(p_->mu);
  auto m = p_->find_mount(mount);
  if (!m || m->kind != Mount::SaveData) return kResultNotMounted;
  Save& s = *m->save;
  if (!s.gen_valid(gen)) return kResultPathNotFound;
  // working := a copy of the chosen generation; every file counts as dirty so the commit writes it all
  std::error_code ec;
  stdfs::remove_all(s.working(), ec);
  stdfs::create_directories(s.working(), ec);
  s.dirty.clear(); s.deleted.clear(); s.dirs.clear();
  stdfs::path src = s.gen_dir(gen);
  for (auto& e : stdfs::recursive_directory_iterator(src, ec)) {
    std::string rel = stdfs::relative(e.path(), src, ec).generic_string();
    if (e.is_directory(ec)) { stdfs::create_directories(s.working() / to_path(rel), ec); s.dirs.insert(rel); }
    else {
      stdfs::create_directories((s.working() / to_path(rel)).parent_path(), ec);
      stdfs::copy_file(e.path(), s.working() / to_path(rel), stdfs::copy_options::overwrite_existing, ec);
      s.dirty.insert(rel);
    }
  }
  // files of the current generation that the restored one lacks must disappear
  std::function<void(const stdfs::path&, const std::string&)> walk = [&](const stdfs::path& d, const std::string& rel) {
    for (auto& e : stdfs::directory_iterator(d, ec)) {
      std::string name = from_path(e.path().filename());
      std::string child = rel.empty() ? name : rel + "/" + name;
      if (e.is_directory(ec)) walk(e.path(), child);
      if (!stdfs::exists(src / to_path(child), ec)) s.deleted.insert(child);
    }
  };
  walk(s.committed(), "");
  return s.do_commit(p_->hook);
}

Fs& instance() {
  static Fs fs;
  return fs;
}

}  // namespace hle::fs
```

`runtime/hle/fs_core.h`:

```h
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Host file system behind nn::fs: named mounts over host directories.
//   rom      read-only, an ordered list of directories ("layers"), first match wins (mod loader hook)
//   savedata crash-safe: writes go to a working copy and become visible to the next mount only at commit()
//   host     plain directory (tests, future sdmc)
// No guest types here, so the tests drive it directly. The guest-facing shims are in fs.cpp.
#pragma once
#include <cstdint>
#include <functional>
#include <memory>
#include <mutex>
#include <string>
#include <vector>

#include "hle.h"

namespace hle::fs {

// ---- result codes: module 2 (fs). Evidence for each is in docs/hle-services.md section "nn::fs result codes".
constexpr uint32_t kResultPathNotFound = result(2, 1);            // main 0x602ca0 / 0x602f6c: desc 1 -> game error 0xd
constexpr uint32_t kResultPathAlreadyExists = result(2, 2);       // 0x602f0c cmp 0x402 after CreateFile; desc 2 -> 0xf
constexpr uint32_t kResultTargetLocked = result(2, 7);            // 0x60362c cmp 0xe00 -> game error 0x11
constexpr uint32_t kResultDirectoryNotEmpty = result(2, 8);       // SDK value; not seen in the game
constexpr uint32_t kResultUsableSpaceNotEnough = result(2, 31);   // 0x603614: desc 30..45 -> game error 0x10
constexpr uint32_t kResultOutOfRange = result(2, 3005);           // SDK value for a short strict read
constexpr uint32_t kResultInvalidArgument = result(2, 6001);      // host-chosen (bad handle, bad path syntax)
constexpr uint32_t kResultNotMounted = result(2, 6002);           // host-chosen
constexpr uint32_t kResultWriteNotPermitted = result(2, 6003);    // host-chosen (write to the read-only rom mount)

enum OpenMode : int { kModeRead = 1, kModeWrite = 2, kModeAppend = 4 };
enum EntryType : int { kDirectory = 0, kFile = 1 };               // 0x8bd348: cbz -> OpenDirectory, cmp 1 -> OpenFile
enum DirMode : int { kOpenDirs = 1, kOpenFiles = 2, kOpenAll = 3 };

using FileId = uint64_t;  // opaque, never 0
using DirId = uint64_t;
struct DirEntry { std::string name; int type; int64_t size; };

struct SimulatedCrash { const char* stage; };  // thrown by test fault hooks

struct SaveGeneration { uint64_t gen; bool current; };

class Fs {
 public:
  Fs();
  ~Fs();
  Fs(const Fs&) = delete;
  Fs& operator=(const Fs&) = delete;

  // ---- mounts
  // Mounts `name` over rom_layers() (first match wins). Fails if no layer exists.
  uint32_t mount_rom(const std::string& name);
  uint32_t mount_save(const std::string& name, const uint64_t uid[2]);
  uint32_t mount_host(const std::string& name, const std::string& dir, bool writable);
  uint32_t unmount(const std::string& name);
  bool is_mounted(const std::string& name);
  // The mod-loader hook: ordered directories, earlier ones win. romfs_root goes last.
  void set_rom_layers(std::vector<std::string> dirs);
  std::vector<std::string> rom_layers() const;
  void set_save_root(const std::string& dir);
  void set_save_backups(int n);

  // ---- files and directories (paths look like "rom:/common/x.drp")
  uint32_t create_file(const std::string& path, int64_t size);
  uint32_t delete_file(const std::string& path);
  uint32_t open_file(FileId* out, const std::string& path, int mode);
  uint32_t close_file(FileId f);
  // out == nullptr: strict form (ReadFile(handle, off, buf, size)): reading past the end fails with kResultOutOfRange.
  // out != nullptr: reads what exists and stores the count.
  uint32_t read_file(FileId f, int64_t off, void* buf, size_t n, size_t* out);
  uint32_t write_file(FileId f, int64_t off, const void* buf, size_t n, bool flush);
  uint32_t flush_file(FileId f);
  uint32_t get_file_size(FileId f, int64_t* out);
  uint32_t set_file_size(FileId f, int64_t size);
  uint32_t get_entry_type(int* out, const std::string& path);
  uint32_t create_directory(const std::string& path);
  uint32_t delete_directory(const std::string& path, bool recursive);
  uint32_t rename_file(const std::string& from, const std::string& to);
  uint32_t open_directory(DirId* out, const std::string& path, int mode);
  uint32_t read_directory(DirId d, DirEntry* out, int64_t max, int64_t* count);  // advances the cursor
  uint32_t get_directory_entry_count(DirId d, int64_t* out);                       // all entries, not the remainder
  uint32_t close_directory(DirId d);

  // ---- save data
  // Makes every change since the last commit durable and visible to the next mount, atomically: the new state is
  // built as a complete generation directory, then a one-line pointer file is replaced by write-temp + rename.
  uint32_t commit(const std::string& mount);
  // Exit path: waits up to `ms` for a commit in progress, then keeps the table lock for good so no new commit can start. True when the
  // lock was taken (a commit that was running has finished); false on timeout. Never returns the lock: call only right before exiting.
  bool drain_for_exit(int ms);
  uint32_t get_free_space(int64_t* out, const std::string& mount);
  std::vector<SaveGeneration> list_generations(const std::string& mount);
  // Makes generation `gen` the current one by committing a copy of it as a new generation.
  uint32_t restore_generation(const std::string& mount, uint64_t gen);

  // Test hook: called at named stages of commit; may throw SimulatedCrash.
  void set_fault_hook(std::function<void(const char* stage)> hook);

 struct Impl;  // implementation detail

 private:
  std::unique_ptr<Impl> p_;
};

Fs& instance();  // the process-wide instance the guest shims use

// "rom:/a/b" -> mount "rom", rel "a/b" (normalized, no leading slash). false on a malformed path.
bool split_path(const std::string& path, std::string* mount, std::string* rel);

}  // namespace hle::fs
```

`runtime/hle/gen_hle_stubs.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
"""Builds analysis/runtime/hle_coverage.tsv and generated/hle_unimplemented.cpp.

Input : analysis/runtime/imports_usage.tsv (the 731 imports of `main`), and the HLE_IMPL / HLE_NOOP registration lines
        in runtime/hle/*.cpp and *.inc.
Output: hle_coverage.tsv        one row per import (status: implemented, lifted-pure-software, stub-noop, todo)
                                plus rows for overrides of sdk-internal symbols that are not `main` imports
        generated/hle_unimplemented.cpp   one logging "not implemented" stub per leftover nn:: import this layer owns
                                (an nn:: import with no override logs name, caller and arguments, then aborts)
Run:    python gen_hle_stubs.py [--all]   (--all also stubs the os / audio / nvn imports owned by other layers)
Never edit the outputs by hand.
"""
import glob
import os
import re
import sys

ROOT = os.path.normpath(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), '..', '..'))
HLE = os.path.join(ROOT, 'runtime', 'hle')

# service (imports_usage column 3) -> (status, owner, note) for imports that have no HLE registration
LIFTED = {
    'libc': 'sdk libc is lifted guest code; linker/DSO symbols are host data (loader)',
    'libc++': 'sdk libc++ is lifted guest code',
    'libc++abi': 'sdk libc++abi is lifted guest code',
    'util': 'nn::util: pure software, no IPC',
    'fontll': 'nn::fontll: pure software, no IPC',
    'image': 'nn::image JPEG: pure software, no IPC',
    'mem': 'nn::mem: pure software, no IPC',
    'result': 'nn::result: pure software',
    'swkbd': 'swkbd argument builders: pure software (ShowKeyboard is overridden)',
    'crypto': 'nn::crypto AES/MD5/SHA1: pure software (random bytes is overridden)',
    'vdk': 'weak data symbol: resolves to null',
    'other': 'weak symbol: resolves to null',
}
# data objects the sdk defines itself (STT_OBJECT in v262144-sdk.elf .dynsym): lifted with the sdk, not functions to stub
LIFTED_DATA = {'_ZN2nn3hid13VibrationNode30DefaultVibrationSampleIntervalE': 'sdk-defined constant (STT_OBJECT)'}
OTHER_OWNER = {'os': 'runtime/os', 'audio': 'runtime/audio', 'nvn': 'runtime/nvn'}


def registrations():
    reg = {}
    pat = re.compile(r'HLE_(IMPL|NOOP)\("(\w+)",\s*"([^"]+)",\s*(\w+)\)')
    files = sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(HLE, '*.cpp')) + glob.glob(os.path.join(HLE, '*.inc')))
    for f in files:
        for m in pat.finditer(open(f, encoding='utf8').read()):
            kind, svc, sym, fn = m.groups()
            reg[sym] = ('implemented' if kind == 'IMPL' else 'stub-noop', svc, os.path.basename(f), fn)
    return reg


def imports():
    rows = []
    for l in open(os.path.join(ROOT, 'analysis', 'runtime', 'imports_usage.tsv'), encoding='utf8'):
        if l.startswith('#') or l.startswith('name\t'):
            continue
        p = l.rstrip('\n').split('\t')
        rows.append(dict(name=p[0], dem=p[1], svc=p[2], boot1=p[10], order=p[11], boot2=p[15]))
    return rows


def main():
    reg = registrations()
    imps = imports()
    names = {r['name'] for r in imps}
    out = []
    stubs = []
    counts = {}
    for r in imps:
        n = r['name']
        if n in reg:
            st, svc, src, fn = reg[n]
            owner, note = 'runtime/hle', '%s:%s' % (src, fn)
        elif n in LIFTED_DATA:
            st, owner, note = 'lifted-pure-software', 'lifted', LIFTED_DATA[n]
        elif r['svc'] in LIFTED:
            st, owner, note = 'lifted-pure-software', 'lifted', LIFTED[r['svc']]
        elif r['svc'] in OTHER_OWNER:
            st, owner, note = 'todo', OTHER_OWNER[r['svc']], 'owned by another layer'
        else:
            st, owner, note = 'todo', 'runtime/hle', 'no override: generated stub logs and aborts'
        counts[st] = counts.get(st, 0) + 1
        boot = 'yes' if r['boot1'] == 'yes' else ('maybe' if r['boot2'] == 'yes' else 'no')
        out.append((st, r['svc'], owner, boot, r['order'], n, r['dem'], note))
        if st == 'todo' and (owner == 'runtime/hle' or '--all' in sys.argv):
            stubs.append(n)
    extra = 0
    for sym, (st, svc, src, fn) in sorted(reg.items()):
        if sym not in names:
            out.append((st, svc, 'runtime/hle', 'n/a', '', sym, sym, 'not a main import (sdk-internal or alias): %s:%s' % (src, fn)))
            extra += 1
    out.sort(key=lambda t: (['implemented', 'stub-noop', 'todo', 'lifted-pure-software'].index(t[0]), t[1], t[5]))
    p = os.path.join(ROOT, 'analysis', 'runtime', 'hle_coverage.tsv')
    with open(p, 'w', encoding='utf8', newline='\n') as f:
        f.write('# file: hle_coverage.tsv\n')
        f.write('# generated by runtime/hle/gen_hle_stubs.py from imports_usage.tsv and the HLE_IMPL/HLE_NOOP registrations; do not edit\n')
        f.write('# one row per import of main (731) plus %d override rows for symbols that are not main imports (boot = n/a)\n' % extra)
        f.write('# status: implemented | lifted-pure-software | stub-noop | todo. todo with owner runtime/os, runtime/audio, runtime/nvn belongs to that layer\n')
        f.write('# boot: yes = reachable from the boot entry points over direct calls (imports_usage boot1), maybe = only via address-taken functions (boot2)\n')
        f.write('status\tservice\towner\tboot\tboot_order\tname\tdemangled\tnote\n')
        for t in out:
            f.write('\t'.join(t) + '\n')
    print(p, counts, 'extra override rows:', extra)

    os.makedirs(os.path.join(ROOT, 'generated'), exist_ok=True)
    gp = os.path.join(ROOT, 'generated', 'hle_unimplemented.cpp')
    with open(gp, 'w', encoding='utf8', newline='\n') as f:
        f.write('// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT\n// Generated by runtime/hle/gen_hle_stubs.py; do not edit. One stub per nn:: import without an override.\n')
        f.write('#include "../runtime/hle/hle.h"\n\nnamespace {\n')
        for i, n in enumerate(stubs):
            f.write('void stub_%d(Cpu* c) { hle::unimplemented(c, "%s"); }\n' % (i, n))
        f.write('const hle::StubEntry kStubs[] = {\n')
        for i, n in enumerate(stubs):
            f.write('  {"%s", stub_%d},\n' % (n, i))
        f.write('  {nullptr, nullptr}};\n')
        f.write('struct Install { Install() { hle::set_generated_stubs(kStubs, sizeof kStubs / sizeof kStubs[0] - 1); } } g_install;\n}  // namespace\n')
    print(gp, len(stubs), 'stubs')


main()
```

`runtime/hle/hid.cpp`:

```cpp
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// nn::hid host overrides. Layouts are the public nn::hid ones, checked against how `main` uses them:
//   SetSupportedNpadIdType list ends with id 0x20 (Handheld) after No1 (0x9258f4 / 0x925944), then
//   SetSupportedNpadStyleSet(3) = FullKey | Handheld (0x925948); touch is initialized if a flag is clear (0x92595c).
//   Six-axis: handle is one 32-bit word stored next to the npad id (0x4c1514-0x4c152c, 0x7fffffff = none);
//   GetSixAxisSensorStates(buf, 16, handle) with a 0x60-byte state stride (0x4c15ec) and angular velocity at +0x1c.
// All four GetNpadState variants write a 0x28-byte state: {s64 samplingNumber; u64 buttons; s32 lx, ly, rx, ry; u32 attributes}.
#include <algorithm>
#include <cmath>
#include <cstring>

#include "hle.h"
#include "hle_config.h"
#include "input_core.h"

namespace hle {
namespace {

enum : uint32_t { kStyleFullKey = 1, kStyleHandheld = 2, kStyleJoyDual = 4, kStyleJoyLeft = 8, kStyleJoyRight = 16 };
enum : uint32_t { kNpadNo1 = 0, kNpadHandheld = 0x20 };
enum : uint32_t { kAttrConnected = 1, kAttrHandheldAll = 0x3f };
constexpr size_t kNpadStateSize = 0x28;

struct HidState {
  uint32_t supported_styles = 0x1f;
  bool inited = false;
  bool six_axis_started = false;
};
HidState g_hid;

uint32_t active_id() { return config().controller_style == 1 ? kNpadHandheld : kNpadNo1; }
uint32_t active_style() { return config().controller_style == 1 ? kStyleHandheld : kStyleFullKey; }

void ensure_init() {
  if (g_hid.inited) return;
  g_hid.inited = true;
  // input.json (version 2); the version 1 input_map.json is migrated once. An invalid file falls back to the defaults and
  // leaves a message for the controls menu (Hub::message).
  const std::string legacy = config().input_map_path == default_input_path() ? legacy_input_path() : std::string();
  input::hub().load_config(config().input_map_path, legacy);
}

void write_npad_state(void* dst, uint32_t id, uint32_t style) {
  std::memset(dst, 0, kNpadStateSize);
  ensure_init();
  input::hub().poll();
  bool match = id == active_id() && style == active_style() && (g_hid.supported_styles & style);
  store<int64_t>(dst, input::hub().sampling_number());
  if (trace_flags & kTraceHid) {   // log each distinct (id, style, match, buttons) once in a row
    static uint64_t last = ~0ull; static int calls = 0; if (++calls % 600 == 0) log("hid: GetNpadState calls=%d buttons=%#llx", calls, (unsigned long long)input::hub().pad().buttons);
    uint64_t cur = match ? input::hub().pad().buttons : 0xffffffffull;
    uint64_t key = (uint64_t)id << 56 ^ (uint64_t)style << 40 ^ cur;
    static int32_t last_rx = 0, last_ry = 0;
    const int32_t rx = match ? input::hub().pad().rx : 0, ry = match ? input::hub().pad().ry : 0;
    if (key != last || rx != last_rx || ry != last_ry) { last = key; last_rx = rx; last_ry = ry; log("hid: GetNpadState id %u style %#x match=%d buttons=%#llx rx=%d ry=%d", id, style, (int)match, (unsigned long long)cur, rx, ry); }
  }
  if (!match) return;
  input::PadSample p = input::hub().pad();
  uint8_t* b = static_cast<uint8_t*>(dst);
  store<uint64_t>(b + 8, p.buttons);
  store<int32_t>(b + 0x10, p.lx); store<int32_t>(b + 0x14, p.ly);
  store<int32_t>(b + 0x18, p.rx); store<int32_t>(b + 0x1c, p.ry);
  store<uint32_t>(b + 0x20, p.connected ? (style == kStyleHandheld ? kAttrHandheldAll : kAttrConnected) : 0u);
}

// ---- initialization and styles
void hid_initialize_npad(Cpu*) { ensure_init(); }
void hid_set_supported_npad_id_type(Cpu* c) {  // (const NpadIdType* ids, size_t n)
  if (trace_flags & kTraceHid) {
    const uint32_t* ids = ptr<const uint32_t>(arg(c, 0));
    for (uint64_t i = 0; i < arg(c, 1); ++i) log("hid: supported npad id %#x", ids[i]);
  }
}
void hid_set_supported_npad_style_set(Cpu* c) { g_hid.supported_styles = arg32(c, 0); }
void hid_get_npad_style_set(Cpu* c) {  // NpadStyleSet GetNpadStyleSet(const NpadIdType&)
  uint32_t id = load<uint32_t>(ptr<void>(arg(c, 0)));
  ret(c, id == active_id() ? (active_style() & g_hid.supported_styles) : 0u);
}
void hid_disconnect_npad(Cpu*) {}
void hid_get_npad_joy_assignment(Cpu* c) { ret(c, 0); }  // Dual
void hid_set_npad_joy_hold_type(Cpu*) {}
void hid_noop(Cpu*) {}

void hid_get_npad_state_fullkey(Cpu* c) { write_npad_state(ptr<void>(arg(c, 0)), load<uint32_t>(ptr<void>(arg(c, 1))), kStyleFullKey); }
void hid_get_npad_state_handheld(Cpu* c) { write_npad_state(ptr<void>(arg(c, 0)), load<uint32_t>(ptr<void>(arg(c, 1))), kStyleHandheld); }
void hid_get_npad_state_joyleft(Cpu* c) { write_npad_state(ptr<void>(arg(c, 0)), load<uint32_t>(ptr<void>(arg(c, 1))), kStyleJoyLeft); }
void hid_get_npad_state_joyright(Cpu* c) { write_npad_state(ptr<void>(arg(c, 0)), load<uint32_t>(ptr<void>(arg(c, 1))), kStyleJoyRight); }

// ---- touch screen: the left mouse button is one finger on the 1280x720 panel
// TouchScreenState<6>: {s64 samplingNumber; s32 count; s32 pad; TouchState touches[6]}; TouchState (0x28 bytes):
// {s64 deltaTime; u32 attributes; s32 fingerId; s32 x, y, diameterX, diameterY, rotationAngle; s32 reserved}
void hid_get_touch_screen_state6(Cpu* c) {
  uint8_t* st = ptr<uint8_t>(arg(c, 0));
  std::memset(st, 0, 8 + 8 + 6 * 0x28);
  ensure_init();
  input::hub().poll();
  input::TouchSample t = input::hub().touch();
  store<int64_t>(st, input::hub().sampling_number());
  store<int32_t>(st + 8, t.count);
  if (t.count) {
    uint8_t* p = st + 16;
    store<uint32_t>(p + 8, 1);   // attributes: start of touch
    store<int32_t>(p + 12, 0);   // finger id
    store<int32_t>(p + 16, t.pt[0].x);
    store<int32_t>(p + 20, t.pt[0].y);
    store<int32_t>(p + 24, 8);   // diameter
    store<int32_t>(p + 28, 8);
  }
}
void hid_get_gesture_states(Cpu* c) { ret(c, 0); }  // int GetGestureStates(GestureState*, int): no gestures

// ---- six-axis motion: a resting sensor (no gyro source on PC yet)
constexpr size_t kSixAxisStateSize = 0x60;
void hid_get_six_axis_handles(Cpu* c) {  // int GetSixAxisSensorHandles(SixAxisSensorHandle* out, int n, const NpadIdType&, NpadStyleSet)
  uint32_t* out = ptr<uint32_t>(arg(c, 0));
  int n = (int)arg32(c, 1);
  uint32_t id = load<uint32_t>(ptr<void>(arg(c, 2)));
  uint32_t style = arg32(c, 3);
  int have = 0;
  if (id == active_id() && (style & active_style())) have = 1;
  else if ((style & kStyleJoyDual) && id == active_id()) have = 2;
  have = std::min(have, n);
  if (trace_flags & kTraceHid) log("hid: GetSixAxisSensorHandles id %u style %#x -> %d", id, style, have);
  for (int i = 0; i < have; ++i) out[i] = ((id & 0xffff) << 8) | (uint32_t)(i + 1);  // nonzero, never 0x7fffffff
  ret(c, (uint64_t)have);
}
void hid_start_six_axis(Cpu*) { g_hid.six_axis_started = true; if (trace_flags & kTraceHid) log("hid: StartSixAxisSensor"); }
void hid_stop_six_axis(Cpu*) { g_hid.six_axis_started = false; }
// With a real or fake gyro (input::RawInput::gyro_present and gyro aim on) the state carries its angular rate; the game never calls these
// today (verified with SNAP_TRACE hid), so this path is untested against the game itself.
bool gyro_live(float* yaw_dps, float* pitch_dps, float* roll_dps) {
  input::RawInput r = input::hub().raw();
  if (!r.gyro_present || !input::gyro_aim_enabled()) return false;
  *yaw_dps = r.gyro_y; *pitch_dps = r.gyro_x; *roll_dps = r.gyro_z;
  return true;
}
void hid_is_six_axis_at_rest(Cpu* c) { float a, b, d; ret(c, gyro_live(&a, &b, &d) && (a * a + b * b + d * d) > 4.0f ? 0 : 1); }  // bool: the game skips gyro aiming while true
void hid_get_six_axis_states(Cpu* c) {  // int GetSixAxisSensorStates(SixAxisSensorState* out, int n, const SixAxisSensorHandle&)
  int n = (int)arg32(c, 1);
  if (trace_flags & kTraceHid) { static int calls = 0; if (calls++ < 20) log("hid: GetSixAxisSensorStates n=%d", n); }
  if (n < 1) { ret(c, 0); return; }
  uint8_t* st = ptr<uint8_t>(arg(c, 0));
  std::memset(st, 0, kSixAxisStateSize);
  int64_t seq = input::hub().sampling_number();
  store<int64_t>(st + 0, 16666666);            // deltaTime ns
  store<int64_t>(st + 8, seq);                 // samplingNumber
  store<float>(st + 0x18, -1.0f);              // acceleration z (face up, at rest)
  float yaw, pitch, roll;
  if (gyro_live(&yaw, &pitch, &roll)) {   // nn::hid angular velocity: 1.0 = one turn per second; x = pitch, y = yaw, z = roll
    store<float>(st + 0x1c, pitch / 360.0f); store<float>(st + 0x20, yaw / 360.0f); store<float>(st + 0x24, roll / 360.0f);
  }
  store<float>(st + 0x34, 1.0f);               // direction matrix = identity
  store<float>(st + 0x44, 1.0f);
  store<float>(st + 0x54, 1.0f);
  ret(c, 1);
}

// ---- vibration: forwards to the backend rumble motors
void hid_get_vibration_handles(Cpu* c) {  // int GetVibrationDeviceHandles(VibrationDeviceHandle* out, int n, const NpadIdType&, NpadStyleSet)
  uint32_t* out = ptr<uint32_t>(arg(c, 0));
  int n = (int)arg32(c, 1);
  uint32_t id = load<uint32_t>(ptr<void>(arg(c, 2)));
  uint32_t style = arg32(c, 3);
  int have = (id == active_id() && (style & active_style())) ? 2 : 0;  // left and right actuators
  have = std::min(have, n);
  if (input::rumble_log_enabled()) log("rumble: GetVibrationDeviceHandles id %u style %#x n=%d -> %d from main+%#llx", id, style, n, have, (unsigned long long)(c->x[30] - 0x7100000000ull));
  for (int i = 0; i < have; ++i) out[i] = ((id & 0xffff) << 8) | (uint32_t)(i + 1);
  ret(c, (uint64_t)have);
}
void hid_send_vibration_value(Cpu* c) {  // (const VibrationDeviceHandle&, const VibrationValue&): {f32 ampLow, freqLow, ampHigh, freqHigh}
  const float* v = ptr<const float>(arg(c, 1));
  if (trace_flags & kTraceHid) log("hid: SendVibrationValue");
  if (input::rumble_log_enabled()) log("rumble: SendVibrationValue handle=%#x ampLow=%.3f freqLow=%.1f ampHigh=%.3f freqHigh=%.1f from main+%#llx", load<uint32_t>(ptr<void>(arg(c, 0))), v[0], v[1], v[2], v[3], (unsigned long long)(c->x[30] - 0x7100000000ull));
  // Two actuators (handle low byte 1 = left, 2 = right) feed one pad: remember each one's amplitudes and send the stronger of
  // the two per motor, so a left-then-right call pair per frame does not flip the motors between two values. NaN counts as 0.
  const auto amp = [](float a) { return std::isfinite(a) ? std::clamp(a, 0.0f, 1.0f) : 0.0f; };
  static float s_low[2] = {0, 0}, s_high[2] = {0, 0};
  const uint32_t h = load<uint32_t>(ptr<void>(arg(c, 0)));
  const int idx = ((h & 0xff) == 2) ? 1 : 0;
  s_low[idx] = amp(v[0]); s_high[idx] = amp(v[2]);
  input::hub().rumble(std::max(s_low[0], s_low[1]), std::max(s_high[0], s_high[1]));
  input::script_event("vibration");   // first call: the lab cutscene hands over the camera (scripted-input anchor, host/skip_intro.txt)
}

// ---- controller applet: one player, the active npad
void hid_show_controller_support(Cpu* c) {  // Result ShowControllerSupport(ControllerSupportResultInfo*, const ControllerSupportArg&)
  uint8_t* r = ptr<uint8_t>(arg(c, 0));
  if (r) { store<int32_t>(r, 1); store<uint32_t>(r + 4, active_id()); }
  ret(c, kSuccess);
}

}  // namespace
```

`runtime/hle/hle.h`:

```h
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Horizon service HLE for the Snap recompilation (runtime/hle). Host overrides are plain GuestFn functions keyed by
// the mangled symbol, following the TotK HOST_OVERRIDE convention (tools/ref/totk/runtime/host.h, MIT): the loader
// binds each Entry by symbol name over every GOT/GLOB_DAT/ABS64 of `main` and `sdk`.
//
// Guest pointers are host pointers (AGENTS.md "CPU and runtime"), so an override reads its arguments straight from the
// AAPCS64 registers in Cpu and dereferences them. Nothing here depends on the lifted game: tests call the overrides
// with a hand-built Cpu.
#pragma once
#include <cstdarg>
#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <cstring>
#include <string>
#include <vector>

#include "../cpu.h"

namespace hle {

// ---- nn::Result: module in bits 0-8, description in bits 9-21 (evidence: main 0x602c90 masks 0x1ff / 0x3ffe00)
constexpr uint32_t result(uint32_t module, uint32_t desc) { return module | (desc << 9); }
constexpr uint32_t result_module(uint32_t r) { return r & 0x1ff; }
constexpr uint32_t result_desc(uint32_t r) { return (r >> 9) & 0x1fff; }
constexpr uint32_t kSuccess = 0;

// ---- logging: "[hle] ..." on stderr, plus an optional sink (tests, the host log)
void log(const char* fmt, ...) __attribute__((format(printf, 1, 2)));
using LogSink = void (*)(const char* line, size_t n);
void set_log_sink(LogSink sink);
// bit 0 fs, 1 hid, 2 other services; env SNAP_HLE_TRACE=fs,hid,svc or all
enum : unsigned { kTraceFs = 1, kTraceHid = 2, kTraceSvc = 4, kTraceOpen = 8 };   // kTraceOpen: SNAP_HLE_TRACE=open logs fs opens only (load-phase markers)
extern unsigned trace_flags;
void init_trace_from_env();

// ---- AAPCS64 argument access
inline uint64_t arg(const Cpu* c, int i) { return c->x[i]; }
inline uint32_t arg32(const Cpu* c, int i) { return (uint32_t)c->x[i]; }
inline void ret(Cpu* c, uint64_t v) { c->x[0] = v; }
template <class T> inline T* ptr(uint64_t a) { return reinterpret_cast<T*>(static_cast<uintptr_t>(a)); }
template <class T> inline T load(const void* p) { T v; std::memcpy(&v, p, sizeof v); return v; }
template <class T> inline void store(void* p, T v) { std::memcpy(p, &v, sizeof v); }

// ---- registry
struct Entry {
  const char* symbol;   // mangled name (or C name) of the guest function this replaces
  GuestFn fn;
  const char* service;  // fs, hid, oe, ...
  const char* status;   // "implemented" or "stub-noop"
};
// Each service file defines one `void register_<svc>(std::vector<Entry>& out)` using these two macros. The
// coverage generator (runtime/hle/gen_hle_stubs.py) parses them, so keep one registration per line.
#define HLE_IMPL(svc, sym, fn) out.push_back(::hle::Entry{sym, fn, svc, "implemented"})
#define HLE_NOOP(svc, sym, fn) out.push_back(::hle::Entry{sym, fn, svc, "stub-noop"})

void register_fs(std::vector<Entry>& out);
void register_hid(std::vector<Entry>& out);
void register_sys(std::vector<Entry>& out);   // oe, pctl, settings, time, account, err, diag, album, friends, ngc, swkbd, vi, nv, crypto, codec
void register_net(std::vector<Entry>& out);   // nifm, nsd, prepo, socket, ssl

const std::vector<Entry>& overrides();         // every override, built once
GuestFn find_override(const char* symbol);     // nullptr if none
// Calls bind(symbol, fn, user) for every override and for every generated "not implemented" stub
// (gen_hle_stubs.py output, optional). The loader passes a hostfn_add_override-style binder (PROPOSED_SHARED_CHANGES.md).
using BindFn = void (*)(const char* symbol, GuestFn fn, void* user);
void bind_all(BindFn bind, void* user);

// Logs the function name, caller (x30) and x0-x7, then aborts. Used by the generated stubs.
// Test hook: when `unimplemented_hook` is set, unimplemented() calls it, sets x0 = 0 and returns instead of aborting.
void unimplemented(Cpu* c, const char* symbol);
extern void (*unimplemented_hook)(const char* symbol);
// Fatal guest errors (nn::diag abort): logs, then aborts unless `fatal_hook` is set (tests).
void fatal(const std::string& message);
extern void (*fatal_hook)(const char* message);

// nn::err and friends show errors through this; the default logs and, unless Config::headless, opens a message box.
using ErrorUiFn = void (*)(const char* title, const char* message);
void set_error_ui(ErrorUiFn fn);
const std::string& last_error_message();

// nn::vi: the opaque native-window handle the guest passes to the NVN window builder (runtime/nvn may use it as a
// token), and the 60 Hz vsync event feeder.
void* vi_native_window();
void vi_stop_vsync();

// gen_hle_stubs.py writes generated/hle_unimplemented.cpp (ignored dir): one logging stub per import without an
// override, registered from a static initializer through set_generated_stubs. Linking it in is optional.
struct StubEntry { const char* symbol; GuestFn fn; };
void set_generated_stubs(const StubEntry* stubs, size_t n);

// ---- services the os worker provides (runtime/os); optional until wired up, see PROPOSED_SHARED_CHANGES.md
struct OsHooks {
  // Initialize a guest nn::os::SystemEventType in place (auto-clear) so it can be signaled from any host thread.
  void (*init_system_event)(void* system_event_type, bool manual_clear) = nullptr;
  void (*signal_system_event)(void* system_event_type) = nullptr;
};
OsHooks& os_hooks();

// ---- small helpers
std::string utf16_to_utf8(const char16_t* s, size_t max = 4096);
std::string hex_u64(uint64_t v);
uint64_t now_unix_seconds();

}  // namespace hle
```

`runtime/hle/hle_config.cpp`:

```cpp
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
#include "hle_config.h"

#include <cstdio>
#include <filesystem>
#include <cstdlib>
#include <fstream>
#include <sstream>

#include "hle.h"
#include "json_lite.h"
#include "profiles.h"
#include "settings.h"
#ifdef _WIN32
#define WIN32_LEAN_AND_MEAN
#define NOMINMAX
#include <windows.h>
#include <knownfolders.h>
#include <shlobj.h>
#endif

namespace hle {

static bool g_save_explicit = false;

static Config g_cfg;
static bool g_cfg_init = false;

static std::string join(const std::string& a, const char* b) {
#ifdef _WIN32
  return a + "\\" + b;
#else
  return a + "/" + b;
#endif
}

#ifdef _WIN32
// %APPDATA% as UTF-8. getenv returns the ANSI code page, which the u8path users (fs_core, settings, profiles) would misread for a
// non-ASCII user name; _wgetenv (or the known-folder API when the variable is missing) is exact.
std::string appdata_utf8() {
  std::wstring w;
  if (const wchar_t* e = _wgetenv(L"APPDATA"); e && *e) w = e;
  else {
    PWSTR p = nullptr;
    if (SUCCEEDED(SHGetKnownFolderPath(FOLDERID_RoamingAppData, 0, nullptr, &p)) && p) w = p;
    if (p) CoTaskMemFree(p);
  }
  if (w.empty()) return ".";
  int n = WideCharToMultiByte(CP_UTF8, 0, w.data(), (int)w.size(), nullptr, 0, nullptr, nullptr);
  std::string s((size_t)(n > 0 ? n : 0), '\0');
  if (n > 0) WideCharToMultiByte(CP_UTF8, 0, w.data(), (int)w.size(), s.data(), n, nullptr, nullptr);
  return s;
}
#endif

std::string default_data_root() {
#ifdef _WIN32
  return appdata_utf8() + "\\SnapRecomp";
#else
  const char* h = std::getenv("HOME");
  return std::string(h ? h : ".") + "/.local/share/SnapRecomp";
#endif
}

std::string default_input_path() {
  const char* d = std::getenv("SNAP_CONFIG_DIR");
  if (d && *d) return join(d, "input.json");
  return join(g_cfg.data_root.empty() ? default_data_root() : g_cfg.data_root, "input.json");
}
std::string legacy_input_path() { return join(join(g_cfg.data_root.empty() ? default_data_root() : g_cfg.data_root, "config"), "input_map.json"); }

std::string uid_dir_name(const uint64_t uid[2]) {
  char b[40];
  std::snprintf(b, sizeof b, "%016llx%016llx", (unsigned long long)uid[0], (unsigned long long)uid[1]);
  return b;
}

void apply_defaults() {
  Config& c = g_cfg;
  if (c.data_root.empty()) c.data_root = default_data_root();
  if (c.save_root.empty()) c.save_root = join(c.data_root, "save");
  if (c.input_map_path.empty()) c.input_map_path = default_input_path();
  if (c.screenshot_dir.empty()) c.screenshot_dir = join(c.data_root, "screenshots");
  g_cfg_init = true;
}

Config& config() {
  if (!g_cfg_init) apply_defaults();
  return g_cfg;
}

static bool parse_uid(const std::string& s, uint64_t out[2]) {
  if (s.size() != 32) return false;
  for (char ch : s) if (!std::isxdigit((unsigned char)ch)) return false;
  out[0] = std::strtoull(s.substr(0, 16).c_str(), nullptr, 16);
  out[1] = std::strtoull(s.substr(16).c_str(), nullptr, 16);
  return true;
}

bool load_config(const std::string& path_in) {
  Config& c = g_cfg;
  c = Config();
  std::string path = path_in;
  if (path.empty()) {
    const char* e = std::getenv("SNAP_HLE_CONFIG");
    if (e && *e) path = e;
    else path = join(join(default_data_root(), "config"), "hle.json");
  }
  bool ok = true;
  std::ifstream f(std::filesystem::u8path(path), std::ios::binary);
  if (f) {
    std::stringstream ss;
    ss << f.rdbuf();
    Json j;
    std::string err;
    if (!json_parse(ss.str(), j, err) || j.type != Json::Obj) {
      log("config %s: invalid JSON (%s); using defaults", path.c_str(), err.c_str());
      ok = false;
    } else {
      if (auto* v = j.get("romfs_root")) c.romfs_root = v->str(c.romfs_root);
      if (auto* v = j.get("rom_layers")) for (auto& e : v->a) if (e.type == Json::Str) c.rom_layers.push_back(e.s);
      if (auto* v = j.get("data_root")) c.data_root = v->str();
      if (auto* v = j.get("save_root")) c.save_root = v->str();
      if (auto* v = j.get("save_backups")) c.save_backups = (int)v->num(c.save_backups);
      if (auto* v = j.get("save_data_size")) c.save_data_size = (int64_t)v->num((double)c.save_data_size);
      if (auto* v = j.get("save_journal_size")) c.save_journal_size = (int64_t)v->num((double)c.save_journal_size);
      if (auto* v = j.get("user_name")) c.user_name = v->str(c.user_name);
      if (auto* v = j.get("uid")) {
        if (!parse_uid(v->str(), c.uid)) log("config: \"uid\" must be 32 hex digits; keeping the default");
      }
      if (auto* v = j.get("language")) c.language = (int)v->num(c.language);
      if (auto* v = j.get("region")) c.region = v->str(c.region);
      if (auto* v = j.get("docked")) c.docked = v->boolean(c.docked);
      if (auto* v = j.get("display_version")) c.display_version = v->str(c.display_version);
      if (auto* v = j.get("player_name")) { if (!v->str().empty()) c.player_name = v->str(); }
      if (auto* v = j.get("headless")) c.headless = v->boolean(c.headless);
      if (auto* v = j.get("input_map")) c.input_map_path = v->str();
      if (auto* v = j.get("screenshot_dir")) c.screenshot_dir = v->str();
      if (auto* v = j.get("controller_style")) {
        c.controller_style = (v->type == Json::Str && v->s == "handheld") ? 1 : (int)v->num(0);
      }
    }
  }
  if (const char* e = std::getenv("SNAP_ROMFS")) if (*e) c.romfs_root = e;
  if (const char* e = std::getenv("SNAP_SAVE_ROOT")) if (*e) c.save_root = e;
  if (const char* e = std::getenv("SNAP_PLAYER_NAME")) if (*e) c.player_name = e;
  if (const char* e = std::getenv("SNAP_SAVE_DIR")) if (*e) c.save_root = e;   // wins over SNAP_SAVE_ROOT; default %APPDATA%\SnapRecomp\save
  if (const char* e = std::getenv("SNAP_HLE_HEADLESS")) if (*e && *e != '0') c.headless = true;
  g_save_explicit = !c.save_root.empty();
  g_cfg_init = false;
  apply_defaults();
  return ok;
}

// Picker window (runtime/ui/ui_picker.cpp); the stub keeps builds without it (unit tests) linking.
extern "C" int snap_ui_pick_profile(const profiles::PickItem* items, int count);
extern "C" int snap_ui_pick_profile_none(const profiles::PickItem*, int) { return -1; }
#pragma comment(linker, "/alternatename:snap_ui_pick_profile=snap_ui_pick_profile_none")

void activate_profiles() {
  Config& c = config();
  const char* pd = std::getenv("SNAP_PROFILES_DIR");
  bool has_pd = pd && *pd;
  if (g_save_explicit && !has_pd) return;   // SNAP_SAVE_DIR / save_root override everything (test runs)
  std::string root = has_pd ? std::string(pd) : join(c.data_root, "profiles");
  std::string legacy = has_pd ? std::string() : join(c.data_root, "save");
  if (const char* e = std::getenv("SNAP_LEGACY_SAVE_DIR")) legacy = e;
  const char* want = std::getenv("SNAP_PROFILE");
  const char* pk = std::getenv("SNAP_PROFILE_PICKER");
  bool no_picker = c.headless || (pk && *pk == '0');
  bool force = (pk && *pk == '1');
#ifdef _WIN32
  if (GetAsyncKeyState(VK_SHIFT) & 0x8000) force = true;   // hold Shift while starting to pick a profile even with only one
#endif
  profiles::Active a = profiles::startup(root, legacy, want ? want : "", no_picker ? nullptr : snap_ui_pick_profile, force);
  if (!a.save_dir.empty()) c.save_root = a.save_dir;
  profiles::set_active(a);
  log("profiles: %s%s%s -> %s", a.on ? "profile " : "profiles off", a.on ? a.name.c_str() : "", a.note.empty() ? "" : " (note)", c.save_root.c_str());
  settings::load();   // this profile's settings.cfg: live controller options, and env vars for the look / SSAO mods (read later, at their first use)
}

}  // namespace hle
```

`runtime/hle/hle_config.h`:
