```cpp
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Save profiles (see profiles.h).
#include "profiles.h"

#include <algorithm>
#include <cctype>
#include <chrono>
#include <cstdio>
#include <cstdlib>
#include <cstring>
#include <ctime>
#include <filesystem>
#include <fstream>
#include <sstream>

#include "hle.h"
#include "json_lite.h"
#ifdef _WIN32
#define WIN32_LEAN_AND_MEAN
#define NOMINMAX
#include <windows.h>
#endif

namespace hle {
namespace profiles {

namespace fs = std::filesystem;

static fs::path P(const std::string& s) { return fs::u8path(s); }
static std::string S(const fs::path& p) { auto u = p.u8string(); return std::string(u.begin(), u.end()); }

int64_t now_seconds() { return (int64_t)std::time(nullptr); }

static std::tm local_tm(int64_t t) {
  std::time_t tt = (std::time_t)t;
  std::tm out{};
#ifdef _WIN32
  localtime_s(&out, &tt);
#else
  localtime_r(&tt, &out);
#endif
  return out;
}
std::string format_time(int64_t t) {
  if (t <= 0) return "never";
  std::tm m = local_tm(t);
  char b[40];
  std::snprintf(b, sizeof b, "%04d-%02d-%02d %02d:%02d", m.tm_year + 1900, m.tm_mon + 1, m.tm_mday, m.tm_hour, m.tm_min);
  return b;
}
static std::string stamp(int64_t t) {
  std::tm m = local_tm(t);
  char b[40];
  std::snprintf(b, sizeof b, "%04d%02d%02d-%02d%02d%02d", m.tm_year + 1900, m.tm_mon + 1, m.tm_mday, m.tm_hour, m.tm_min, m.tm_sec);
  return b;
}
std::string format_size(int64_t bytes) {
  char b[40];
  if (bytes < 1024) std::snprintf(b, sizeof b, "%lld B", (long long)bytes);
  else if (bytes < (1 << 20)) std::snprintf(b, sizeof b, "%.1f KB", bytes / 1024.0);
  else if (bytes < (1ll << 30)) std::snprintf(b, sizeof b, "%.1f MB", bytes / 1048576.0);
  else std::snprintf(b, sizeof b, "%.2f GB", bytes / 1073741824.0);
  return b;
}

std::string sanitize_name(const std::string& s) {
  std::string o;
  for (unsigned char c : s) {
    if (c < 32 || std::strchr("<>:\"/\\|?*", c)) o += '_';
    else o += (char)c;
  }
  while (!o.empty() && (o.back() == ' ' || o.back() == '.')) o.pop_back();
  if (o.empty()) o = "profile";
  return o;
}

// ---- file helpers -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

static void tree_stats(const fs::path& d, int64_t* files, int64_t* bytes) {
  std::error_code ec;
  if (!fs::exists(d, ec)) return;
  for (fs::recursive_directory_iterator it(d, fs::directory_options::skip_permission_denied, ec), end; !ec && it != end; it.increment(ec)) {
    std::error_code e2;
    if (it->is_regular_file(e2)) { ++*files; auto sz = it->file_size(e2); if (!e2) *bytes += (int64_t)sz; }
  }
}
static int64_t tree_bytes(const fs::path& d) { int64_t f = 0, b = 0; tree_stats(d, &f, &b); return b; }

static bool read_text(const fs::path& p, std::string* out) {
  std::ifstream f(p, std::ios::binary);
  if (!f) return false;
  std::stringstream ss;
  ss << f.rdbuf();
  *out = ss.str();
  return true;
}
static bool write_atomic(const fs::path& target, const std::string& text) {
  std::error_code ec;
  fs::create_directories(target.parent_path(), ec);
  fs::path tmp = target;
  tmp += ".tmp";
  {
    std::ofstream f(tmp, std::ios::binary | std::ios::trunc);
    if (!f) return false;
    f << text;
    f.flush();
    if (!f) return false;
  }
  fs::rename(tmp, target, ec);
  if (ec) { fs::remove(tmp, ec); return false; }
  return true;
}
static bool same_bytes(const fs::path& a, const fs::path& b) {
  std::string x, y;
  return read_text(a, &x) && read_text(b, &y) && x == y;
}

// "SNAPSAVE1\n<n>\n<check>\n"; returns false when missing or torn
static bool read_current(const fs::path& uid_dir, uint64_t* n) {
  std::ifstream f(uid_dir / "CURRENT", std::ios::binary);
  if (!f) return false;
  std::string magic;
  unsigned long long g = 0, chk = 0;
  if (!(f >> magic >> g >> chk) || magic != "SNAPSAVE1") return false;
  if ((uint32_t)chk != ((uint32_t)(g * 2654435761u) ^ 0x534e4150u)) return false;
  *n = g;
  return true;
}
static bool gen_complete(const fs::path& uid_dir, uint64_t n) {
  std::error_code ec;
  return fs::exists(uid_dir / "gens" / (std::to_string(n) + ".ok"), ec) && fs::is_directory(uid_dir / "gens" / std::to_string(n), ec);
}
static bool newest_complete(const fs::path& uid_dir, uint64_t* out) {
  std::error_code ec;
  bool found = false;
  for (fs::directory_iterator it(uid_dir / "gens", ec), end; !ec && it != end; it.increment(ec)) {
    if (it->path().extension() != ".ok") continue;
    uint64_t n = std::strtoull(it->path().stem().string().c_str(), nullptr, 10);
    if (gen_complete(uid_dir, n) && (!found || n > *out)) { *out = n; found = true; }
  }
  return found;
}

static bool copy_uid(const fs::path& src, const fs::path& dst, std::string* err) {
  std::error_code ec;
  uint64_t n = 0;
  bool have_ptr = read_current(src, &n) && gen_complete(src, n);
  if (!have_ptr && !newest_complete(src, &n)) return true;   // nothing saved for this user
  fs::create_directories(dst / "gens", ec);
  fs::copy(src / "gens" / std::to_string(n), dst / "gens" / std::to_string(n), fs::copy_options::recursive | fs::copy_options::overwrite_existing, ec);
  if (ec) { if (err) *err = "copy failed: " + ec.message(); return false; }
  if (tree_bytes(src / "gens" / std::to_string(n)) != tree_bytes(dst / "gens" / std::to_string(n))) { if (err) *err = "copy verification failed"; return false; }
  { std::ofstream f(dst / "gens" / (std::to_string(n) + ".ok"), std::ios::binary); f << "ok\n"; if (!f) { if (err) *err = "cannot write .ok"; return false; } }
  // pointer last, atomically; when the source pointer was torn the mount repairs it from the newest complete generation
  if (have_ptr) {
    std::string cur;
    if (!read_text(src / "CURRENT", &cur) || !write_atomic(dst / "CURRENT", cur)) { if (err) *err = "cannot write CURRENT"; return false; }
  }
  return true;
}

bool copy_consistent(const std::string& src_root, const std::string& dst_root, std::string* err) {
  std::error_code ec;
  fs::create_directories(P(dst_root), ec);
  for (fs::directory_iterator it(P(src_root), ec), end; !ec && it != end; it.increment(ec)) {
    std::error_code e2;
    if (!it->is_directory(e2)) continue;
    if (!copy_uid(it->path(), P(dst_root) / it->path().filename(), err)) return false;
  }
  return true;
}

bool looks_like_save(const std::string& dir) {
  std::error_code ec;
  fs::path d = P(dir);
  if (!fs::is_directory(d, ec)) return false;
  if (fs::exists(d / "CURRENT", ec) || fs::is_directory(d / "gens", ec)) return true;
  for (fs::directory_iterator it(d, ec), end; !ec && it != end; it.increment(ec)) {
    std::error_code e2;
    if (it->is_directory(e2) && (fs::exists(it->path() / "CURRENT", e2) || fs::is_directory(it->path() / "gens", e2))) return true;
  }
  return false;
}

// ---- Store --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Store::Store(std::string root) : root_(std::move(root)) {}

static std::string lower(std::string s) { for (auto& c : s) c = (char)std::tolower((unsigned char)c); return s; }

const Profile* Store::find(const std::string& k) const {
  for (auto& p : profs_) if (p.id == k) return &p;
  for (auto& p : profs_) if (lower(p.name) == lower(k)) return &p;
  return nullptr;
}
std::string Store::save_dir(const std::string& id) const { return S(P(root_) / P(id) / "save"); }

bool Store::load() {
  profs_.clear(); pending_.clear(); last_used_.clear(); msg_.clear(); next_n_ = 1;
  fs::path jp = P(root_) / "profiles.json";
  std::error_code ec;
  if (!fs::exists(jp, ec)) return true;
  std::string text;
  Json j;
  std::string e;
  if (!read_text(jp, &text) || !json_parse(text, j, e) || j.type != Json::Obj) {
    fs::path bad = jp; bad += ".invalid";
    fs::copy_file(jp, bad, fs::copy_options::overwrite_existing, ec);
    msg_ = "profiles.json was unreadable (kept as profiles.json.invalid); profiles rebuilt from their folders.";
    for (fs::directory_iterator it(P(root_), ec), end; !ec && it != end; it.increment(ec)) {
      std::string n = it->path().filename().string();
      std::error_code e2;
      if (it->is_directory(e2) && n.size() > 1 && n[0] == 'p' && std::isdigit((unsigned char)n[1])) {
        Profile p; p.id = n; p.name = "Recovered " + n; p.created = now_seconds();
        profs_.push_back(p);
        next_n_ = std::max(next_n_, atoi(n.c_str() + 1) + 1);
      }
    }
    save();
    return false;
  }
  if (auto* v = j.get("next")) next_n_ = std::max(1, (int)v->num(1));
  if (auto* v = j.get("last_used")) last_used_ = v->str();
  if (auto* v = j.get("profiles")) for (auto& o : v->a) {
    Profile p;
    if (auto* x = o.get("id")) p.id = x->str();
    if (auto* x = o.get("name")) p.name = x->str();
    if (auto* x = o.get("created")) p.created = (int64_t)x->num();
    if (auto* x = o.get("last_played")) p.last_played = (int64_t)x->num();
    if (!p.id.empty() && !p.name.empty()) profs_.push_back(p);
  }
  if (auto* v = j.get("pending")) for (auto& o : v->a) {
    PendingOp q;
    if (auto* x = o.get("op")) q.op = x->str();
    if (auto* x = o.get("id")) q.id = x->str();
    if (!q.op.empty() && !q.id.empty()) pending_.push_back(q);
  }
  return true;
}

bool Store::save() {
  Json j = Json::object();
  j.set("version", Json::number(1));
  j.set("next", Json::number(next_n_));
  j.set("last_used", Json::string(last_used_));
  Json a = Json::array();
  for (auto& p : profs_) {
    Json o = Json::object();
    o.set("id", Json::string(p.id));
    o.set("name", Json::string(p.name));
    o.set("created", Json::number((double)p.created));
    o.set("last_played", Json::number((double)p.last_played));
    a.a.push_back(o);
  }
  j.set("profiles", a);
  Json pe = Json::array();
  for (auto& q : pending_) {
    Json o = Json::object();
    o.set("op", Json::string(q.op));
    o.set("id", Json::string(q.id));
    pe.a.push_back(o);
  }
  j.set("pending", pe);
  std::string text;
  json_dump(j, text);
  return write_atomic(P(root_) / "profiles.json", text + "\n");
}

std::string Store::next_id() {
  std::error_code ec;
  for (;;) {
    std::string id = "p" + std::to_string(next_n_++);
    if (!fs::exists(P(root_) / P(id), ec)) return id;
  }
}

std::string Store::next_free_name() const {
  for (int i = 1;; ++i) {
    std::string n = "Profile " + std::to_string(i);
    if (!find(n)) return n;
  }
}

static bool valid_name(const Store& s, const std::string& raw, const std::string& self_id, std::string* name, std::string* err) {
  size_t b = raw.find_first_not_of(" \t"), e = raw.find_last_not_of(" \t");
  std::string n = b == std::string::npos ? "" : raw.substr(b, e - b + 1);
  if (n.empty()) { if (err) *err = "The name is empty."; return false; }
  if (n.size() > 40) { if (err) *err = "The name is longer than 40 characters."; return false; }
  for (unsigned char c : n) if (c < 32) { if (err) *err = "The name has control characters."; return false; }
  if (n[0] == '_') { if (err) *err = "The name cannot start with an underscore."; return false; }
  if (const Profile* o = s.find(n)) if (o->id != self_id && lower(o->name) == lower(n)) { if (err) *err = "A profile named \"" + n + "\" already exists."; return false; }
  *name = n;
  return true;
}

std::string Store::create(const std::string& raw, std::string* err) {
  std::string name;
  if (!valid_name(*this, raw, "", &name, err)) return "";
  Profile p;
  p.id = next_id();
  p.name = name;
  p.created = now_seconds();
  std::error_code ec;
  fs::create_directories(P(save_dir(p.id)), ec);
  if (ec) { if (err) *err = "Cannot create " + save_dir(p.id) + ": " + ec.message(); return ""; }
  profs_.push_back(p);
  if (!save()) { if (err) *err = "Cannot write profiles.json"; return ""; }
  return p.id;
}

bool Store::rename(const std::string& id, const std::string& raw, std::string* err) {
  std::string name;
  if (!valid_name(*this, raw, id, &name, err)) return false;
  for (auto& p : profs_) if (p.id == id) { p.name = name; return save(); }
  if (err) *err = "No such profile.";
  return false;
}

void Store::set_last_used(const std::string& id) {
  last_used_ = id;
  for (auto& p : profs_) if (p.id == id) p.last_played = now_seconds();
  save();
}

int64_t Store::size_bytes(const std::string& id) const { return tree_bytes(P(save_dir(id))); }
bool Store::has_data(const std::string& id) const {
  int64_t f = 0, b = 0;
  tree_stats(P(save_dir(id)), &f, &b);
  return f > 0;
}

std::string Store::duplicate(const std::string& id, const std::string& raw, std::string* err) {
  if (!find(id)) { if (err) *err = "No such profile."; return ""; }
  std::string nid = create(raw, err);
  if (nid.empty()) return "";
  std::string e2;
  if (!copy_consistent(save_dir(id), save_dir(nid), &e2)) {
    if (err) *err = e2;
    std::error_code ec;
    fs::remove_all(P(root_) / P(nid), ec);   // our own half-made copy
    profs_.erase(std::remove_if(profs_.begin(), profs_.end(), [&](const Profile& p) { return p.id == nid; }), profs_.end());
    save();
    return "";
  }
  return nid;
}

std::string Store::trash_move(const Profile& p, const char* kind, std::string* err) {
  std::error_code ec;
  int64_t t = now_seconds();
  std::string base = sanitize_name(p.name) + "-" + stamp(t), folder = base;
  for (int i = 2; fs::exists(P(root_) / "_trash" / P(folder), ec); ++i) folder = base + "-" + std::to_string(i);
  fs::path dir = P(root_) / "_trash" / P(folder);
  fs::create_directories(dir, ec);
  if (ec) { if (err) *err = "Cannot create the trash folder: " + ec.message(); return ""; }
  fs::path src = P(save_dir(p.id));
  if (fs::exists(src, ec)) {
    fs::rename(src, dir / "save", ec);
    if (ec) {   // other volume or locked: copy then verify, and only then remove the source
      std::error_code e2;
      fs::copy(src, dir / "save", fs::copy_options::recursive, e2);
      int64_t f1 = 0, b1 = 0, f2 = 0, b2 = 0;
      tree_stats(src, &f1, &b1); tree_stats(dir / "save", &f2, &b2);
      if (e2 || f1 != f2 || b1 != b2) { fs::remove_all(dir, e2); if (err) *err = "Cannot move the save to the trash: " + ec.message(); return ""; }
      fs::remove_all(src, e2);
    }
  } else {
    fs::create_directories(dir / "save", ec);
  }
  Json m = Json::object();
  m.set("name", Json::string(p.name));
  m.set("kind", Json::string(kind));
  m.set("when", Json::number((double)t));
  m.set("profile_id", Json::string(p.id));
  std::string text;
  json_dump(m, text);
  write_atomic(dir / "meta.json", text + "\n");
  return folder;
}

bool Store::clear(const std::string& id, std::string* err) {
  const Profile* p = find(id);
  if (!p) { if (err) *err = "No such profile."; return false; }
  Profile copy = *p;
  if (trash_move(copy, "clear", err).empty()) return false;
  std::error_code ec;
  fs::create_directories(P(save_dir(copy.id)), ec);
  prune_trash();
  return true;
}

bool Store::remove(const std::string& id, std::string* err) {
  const Profile* p = find(id);
  if (!p) { if (err) *err = "No such profile."; return false; }
  Profile copy = *p;
  if (trash_move(copy, "delete", err).empty()) return false;
  std::error_code ec;
  fs::remove(P(root_) / P(copy.id), ec);   // empty folder only
  profs_.erase(std::remove_if(profs_.begin(), profs_.end(), [&](const Profile& q) { return q.id == copy.id; }), profs_.end());
  pending_.erase(std::remove_if(pending_.begin(), pending_.end(), [&](const PendingOp& q) { return q.id == copy.id; }), pending_.end());
  if (last_used_ == copy.id) last_used_ = profs_.empty() ? "" : profs_.front().id;
  save();
  prune_trash();
  return true;
}

std::vector<TrashEntry> Store::trash_list() const {
  std::vector<TrashEntry> v;
  std::error_code ec;
  for (fs::directory_iterator it(P(root_) / "_trash", ec), end; !ec && it != end; it.increment(ec)) {
    std::error_code e2;
    if (!it->is_directory(e2)) continue;
    TrashEntry t;
    t.folder = it->path().filename().string();
    t.name = t.folder;
    std::string text;
    Json j;
    std::string e;
    if (read_text(it->path() / "meta.json", &text) && json_parse(text, j, e)) {
      if (auto* x = j.get("name")) t.name = x->str(t.name);
      if (auto* x = j.get("kind")) t.kind = x->str();
      if (auto* x = j.get("when")) t.when = (int64_t)x->num();
    }
    t.size = tree_bytes(it->path() / "save");
    v.push_back(t);
  }
  std::sort(v.begin(), v.end(), [](const TrashEntry& a, const TrashEntry& b) { return a.when != b.when ? a.when > b.when : a.folder > b.folder; });
  return v;
}

void Store::prune_trash(int keep) {
  auto v = trash_list();
  std::error_code ec;
  for (size_t i = (size_t)keep; i < v.size(); ++i) fs::remove_all(P(root_) / "_trash" / P(v[i].folder), ec);
}

std::string Store::restore(const std::string& folder, std::string* err) {
  fs::path dir = P(root_) / "_trash" / P(folder);
  std::error_code ec;
  if (!fs::is_directory(dir / "save", ec)) { if (err) *err = "That trash entry has no saved data."; return ""; }
  std::string name = folder;
  for (auto& t : trash_list()) if (t.folder == folder) name = t.name;
  std::string want = name + " (restored)", cand = want;
  for (int i = 2; find(cand); ++i) cand = want + " " + std::to_string(i);
  std::string id = create(cand, err);
  if (id.empty()) return "";
  fs::remove(P(save_dir(id)), ec);   // empty folder made by create
  fs::rename(dir / "save", P(save_dir(id)), ec);
  if (ec) {
    std::error_code e2;
    fs::copy(dir / "save", P(save_dir(id)), fs::copy_options::recursive, e2);
    if (e2) { if (err) *err = "Cannot restore: " + e2.message(); remove(id, nullptr); return ""; }
  }
  fs::remove_all(dir, ec);   // only meta.json (and a copied save) remain
  return id;
}

std::string Store::import_folder(const std::string& src_in, const std::string& raw, std::string* err) {
  fs::path src = P(src_in);
  std::error_code ec;
  if (fs::is_directory(src / "save", ec) && looks_like_save(S(src / "save"))) src = src / "save";
  if (!looks_like_save(S(src))) { if (err) *err = "That folder holds no save (no CURRENT file or gens folder)."; return ""; }
  std::string id = create(raw, err);
  if (id.empty()) return "";
  std::string e2;
  bool ok;
  if (fs::exists(src / "CURRENT", ec) || fs::is_directory(src / "gens", ec)) {
    // a single user folder: keep its name when it is a 32 hex digit uid, else use the default uid
    std::string n = src.filename().string();
    bool hex = n.size() == 32 && std::all_of(n.begin(), n.end(), [](unsigned char c) { return std::isxdigit(c) != 0; });
    ok = copy_uid(src, P(save_dir(id)) / (hex ? n : std::string("534e4150524543310000000000000001")), &e2);
  } else {
    ok = copy_consistent(S(src), save_dir(id), &e2);
  }
  if (!ok || !has_data(id)) {
    if (err) *err = ok ? "The folder has no complete save generation." : e2;
    fs::remove_all(P(root_) / P(id), ec);
    profs_.erase(std::remove_if(profs_.begin(), profs_.end(), [&](const Profile& q) { return q.id == id; }), profs_.end());
    save();
    return "";
  }
  return id;
}

bool Store::migrate_legacy(const std::string& legacy, std::string* err) {
  std::error_code ec;
  fs::path src = P(legacy);
  if (!fs::is_directory(src, ec)) return true;
  std::string id = create("Profile 1", err);
  if (id.empty()) return false;
  fs::path dst = P(save_dir(id));
  fs::copy(src, dst, fs::copy_options::recursive | fs::copy_options::overwrite_existing, ec);
  int64_t f1 = 0, b1 = 0, f2 = 0, b2 = 0;
  tree_stats(src, &f1, &b1); tree_stats(dst, &f2, &b2);
  bool ok = !ec && f1 == f2 && b1 == b2;
  if (ok) {   // pointer files must match byte for byte
    for (fs::recursive_directory_iterator it(src, ec), end; !ec && it != end; it.increment(ec))
      if (it->path().filename() == "CURRENT" && !same_bytes(it->path(), dst / fs::relative(it->path(), src))) ok = false;
  }
  if (!ok) {
    if (err) *err = "The old save could not be copied and verified; it was left where it is.";
    fs::remove_all(P(root_) / P(id), ec);
    profs_.clear();
    next_n_ = 1;
    save();
    return false;
  }
  char d[16];
  std::tm m = local_tm(now_seconds());
  std::snprintf(d, sizeof d, "%04d%02d%02d", m.tm_year + 1900, m.tm_mon + 1, m.tm_mday);
  fs::path moved = src;
  moved += std::string(".migrated-") + d;
  for (int i = 2; fs::exists(moved, ec); ++i) { moved = src; moved += std::string(".migrated-") + d + "-" + std::to_string(i); }
  fs::rename(src, moved, ec);
  if (ec) log("profiles: copied the old save into Profile 1 but could not rename %s: %s", legacy.c_str(), ec.message().c_str());
  else log("profiles: moved the old save into Profile 1; the original is %s", S(moved).c_str());
  return true;
}

void Store::queue(const std::string& op, const std::string& id) {
  if (!is_pending(id, op.c_str())) pending_.push_back({op, id});
  save();
}
bool Store::is_pending(const std::string& id, const char* op) const {
  for (auto& q : pending_) if (q.id == id && (!op || q.op == op)) return true;
  return false;
}
void Store::apply_pending() {
  auto ops = pending_;
  pending_.clear();
  for (auto& q : ops) {
    std::string e;
    bool ok = q.op == "delete" ? remove(q.id, &e) : clear(q.id, &e);
    if (!ok) log("profiles: pending %s of %s failed: %s", q.op.c_str(), q.id.c_str(), e.c_str());
  }
  save();
}

// ---- startup ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

static Active g_active;
const Active& active() { return g_active; }
void set_active(const Active& a) { g_active = a; }

static bool dir_nonempty(const fs::path& d) {
  std::error_code ec;
  if (!fs::is_directory(d, ec)) return false;
  return fs::directory_iterator(d, ec) != fs::directory_iterator();
}

Active startup(const std::string& root, const std::string& legacy, const std::string& want, PickerFn picker, bool force_picker) {
#ifdef _WIN32
  if (const char* w = std::getenv("SNAP_RESTART_WAIT_PID")) {   // a restart: wait for the old process to release its save
    DWORD pid = (DWORD)std::atoi(w);
    if (pid) if (HANDLE h = OpenProcess(SYNCHRONIZE, FALSE, pid)) { WaitForSingleObject(h, 15000); CloseHandle(h); }
  }
#endif
  Active a;
  a.root = root;
  Store s(root);
  s.load();
  if (!s.message().empty()) a.note = s.message();
  if (s.list().empty() && !legacy.empty() && dir_nonempty(P(legacy))) {
    std::string e;
    if (!s.migrate_legacy(legacy, &e)) {
      log("profiles: %s", e.c_str());
      a.on = false;
      a.save_dir = legacy;
      a.note = e;
      return a;
    }
    a.note = "Your old save was moved into \"Profile 1\". The original folder was kept as save.migrated-<date>.";
  }
  s.apply_pending();
  std::string e;
  if (s.list().empty()) s.create("Profile 1", &e);
  std::string id;
  if (!want.empty()) {
    if (const Profile* p = s.find(want)) id = p->id;
    else id = s.create(want, &e);
  }
  if (id.empty() && picker && (s.list().size() > 1 || force_picker)) {
    std::vector<PickItem> items;
    for (auto& p : s.list()) items.push_back({p.name.c_str(), p.last_played, s.size_bytes(p.id)});
    int idx = picker(items.data(), (int)items.size());
    if (idx == (int)items.size()) id = s.create(s.next_free_name(), &e);
    else if (idx >= 0 && idx < (int)items.size()) id = s.list()[(size_t)idx].id;
  }
  if (id.empty()) {
    const Profile* p = s.find(s.last_used());
    id = p ? p->id : (s.list().empty() ? "" : s.list().front().id);
  }
  if (id.empty()) { a.note = "No profile could be created: " + e; a.on = false; a.save_dir = legacy; return a; }
  s.set_last_used(id);
  s.prune_trash();
  a.on = true;
  a.id = id;
  a.name = s.find(id)->name;
  a.save_dir = s.save_dir(id);
  g_active = a;
  return a;
}

}  // namespace profiles
}  // namespace hle
```

`runtime/hle/profiles.h`:

```h
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Save profiles: several independent saves, picked at startup or from the F1 overlay.
//   <root>/profiles.json              names, last used profile, timestamps, pending actions (written atomically)
//   <root>/<id>/save/<uid>/...        one save root per profile (the layout the fs save layer uses)
//   <root>/_trash/<name>-<stamp>/     Clear and Delete move data here (meta.json + save/); the newest 10 are kept
// <root> is %APPDATA%\SnapRecomp\profiles (env SNAP_PROFILES_DIR overrides). Env SNAP_SAVE_DIR switches profiles off
// (test runs) unless SNAP_PROFILES_DIR is set too.
// Files of the profile the running game has mounted are never changed here: Clear and Delete of the active profile
// are queued in profiles.json ("pending") and applied at the next startup, before the save mounts.
#pragma once
#include <cstdint>
#include <string>
#include <vector>

namespace hle {
namespace profiles {

struct Profile {
  std::string id;
  std::string name;
  int64_t created = 0;       // unix seconds
  int64_t last_played = 0;   // 0 = never
};

struct TrashEntry {
  std::string folder;        // directory name under _trash
  std::string name;          // profile name when it was trashed
  std::string kind;          // "clear" or "delete"
  int64_t when = 0;
  int64_t size = 0;
};

struct PendingOp { std::string op, id; };   // op: "clear" or "delete"

class Store {
 public:
  explicit Store(std::string root);
  const std::string& root() const { return root_; }
  // Reads profiles.json; a missing file is an empty store, an invalid one is kept as profiles.json.invalid and the store is
  // rebuilt from the profile folders. Returns false only when a message should be shown (see `message`).
  bool load();
  bool save();
  const std::string& message() const { return msg_; }

  const std::vector<Profile>& list() const { return profs_; }
  const Profile* find(const std::string& name_or_id) const;
  std::string save_dir(const std::string& id) const;          // <root>/<id>/save
  std::string last_used() const { return last_used_; }
  void set_last_used(const std::string& id);                  // also stamps last_played
  int64_t size_bytes(const std::string& id) const;            // total size of the profile's save files
  bool has_data(const std::string& id) const;                 // any save file present

  // Each returns the id (or true) on success; on failure an empty string / false with `err` set.
  std::string create(const std::string& name, std::string* err);
  std::string next_free_name() const;                         // "Profile N"
  bool rename(const std::string& id, const std::string& name, std::string* err);
  std::string duplicate(const std::string& id, const std::string& new_name, std::string* err);   // copies one consistent generation per user
  bool clear(const std::string& id, std::string* err);        // save moves to _trash, profile stays (empty)
  bool remove(const std::string& id, std::string* err);       // save moves to _trash, profile entry goes
  std::vector<TrashEntry> trash_list() const;                 // newest first
  std::string restore(const std::string& trash_folder, std::string* err);   // new profile "<name> (restored)"
  void prune_trash(int keep = 10);
  // Imports the save in `src` (a save root holding <uid>/CURRENT, a single uid folder, or a profile folder with save/).
  std::string import_folder(const std::string& src, const std::string& name, std::string* err);
  // Moves <legacy> (the old single save folder) into a new profile "Profile 1": copy, verify, rename the old folder to
  // save.migrated-<date>. Never deletes. Returns false (legacy untouched, `err` set) if the copy cannot be verified.
  bool migrate_legacy(const std::string& legacy, std::string* err);

  // Pending actions for a profile that is mounted right now.
  void queue(const std::string& op, const std::string& id);
  const std::vector<PendingOp>& pending() const { return pending_; }
  bool is_pending(const std::string& id, const char* op = nullptr) const;
  void apply_pending();                                       // call before anything is mounted

 private:
  std::string next_id();
  std::string trash_move(const Profile& p, const char* kind, std::string* err);
  std::string root_, last_used_, msg_;
  std::vector<Profile> profs_;
  std::vector<PendingOp> pending_;
  int next_n_ = 1;
};

// Copies <src_save_root> to <dst_save_root> as one consistent generation per user (CURRENT, its gen dir and .ok).
bool copy_consistent(const std::string& src_save_root, const std::string& dst_save_root, std::string* err);
// True when <dir> looks like a save root (a <uid>/CURRENT inside), or a uid folder (CURRENT inside).
bool looks_like_save(const std::string& dir);
std::string sanitize_name(const std::string& s);
std::string format_time(int64_t t);       // "2026-11-11 14:05" local, "never" for 0
std::string format_size(int64_t bytes);   // "12.3 MB"
int64_t now_seconds();

// ---- startup
struct PickItem { const char* name; int64_t last_played; int64_t size; };
// Returns the chosen index; n (== count) means "New profile"; -1 means no choice (use the last used one).
typedef int (*PickerFn)(const PickItem* items, int count);

struct Active {
  bool on = false;           // profiles are in use
  std::string root, id, name, save_dir, note;
};
const Active& active();
void set_active(const Active& a);   // tests
// Resolves the profile for this run and returns the save root to use. Applies pending actions and the legacy migration first.
// `force_picker`: show the picker even with one profile. Without a picker function the last used profile is taken.
Active startup(const std::string& root, const std::string& legacy_save, const std::string& want, PickerFn picker, bool force_picker);

}  // namespace profiles
}  // namespace hle
```

`runtime/hle/services_net.cpp`:

```cpp
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// nn::nifm, nn::nsd, nn::prepo, nn::socket, nn::ssl: the console is permanently offline. Every network entry point
// fails the way a console without a connection does (never hangs, never crashes).
// Registration list: reg_net.inc (generated from imports_usage.tsv; one HLE_IMPL/HLE_NOOP per line).
#include <atomic>
#include <cstdio>
#include <cstring>

#include "svc_common.h"

namespace hle {

namespace {
constexpr int kBsdEBADF = 9;
constexpr int kBsdENETDOWN = 50;  // FreeBSD numbering, as Horizon uses
constexpr int kBsdEAI_NONAME = 8;
constexpr int kBsdAF_INET = 2;
thread_local char t_ntoa[16];
}  // namespace

int& sock_errno() {
  thread_local int e = 0;
  return e;
}

void sock_bswap32(Cpu* c) { uint32_t v = arg32(c, 0); ret(c, __builtin_bswap32(v)); }
void sock_bswap16(Cpu* c) { uint16_t v = (uint16_t)arg(c, 0); ret(c, __builtin_bswap16(v)); }
void sock_get_last_errno(Cpu* c) { ret(c, (uint64_t)(uint32_t)sock_errno()); }
void sock_set_last_errno(Cpu* c) { sock_errno() = (int)arg32(c, 0); }

void sock_fail(Cpu* c) {
  sock_errno() = kBsdENETDOWN;
  ret(c, (uint64_t)(int64_t)-1);
}

void sock_close(Cpu* c) {
  sock_errno() = kBsdEBADF;  // no descriptor is ever handed out
  ret(c, (uint64_t)(int64_t)-1);
}

void sock_inet_ntoa(Cpu* c) {
  uint32_t a = arg32(c, 0);  // in_addr by value, network byte order in memory order
  std::snprintf(t_ntoa, sizeof t_ntoa, "%u.%u.%u.%u", a & 0xff, (a >> 8) & 0xff, (a >> 16) & 0xff, a >> 24);
  ret(c, (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)t_ntoa);
}

void sock_inet_ntop(Cpu* c) {
  if ((int)arg32(c, 0) != kBsdAF_INET || !arg(c, 1) || !arg(c, 2) || arg32(c, 3) < 16) { sock_errno() = 47; ret(c, 0); return; }
  const uint8_t* a = ptr<const uint8_t>(arg(c, 1));
  std::snprintf(ptr<char>(arg(c, 2)), arg32(c, 3), "%u.%u.%u.%u", a[0], a[1], a[2], a[3]);
  ret(c, arg(c, 2));
}

void sock_inet_pton(Cpu* c) {
  if ((int)arg32(c, 0) != kBsdAF_INET) { ret(c, (uint64_t)(int64_t)-1); return; }
  unsigned v[4];
  char tail;
  if (!arg(c, 1) || std::sscanf(ptr<const char>(arg(c, 1)), "%u.%u.%u.%u%c", &v[0], &v[1], &v[2], &v[3], &tail) != 4 ||
      v[0] > 255 || v[1] > 255 || v[2] > 255 || v[3] > 255) { ret(c, 0); return; }
  uint8_t* o = ptr<uint8_t>(arg(c, 2));
  for (int i = 0; i < 4; ++i) o[i] = (uint8_t)v[i];
  ret(c, 1);
}

void sock_get_addr_info(Cpu* c) {
  if (uint64_t p = arg(c, 3)) store<void*>(ptr<void>(p), nullptr);
  ret(c, kBsdEAI_NONAME);
}

void nsd_resolve_ex(Cpu* c) {
  // Result ResolveEx(Fqdn* out, const Fqdn& in): the name resolves to itself (no environment switching offline).
  if (arg(c, 0) && arg(c, 1)) std::memmove(ptr<void>(arg(c, 0)), ptr<void>(arg(c, 1)), 256);
  ret(c, 0);
}

// Offline notes for the log: how often the game's online task asks (auto-upload / LenTalk), with the caller address.
void nifm_log_call(Cpu* c, const char* what) {
  static std::atomic<int> n{0};
  int k = n++;
  if (k < 12) log("nifm::%s (offline) caller %s", what, hex_u64(c->x[30]).c_str());
}
void nifm_submit(Cpu* c) { nifm_log_call(c, "SubmitNetworkRequestAndWait"); }
void nifm_is_available(Cpu* c) { nifm_log_call(c, "IsNetworkAvailable"); ret(c, 0); }
void nifm_handle_error(Cpu* c) { nifm_log_call(c, "HandleNetworkRequestErrorResult"); ret(c, 0); }

void register_net(std::vector<Entry>& out) {
#include "reg_net.inc"
  // libc write()/read() on a socket descriptor route here (sdk libc); no descriptor exists, so they fail.
  HLE_IMPL("socket", "_ZN2nn6socket5WriteEiPKvm", sock_fail);
  HLE_IMPL("socket", "_ZN2nn6socket4ReadEiPvm", sock_fail);
}

}  // namespace hle
```

```cpp
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// nn::oe, nn::err, nn::time, nn::settings, nn::account, nn::album, nn::ngc, nn::swkbd, nn::vi, nn::crypto, nn::diag.
// Registration list: reg_sys.inc (generated from imports_usage.tsv; one HLE_IMPL/HLE_NOOP per line).

// [pace] runtime/nvn/nvn_pace.cpp: the guest vsync follows the same frame clock as the host limiter. Builds without the NVN
// layer fall back to the stubs (wait returns 0 = keep the local 60 Hz loop).
extern "C" int snap_pace_vsync_wait(int64_t* last);
extern "C" void snap_pace_vsync_note();
extern "C" int snap_pace_vsync_wait_none(int64_t*) { return 0; }

namespace hle {

// ---- nn::settings::LanguageCode: 8 chars, returned by value in x0 (little endian)
const char* const kLanguageCodes[] = {"ja", "en-US", "fr", "de", "it", "es", "zh-CN", "ko", "nl", "pt",
                                      "ru", "zh-TW", "en-GB", "fr-CA", "es-419", "zh-Hans-CN", "zh-Hant-TW", "pt-BR"};
constexpr int kLanguageCount = (int)(sizeof kLanguageCodes / sizeof kLanguageCodes[0]);

uint64_t language_code(int lang) {
  if (lang < 0 || lang >= kLanguageCount) lang = 1;
  char b[8] = {};
  std::strncpy(b, kLanguageCodes[lang], 7);
  uint64_t v;
  std::memcpy(&v, b, 8);
  return v;
}

std::string g_last_error;
ErrorUiFn g_error_ui = nullptr;

void default_error_ui(const char* title, const char* message) {
  log("%s: %s", title, message);
#ifdef _WIN32
  if (!config().headless) MessageBoxA(nullptr, message, title, MB_OK | MB_ICONERROR | MB_TOPMOST | MB_SETFOREGROUND);  // never hide behind a fullscreen game window
#endif
}

void show_error(const std::string& message) {
  g_last_error = message;
  (g_error_ui ? g_error_ui : default_error_ui)("Pokemon Snap", message.c_str());
}

// ---- days <-> civil date (Howard Hinnant's algorithms)
int64_t days_from_civil(int64_t y, unsigned m, unsigned d) {
  y -= m <= 2;
  const int64_t era = (y >= 0 ? y : y - 399) / 400;
  const unsigned yoe = (unsigned)(y - era * 400);
  const unsigned doy = (153 * (m + (m > 2 ? -3 : 9)) + 2) / 5 + d - 1;
  const unsigned doe = yoe * 365 + yoe / 4 - yoe / 100 + doy;
  return era * 146097 + (int64_t)doe - 719468;
}

void civil_from_days(int64_t z, int64_t& y, unsigned& m, unsigned& d) {
  z += 719468;
  const int64_t era = (z >= 0 ? z : z - 146096) / 146097;
  const unsigned doe = (unsigned)(z - era * 146097);
  const unsigned yoe = (doe - doe / 1460 + doe / 36524 - doe / 146096) / 365;
  y = (int64_t)yoe + era * 400;
  const unsigned doy = doe - (365 * yoe + yoe / 4 - yoe / 100);
  const unsigned mp = (5 * doy + 2) / 153;
  d = doy - (153 * mp + 2) / 5 + 1;
  m = mp < 10 ? mp + 3 : mp - 9;
  y += m <= 2;
}

// ---- PNG (stored deflate blocks; no compression library needed)
uint32_t crc32_update(uint32_t crc, const uint8_t* p, size_t n) {
  static uint32_t table[256];
  static std::once_flag once;
  std::call_once(once, [] {
    for (uint32_t i = 0; i < 256; ++i) {
      uint32_t c = i;
      for (int k = 0; k < 8; ++k) c = (c & 1) ? 0xEDB88320u ^ (c >> 1) : c >> 1;
      table[i] = c;
    }
  });
  crc = ~crc;
  for (size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) crc = table[(crc ^ p[i]) & 0xff] ^ (crc >> 8);
  return ~crc;
}

void put_be32(std::string& s, uint32_t v) {
  for (int i = 3; i >= 0; --i) s += (char)(v >> (i * 8));
}

void png_chunk(std::string& out, const char* type, const std::string& data) {
  put_be32(out, (uint32_t)data.size());
  std::string td = std::string(type, 4) + data;
  out += td;
  put_be32(out, crc32_update(0, reinterpret_cast<const uint8_t*>(td.data()), td.size()));
}

std::string encode_png_rgba(const uint8_t* rgba, uint32_t w, uint32_t h) {
  std::string raw;
  raw.reserve((size_t)(w * 4 + 1) * h);
  for (uint32_t y = 0; y < h; ++y) {
    raw += '\0';
    raw.append(reinterpret_cast<const char*>(rgba + (size_t)y * w * 4), (size_t)w * 4);
  }
  std::string z = "\x78\x01";
  uint32_t a = 1, b = 0;
  for (unsigned char ch : raw) { a = (a + ch) % 65521; b = (b + a) % 65521; }
  for (size_t pos = 0; pos < raw.size() || pos == 0;) {
    size_t n = std::min<size_t>(65535, raw.size() - pos);
    bool last = pos + n >= raw.size();
    z += (char)(last ? 1 : 0);
    z += (char)(n & 0xff); z += (char)(n >> 8);
    z += (char)(~n & 0xff); z += (char)((~n >> 8) & 0xff);
    z.append(raw, pos, n);
    pos += n;
    if (last) break;
  }
  put_be32(z, (b << 16) | a);
  std::string out = "\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n";
  std::string ihdr;
  put_be32(ihdr, w); put_be32(ihdr, h);
  ihdr += '\x08'; ihdr += '\x06'; ihdr += '\0'; ihdr += '\0'; ihdr += '\0';
  png_chunk(out, "IHDR", ihdr);
  png_chunk(out, "IDAT", z);
  png_chunk(out, "IEND", "");
  return out;
}

// ---- vsync feeder
struct Vsync {
  std::thread th;
  std::atomic<bool> run{false};
  void* event = nullptr;
};
Vsync& vsync() { static Vsync v; return v; }

// Applet notification queue (nn::oe::Message values: 15 FocusStateChanged, 16 Resume, 30 OperationModeChanged). The host window code
// (host/window_opts.cpp) posts here; the game polls TryPopNotificationMessage once per frame (its handler is at main+0x5dc3f0).
static std::mutex g_oe_mu;
static std::vector<uint32_t> g_oe_q;
void oe_post_message(uint32_t msg) { std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lk(g_oe_mu); if (g_oe_q.size() < 16) g_oe_q.push_back(msg); }
void oe_try_pop_notification_message(Cpu* c) {
  uint32_t m = 0; bool have = false;
  { std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lk(g_oe_mu); if (!g_oe_q.empty()) { m = g_oe_q.front(); g_oe_q.erase(g_oe_q.begin()); have = true; } }
  if (uint64_t p = arg(c, 0)) store<uint32_t>(ptr<void>(p), m);
  ret(c, have ? 1 : 0);
}

// Zone used by ToCalendarTime: the host's local zone (Windows setting, DST by the CRT's rules for the date; env TZ overrides it,
// which the tests use to pin a zone). SNAP_TIME_ZONE=utc forces UTC.
struct LocalTime { int64_t offset; bool dst; char name[8]; };
LocalTime local_zone_at(int64_t t) {
  LocalTime z{0, false, {'U', 'T', 'C', 0, 0, 0, 0, 0}};
  const char* e = std::getenv("SNAP_TIME_ZONE");
  if (e && (e[0] == 'u' || e[0] == 'U')) return z;
#ifdef _WIN32
  __time64_t tt = (__time64_t)t;
  struct tm lt;
  if (_localtime64_s(&lt, &tt) == 0) {
    int64_t days = days_from_civil(lt.tm_year + 1900, (unsigned)lt.tm_mon + 1, (unsigned)lt.tm_mday);
    z.offset = days * 86400 + lt.tm_hour * 3600 + lt.tm_min * 60 + lt.tm_sec - t;
    z.dst = lt.tm_isdst > 0;
    char nm[64] = {};
    size_t n = 0;
    _get_tzname(&n, nm, sizeof nm, z.dst ? 1 : 0);
    std::memset(z.name, 0, sizeof z.name);
    // Windows names ("Eastern Standard Time") do not fit the 8-char field: keep the initials ("EST")
    int k = 0;
    if (std::strchr(nm, ' ')) {
      for (const char* q = nm; *q && k < 7; ++q) if (q == nm || q[-1] == ' ') z.name[k++] = *q;
    } else {
      std::strncpy(z.name, nm, 7);
    }
  }
#endif
  return z;
}

void time_to_calendar_time(Cpu* c) {
  // Result ToCalendarTime(CalendarTime*, CalendarAdditionalInfo*, const PosixTime&, const TimeZoneRule&)
  // CalendarAdditionalInfo: i32 dayOfWeek, i32 dayOfYear, char name[8], bool isDst (+16), i32 utcOffset (+20)
  int64_t utc = load<int64_t>(ptr<void>(arg(c, 2)));
  LocalTime z = local_zone_at(utc);
  int64_t t = utc + z.offset;
  int64_t days = t >= 0 ? t / 86400 : -((-t + 86399) / 86400);
  int64_t secs = t - days * 86400;
  int64_t y; unsigned m, d;
  civil_from_days(days, y, m, d);
  if (uint64_t p = arg(c, 0)) {
    uint8_t* o = ptr<uint8_t>(p);
    store<int16_t>(o, (int16_t)y);
    o[2] = (uint8_t)m; o[3] = (uint8_t)d;
    o[4] = (uint8_t)(secs / 3600); o[5] = (uint8_t)(secs / 60 % 60); o[6] = (uint8_t)(secs % 60);
  }
  if (uint64_t p = arg(c, 1)) {
    uint8_t* o = ptr<uint8_t>(p);
    std::memset(o, 0, 24);
    int64_t dow = ((days % 7) + 11) % 7;  // 1970-01-01 was a Thursday (4)
    store<int32_t>(o, (int32_t)dow);
    store<int32_t>(o + 4, (int32_t)(days - days_from_civil(y, 1, 1)));
    std::memcpy(o + 8, z.name, 8);
    o[16] = z.dst ? 1 : 0;
    store<int32_t>(o + 20, (int32_t)z.offset);
  }
  ret(c, 0);
}

void time_to_posix_time_from_utc(Cpu* c) {
  const uint8_t* o = ptr<uint8_t>(arg(c, 0));
  int64_t y = load<int16_t>(o);
  int64_t t = days_from_civil(y, o[2], o[3]) * 86400 + o[4] * 3600 + o[5] * 60 + o[6];
  ret(c, (uint64_t)t);
}

void time_clock_now(Cpu* c) { ret(c, now_unix_seconds()); }
void time_to_time_t(Cpu* c) { ret(c, (uint64_t)load<int64_t>(ptr<void>(arg(c, 0)))); }

  if (uint64_t p = arg(c, 0)) store<int64_t>(ptr<void>(p), (int64_t)now_unix_seconds());
  ret(c, 0);

// ---- nn::album
constexpr uint32_t kResultAlbumSaveFailed = result(3, 1);   // host-chosen: the screenshot file could not be created
void album_save_screenshot(Cpu* c) {
  const uint8_t* data = ptr<const uint8_t>(arg(c, 0));
  size_t size = (size_t)arg(c, 1);
  uint32_t image_size = arg32(c, 2);
  // ImageSize values are not seen at a call site in `main`: 0 = 1280x720, 1 = 1920x1080 are the SDK order; anything
  // else is derived from the data size (RGBA8, 16:9).
  uint32_t w = 1280, h = 720;
  if (image_size == 1) { w = 1920; h = 1080; }
  if (size != (size_t)w * h * 4) {
    if (size % 4 || size < 16) { ret(c, 0); return; }
    size_t px = size / 4;
    h = (uint32_t)std::llround(std::sqrt((double)px * 9.0 / 16.0));
    w = h ? (uint32_t)(px / h) : 0;
    if (!w || (size_t)w * h * 4 != size) { log("album::SaveScreenshot: unexpected size %zu", size); ret(c, 0); return; }
  }
  std::string dir = config().screenshot_dir.empty() ? config().data_root + "/screenshots" : config().screenshot_dir;
  std::error_code ec;
  std::filesystem::create_directories(std::filesystem::u8path(dir), ec);
  static std::atomic<int> counter{0};
  char name[64];
  std::snprintf(name, sizeof name, "/snap_%llu_%03d.png", (unsigned long long)now_unix_seconds(), counter++);
  // Open the target now so a bad folder or full disk is reported to the game; encode and write on a worker thread (the PNG encode of a
  // 1080p frame is slow enough to hitch the guest thread). The pixels are copied first: the guest reuses the buffer after the call.
  auto file = std::make_shared<std::ofstream>(std::filesystem::u8path(dir + name), std::ios::binary | std::ios::trunc);
  if (ec || !*file) {
    log("album::SaveScreenshot: cannot create %s%s", dir.c_str(), name);
    ret(c, kResultAlbumSaveFailed);
    return;
  }
  auto px = std::make_shared<std::vector<uint8_t>>(data, data + size);
  const std::string shown = dir + name;
  std::thread([file, px, w, h, shown] {
    std::string png = encode_png_rgba(px->data(), w, h);
    file->write(png.data(), (std::streamsize)png.size());
    file->close();
    if (*file) log("album: saved %s (%ux%u)", shown.c_str(), w, h);
    else log("album: write failed for %s", shown.c_str());
  }).detach();
  ret(c, 0);
}

// ---- nn::ngc, swkbd, crypto
void ngc_count_numbers(Cpu* c) {
  const char16_t* s = ptr<const char16_t>(arg(c, 0));
  int n = 0;
  for (; s && *s; ++s) if ((*s >= u'0' && *s <= u'9') || (*s >= 0xFF10 && *s <= 0xFF19)) ++n;
  ret(c, (uint64_t)n);
}

// There is no on-screen keyboard in the host: the player name is fixed ("Ash", or SNAP_PLAYER_NAME). The game calls this every
// frame while a name prompt is open and re-opens it on cancel, so cancelling stalls the profile creation.
// nn::swkbd::String {char16_t* ptr; int bufferChars;} (layout confirmed from the call site: ptr nonzero, size > 0).
void swkbd_show_keyboard(Cpu* c) {
  uint8_t* st = ptr<uint8_t>(arg(c, 0));
  char16_t* out = st ? load<char16_t*>(st) : nullptr;
  int cap = st ? (int)load<int32_t>(st + 8) : 0;
  static bool once = false;
  if (!once) { once = true; log("swkbd::ShowKeyboard: String ptr %p cap %d (host answers with a fixed name)", (void*)out, cap); }
  if (!out) { ret(c, kResultSwkbdCanceled); return; }
  input::script_event("swkbd");
  const std::string& nm8 = config().player_name.empty() ? std::string("Ash") : config().player_name;   // default "Ash"
  int n = 0;
  int lim = cap == 1 ? 0 : (cap > 1 && cap < 64 ? cap - 1 : 8);   // a 1-char buffer only has room for the terminator
  for (size_t i = 0; i < nm8.size() && n < lim;) {   // UTF-8 to UTF-16 (a code point above the BMP needs two units)
    const uint8_t b = (uint8_t)nm8[i];
    uint32_t cp = b; int len = 1;
    if (b >= 0xF0) { cp = b & 7; len = 4; }
    else if (b >= 0xE0) { cp = b & 15; len = 3; }
    else if (b >= 0xC0) { cp = b & 31; len = 2; }
    if (i + (size_t)len > nm8.size()) break;
    for (int k = 1; k < len; ++k) cp = (cp << 6) | ((uint8_t)nm8[i + (size_t)k] & 63);
    i += (size_t)len;
    if (cp >= 0x10000) {
      if (n + 2 > lim) break;
      cp -= 0x10000; out[n++] = (char16_t)(0xD800 + (cp >> 10)); out[n++] = (char16_t)(0xDC00 + (cp & 0x3ff));
    } else out[n++] = (char16_t)cp;
  }
  out[n] = 0;
  ret(c, 0);
}

void crypto_random_bytes(Cpu* c) {
  static std::mutex m;
  static std::mt19937_64 rng{std::random_device{}()};
  uint8_t* p = ptr<uint8_t>(arg(c, 0));
  size_t n = (size_t)arg(c, 1);
  std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lk(m);
  for (size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) p[i] = (uint8_t)(rng() >> 24);
  ret(c, 0);
}

void vi_get_display_vsync_event(Cpu* c) {
  void* ev = ptr<void>(arg(c, 0));
  auto& v = vsync();
  if (!os_hooks().init_system_event || !os_hooks().signal_system_event) {
    log("vi::GetDisplayVsyncEvent: no os hooks installed (see PROPOSED_SHARED_CHANGES.md)");
    ret(c, 0);
    return;
  }
  os_hooks().init_system_event(ev, false);
  vi_stop_vsync();
  v.event = ev;
  v.run = true;
  v.th = std::thread([&v] {
    int64_t last = 0;
    if (snap_pace_vsync_wait(&last)) {   // [pace] default: ticks of the shared frame clock (display vblanks when locked)
      os_hooks().signal_system_event(v.event);
      while (v.run && snap_pace_vsync_wait(&last)) os_hooks().signal_system_event(v.event);
      return;
    }
    // SNAP_PACE=legacy: free-running 60 Hz. SNAP_VSYNC_HZ=<hz> is a test knob (does the game pace itself on this event?).
    const char* hzEnv = getenv("SNAP_VSYNC_HZ");
    const std::chrono::nanoseconds period(hzEnv && atof(hzEnv) > 1 ? (int64_t)(1e9 / atof(hzEnv)) : (int64_t)16667000);
    auto next = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
    while (v.run) {
      next += period;
      std::this_thread::sleep_until(next);
      os_hooks().signal_system_event(v.event);
      snap_pace_vsync_note();
    }
  });
  ret(c, 0);
}

}
```

`runtime/hle/settings.cpp`:

```cpp
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
#include "settings.h"

#include <cstdio>
#include <cstdlib>
#include <filesystem>
#include <fstream>
#include <map>
#include <mutex>
#include <sstream>
#include <vector>

#include "hle.h"
#include "hle_config.h"
#include "input_core.h"
#include "profiles.h"

#ifdef _WIN32
#define NOMINMAX
#define WIN32_LEAN_AND_MEAN
#include <windows.h>
#endif

namespace fs = std::filesystem;

namespace hle::settings {

namespace {
std::mutex g_mu;
std::map<std::string, std::string> g_kv;
std::string g_path;
std::vector<std::string> g_exported;   // env vars this layer set (so a restart does not pass them on as if the user had set them)

fs::path P(const std::string& s) { return fs::u8path(s); }
std::string path_str(const fs::path& p) { auto u = p.u8string(); return std::string(u.begin(), u.end()); }

void write_file();
void read_file() {
  g_kv.clear();
  if (g_path.empty()) return;
  std::ifstream f(P(g_path));
  std::string line;
  while (std::getline(f, line)) {
    if (!line.empty() && line.back() == '\r') line.pop_back();
    size_t eq = line.find('=');
    if (line.empty() || line[0] == '#' || eq == std::string::npos) continue;
    g_kv[line.substr(0, eq)] = line.substr(eq + 1);
  }
  // Migration (2026-11-13): the old "gfx_draw_distance" (env SNAP_DRAW_DISTANCE, 1..4 in the UI, moved LOD switches and cull together) became
  // "gfx_lod_dist" (switches) plus "gfx_draw_dist" (cull only), both 1..8. Carry an old value over so it keeps the same look.
  auto old = g_kv.find("gfx_draw_distance");
  if (old != g_kv.end()) {
    double v = std::atof(old->second.c_str());
    if (v >= 1.0) {
      if (v > 8.0) v = 8.0;
      char b[32];
      std::snprintf(b, sizeof b, "%.2f", v);
      if (!g_kv.count("gfx_lod_dist")) g_kv["gfx_lod_dist"] = b;
      if (!g_kv.count("gfx_draw_dist")) g_kv["gfx_draw_dist"] = b;
    }
    g_kv.erase(old);
    write_file();
  }
}

void write_file() {
  if (g_path.empty()) return;
  std::error_code ec;
  fs::create_directories(P(g_path).parent_path(), ec);
  std::string tmp = g_path + ".tmp";
  {
    std::ofstream f(P(tmp), std::ios::trunc);
    f << "# per-profile settings (edited by the F1 menu)\n";
    for (auto& [k, v] : g_kv) f << k << "=" << v << "\n";
    if (!f.good()) return;
  }
  fs::rename(P(tmp), P(g_path), ec);
  if (ec) { fs::remove(P(g_path), ec); fs::rename(P(tmp), P(g_path), ec); }
}

// Settings that reach the game through an env var read at start (the F1 menu's "restart needed" options). The key is stored only when the user chose
// something; "" and "default" mean "leave the variable alone" (the game's own behavior). An env var set by hand always wins (set_env_if_unset).
const struct { const char* key; const char* env; } kEnvKeys[] = {
    {"gfx_render_scale", "SNAP_RENDER_SCALE"}, {"gfx_aniso", "SNAP_ANISO"},           {"gfx_lod_bias", "SNAP_LOD_BIAS"},
    {"gfx_shadow_res", "SNAP_SHADOW_RES"},     {"ssao_quality", "SNAP_SSAO_QUALITY"}, {"gfx_lighting", "SNAP_LIGHTING"},
    {"gfx_aa", "SNAP_AA"},                     {"gfx_sharpen", "SNAP_SHARPEN"},       {"gfx_upscaler", "SNAP_UPSCALER"},
    {"gfx_upscale_quality", "SNAP_UPSCALE_QUALITY"}, {"gfx_hdr", "SNAP_HDR"},        {"gfx_hdr_peak", "SNAP_HDR_PEAK"},
    {"gfx_hdr_paper", "SNAP_HDR_PAPER"},       {"gfx_draw_dist", "SNAP_DRAW_DIST"}, {"gfx_lod_dist", "SNAP_LOD_DIST"}, {"gfx_lod_force0", "SNAP_LOD_FORCE0"},   // gfx_fov removed (owner 2026-11-12): a saved value is ignored
    {"gfx_full_rate_anim", "SNAP_FULL_RATE_ANIM"}, {"gfx_ui_font", "SNAP_UI_FONT_SCALE"}, {"fast_boot", "SNAP_FAST_BOOT"},
    {"gfx_ssao_samples", "SNAP_SSAO_SAMPLES"}, {"gfx_ssao_hbao", "SNAP_SSAO_HBAO"},
    {"photo_export", "SNAP_PHOTO_EXPORT"},    {"photo_dir", "SNAP_PHOTO_DIR"},    {"neo_speed", "SNAP_NEO_SPEED"}, {"film", "SNAP_FILM"},
    {"skip_cutscenes", "SNAP_SKIP_CUTSCENES"},
};

// F1 post-process rows: key -> render pass names (comma list) the host switches off through SNAP_PASS_OFF.
const struct { const char* key; const char* passes; } kPassKeys[] = {
    {"gfx_pass_bloom", "BloomCreate,BloomDraw"}, {"gfx_pass_dof", "DOFBlurX,DOFBlurY,DOF"},
    {"gfx_pass_grain", "FilmGrain"},            {"gfx_pass_aberration", "ChromaticAberration"},
};

float to_float(const std::string& s, float def) { return s.empty() ? def : (float)std::atof(s.c_str()); }

void set_env_if_unset(const char* name, const std::string& value) {
  const char* cur = std::getenv(name);
  if (cur && *cur) return;
  if (value.empty()) return;
#ifdef _WIN32
  _putenv_s(name, value.c_str());
#else
  setenv(name, value.c_str(), 0);
#endif
  g_exported.push_back(name);
}
}  // namespace

std::string file_path() { std::lock_guard<std::mutex> g(g_mu); return g_path; }

void use_path_for_test(const std::string& path) {
  { std::lock_guard<std::mutex> g(g_mu); g_path = path; read_file(); }
  apply(false);
}

void load() {
  {
    std::lock_guard<std::mutex> g(g_mu);
    const profiles::Active& a = profiles::active();
    if (a.on && !a.id.empty()) g_path = path_str(fs::path(P(a.root)) / a.id / "settings.cfg");
    else g_path = path_str(P(config().data_root) / "settings.cfg");
    read_file();
  }
  apply(true);
}

std::string get(const std::string& key, const std::string& def) {
  std::lock_guard<std::mutex> g(g_mu);
  auto it = g_kv.find(key);
  return it == g_kv.end() ? def : it->second;
}
bool get_bool(const std::string& key, bool def) {
  std::string v = get(key, def ? "1" : "0");
  return !v.empty() && v != "0";
}
float get_float(const std::string& key, float def) { return to_float(get(key, ""), def); }

void set(const std::string& key, const std::string& value) {
  {
    std::lock_guard<std::mutex> g(g_mu);
    g_kv[key] = value;
    write_file();
  }
  apply(false);
}
void set_bool(const std::string& key, bool v) { set(key, v ? "1" : "0"); }
void set_float(const std::string& key, float v) { char b[32]; std::snprintf(b, sizeof b, "%.3f", v); set(key, b); }

void forget_exported_env() {
  for (auto& n : g_exported) {
#ifdef _WIN32
    _putenv_s(n.c_str(), "");
#else
    unsetenv(n.c_str());
#endif
  }
  g_exported.clear();
}

void apply(bool env) {
  // live: controller effects
  input::PadFx& fx = input::pad_fx();
  fx.gyro_on = get_bool("gyro_on", false);
  fx.gyro_sens = get_float("gyro_sens", 1.0f);
  fx.gyro_invert_x = get_bool("gyro_invert_x", false);
  fx.gyro_invert_y = get_bool("gyro_invert_y", false);
  fx.rumble_on = get_bool("rumble_on", true);
  fx.rumble_strength = get_float("rumble_strength", 1.0f);
  if (!env) return;
  // next start: env-var mods
  std::string look = get("look", "neutral");
  if (look != "neutral" && !look.empty()) {
    char b[64];
    std::snprintf(b, sizeof b, "%s:%.2f", look.c_str(), get_float("look_intensity", 1.0f));
    set_env_if_unset("SNAP_LOOK", b);
  }
  for (auto& m : kEnvKeys) {
    std::string v = get(m.key, "");
    if (v.empty() || v == "default") continue;
    set_env_if_unset(m.env, v);
  }
  {   // post-process toggles: every gfx_pass_* key set to "off" adds its pass names to SNAP_PASS_OFF (host/mods/gamemods.cpp)
    std::string off;
    for (auto& m : kPassKeys) if (get(m.key, "") == "off") off += (off.empty() ? "" : ",") + std::string(m.passes);
    set_env_if_unset("SNAP_PASS_OFF", off);
  }
  std::string ws = get("win_size", "");   // "WxH": windowed client size (the remembered window.json size otherwise)
  int w = 0, h = 0;
  if (std::sscanf(ws.c_str(), "%dx%d", &w, &h) == 2 && w >= 320 && h >= 180) {
    set_env_if_unset("SNAP_WINDOW_W", std::to_string(w));
    set_env_if_unset("SNAP_WINDOW_H", std::to_string(h));
  }
}

const char* env_name(const std::string& key) {
  if (key == "look" || key == "look_intensity") return "SNAP_LOOK";
  if (key == "win_size") return "SNAP_WINDOW_W";
  for (auto& m : kPassKeys) if (key == m.key) return "SNAP_PASS_OFF";
  for (auto& m : kEnvKeys) if (key == m.key) return m.env;
  return nullptr;
}

bool env_wins(const std::string& key) {
  const char* n = env_name(key);
  if (!n) return false;
  const char* cur = std::getenv(n);
  if (!cur || !*cur) return false;
  std::lock_guard<std::mutex> g(g_mu);
  for (auto& e : g_exported) if (e == n) return false;   // we set it ourselves from this file
  return true;
}

bool has(const std::string& key) {
  std::lock_guard<std::mutex> g(g_mu);
  return g_kv.count(key) != 0;
}

void erase(const std::string& key) {
  { std::lock_guard<std::mutex> g(g_mu); g_kv.erase(key); write_file(); }
  apply(false);
}

}  // namespace hle::settings
```

```h
// Shared one-line handlers and host-chosen result codes for the small services.
#pragma once
#include "hle.h"

namespace hle {

// Results the host returns for "this service is unavailable offline". The game only tests success versus failure
// for these (nnResultIsFailure at 25 sites); the module/description values follow the SDK ranges but are not read
// by any compare found in `main`.
```

`runtime/hle/visual_defaults.h`:

```h
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// The visual settings whose defaults can differ from the original game, in ONE table (project code, ours).
//
// Each row has two values: the original game's ("original") and this port's extras ("enhanced"). kDefaultEnhanced picks which column is
// the default when nothing is set. The owner chose the original look as the default on 2026-11-13; flip the one constant below to change that.
// SNAP_PROFILE=original|enhanced overrides the choice for one run (all rows at once). A value set on its own (env var, or a saved F1 menu
// choice, which settings.cpp exports as env) always wins over the profile, so every extra still works through its own switch.
//
// Readers use snapdef::get("SNAP_...") instead of getenv: it returns the env value when set (non-empty), else the profile's value.
// A code path that must know whether the user chose a value explicitly (SNAP_AA with an upscaler) keeps using getenv.
// SNAP_LOD_BIAS is not a row: "auto" already follows the render scale and is a no-op at 1x, so original and enhanced behave the same.
#pragma once
#include <cstdlib>
#include <cstring>

namespace snapdef {
constexpr bool kDefaultEnhanced = false;   // the one flip: true = ssaa2+smaa, CAS 0.3, 16x aniso, font supersampling, PNG export by default

struct Def {
  const char* key;        // env var name (the settings layer exports the F1 menu choice under this name)
  const char* original;   // the original game's behavior
  const char* enhanced;   // this port's extra
  const char* original_text;   // plain-language names for the F1 menu labels
  const char* enhanced_text;
};
inline const Def* table(int* n) {
  static const Def t[] = {
      {"SNAP_AA", "original", "ssaa2+smaa", "the game's own FXAA", "2x supersampling + SMAA"},
      {"SNAP_SHARPEN", "0.00", "0.30", "off", "0.30"},                                    // CAS sharpening strength
      {"SNAP_ANISO", "0", "16", "off, the game's own filtering", "16x"},                  // anisotropic filtering (0 = leave the game's)
      {"SNAP_UI_FONT_SCALE", "off", "auto", "off, as the game ships", "automatic: 2x at 1440p and above"},
      {"SNAP_PHOTO_EXPORT", "0", "1", "off", "on"},                                       // a PNG file per kept photo
  };
  *n = (int)(sizeof t / sizeof t[0]);
  return t;
}
inline bool enhanced() {
  const char* p = getenv("SNAP_PROFILE");
  if (p && *p) {
    if (!_stricmp(p, "enhanced")) return true;
    if (!_stricmp(p, "original")) return false;
  }
  return kDefaultEnhanced;
}
inline const Def* find(const char* key) {
  int n; const Def* t = table(&n);
  for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) if (!strcmp(t[i].key, key)) return &t[i];
  return nullptr;
}
// The profile's value for a key, ignoring the environment (what the F1 menu shows as the default). nullptr for an unknown key.
inline const char* def(const char* key) { const Def* d = find(key); return d ? (enhanced() ? d->enhanced : d->original) : nullptr; }
inline const char* def_text(const char* key) { const Def* d = find(key); return d ? (enhanced() ? d->enhanced_text : d->original_text) : ""; }
// The effective value: the env var when set and non-empty, else the profile's value.
inline const char* get(const char* key) {
  const char* e = getenv(key);
  return (e && *e) ? e : def(key);
}
}  // namespace snapdef

```

`runtime/mods/mods.cpp`:

```cpp
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Loose-file DRP entry mods: the hook the lifted DRP entry worker calls (project code, ours). Guide: docs/mods.md.
//
// Hook point: main+0x5e3a58, inside the worker at main+0x5e38b0 that decompresses one DRP entry (the only caller of
// OodleLZ_Decompress, main+0x7240, at 0x5e3b84). recomp/snap_gen.py MAIN_INLINE_HOOKS makes the generated code call
// rt_mod_entry(Cpu*) just before the instruction there. At that point (callee-saved registers are always in the Cpu):
//   x20 = the entry's chunk in memory (already decrypted): crc32 of the data, 'resd', total, ext crc, csize, dsize,
//         NUL-terminated name at +0x18, padded to 4 bytes, then the payload
//   x24 = the request object (a std::string with the entry name at +0x10)
// The worker allocates the output buffer from the chunk's dsize, then either memcpy()s the payload (csize == dsize), runs
// Oodle, and finally checks crc32(output, dsize) against the chunk's first word. A replacement therefore needs no other
// patch: the hook swaps x20 for a host-built chunk whose csize == dsize == the file size and whose crc is the file's.
// A larger file just means a larger dsize, so the game allocates what it needs.
#include <windows.h>

#include <algorithm>
#include <atomic>
#include <cstdio>
#include <cstring>
#include <map>
#include <memory>
#include <unordered_map>
#include <mutex>
#include <string>
#include <vector>

#include "../cpu.h"
#include "mods_core.h"

namespace {

mods::Index g_index;
std::atomic<int> g_state{0};   // 0 = not loaded, 1 = no overrides, 2 = overrides present
std::once_flag g_once;
std::atomic<unsigned> g_hits{0}, g_misses{0}, g_failed{0};

struct HitCount { std::atomic<unsigned> n{0}; };
std::vector<HitCount*> g_counts;   // by index into g_labels
std::vector<const mods::Override*> g_ovr;

void summary() {
  if (g_state.load() != 2) return;
  fprintf(stderr, "[mods] summary: %u replacements served, %u failed, %zu overrides installed\n",
          g_hits.load(), g_failed.load(), g_index.map.size());
  for (size_t i = 0; i < g_ovr.size(); i++)
    if (g_counts[i]->n) fprintf(stderr, "[mods]   %s <- %s x%u\n", g_ovr[i]->label.c_str(), g_index.packs[g_ovr[i]->pack].id.c_str(), g_counts[i]->n.load());
}

void init() {
  std::string root = mods::default_root();
  std::vector<std::string> warn;
  mods::load(root, g_index, warn);
  for (auto& w : warn) fprintf(stderr, "[mods] warning: %s\n", w.c_str());
  for (auto& c : g_index.conflicts) fprintf(stderr, "[mods] conflict: %s\n", c.c_str());
  if (g_index.empty()) {
    if (!g_index.packs.empty()) fprintf(stderr, "[mods] root %s: %zu packs, no overrides\n", root.c_str(), g_index.packs.size());
    g_state = 1;
    return;
  }
  fprintf(stderr, "[mods] root %s: %zu overrides\n", root.c_str(), g_index.map.size());
  for (auto& kv : g_index.map) {
    g_ovr.push_back(&kv.second);
    g_counts.push_back(new HitCount());
    fprintf(stderr, "[mods] %s <- %s\n", kv.second.label.c_str(), g_index.packs[kv.second.pack].id.c_str());
  }
  atexit(summary);
  g_state = 2;
}

std::vector<uint8_t>& scratch() { static thread_local std::vector<uint8_t> v; return v; }

bool read_file(const std::string& path, std::vector<uint8_t>& out) {
  HANDLE h = CreateFileA(path.c_str(), GENERIC_READ, FILE_SHARE_READ | FILE_SHARE_WRITE, nullptr, OPEN_EXISTING, FILE_ATTRIBUTE_NORMAL, nullptr);
  if (h == INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE) return false;
  LARGE_INTEGER sz;
  bool ok = GetFileSizeEx(h, &sz) && sz.QuadPart < (1ll << 31);
  if (ok) {
    out.resize((size_t)sz.QuadPart);
    size_t done = 0;
    while (ok && done < out.size()) {
      DWORD got = 0;
      ok = ReadFile(h, out.data() + done, (DWORD)std::min<size_t>(out.size() - done, 1u << 24), &got, nullptr) && got;
      done += got;
    }
  }
  CloseHandle(h);
  return ok;
}

// Structural check of a replacement nutexb (ext id 5C156DBC) so a malformed file falls back to the original instead of
// reaching the renderer. Footer (last 0xb0 bytes): u32 w,h,depth,format,dim,mips,tile,layers,data_size,"XET ",version at
// footer+0x84. Returns a reason string, or nullptr when it looks sane. Sizes are NOT compared with the original (any size is fine).
const char* nutexb_problem(const std::vector<uint8_t>& d) {
  if (d.size() < 0xb0 + 16) return "smaller than a nutexb footer";
  const uint8_t* f = d.data() + d.size() - 0xb0;
  uint32_t v[11];
  std::memcpy(v, f + 0x84, sizeof v);
  if (v[9] != 0x54455820u) return "no XET footer magic";
  uint32_t w = v[0], h = v[1], depth = v[2], dim = v[4], mips = v[5], layers = v[7], dsz = v[8];
  if (!w || !h || w > 16384 || h > 16384) return "bad width or height";
  if (!depth || depth > 2048 || !layers || layers > 64) return "bad depth or layer count";
  if (dim != 2 && dim != 3 && dim != 4) return "bad dimension";
  if (!mips || mips > 15) return "bad mip count";
  if ((w >> (mips - 1)) == 0 && (h >> (mips - 1)) == 0) return "more mips than the size allows";
  if ((uint64_t)dsz + 0xb0 > d.size()) return "data size larger than the file";
  uint64_t sum = 0;
  uint32_t ms[16];
  std::memcpy(ms, f, sizeof ms);
  for (uint32_t i = 0; i < mips; i++) sum += ms[i];
  if (sum == 0 || sum > dsz) return "mip sizes do not fit the data size";
  return nullptr;
}

}  // namespace

// ---- SNAP_MODS_AB=<P> (test aid, off when unset): in-run before/after of replaced textures. While (present count / P) is
// odd the renderer shows the ORIGINAL texture, otherwise the replacement. Each replaced nutexb is paired with the original
// file from SNAP_MODS_AB_ORIG (default extracted/drp-v262144, same relative path as in the pack); the renderer
// (runtime/nvn/nvn_draw.cpp ResolveHandle) finds the pair by comparing the guest texture's bytes with the replacement and
// samples a second image built from the original at bind time. Both versions stay resident; nothing is re-uploaded.
namespace {
struct AbEntry {
  std::shared_ptr<const std::vector<uint8_t>> repl, orig;
  uint32_t rw, rh, rm, ow, oh, om;   // replacement and original width, height, mip count
  size_t cmp;                        // bytes of the replacement data compared with the guest's copy
};
std::mutex g_ab_mu;
std::vector<AbEntry> g_ab;

bool ab_footer(const std::vector<uint8_t>& d, uint32_t* w, uint32_t* h, uint32_t* mips, uint32_t* fmt, uint32_t* dsz) {
  if (d.size() < 0xb0 + 16) return false;
  uint32_t v[11];
  std::memcpy(v, d.data() + d.size() - 0xb0 + 0x84, sizeof v);
  if (v[9] != 0x54455820u) return false;
  *w = v[0]; *h = v[1]; *fmt = v[3]; *mips = v[5]; *dsz = v[8];
  return true;
}

void ab_register(const mods::Override* o, const std::shared_ptr<const std::vector<uint8_t>>& repl) {
  static const char* e = getenv("SNAP_MODS_AB_ORIG");
  const std::string root = e && *e ? e : "extracted/drp-v262144";
  const std::string& dir = g_index.packs[o->pack].dir;
  std::string f = o->file;
  for (auto& ch : f) if (ch == '\\') ch = '/';
  std::string d = dir;
  for (auto& ch : d) if (ch == '\\') ch = '/';
  if (f.size() <= d.size() + 1 || f.compare(0, d.size(), d) != 0) return;
  auto orig = std::make_shared<std::vector<uint8_t>>();
  if (!read_file(root + "/" + f.substr(d.size() + 1), *orig)) { fprintf(stderr, "[mods-ab] no original for %s under %s\n", o->label.c_str(), root.c_str()); return; }
  uint32_t rw, rh, rm, rf, rd, ow, oh, om, of, od;
  if (!ab_footer(*repl, &rw, &rh, &rm, &rf, &rd) || !ab_footer(*orig, &ow, &oh, &om, &of, &od) || rf != of) return;
  if (rd == 0 || rd > repl->size() - 0xb0) return;   // a bad footer data size would read past the file (or match any texture of the same size)
  std::lock_guard<std::mutex> g(g_ab_mu);
  g_ab.push_back(AbEntry{repl, orig, rw, rh, rm, ow, oh, om, std::min<size_t>(rd, 4096)});
  if (getenv("SNAP_MODS_AB_LOG")) fprintf(stderr, "[mods-ab] registered %s: replacement %ux%u/%u, original %ux%u/%u\n", o->label.c_str(), rw, rh, rm, ow, oh, om);
}
}  // namespace

// Renderer side: the period (0 = off).
extern "C" unsigned snap_mods_ab_period() {
  static const unsigned p = getenv("SNAP_MODS_AB") ? (unsigned)strtoul(getenv("SNAP_MODS_AB"), nullptr, 0) : 0;
  return p;
}
// Renderer side: `src` is the guest's copy of a texture of w x h x mips. Returns the original's data and size, or null.
extern "C" const uint8_t* snap_mods_ab_original(const uint8_t* src, uint32_t w, uint32_t h, uint32_t mips,
                                                 uint32_t* ow, uint32_t* oh, uint32_t* om) {
  std::lock_guard<std::mutex> g(g_ab_mu);
  static const bool dbg = getenv("SNAP_MODS_AB_LOG") != nullptr;
  for (auto& e : g_ab) {
    if (e.rw == w && e.rh == h && e.rm == mips && dbg) {
      static int n = 0;
      if (e.rw >= 4096 && n++ < 40) {
        size_t k = 0;
        while (k < e.cmp && e.repl->data()[k] == src[k]) k++;
        fprintf(stderr, "[mods-ab] size match %ux%u/%u: first difference at byte %zu of %zu (repl %02x guest %02x, guest head %02x%02x%02x%02x, repl head %02x%02x%02x%02x)\n", w, h, mips, k, e.cmp,
                k < e.cmp ? e.repl->data()[k] : 0, k < e.cmp ? src[k] : 0, src[0], src[1], src[2], src[3], (*e.repl)[0], (*e.repl)[1], (*e.repl)[2], (*e.repl)[3]);
      }
    }
    if (e.rw != w || e.rh != h || e.rm != mips || std::memcmp(e.repl->data(), src, e.cmp) != 0) continue;
    *ow = e.ow; *oh = e.oh; *om = e.om;
    return e.orig->data();
  }
  return nullptr;
}

// Archive path (normalized, e.g. "common/ui/master/foo.drp") of the entry worker's current chunk; false when unknown.
bool mods_archive_of(Cpu* c, std::string* out);

static std::mutex g_file_mu;
static std::unordered_map<const mods::Override*, std::shared_ptr<const std::vector<uint8_t>>> g_files;

// [perf] Built-chunk cache (perf pass 4, 2026-11-13): the first hit of an override builds the replacement chunk (header +
// payload + crc32) once; later hits whose original header is the same hand the guest that shared, read-only chunk (the worker
// only reads it: memcpy or Oodle, then its own crc32 of the output). Before, every hit allocated, copied and crc32'd up to 22 MB
// per entry inside the game's loader (which holds a guest lock meanwhile), so loader threads queued on it. Built chunks are
// never freed (one per override). SNAP_MODS_CHUNK_CACHE=0 restores the per-hit build.
namespace {
struct BuiltChunk { std::vector<uint8_t> v; size_t hdr; };
std::mutex g_built_mu;
std::unordered_map<const mods::Override*, const BuiltChunk*> g_built;
bool chunk_cache_on() {
  static const bool on = [] { const char* e = getenv("SNAP_MODS_CHUNK_CACHE"); return !(e && *e == '0'); }();
  return on;
}
// The original header bytes that the replacement keeps (resd, ext crc, name); the others are rewritten by build_chunk.
bool same_header(const BuiltChunk* b, const uint8_t* chunk, size_t hdr) {
  return b->hdr == hdr && std::memcmp(b->v.data() + 0x04, chunk + 0x04, 4) == 0 && std::memcmp(b->v.data() + 0x0c, chunk + 0x0c, 4) == 0 &&
         std::memcmp(b->v.data() + 0x18, chunk + 0x18, hdr - 0x18) == 0;
}
}  // namespace

extern "C" void rt_mod_entry(Cpu* c) {
  int st = g_state.load(std::memory_order_acquire);
  if (st == 1) return;
  if (st == 0) { std::call_once(g_once, init); st = g_state.load(); if (st == 1) return; }
  if (g_index.empty()) return;
  const uint8_t* chunk = (const uint8_t*)c->x[20];
  if (!chunk) return;
  std::string archive;
  if (!mods_archive_of(c, &archive)) { if (g_misses++ < 5) fprintf(stderr, "[mods] archive of chunk %s unknown (no recorded read covers it)\n", (const char*)chunk + 0x18); return; }
  const char* name = (const char*)chunk + 0x18;
  size_t nlen = strnlen(name, 256);
  uint32_t extcrc;
  std::memcpy(&extcrc, chunk + 0x0c, 4);
  static const bool trace = getenv("SNAP_MODS_TRACE") != nullptr;   // log every entry the worker sees: archive/name.extcrc
  if (trace) fprintf(stderr, "[mods] entry %s/%s.%08x\n", archive.c_str(), name, extcrc);
  const mods::Override* o = g_index.find(archive, std::string(name, nlen), extcrc);
  if (!o) return;
  auto& buf = scratch();
  const size_t hdr_len = mods::chunk_header_len(nlen);
  auto count_hit = [&](size_t bytes) {
    size_t idx = 0;
    for (; idx < g_ovr.size(); idx++) if (g_ovr[idx] == o) break;
    if (idx < g_ovr.size() && g_counts[idx]->n++ == 0)
      fprintf(stderr, "[mods] hit %s <- %s (%zu bytes)\n", o->label.c_str(), g_index.packs[o->pack].id.c_str(), bytes);
    g_hits++;
    static const int delay_ms = getenv("SNAP_MODS_DELAY_MS") ? atoi(getenv("SNAP_MODS_DELAY_MS")) : 0;   // test aid: make each hit as slow as the old per-hit disk read
    if (delay_ms > 0) Sleep((DWORD)delay_ms);
  };
  if (chunk_cache_on()) {   // [perf] fast path: a chunk built by an earlier hit
    const BuiltChunk* b = nullptr;
    { std::lock_guard<std::mutex> g(g_built_mu); auto it = g_built.find(o); if (it != g_built.end()) b = it->second; }
    if (b && same_header(b, chunk, hdr_len)) {
      count_hit(b->v.size() - b->hdr);
      c->x[20] = (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)b->v.data();   // shared and never freed
      return;
    }
  }
  // Replacement files are read and validated once, then shared: the game reloads the same entries over and over, and a
  // disk read per hit (up to 22 MB each) made loading about 15x slower with a large mod set.
  std::shared_ptr<const std::vector<uint8_t>> sp;
  {
    std::lock_guard<std::mutex> g(g_file_mu);
    auto f = g_files.find(o);
    if (f != g_files.end()) sp = f->second;
  }
  if (!sp) {
    auto fresh = std::make_shared<std::vector<uint8_t>>();
    if (!read_file(o->file, *fresh)) {
      if (g_failed++ < 20) fprintf(stderr, "[mods] cannot read %s (%s): using the original\n", o->file.c_str(), o->label.c_str());
      return;
    }
    if (extcrc == 0x5c156dbcu) {
      if (const char* why = nutexb_problem(*fresh)) {
        if (g_failed++ < 20) fprintf(stderr, "[mods] skipped %s <- %s: invalid nutexb (%s), using the original\n", o->label.c_str(), g_index.packs[o->pack].id.c_str(), why);
        fresh->clear();   // cache the rejection (empty) so it is not re-read
      }
    }
    sp = fresh;
    if (!fresh->empty() && extcrc == 0x5c156dbcu && snap_mods_ab_period()) ab_register(o, sp);
    std::lock_guard<std::mutex> g(g_file_mu);
    g_files.emplace(o, sp);
  }
  if (sp->empty()) return;
  const std::vector<uint8_t>& data = *sp;
  if (chunk_cache_on()) {   // [perf] first hit (or a different original header): build once and publish if this override has none yet
    auto* nb = new BuiltChunk{mods::build_chunk(chunk, hdr_len, data.data(), data.size()), hdr_len};
    const BuiltChunk* use = nb;
    {
      std::lock_guard<std::mutex> g(g_built_mu);
      auto it = g_built.find(o);
      if (it == g_built.end()) g_built.emplace(o, nb);
      else if (same_header(it->second, chunk, hdr_len)) { use = it->second; }   // another thread won the race
      else { buf = std::move(nb->v); delete nb; nb = nullptr; use = nullptr; }  // header differs from the published one: private copy
    }
    if (use != nb && nb) delete nb;
    if (use) {
      { std::lock_guard<std::mutex> g(g_file_mu); auto f = g_files.find(o); if (f != g_files.end() && !f->second->empty()) g_files.erase(f); }   // the chunk holds the data now
      count_hit(data.size());
      c->x[20] = (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)use->v.data();
      return;
    }
    count_hit(data.size());
    c->x[20] = (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)buf.data();
    return;
  }
  buf = mods::build_chunk(chunk, hdr_len, data.data(), data.size());
  count_hit(data.size());
  c->x[20] = (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)buf.data();   // held until this thread's next replacement: the worker is done with it by then
}

// ---- which archive is a chunk from? The request object carries only the entry name, so the host remembers, per read
// buffer, the DRP the game read into it (nn::fs::ReadFile taps in runtime/hle/fs.cpp). A chunk pointer lies inside the
// buffer of the read that loaded it; a later read into the same memory replaces the older record.
extern void (*g_snap_fs_tap_open)(uint64_t id, const char* path);
extern void (*g_snap_fs_tap_close)(uint64_t id);
extern void (*g_snap_fs_tap_read)(uint64_t id, const void* buf, size_t n);

namespace {
std::mutex g_tap_mu;
std::map<uint64_t, std::string> g_handles;                           // file handle -> normalized .drp path
struct Range { uint64_t end; std::string archive; };
std::map<uint64_t, Range> g_ranges;                                  // buffer start -> record

void tap_open(uint64_t id, const char* path) {
  std::string a = mods::norm_archive(path);
  if (a.size() < 4 || a.compare(a.size() - 4, 4, ".drp") != 0) return;
  std::lock_guard<std::mutex> g(g_tap_mu);
  g_handles[id] = a;
}
void tap_close(uint64_t id) {
  std::lock_guard<std::mutex> g(g_tap_mu);
  g_handles.erase(id);
}
void tap_read(uint64_t id, const void* buf, size_t n) {
  std::lock_guard<std::mutex> g(g_tap_mu);
  auto h = g_handles.find(id);
  if (h == g_handles.end() || !n) return;
  uint64_t b = (uint64_t)(uintptr_t)buf, e = b + n;
  auto it = g_ranges.lower_bound(b);
  if (it != g_ranges.begin()) { auto p = std::prev(it); if (p->second.end > b) it = p; }
  while (it != g_ranges.end() && it->first < e) it = g_ranges.erase(it);   // overlapped records are stale
  g_ranges[b] = Range{e, h->second};
}

struct Installer {
  Installer() {
    std::call_once(g_once, init);
    if (g_state.load() == 2) { g_snap_fs_tap_open = tap_open; g_snap_fs_tap_close = tap_close; g_snap_fs_tap_read = tap_read; }
  }
} g_installer;
}  // namespace

bool mods_archive_of(Cpu* c, std::string* out) {
  uint64_t a = c->x[20];
  std::lock_guard<std::mutex> g(g_tap_mu);
  auto it = g_ranges.upper_bound(a);
  if (it == g_ranges.begin()) return false;
  --it;
  if (a >= it->second.end) return false;
  *out = it->second.archive;
  return true;
}
```
