```cpp
float EnvF(const char* n, float d) { const char* e = getenv(n); return (e && *e) ? (float)atof(e) : d; }
// SNAP_HDR=off|hdr10|scrgb (1 = hdr10, 0 = off). g_active is what the swapchain actually uses after the fallback chain scrgb -> hdr10 -> SDR.
enum Mode { M_OFF, M_HDR10, M_SCRGB };
Mode g_want = [] {
  const char* e = getenv("SNAP_HDR");
  if (!e || !*e || !strcmp(e, "0") || !_stricmp(e, "off")) return M_OFF;
  if (!_stricmp(e, "scrgb")) return M_SCRGB;
  return M_HDR10;
}();
Mode g_active = M_OFF;
bool g_req = g_want != M_OFF;
float EnvF2(const char* a, const char* b, float d) { const char* e = getenv(a); if (e && *e) return (float)atof(e); return EnvF(b, d); }
float g_peak = 1000.f;      // resolved in PickFormat (SNAP_HDR_PEAK_NITS, else the display's MaxLuminance, else 1000)
float g_paper = 200.f;
bool g_peakResolved = false;
float g_expand = std::clamp(EnvF("SNAP_HDR_EXPAND", 0.3f), 0.f, 1.f);   // how far near-white is lifted (a plain SDR frame cannot tell UI white from a highlight)

// DXGI_OUTPUT_DESC1::MaxLuminance of the output the window is on (0 when unavailable, e.g. no HDR display or a hidden desktop).
float QueryDisplayPeak(void* hwnd) {
  typedef HRESULT(WINAPI * PFN_CF1)(REFIID, void**);
  HMODULE m = LoadLibraryA("dxgi.dll");
  if (!m) return 0;
  auto cf = (PFN_CF1)GetProcAddress(m, "CreateDXGIFactory1");
  IDXGIFactory1* fac = nullptr;
  float peak = 0;
  if (cf && SUCCEEDED(cf(__uuidof(IDXGIFactory1), (void**)&fac)) && fac) {
    HMONITOR mon = hwnd ? MonitorFromWindow((HWND)hwnd, MONITOR_DEFAULTTOPRIMARY) : nullptr;
    float any = 0;
    IDXGIAdapter1* ad = nullptr;
    for (UINT i = 0; fac->EnumAdapters1(i, &ad) == S_OK; i++) {
      IDXGIOutput* out = nullptr;
      for (UINT j = 0; ad->EnumOutputs(j, &out) == S_OK; j++) {
        IDXGIOutput6* o6 = nullptr;
        if (SUCCEEDED(out->QueryInterface(__uuidof(IDXGIOutput6), (void**)&o6)) && o6) {
          DXGI_OUTPUT_DESC1 d{};
          if (SUCCEEDED(o6->GetDesc1(&d))) {
            if (!any) any = d.MaxLuminance;
            if (mon && d.Monitor == mon) peak = d.MaxLuminance;
          }
          o6->Release();
        }
        out->Release();
      }
      ad->Release();
    }
    if (peak <= 0) peak = any;
    fac->Release();
  }
  return peak;
}
void ResolveNits(void* hwnd) {
  if (g_peakResolved) return;
  g_peakResolved = true;
  g_paper = EnvF2("SNAP_HDR_PAPER_NITS", "SNAP_HDR_PAPER", 200.f);
  const char* e = getenv("SNAP_HDR_PEAK_NITS"); if (!e || !*e) e = getenv("SNAP_HDR_PEAK");
  if (e && *e) g_peak = (float)atof(e);
  else {
    const float d = QueryDisplayPeak(hwnd);
    if (d >= 300.f) { g_peak = d; fprintf(stderr, "hdr: display MaxLuminance %.0f nits (DXGI_OUTPUT_DESC1) used as the peak\n", d); }
    else fprintf(stderr, "hdr: display MaxLuminance %s; peak defaults to 1000 nits (set SNAP_HDR_PEAK_NITS)\n", d > 0 ? "is an SDR value" : "unavailable");
  }
  g_peak = std::max(g_peak, 100.f);
  g_paper = std::clamp(g_paper, 20.f, g_peak);
}
PFN_vkSetHdrMetadataEXT pSetHdr = nullptr;
bool g_haveMeta = false;

struct State {
  VkDevice dev = VK_NULL_HANDLE;
  VkFormat fmt = VK_FORMAT_UNDEFINED;
  VkDescriptorSetLayout dsl = VK_NULL_HANDLE;
  VkPipelineLayout pl = VK_NULL_HANDLE;
  VkPipeline pipe = VK_NULL_HANDLE;
  VkDescriptorPool pool = VK_NULL_HANDLE;
  VkSampler samp = VK_NULL_HANDLE;
  struct SrcRes { VkImageView view; VkImageView layerView; VkImage layer; VkDescriptorSet set; };
  std::map<VkImage, SrcRes> src;
  VkSwapchainKHR sc = VK_NULL_HANDLE;
  std::map<VkImage, VkImageView> dstViews;
  uint32_t sets = 0;
  bool failed = false;
} S;

void DropDst() {
  for (auto& kv : S.dstViews) vkDestroyImageView(S.dev, kv.second, nullptr);
  S.dstViews.clear();
}

bool Build(const Frame& f) {
  if (S.dev && (S.dev != f.device || S.fmt != f.dstFmt)) {
    vkDeviceWaitIdle(S.dev);
    DropDst();
    if (S.pipe) vkDestroyPipeline(S.dev, S.pipe, nullptr);
    S.pipe = VK_NULL_HANDLE;
  }
  S.dev = f.device;
  VkDevice d = S.dev;
  if (!S.samp) {
    VkSamplerCreateInfo si{VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_SAMPLER_CREATE_INFO};
    si.magFilter = si.minFilter = VK_FILTER_LINEAR;
    si.addressModeU = si.addressModeV = si.addressModeW = VK_SAMPLER_ADDRESS_MODE_CLAMP_TO_EDGE;
    if (vkCreateSampler(d, &si, nullptr, &S.samp) != VK_SUCCESS) return false;
    VkDescriptorSetLayoutBinding b[2] = {{0, VK_DESCRIPTOR_TYPE_COMBINED_IMAGE_SAMPLER, 1, VK_SHADER_STAGE_FRAGMENT_BIT, nullptr},
                                         {1, VK_DESCRIPTOR_TYPE_COMBINED_IMAGE_SAMPLER, 1, VK_SHADER_STAGE_FRAGMENT_BIT, nullptr}};
    VkDescriptorSetLayoutCreateInfo dl{VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_DESCRIPTOR_SET_LAYOUT_CREATE_INFO};
    dl.bindingCount = 2; dl.pBindings = b;
    if (vkCreateDescriptorSetLayout(d, &dl, nullptr, &S.dsl) != VK_SUCCESS) return false;
    VkPushConstantRange pcr{VK_SHADER_STAGE_FRAGMENT_BIT, 0, 48};
    VkPipelineLayoutCreateInfo pli{VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_PIPELINE_LAYOUT_CREATE_INFO};
    pli.setLayoutCount = 1; pli.pSetLayouts = &S.dsl; pli.pushConstantRangeCount = 1; pli.pPushConstantRanges = &pcr;
    if (vkCreatePipelineLayout(d, &pli, nullptr, &S.pl) != VK_SUCCESS) return false;
    VkDescriptorPoolSize ps{VK_DESCRIPTOR_TYPE_COMBINED_IMAGE_SAMPLER, 32};
    VkDescriptorPoolCreateInfo dp{VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_DESCRIPTOR_POOL_CREATE_INFO};
    dp.flags = VK_DESCRIPTOR_POOL_CREATE_FREE_DESCRIPTOR_SET_BIT; dp.maxSets = 16; dp.poolSizeCount = 1; dp.pPoolSizes = &ps;
    if (vkCreateDescriptorPool(d, &dp, nullptr, &S.pool) != VK_SUCCESS) return false;
  }
  if (!S.pipe) {
    VkShaderModule vs, fs;
    VkShaderModuleCreateInfo sm{VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_SHADER_MODULE_CREATE_INFO};
    sm.codeSize = sizeof kHdrVertSpv; sm.pCode = kHdrVertSpv;
    if (vkCreateShaderModule(d, &sm, nullptr, &vs) != VK_SUCCESS) return false;
    sm.codeSize = sizeof kHdrFragSpv; sm.pCode = kHdrFragSpv;
    if (vkCreateShaderModule(d, &sm, nullptr, &fs) != VK_SUCCESS) { vkDestroyShaderModule(d, vs, nullptr); return false; }
    VkPipelineShaderStageCreateInfo st[2]{};
    st[0].sType = st[1].sType = VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_PIPELINE_SHADER_STAGE_CREATE_INFO;
    st[0].stage = VK_SHADER_STAGE_VERTEX_BIT; st[0].module = vs; st[0].pName = "main";
    st[1].stage = VK_SHADER_STAGE_FRAGMENT_BIT; st[1].module = fs; st[1].pName = "main";
    VkPipelineVertexInputStateCreateInfo vi{VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_PIPELINE_VERTEX_INPUT_STATE_CREATE_INFO};
    VkPipelineInputAssemblyStateCreateInfo ia{VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_PIPELINE_INPUT_ASSEMBLY_STATE_CREATE_INFO};
    ia.topology = VK_PRIMITIVE_TOPOLOGY_TRIANGLE_LIST;
    VkPipelineViewportStateCreateInfo vp{VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_PIPELINE_VIEWPORT_STATE_CREATE_INFO};
    vp.viewportCount = 1; vp.scissorCount = 1;
    VkPipelineRasterizationStateCreateInfo rs{VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_PIPELINE_RASTERIZATION_STATE_CREATE_INFO};
    rs.polygonMode = VK_POLYGON_MODE_FILL; rs.cullMode = VK_CULL_MODE_NONE; rs.frontFace = VK_FRONT_FACE_COUNTER_CLOCKWISE; rs.lineWidth = 1.0f;
    VkPipelineMultisampleStateCreateInfo ms{VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_PIPELINE_MULTISAMPLE_STATE_CREATE_INFO};
    ms.rasterizationSamples = VK_SAMPLE_COUNT_1_BIT;
    VkPipelineColorBlendAttachmentState cba{}; cba.colorWriteMask = 0xF;
    VkPipelineColorBlendStateCreateInfo cb{VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_PIPELINE_COLOR_BLEND_STATE_CREATE_INFO};
    cb.attachmentCount = 1; cb.pAttachments = &cba;
    VkDynamicState dyn[2] = {VK_DYNAMIC_STATE_VIEWPORT, VK_DYNAMIC_STATE_SCISSOR};
    VkPipelineDynamicStateCreateInfo ds{VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_PIPELINE_DYNAMIC_STATE_CREATE_INFO};
    ds.dynamicStateCount = 2; ds.pDynamicStates = dyn;
    VkPipelineRenderingCreateInfo ri{VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_PIPELINE_RENDERING_CREATE_INFO};
    ri.colorAttachmentCount = 1; ri.pColorAttachmentFormats = &f.dstFmt;
    VkGraphicsPipelineCreateInfo gp{VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_GRAPHICS_PIPELINE_CREATE_INFO, &ri};
    gp.stageCount = 2; gp.pStages = st; gp.pVertexInputState = &vi; gp.pInputAssemblyState = &ia; gp.pViewportState = &vp;
    gp.pRasterizationState = &rs; gp.pMultisampleState = &ms; gp.pColorBlendState = &cb; gp.pDynamicState = &ds;
    gp.layout = S.pl;
    VkResult r = vkCreateGraphicsPipelines(d, VK_NULL_HANDLE, 1, &gp, nullptr, &S.pipe);
    vkDestroyShaderModule(d, vs, nullptr);
    vkDestroyShaderModule(d, fs, nullptr);
    if (r != VK_SUCCESS) return false;
    S.fmt = f.dstFmt;
  }
  return true;
}

void Barrier(VkCommandBuffer cb, VkImage img, VkImageLayout from, VkImageLayout to, VkPipelineStageFlags2 ss, VkAccessFlags2 sa, VkPipelineStageFlags2 ds, VkAccessFlags2 da) {
  VkImageMemoryBarrier2 b{VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_IMAGE_MEMORY_BARRIER_2};
  b.srcStageMask = ss; b.srcAccessMask = sa; b.dstStageMask = ds; b.dstAccessMask = da;
  b.oldLayout = from; b.newLayout = to;
  b.srcQueueFamilyIndex = b.dstQueueFamilyIndex = VK_QUEUE_FAMILY_IGNORED;
  b.image = img; b.subresourceRange = {VK_IMAGE_ASPECT_COLOR_BIT, 0, 1, 0, 1};
  VkDependencyInfo di{VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_DEPENDENCY_INFO};
  di.imageMemoryBarrierCount = 1; di.pImageMemoryBarriers = &b;
  vkCmdPipelineBarrier2(cb, &di);
}

bool IsSrgb(VkFormat f) { return f == VK_FORMAT_R8G8B8A8_SRGB || f == VK_FORMAT_B8G8R8A8_SRGB; }

}  // namespace

bool Requested() { return g_req; }
bool IsScrgb() { return g_active == M_SCRGB; }
float Peak() { return g_peak; }
float Paper() { return g_paper; }
const char* ModeName() { return g_active == M_SCRGB ? "scrgb (inverse tone map)" : "hdr10 (inverse tone map)"; }

void AppendInstanceExt(std::vector<const char*>& ext) {
  if (!g_req) return;
  uint32_t n = 0;
  vkEnumerateInstanceExtensionProperties(nullptr, &n, nullptr);
  std::vector<VkExtensionProperties> p(n);
  vkEnumerateInstanceExtensionProperties(nullptr, &n, p.data());
  for (auto& e : p)
    if (!strcmp(e.extensionName, VK_EXT_SWAPCHAIN_COLOR_SPACE_EXTENSION_NAME)) { ext.push_back(VK_EXT_SWAPCHAIN_COLOR_SPACE_EXTENSION_NAME); return; }
  fprintf(stderr, "hdr: SNAP_HDR=1 but the instance lacks %s; the output stays SDR\n", VK_EXT_SWAPCHAIN_COLOR_SPACE_EXTENSION_NAME);
}

void AppendDeviceExt(VkPhysicalDevice phys, std::vector<const char*>& ext) {
  if (!g_req) return;
  uint32_t n = 0;
  vkEnumerateDeviceExtensionProperties(phys, nullptr, &n, nullptr);
  std::vector<VkExtensionProperties> p(n);
  vkEnumerateDeviceExtensionProperties(phys, nullptr, &n, p.data());
  for (auto& e : p)
    if (!strcmp(e.extensionName, VK_EXT_HDR_METADATA_EXTENSION_NAME)) { ext.push_back(VK_EXT_HDR_METADATA_EXTENSION_NAME); g_haveMeta = true; return; }
  fprintf(stderr, "hdr: device lacks %s; HDR10 will be created without static metadata\n", VK_EXT_HDR_METADATA_EXTENSION_NAME);
}

void LoadDeviceFuncs(VkDevice dev) {
  if (g_haveMeta) pSetHdr = (PFN_vkSetHdrMetadataEXT)vkGetDeviceProcAddr(dev, "vkSetHdrMetadataEXT");
}

bool PickFormat(const VkSurfaceFormatKHR* fm, uint32_t n, VkSurfaceFormatKHR* out, void* hwnd) {
  ResolveNits(hwnd);
  if (S.failed) { fprintf(stderr, "hdr: the HDR pass failed earlier; staying SDR\n"); return false; }
  std::string l;
  for (uint32_t i = 0; i < n; i++) { char b[40]; snprintf(b, sizeof b, " %d/%d", (int)fm[i].format, (int)fm[i].colorSpace); l += b; }
  if (g_want == M_SCRGB) {
    for (uint32_t i = 0; i < n; i++)
      if (fm[i].format == VK_FORMAT_R16G16B16A16_SFLOAT && fm[i].colorSpace == VK_COLOR_SPACE_EXTENDED_SRGB_LINEAR_EXT) { *out = fm[i]; g_active = M_SCRGB; return true; }
    fprintf(stderr, "hdr: RGBA16F + EXTENDED_SRGB_LINEAR (scRGB) not offered (surface formats format/colorspace:%s); trying HDR10\n", l.c_str());
  }
  for (uint32_t i = 0; i < n; i++)
    if (fm[i].format == VK_FORMAT_A2B10G10R10_UNORM_PACK32 && fm[i].colorSpace == VK_COLOR_SPACE_HDR10_ST2084_EXT) { *out = fm[i]; g_active = M_HDR10; return true; }
  fprintf(stderr, "hdr: A2B10G10R10 + HDR10_ST2084 not offered by the display/driver (surface formats format/colorspace:%s); falling back to SDR\n", l.c_str());
  g_active = M_OFF;
  return false;
}

void SetMetadata(VkDevice dev, VkSwapchainKHR sc) {
  if (!pSetHdr) return;
  VkHdrMetadataEXT m{VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_HDR_METADATA_EXT};
  m.displayPrimaryRed = {0.708f, 0.292f}; m.displayPrimaryGreen = {0.170f, 0.797f}; m.displayPrimaryBlue = {0.131f, 0.046f};
  m.whitePoint = {0.3127f, 0.3290f};
  m.maxLuminance = g_peak; m.minLuminance = 0.001f;
  m.maxContentLightLevel = g_peak; m.maxFrameAverageLightLevel = g_paper;
  pSetHdr(dev, 1, &sc, &m);
}

namespace {
struct ScratchState {
  VkDevice dev = VK_NULL_HANDLE; VkExtent2D ext{};
  VkImage img[2]{}; VkDeviceMemory mem[2]{};
} SS;
bool MakeImg(VkPhysicalDevice phys, VkDevice d, VkExtent2D ext, VkFormat fmt, VkImageUsageFlags use, VkImage* im, VkDeviceMemory* mem) {
  VkImageCreateInfo ci{VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_IMAGE_CREATE_INFO};
  ci.imageType = VK_IMAGE_TYPE_2D; ci.format = fmt; ci.extent = {ext.width, ext.height, 1}; ci.mipLevels = ci.arrayLayers = 1;
  ci.samples = VK_SAMPLE_COUNT_1_BIT; ci.tiling = VK_IMAGE_TILING_OPTIMAL; ci.usage = use; ci.initialLayout = VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_UNDEFINED;
  if (vkCreateImage(d, &ci, nullptr, im) != VK_SUCCESS) return false;
  VkMemoryRequirements mr; vkGetImageMemoryRequirements(d, *im, &mr);
  VkPhysicalDeviceMemoryProperties mp; vkGetPhysicalDeviceMemoryProperties(phys, &mp);
  uint32_t t = UINT32_MAX;
  for (uint32_t i = 0; i < mp.memoryTypeCount; i++)
    if ((mr.memoryTypeBits & (1u << i)) && (mp.memoryTypes[i].propertyFlags & VK_MEMORY_PROPERTY_DEVICE_LOCAL_BIT)) { t = i; break; }
  if (t == UINT32_MAX) return false;
  VkMemoryAllocateInfo ai{VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_MEMORY_ALLOCATE_INFO}; ai.allocationSize = mr.size; ai.memoryTypeIndex = t;
  if (vkAllocateMemory(d, &ai, nullptr, mem) != VK_SUCCESS) return false;
  return vkBindImageMemory(d, *im, *mem, 0) == VK_SUCCESS;
}
void DropScratch() {
  if (!SS.dev) return;
  vkDeviceWaitIdle(SS.dev);
  for (auto& kv : S.src) { vkDestroyImageView(SS.dev, kv.second.view, nullptr); vkDestroyImageView(SS.dev, kv.second.layerView, nullptr); vkFreeDescriptorSets(SS.dev, S.pool, 1, &kv.second.set); }
  S.src.clear(); S.sets = 0;
  for (int i = 0; i < 2; i++) { if (SS.img[i]) vkDestroyImage(SS.dev, SS.img[i], nullptr); if (SS.mem[i]) vkFreeMemory(SS.dev, SS.mem[i], nullptr); SS.img[i] = VK_NULL_HANDLE; SS.mem[i] = VK_NULL_HANDLE; }
  SS.dev = VK_NULL_HANDLE;
}
}  // namespace

bool PrepScratch(VkCommandBuffer cb, VkPhysicalDevice phys, VkDevice dev, VkExtent2D ext, Scratch* out) {
  if (S.failed) return false;
  if (SS.dev && (SS.dev != dev || SS.ext.width != ext.width || SS.ext.height != ext.height)) DropScratch();
  if (!SS.dev) {
    const VkImageUsageFlags u = VK_IMAGE_USAGE_TRANSFER_DST_BIT | VK_IMAGE_USAGE_TRANSFER_SRC_BIT | VK_IMAGE_USAGE_COLOR_ATTACHMENT_BIT | VK_IMAGE_USAGE_SAMPLED_BIT;
    if (!MakeImg(phys, dev, ext, VK_FORMAT_R8G8B8A8_SRGB, u, &SS.img[0], &SS.mem[0]) || !MakeImg(phys, dev, ext, VK_FORMAT_R8G8B8A8_UNORM, u, &SS.img[1], &SS.mem[1])) {
      SS.dev = dev; DropScratch(); S.failed = true; fprintf(stderr, "hdr: scratch image setup failed\n"); return false;
    }
    SS.dev = dev; SS.ext = ext;
  }
  out->sdr = SS.img[0]; out->sdrFmt = VK_FORMAT_R8G8B8A8_SRGB; out->layer = SS.img[1]; out->layerFmt = VK_FORMAT_R8G8B8A8_UNORM;
  VkImageSubresourceRange rg{VK_IMAGE_ASPECT_COLOR_BIT, 0, 1, 0, 1};
  out->dbg = getenv("SNAP_HDR_DBG") ? atoi(getenv("SNAP_HDR_DBG")) : 0;
  VkClearColorValue black{{out->dbg == 1 ? 1.f : 0.f, 0.f, 0.f, 1.f}}, clear{{0.f, 0.f, 0.f, 0.f}};
  for (int i = 0; i < 2; i++) {
    Barrier(cb, SS.img[i], VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_UNDEFINED, VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_TRANSFER_DST_OPTIMAL, VK_PIPELINE_STAGE_2_ALL_COMMANDS_BIT, VK_ACCESS_2_MEMORY_READ_BIT | VK_ACCESS_2_MEMORY_WRITE_BIT,
            VK_PIPELINE_STAGE_2_ALL_COMMANDS_BIT, VK_ACCESS_2_TRANSFER_WRITE_BIT);
    vkCmdClearColorImage(cb, SS.img[i], VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_TRANSFER_DST_OPTIMAL, i ? &clear : &black, 1, &rg);
    Barrier(cb, SS.img[i], VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_TRANSFER_DST_OPTIMAL, VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_TRANSFER_DST_OPTIMAL, VK_PIPELINE_STAGE_2_ALL_COMMANDS_BIT, VK_ACCESS_2_TRANSFER_WRITE_BIT,
            VK_PIPELINE_STAGE_2_ALL_COMMANDS_BIT, VK_ACCESS_2_MEMORY_READ_BIT | VK_ACCESS_2_MEMORY_WRITE_BIT);
  }
  return true;
}

bool Record(const Frame& f) {
  if (S.failed) return false;
  if (S.sc != f.sc) { if (S.dev) { vkDeviceWaitIdle(S.dev); DropDst(); } S.sc = f.sc; }
  if (!Build(f)) { S.failed = true; fprintf(stderr, "hdr: pass setup failed; blitting SDR\n"); return false; }
  VkDevice d = f.device;
  auto it = S.src.find(f.src);
  if (it != S.src.end() && it->second.layer != f.layer) { vkDeviceWaitIdle(d); vkDestroyImageView(d, it->second.view, nullptr); vkDestroyImageView(d, it->second.layerView, nullptr); vkFreeDescriptorSets(d, S.pool, 1, &it->second.set); S.sets--; S.src.erase(it); it = S.src.end(); }
  if (it == S.src.end()) {
    if (S.sets >= 16) { S.failed = true; return false; }
    State::SrcRes r{};
    VkImageViewCreateInfo vc{VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_IMAGE_VIEW_CREATE_INFO};
    vc.image = f.src; vc.viewType = VK_IMAGE_VIEW_TYPE_2D; vc.format = f.srcFmt;
    vc.subresourceRange = {VK_IMAGE_ASPECT_COLOR_BIT, 0, 1, 0, 1};
    if (vkCreateImageView(d, &vc, nullptr, &r.view) != VK_SUCCESS) { S.failed = true; return false; }
    VkDescriptorSetAllocateInfo da{VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_DESCRIPTOR_SET_ALLOCATE_INFO};
    da.descriptorPool = S.pool; da.descriptorSetCount = 1; da.pSetLayouts = &S.dsl;
    if (vkAllocateDescriptorSets(d, &da, &r.set) != VK_SUCCESS) { S.failed = true; return false; }
    S.sets++;
    vc.image = f.layer; vc.format = VK_FORMAT_R8G8B8A8_UNORM;
    if (vkCreateImageView(d, &vc, nullptr, &r.layerView) != VK_SUCCESS) { S.failed = true; return false; }
    r.layer = f.layer;
    VkDescriptorImageInfo di[2] = {{S.samp, r.view, VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_SHADER_READ_ONLY_OPTIMAL}, {S.samp, r.layerView, VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_SHADER_READ_ONLY_OPTIMAL}};
    VkWriteDescriptorSet w[2]{{VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_WRITE_DESCRIPTOR_SET}, {VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_WRITE_DESCRIPTOR_SET}};
    for (int i = 0; i < 2; i++) { w[i].dstSet = r.set; w[i].dstBinding = i; w[i].descriptorCount = 1; w[i].descriptorType = VK_DESCRIPTOR_TYPE_COMBINED_IMAGE_SAMPLER; w[i].pImageInfo = &di[i]; }
    vkUpdateDescriptorSets(d, 2, w, 0, nullptr);
    it = S.src.emplace(f.src, r).first;
  }
  auto dv = S.dstViews.find(f.dst);
  if (dv == S.dstViews.end()) {
    VkImageView v;
    VkImageViewCreateInfo vc{VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_IMAGE_VIEW_CREATE_INFO};
    vc.image = f.dst; vc.viewType = VK_IMAGE_VIEW_TYPE_2D; vc.format = f.dstFmt;
    vc.subresourceRange = {VK_IMAGE_ASPECT_COLOR_BIT, 0, 1, 0, 1};
    if (vkCreateImageView(d, &vc, nullptr, &v) != VK_SUCCESS) { S.failed = true; return false; }
    dv = S.dstViews.emplace(f.dst, v).first;
  }
  VkCommandBuffer cb = f.cb;
  for (VkImage im : {f.src, f.layer})   // the scratch images come back from the look/overlay passes in TRANSFER_DST
    Barrier(cb, im, VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_TRANSFER_DST_OPTIMAL, VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_SHADER_READ_ONLY_OPTIMAL, VK_PIPELINE_STAGE_2_ALL_COMMANDS_BIT, VK_ACCESS_2_MEMORY_WRITE_BIT,
            VK_PIPELINE_STAGE_2_FRAGMENT_SHADER_BIT, VK_ACCESS_2_SHADER_READ_BIT);
  Barrier(cb, f.dst, VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_UNDEFINED, VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_COLOR_ATTACHMENT_OPTIMAL, VK_PIPELINE_STAGE_2_ALL_COMMANDS_BIT, 0,
          VK_PIPELINE_STAGE_2_COLOR_ATTACHMENT_OUTPUT_BIT, VK_ACCESS_2_COLOR_ATTACHMENT_WRITE_BIT);
  VkRenderingAttachmentInfo ca{VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_RENDERING_ATTACHMENT_INFO};
  ca.imageView = dv->second; ca.imageLayout = VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_COLOR_ATTACHMENT_OPTIMAL;
  ca.loadOp = VK_ATTACHMENT_LOAD_OP_CLEAR; ca.storeOp = VK_ATTACHMENT_STORE_OP_STORE; ca.clearValue.color = {{0.f, 0.f, 0.f, 1.f}};
  VkRenderingInfo ri{VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_RENDERING_INFO};
  ri.renderArea = {{0, 0}, f.dstExt}; ri.layerCount = 1; ri.colorAttachmentCount = 1; ri.pColorAttachments = &ca;
  vkCmdBeginRendering(cb, &ri);
  vkCmdBindPipeline(cb, VK_PIPELINE_BIND_POINT_GRAPHICS, S.pipe);
  vkCmdBindDescriptorSets(cb, VK_PIPELINE_BIND_POINT_GRAPHICS, S.pl, 0, 1, &it->second.set, 0, nullptr);
  VkViewport vp{(float)f.dx, (float)f.dy, (float)f.dw, (float)f.dh, 0.f, 1.f};
  VkRect2D sc{{f.dx, f.dy}, {(uint32_t)f.dw, (uint32_t)f.dh}};
  vkCmdSetViewport(cb, 0, 1, &vp);
  vkCmdSetScissor(cb, 0, 1, &sc);
  const float iw = 1.0f / (float)f.srcW, ih = 1.0f / (float)f.srcH;
  const float pc[12] = {f.sx * iw, f.sy * ih, f.sw * iw, f.sh * ih, g_paper, g_peak, IsSrgb(f.srcFmt) ? 1.f : 0.f, g_expand, g_active == M_SCRGB ? 1.f : 0.f, 0.f, 0.f, 0.f};
  vkCmdPushConstants(cb, S.pl, VK_SHADER_STAGE_FRAGMENT_BIT, 0, sizeof pc, pc);
  vkCmdDraw(cb, 3, 1, 0, 0);
  vkCmdEndRendering(cb);
  Barrier(cb, f.dst, VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_COLOR_ATTACHMENT_OPTIMAL, VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_TRANSFER_DST_OPTIMAL, VK_PIPELINE_STAGE_2_COLOR_ATTACHMENT_OUTPUT_BIT,
          VK_ACCESS_2_COLOR_ATTACHMENT_WRITE_BIT, VK_PIPELINE_STAGE_2_ALL_COMMANDS_BIT, VK_ACCESS_2_MEMORY_READ_BIT | VK_ACCESS_2_MEMORY_WRITE_BIT);
  return true;
}

namespace {
float PqEotf(float e) {
  const float m1 = 0.1593017578125f, m2 = 78.84375f, c1 = 0.8359375f, c2 = 18.8515625f, c3 = 18.6875f;
  const float p = std::pow(std::max(e, 0.f), 1.f / m2);
  return 10000.f * std::pow(std::max(p - c1, 0.f) / (c2 - c3 * p), 1.f / m1);
}
float SrgbOetf(float x) { x = std::clamp(x, 0.f, 1.f); return x <= 0.0031308f ? x * 12.92f : 1.055f * std::pow(x, 1.f / 2.4f) - 0.055f; }
void WriteBmp(const std::string& path, const std::vector<uint8_t>& rgb, uint32_t w, uint32_t h) {
  std::vector<uint8_t> out((size_t)w * h * 3 + 54, 0);
  uint8_t* o = out.data();
  auto le32 = [&](int off, uint32_t x) { memcpy(o + off, &x, 4); };
  o[0] = 'B'; o[1] = 'M'; le32(2, (uint32_t)out.size()); le32(10, 54); le32(14, 40); le32(18, w); le32(22, (uint32_t)(-(int)h)); o[26] = 1; o[28] = 24;
  le32(34, (uint32_t)((size_t)w * h * 3));
  for (size_t i = 0; i < (size_t)w * h; i++) { o[54 + i * 3] = rgb[i * 3 + 2]; o[55 + i * 3] = rgb[i * 3 + 1]; o[56 + i * 3] = rgb[i * 3]; }
  if (FILE* f = fopen(path.c_str(), "wb")) { fwrite(out.data(), 1, out.size(), f); fclose(f); }
}
}  // namespace

namespace {
float HalfToFloat(uint16_t h) {
  const uint32_t s = (h >> 15) & 1, e = (h >> 10) & 31, m = h & 1023;
  float v;
  if (e == 0) v = std::ldexp((float)m, -24);
  else if (e == 31) v = m ? 0.f : 65504.f;
  else v = std::ldexp((float)(m + 1024), (int)e - 25);
  return s ? -v : v;
}
}  // namespace

void DumpPQ(const char* base, const void* px, uint32_t w, uint32_t h) {
  const bool sc = g_active == M_SCRGB;
  const uint32_t* p32 = static_cast<const uint32_t*>(px);
  const uint16_t* p16 = static_cast<const uint16_t*>(px);
  // linear Rec.709 nits of one pixel
  auto nitsAt = [&](uint32_t x, uint32_t y, float out[3]) {
    if (sc) {
      const uint16_t* t = p16 + ((size_t)y * w + x) * 4;
      for (int k = 0; k < 3; k++) out[k] = HalfToFloat(t[k]) * 80.f;
      return;
    }
    const uint32_t v = p32[(size_t)y * w + x];
    const float c[3] = {PqEotf((v & 1023) / 1023.f), PqEotf(((v >> 10) & 1023) / 1023.f), PqEotf(((v >> 20) & 1023) / 1023.f)};
    out[0] = 1.6605f * c[0] - 0.5876f * c[1] - 0.0728f * c[2];   // Rec.2020 -> Rec.709
    out[1] = -0.1246f * c[0] + 1.1329f * c[1] - 0.0083f * c[2];
    out[2] = -0.0182f * c[0] - 0.1006f * c[1] + 1.1187f * c[2];
  };
  const uint32_t W = w / 2, H = h / 2;   // half-size preview, point sampled
  std::vector<uint8_t> a((size_t)W * H * 3), b((size_t)W * H * 3);
  double sum = 0, maxN = 0; uint64_t over = 0, n = 0;
  for (uint32_t y = 0; y < H; y++)
    for (uint32_t x = 0; x < W; x++) {
      float c[3];
      nitsAt(x * 2, y * 2, c);
      const float r = c[0], g = c[1], bl = c[2];
      const float lum = 0.2126f * r + 0.7152f * g + 0.0722f * bl;
      sum += lum; maxN = std::max<double>(maxN, lum); n++; if (lum > g_paper * 1.05f) over++;
      auto tm = [&](float nits) { float t = nits / g_paper; if (t > 0.8f) t = 0.8f + 0.2f * (1.f - std::exp(-(t - 0.8f) / 0.2f)); return SrgbOetf(t); };
      const size_t o = ((size_t)y * W + x) * 3;
      a[o] = (uint8_t)(tm(r) * 255.f + 0.5f); a[o + 1] = (uint8_t)(tm(g) * 255.f + 0.5f); a[o + 2] = (uint8_t)(tm(bl) * 255.f + 0.5f);
      if (lum <= g_paper) { const uint8_t gv = (uint8_t)(SrgbOetf(lum / g_paper) * 128.f); b[o] = b[o + 1] = b[o + 2] = gv; }
      else {   // above paper white: log scale to the peak, dark blue -> cyan -> yellow -> red
        const float t = std::clamp(std::log2(lum / g_paper) / std::max(std::log2(g_peak / g_paper), 0.01f), 0.f, 1.f);
        const float cr = std::clamp(t * 2.f - 0.6f, 0.f, 1.f), cg = std::clamp(t < 0.5f ? t * 2.f : 2.f - t * 2.f, 0.f, 1.f), cb2 = std::clamp(1.f - t * 2.f, 0.2f, 1.f);
        b[o] = (uint8_t)(255 * cr); b[o + 1] = (uint8_t)(255 * cg); b[o + 2] = (uint8_t)(255 * cb2);
      }
    }
  WriteBmp(std::string(base) + ".bmp", a, W, H);
  WriteBmp(std::string(base) + "_nits.bmp", b, W, H);
  // Banding probe: the green channel down the centre column of the top quarter (sky in the course frames). Counts distinct stored code
  // values and gives the relative size of one code step at the strip's mean level.
  std::map<uint32_t, int> codes; double sMean = 0; uint32_t sN = h / 4; uint32_t gMid = 0;
  for (uint32_t y = 0; y < sN; y++) {
    float c[3]; nitsAt(w / 2, y, c); sMean += c[1];
    const uint32_t code = sc ? (uint32_t)p16[((size_t)y * w + w / 2) * 4 + 1] : ((p32[(size_t)y * w + w / 2] >> 10) & 1023);
    codes[code]++; gMid = code;
  }
  sMean /= std::max<uint32_t>(sN, 1);
  double stepPct = 0;
  if (sc) { const float a0 = HalfToFloat((uint16_t)gMid), a1 = HalfToFloat((uint16_t)(gMid + 1)); stepPct = a0 > 0 ? 100.0 * (a1 - a0) / a0 : 0; }
  else { const float a0 = PqEotf(gMid / 1023.f), a1 = PqEotf((gMid + 1) / 1023.f); stepPct = a0 > 0 ? 100.0 * (a1 - a0) / a0 : 0; }
  fprintf(stderr, "hdr: dump %s %ux%u %s mean %.1f nits, max %.1f nits, %.2f%% of pixels above paper white (%.0f); sky strip: %zu distinct G codes in %u rows, mean %.1f nits, one code step = %.3f%%\n", base, w, h,
          sc ? "scRGB" : "HDR10", sum / std::max<uint64_t>(n, 1), maxN, 100.0 * (double)over / (double)std::max<uint64_t>(n, 1), g_paper, codes.size(), sN, sMean, stepPct);
}

}  // namespace snap_hdr
```

`runtime/nvn/nvn_hdr.h`:

```h
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// HDR10 output (owner-approved, off by default: SNAP_HDR=hdr10|scrgb). Project code, ours.
//
// The NVN layer's present step normally blits the game's window texture into an SDR swapchain. With SNAP_HDR=hdr10|scrgb and a display/driver that
// offers A2B10G10R10 + HDR10_ST2084 (VK_EXT_swapchain_colorspace), the swapchain is created in that format, VK_EXT_hdr_metadata is set, and
// this file draws the frame through a PQ pass instead of the blit. Photo capture, thumbnails and scoring read the game's own render
// targets and never see this output. Settings (env): SNAP_HDR=hdr10|scrgb, SNAP_HDR_PEAK_NITS (default: the display MaxLuminance, else 1000), SNAP_HDR_PAPER_NITS
// (default 200), SNAP_HDR_EXPAND (0..1, default 0.3).
#pragma once
#include <vulkan/vulkan.h>
#include "nvn_vkcount.h"

#include <vector>

namespace snap_hdr {

bool Requested();            // SNAP_HDR=hdr10|scrgb
float Peak();
float Paper();
const char* ModeName();      // "itm" or "guided"

// Instance/device extension helpers: append VK_EXT_swapchain_colorspace / VK_EXT_hdr_metadata when requested and available.
void AppendInstanceExt(std::vector<const char*>& ext);
void AppendDeviceExt(VkPhysicalDevice phys, std::vector<const char*>& ext);
void LoadDeviceFuncs(VkDevice dev);

// Chooses the HDR10 surface format. Logs a one-line reason and returns false when the surface does not offer it (caller falls back to SDR).
bool PickFormat(const VkSurfaceFormatKHR* fm, uint32_t n, VkSurfaceFormatKHR* out, void* hwnd);   // scRGB first if SNAP_HDR=scrgb, then HDR10
bool IsScrgb();   // the active swapchain is scRGB (RGBA16F), else A2B10G10R10 PQ
void SetMetadata(VkDevice dev, VkSwapchainKHR sc);   // after vkCreateSwapchainKHR

struct Frame {
  VkPhysicalDevice phys; VkDevice device; VkCommandBuffer cb;
  VkImage dst; VkFormat dstFmt; VkExtent2D dstExt; VkSwapchainKHR sc;   // dst: UNDEFINED in, TRANSFER_DST_OPTIMAL out
  VkImage src; VkFormat srcFmt; uint32_t srcW, srcH;                    // src: the SDR scratch image (TRANSFER_DST_OPTIMAL in, SHADER_READ_ONLY out)
  int sx, sy, sw, sh;                                                   // source rect (pixels)
  int dx, dy, dw, dh;                                                   // destination rect (pixels, letterboxed)
  VkImage layer;                                                        // overlay layer from PrepScratch (TRANSFER_DST_OPTIMAL in, SHADER_READ_ONLY out)
};
// SDR scratch images for the HDR path: `sdr` (RGBA8 sRGB, extent of the swapchain) takes the scene blit and SNAP_LOOK; `layer` (RGBA8 UNORM, cleared to
// transparent) takes the F1 overlay. Both come back in TRANSFER_DST_OPTIMAL, the layout snap_look_present/snap_ui_present expect.
struct Scratch { VkImage sdr; VkFormat sdrFmt; VkImage layer; VkFormat layerFmt; int dbg; };
bool PrepScratch(VkCommandBuffer cb, VkPhysicalDevice phys, VkDevice dev, VkExtent2D ext, Scratch* out);
bool Record(const Frame& f);   // false = setup failed (the caller should fall back to the blit)

// Debug dump: writes <base>.bmp (SDR preview of the PQ image) and <base>_nits.bmp (highlight map) from a copy of the swapchain image
// (A2B10G10R10 words) and logs luminance statistics.
void DumpPQ(const char* base, const void* px, uint32_t w, uint32_t h);   // px: A2B10G10R10 words, or RGBA16F texels when IsScrgb()

}  // namespace snap_hdr
```

```h
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Public surface of the NVN->Vulkan layer. The lifted game receives its NVN function table through
// nvnBootstrapLoader (the only real NVN import, [analysis/runtime/nvn_usage.md]).
#pragma once
#include <cstdint>

#if defined(_WIN32)
#define NVN_HOST_EXPORT extern "C" __declspec(dllexport)
#else
#define NVN_HOST_EXPORT extern "C" __attribute__((visibility("default")))
#endif

// The real NVN loader entry: returns the function for an exact NVN name ("nvnDeviceGetProcAddress",
// "nvnDeviceInitialize", ...) or nullptr. nvnDeviceGetProcAddress(device, name) returns the same table.
NVN_HOST_EXPORT void (*nvnBootstrapLoader(const char* name))(void);

// ---- Host-side controls (not part of NVN) -------------------------------------------------------------
// Must be called before nvnDeviceInitialize. Validation layers are also enabled by env NVN_VK_VALIDATION=1.
NVN_HOST_EXPORT void nvnHostSetValidation(int enable);
NVN_HOST_EXPORT uint32_t nvnHostValidationErrors(void);
NVN_HOST_EXPORT uint32_t nvnHostValidationWarnings(void);
// Frame limiter: rate in Hz of NVN present interval 1 (the Switch panel is 60 Hz). Interval n paces to n/hz s.
// 0 disables the limiter (presentation then follows the display's FIFO vsync only). Default 60.
NVN_HOST_EXPORT void nvnHostSetFramePacing(double hz);
// Render-target resolution scale (off by default: 1.0 matches the original). Applies to plain render targets
// (TextureFlags COMPRESSIBLE, not DISPLAY/LINEAR, 2D or 2D array, single sample) created after the call, so set it before the
// game creates its textures. The guest still sees the original size from every NVN getter; viewports, scissors and clear
// regions are scaled at replay; copies between targets of different scale become blits. Exempt targets keep scale 1:
//   - by signature: nvnHostAddScaleExemption(width, height, nvnFormat, depthOnly), -1 = any,
//   - by tag: call nvnHostSetNextTextureTag(tag) right before the allocation and nvnHostAddScaleExemptionTag(tag) once,
//   - by guest call site (built in): the Evaluation depth target, created from main+0x5c3d38 ("Evaluation DepthStencil"), is
//     found in the guest frame-pointer chain of its TextureInitialize call (nvnHostSetGuestFrame, set by the generated bridge).
//     nvnHostClearScaleExemptions also turns this off.
// nvnHostGetTextureHostSize reports the Vulkan image size of a guest texture (0 if it is not a texture).
NVN_HOST_EXPORT void nvnHostSetRenderScale(float scale);
NVN_HOST_EXPORT float nvnHostGetRenderScale(void);
NVN_HOST_EXPORT void nvnHostAddScaleExemption(int width, int height, int nvnFormat, int depthOnly);
NVN_HOST_EXPORT void nvnHostClearScaleExemptions(void);
NVN_HOST_EXPORT void nvnHostSetNextTextureTag(uint32_t tag);
NVN_HOST_EXPORT void nvnHostAddScaleExemptionTag(uint32_t tag);
NVN_HOST_EXPORT int nvnHostGetTextureHostSize(const void* guestTexture, int* width, int* height);
// Guest frame pointer (x29) and link register (x30) of the NVN call about to run; the bridge sets it for TextureInitialize only.
NVN_HOST_EXPORT void nvnHostSetGuestFrame(uint64_t fp, uint64_t lr);
// Anisotropic filtering override applied at SamplerInitialize to mipmapped, non-comparison samplers (the game uses 1x).
// Default 16 (host default since 2026-11-12); 0 = off (original 1x). Must be set before samplers are created. Env SNAP_ANISO=0..16.
NVN_HOST_EXPORT void nvnHostSetAnisotropyOverride(float maxAnisotropy);
// Anisotropy applies only to mipmapped samplers with linear min and mag filters and no depth compare; point, nearest and shadow-compare
// samplers keep the game's value. Clamped to the device limit. Read-back: nvnHostGetAnisotropyOverride (0 = off).
NVN_HOST_EXPORT float nvnHostGetAnisotropyOverride(void);
// LOD bias added to the game's bias on mipmapped, non-compare samplers (set before samplers are created). Auto = -log2(output /
// render resolution), the upscaler bias: 0 at native render scale (a 2x target already samples one mip finer), negative only when
// the scene renders below the output size. Env: SNAP_LOD_BIAS=<float>|auto; unset = auto. At native 4K, -1 is sharper still in
// stills (analysis/mods/compare/lod_crop_s2.png) but samples two mips finer than 1080p and may shimmer in motion; it is opt-in.
NVN_HOST_EXPORT void nvnHostSetLodBias(float bias);
NVN_HOST_EXPORT void nvnHostSetLodBiasAuto(int on);
// Side of the 1024x1024 depth shadow maps (1024 = original, 2048, 4096; set before the game creates them). Independent of the render scale.
NVN_HOST_EXPORT void nvnHostSetShadowResolution(int side);
NVN_HOST_EXPORT int nvnHostGetShadowResolution(void);
// Whether window (DISPLAY) textures follow the render scale (default 1). Needed for a real 4K frame: the game composes UI into them.
NVN_HOST_EXPORT void nvnHostSetScaleDisplay(int on);
// Environment read once at DeviceInitialize: SNAP_RENDER_SCALE, SNAP_ANISO (1..16), SNAP_LOD_BIAS, SNAP_SHADOW_RES. The output
// (swapchain) resolution is the window size: SNAP_WINDOW_W / SNAP_WINDOW_H (host/window_opts.cpp).
// Number of guest entry points registered in the getProcAddress table.
NVN_HOST_EXPORT int nvnHostProcCount(void);
// Name of the idx-th registered entry point (0 <= idx < count), for tests and coverage reports.
NVN_HOST_EXPORT const char* nvnHostProcName(int idx);

// Present/render-pass interception hooks (see docs/nvn-vulkan-design.md, "Interception hooks").
// All callbacks run on the thread that issued the NVN call. Observers in this milestone.
struct NvnHostHooks {
  void* user;
  // Called when QueuePresentTexture starts: guest slot, source size in pixels. Returns nothing yet; later
  // milestones let the hook replace the present blit (scene->output scaler, DLSS, UI composite).
  void (*on_present)(void* user, int slot, int src_w, int src_h);
  // Called for each submitted command list before replay: number of recorded commands.
  void (*on_submit)(void* user, int list_index, int command_count);
};
NVN_HOST_EXPORT void nvnHostSetHooks(const NvnHostHooks* hooks);
```

`runtime/nvn/nvn_internal.h`:

```h
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Host-side objects behind the opaque guest NVN structs. Guest memory only holds {magic, impl*}.
#pragma once
#ifndef VK_USE_PLATFORM_WIN32_KHR
#define VK_USE_PLATFORM_WIN32_KHR
#endif
#ifndef NOMINMAX
#define NOMINMAX
#endif
#ifndef WIN32_LEAN_AND_MEAN
#define WIN32_LEAN_AND_MEAN
#endif
#include <vulkan/vulkan.h>
#include "nvn_vkcount.h"

#include <array>
#include <atomic>
#include <cstdarg>
#include <cstdio>
#include <functional>
#include <map>
#include <mutex>
#include <string>
#include <unordered_map>
#include <unordered_set>
#include <vector>

#include "nvn_host.h"
#include "nvn_types.h"

namespace nvn {

// ---- logging -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
void Log(const char* fmt, ...);        // only with env NVN_LOG=1
void LogError(const char* fmt, ...);   // always (stderr)

// ---- guest object header ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
enum : uint64_t {
  MAGIC_DEVICE = 0x4e564e4445563031ull, MAGIC_QUEUE = 0x4e564e5155453031ull,
  MAGIC_CB = 0x4e564e4342303031ull, MAGIC_POOL = 0x4e564e504f4f4c31ull,
  MAGIC_TEXTURE = 0x4e564e5445583031ull, MAGIC_SYNC = 0x4e564e53594e4331ull,
  MAGIC_WINDOW = 0x4e564e57494e3031ull, MAGIC_BUFFER = 0x4e564e4255463031ull, MAGIC_PROGRAM = 0x4e564e5052473031ull,
  MAGIC_TEXPOOL = 0x4e564e5450303031ull, MAGIC_SAMPPOOL = 0x4e564e5350303031ull, MAGIC_SAMPLER = 0x4e564e534d503031ull,
};
struct ObjHdr { uint64_t magic; void* impl; };

template <class T>
T* Impl(const void* guest, uint64_t magic) {
  auto* h = static_cast<const ObjHdr*>(guest);
  if (!h || h->magic != magic || !h->impl) return nullptr;
  return static_cast<T*>(h->impl);
}
inline void Bind(void* guest, uint64_t magic, void* impl) {
  auto* h = static_cast<ObjHdr*>(guest);
  h->magic = magic;
  h->impl = impl;
}
inline void Unbind(void* guest) {
  auto* h = static_cast<ObjHdr*>(guest);
  h->magic = 0;
  h->impl = nullptr;
}

// ---- builders (live in guest memory, written in place; must fit kBuilderMax) -------------------------------
struct DeviceBuilder { int flags; };
struct QueueBuilder { void* device; int flags; uint64_t cmdSize, computeSize, ctrlSize; };
struct PoolBuilder { void* device; void* storage; uint64_t size; int flags; };
struct WindowBuilder { void* device; void* native; int count; void* const* textures; };
struct TextureBuilder {  // up to 0x80 bytes
  void* device; int flags, target, width, height, depth, levels, format, samples;
  void* pool; int64_t poolOffset; int stride; const void* packaged;
};
struct BufferBuilder { void* device; void* pool; int64_t offset; uint64_t size; };
struct SamplerBuilder {  // up to 0x60 bytes
  void* device; int minFilter, magFilter, wrap[3]; float lodMin, lodMax, lodBias; int compareMode, compareFunc;
  float border[4]; float aniso; int reduction;
};
// Guest NVNtextureView (0x10 bytes), written in place by TextureViewSet*. flags: 1 levels, 2 layers, 4 format, 8 target,
// 0x10 depth/stencil mode, 0x20 swizzle. [TOTK-NVN] object size 0x10.
struct TexView {
  uint8_t flags, target, format, dsMode, swz[4], lvlBase, lvlNum; uint16_t layerBase, layerNum;
};
static_assert(sizeof(TexView) <= 0x10);
static_assert(sizeof(BufferBuilder) <= kBuilderMax && sizeof(SamplerBuilder) <= 0x60);
static_assert(sizeof(DeviceBuilder) <= kBuilderMax && sizeof(QueueBuilder) <= kBuilderMax &&
              sizeof(PoolBuilder) <= kBuilderMax && sizeof(WindowBuilder) <= kBuilderMax);
static_assert(sizeof(TextureBuilder) <= kTextureBuilderMax);

struct Host;
struct TextureImpl;
struct WindowImpl;
struct QueueImpl;
// A window of an image's mip levels and array layers (all counts >= 1 once clamped).
struct SubRange {
  uint32_t lb = 0, ln = 1, yb = 0, yn = 1;
  bool Overlaps(const SubRange& o) const { return lb < o.lb + o.ln && o.lb < lb + ln && yb < o.yb + o.yn && o.yb < yb + yn; }
};

// ---- format table ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
// kind: 0 float/norm, 1 uint, 2 sint. bytes = bytes per texel, or per block for block-compressed formats (bw x bh texels).
// astcW/astcH != 0: the guest format is ASTC; when vk is not an ASTC format the texture is CPU-decoded (and transcoded to
// BC7 if vk is BC7) at upload time, so bytes/bw/bh then describe the Vulkan format and the guest block size is astcW x astcH.
struct FormatInfo { VkFormat vk; uint32_t bytes; VkImageAspectFlags aspect; uint8_t kind; uint8_t bw = 1, bh = 1, astcW = 0, astcH = 0; bool srgb = false; };
const FormatInfo* LookupFormat(int nvnFormat);  // nullptr if not mapped (logged by the caller)

// ---- recorded commands (Vulkan-free; replayed at submit) ---------------------------------------------------
enum class Op : uint8_t {
  SetRenderTargets, ClearColor, ClearDepthStencil, SetViewports, SetScissors, Barrier,
  // phase 1 (draw state is recorded by value; replay resolves addresses/handles at submit)
  BindProgram, BindBlend, BindColor, BindChannelMask, BindMultisample, BindPolygon, BindDepthStencil,
  BindVertexAttribs, BindVertexStreams, BindVertexBuffers, BindUbo, BindSsbo, BindTexture, BindImage,
  SetTexturePool, SetSamplerPool, StencilValueMask, StencilMask, StencilRef, PolygonOffset,
  Draw, DrawIndexed, CopyBufferToTexture,
  // phase 3
  SetAlphaRef, SetPatchSize, DrawIndirect, DrawIndexedIndirect, Dispatch, CopyTextureToBuffer, CopyTextureToTexture, ReportCounter,
};
struct TexPoolImpl;
struct SampPoolImpl;
struct ProgramImpl;
struct Cmd {
  Op op;
  int i[6] = {};
  float f[4] = {};
  TextureImpl* tex[9] = {};   // SetRenderTargets: colors[0..7], depth at [8]; CopyBufferToTexture: tex[0]
  uint64_t a[4] = {};         // addresses / packed state words / handles
  void* p[2] = {};            // ProgramImpl*, pool impls
  std::vector<uint8_t> blob;  // arrays (vertex attribs, streams, copy region + view)
};
// id = the CommandHandle given to the guest (nvn_life.cpp); refs/submitted are guarded by the list table's mutex.
struct CmdList { std::vector<Cmd> cmds; uint64_t id = 0; int refs = 1; bool submitted = false; };

struct CommandBufferImpl {
  Host* host = nullptr;
  bool recording = false;
  CommandBufferMemoryCallback cb = nullptr;
  void* cbData = nullptr;
  std::vector<Cmd> cmds;
  size_t cmdsHigh = 0;   // [cpuprof] largest recording of this buffer: EndRecording reserves this much in the next vector
  // memory handed to us by the guest (kept for diagnostics; NVN command words are never written)
  uint64_t commandBytes = 0, controlBytes = 0;
};

struct PoolImpl {
  Host* host = nullptr;
  void* storage = nullptr;  // guest pointer == host pointer
  void* guest = nullptr;    // the guest NVNmemoryPool object (returned by BufferGetMemoryPool)
  uint64_t size = 0;
  uint64_t va = 0;          // synthetic GPU virtual address of the pool start (see Host::RegisterPool)
  int flags = 0;
  // Lazy Vulkan mirror (see EnsureBacking)
  VkBuffer buffer = VK_NULL_HANDLE;
  VkDeviceMemory memory = VK_NULL_HANDLE;
  uint8_t* mapped = nullptr;
  // Byte ranges the GPU writes (storage-buffer outputs, e.g. skinning compute). SyncPoolRange skips them: the CPU copy is stale there.
  std::mutex gpuMutex;
  std::vector<std::pair<uint64_t, uint64_t>> gpuRanges;   // [begin, end)
  // Ranges already copied into the mirror during the current SubmitLists (SyncPoolRangeOnce); valid while syncEpoch == g_replayEpoch.
  uint64_t syncEpoch = 0;
  std::vector<std::pair<uint64_t, uint64_t>> synced;
  // Fragment-shader SSBO writes into this CPU pool that are submitted but not yet copied back to guest memory (Readback kind 3).
  std::atomic<int> wbPending{0};
  // SNAP_POOL_LOG=1: bytes of live buffers and textures placed in this pool (sub-allocation arenas), for the B1 null-pool triage
  std::atomic<int64_t> subLive{0}, subPeak{0};
  std::atomic<int> subCount{0};
  // [perf] dirty-page sync (SyncPoolRangeOnce): 0 = not set up, 1 = GetWriteWatch tracks the storage, -1 = unusable (full copies).
  int8_t ww = 0;
  // [cpuprof] one whole-pool dirty snapshot (GetWriteWatch without reset) per replay epoch; a range with no page dirty in it skips its
  // own GetWriteWatch syscall (SNAP_POOLSYNC_SNAPSHOT=0: a syscall per range, as before). Guarded by gpuMutex.
  uint64_t wwSnapEpoch = 0;
  std::vector<uint64_t> wwBits;   // one bit per 4 KiB page of the storage
  std::atomic<bool> wbPool{false};   // has fragment-shader write-backs (photo evaluation): always full copies, as before
  bool Cpu() const { return !(flags & MP_CPU_NO_ACCESS); }
};
bool EnsureBacking(PoolImpl* p);
bool PoolAcctOn();                                   // SNAP_POOL_LOG=1 (nvn_gfx.cpp)
void PoolAcct(PoolImpl* p, uint64_t va, int64_t bytes);   // +bytes when a buffer/texture is placed in p (va = p->va), -bytes at finalize; ignored if p is gone
void PoolAcctDump(const char* why);                  // every pool of 1 MiB or more: size, live, peak, count
// SNAP_ARENA_LOG=1 (nvn_gfx.cpp): the game's GPU arenas (allocator main+0x911fc0): which arena a buffer/texture sits in, per guest
// call-site owner. ArenaAcct returns an owner slot (-1 = not in an arena / off); ArenaUnacct(slot, bytes) at finalize.
bool ArenaAcctOn();

void ArenaUnacct(int slot, int64_t bytes, int born = -1);   // born = present count at creation (lifetime stats)
void ArenaDump(const char* why);

void OwnPoolReap(struct QueueImpl* q);  // called at present under queueMutex: stamps / destroys retired fallback pools
// Copy [off, off+size) of the guest storage into the Vulkan mirror (call before the GPU reads that range).
void SyncPoolRange(PoolImpl* p, uint64_t off, uint64_t size);
// Replay-time variant: copies a range at most once per SubmitLists (the guest is blocked inside the submit, so the CPU bytes cannot change
// between two draws of the same list). Draws that bind the same big buffer range repeatedly used to copy it every time.

// ownPool: the guest passed no memory pool (its GPU arena was full, crash B1) and the host gave the buffer private storage
struct BufferImpl { PoolImpl* pool = nullptr; int64_t offset = 0; uint64_t size = 0; uint64_t acctVa = 0; bool ownPool = false; int arenaSlot = -1; int arenaBorn = 0; };
struct SamplerImpl { Host* host = nullptr; VkSampler sampler = VK_NULL_HANDLE; SamplerBuilder b{}; };
// seq is a sequence lock: odd while TexturePoolRegisterTexture rewrites the slot, so ResolveHandle (replay thread) always copies a
// matching {tex, view} pair (re-registration of a live id during replay used to be able to pair the old texture with the new view).
struct TexSlot { std::atomic<uint32_t> seq{0}; TextureImpl* tex = nullptr; TexView view{}; bool hasView = false; };
// Descriptor table indexed by pool id (20-bit texture / 12-bit sampler handle fields). Loader threads register descriptors while the
// render thread replays draws that read them (on the GPU these are independent descriptor words). An unordered_map here crashed
// about 1.5% of runs: an insert rehashed the buckets under a concurrent find in ResolveHandle (host read of 0x10 inside
// QueueSubmitCommands, guest main+0x904304). Chunks are allocated once and never move, so Find needs no lock.
template <class T> struct SlotTable {
  static constexpr unsigned kChunkBits = 10, kChunk = 1u << kChunkBits, kIds = 1u << 20, kChunks = kIds >> kChunkBits;
  std::atomic<T*> chunks[kChunks] = {};
  SlotTable() = default;
  SlotTable(const SlotTable&) = delete;
  SlotTable& operator=(const SlotTable&) = delete;
  ~SlotTable() { for (auto& c : chunks) delete[] c.load(std::memory_order_relaxed); }
  // nullptr when the id is out of range or its chunk was never written (= never registered)
  T* Find(int id) const {
    if ((unsigned)id >= kIds) return nullptr;
    T* c = chunks[(unsigned)id >> kChunkBits].load(std::memory_order_acquire);
    return c ? &c[(unsigned)id & (kChunk - 1)] : nullptr;
  }
  T* At(int id) {   // the slot for a write (allocates its chunk); nullptr when out of range
    if ((unsigned)id >= kIds) return nullptr;
    std::atomic<T*>& a = chunks[(unsigned)id >> kChunkBits];
    T* c = a.load(std::memory_order_acquire);
    if (!c) {
      T* fresh = new T[kChunk]();
      if (a.compare_exchange_strong(c, fresh, std::memory_order_acq_rel, std::memory_order_acquire)) c = fresh;
      else delete[] fresh;   // another thread installed it first; c now holds that chunk
    }
    return &c[(unsigned)id & (kChunk - 1)];
  }
};
struct TexPoolImpl { Host* host = nullptr; SlotTable<TexSlot> slots; };
struct SampPoolImpl { Host* host = nullptr; SlotTable<SamplerImpl*> slots; };

struct TextureImpl {
  PoolImpl* acctPool = nullptr; uint64_t acctVa = 0; int64_t acctBytes = 0;   // SNAP_POOL_LOG accounting (PoolAcct)
  int arenaSlot = -1; int64_t arenaBytes = 0;                                  // SNAP_ARENA_LOG accounting (ArenaAcct)
  int lastDrawPresent = -10; int drawStreak = 0;   // GetPipeline: consecutive presented frames this texture was drawn to (a pending pipeline may only be skipped for per-frame targets)
  Host* host = nullptr;
  TextureBuilder b{};
  const FormatInfo* fi = nullptr;
  VkImage image = VK_NULL_HANDLE;
  VkDeviceMemory memory = VK_NULL_HANDLE;
  VkImageLayout layout = VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_UNDEFINED;
  uint32_t hostW = 0, hostH = 0;   // image size when render-target scaling applies (0 = same as the guest size)
  float scale = 1.0f;
  uint32_t HW() const { return hostW ? hostW : (uint32_t)b.width; }
  uint32_t HH() const { return hostH ? hostH : (uint32_t)b.height; }
  TextureImpl* abAlt = nullptr; bool abTried = false;   // SNAP_MODS_AB test aid: the original-texture twin of a replaced texture (see ResolveHandle)
  bool uploaded = false;   // contents defined (static data uploaded, copied to, or rendered to)
  uint64_t srcHash = 0, hashSeq = 0;   // CPU-written (linear) pool textures: hash of the guest bytes at the last upload, replay that checked it
  std::unordered_map<std::string, VkImageView> views;   // see TextureImpl::View
  std::unordered_map<VkImageView, VkImageViewType> viewTypes;   // the type each cached view was created with (tests, diagnostics)
  VkImageViewType ViewTypeOf(VkImageView v) const { auto it = viewTypes.find(v); return it == viewTypes.end() ? VK_IMAGE_VIEW_TYPE_MAX_ENUM : it->second; }
  // Per-subresource layouts. `layout` is the layout of every subresource while subLayout is empty; after a ranged transition
  // subLayout holds one entry per (layer * imgLevels + level) and `layout` is meaningless until it collapses again.
  std::vector<VkImageLayout> subLayout;
  uint32_t imgLevels = 1, imgLayers = 1;   // of the VkImage (set by EnsureImage)
  VkImageCreateFlags ci_flags = 0;         // flags the VkImage was created with
  TextureImpl* bcShadow = nullptr;
  TextureImpl* xferShadow = nullptr;   // scaled texture: guest-size stand-in for guest-resolution copies (nvn_xfer.cpp), freed with it
  uint32_t bcSubLevel = 0, bcSubLayer = 0;  // on a bcShadow: the level / layer of the BC texture it stands in for          // block-compressed render target: the uncompressed stand-in drawn into (RedirectCompressedTargets)
  bool EnsureImage();
  uint32_t LevelW(uint32_t l) const { return std::max(1u, HW() >> l); }
  uint32_t LevelH(uint32_t l) const { return std::max(1u, HH() >> l); }
  // Subresource range (level/layer window) a TexView selects, clamped to the image.
  SubRange RangeOf(const TexView* v) const;
  // Image view for a TexView (nullptr = the whole texture); sampled = true gives a view usable in a descriptor
  // (single aspect: depth for depth/stencil formats unless the view asks for stencil). shaderType is the translated
  // shader's SamplerType (0 = use the texture's own target): the view type follows the shader's declared dimension and
  // arrayness. `range` overrides the level/layer window of the TexView; nullptr means v's own window. Returns
  // VK_NULL_HANDLE when the texture cannot be viewed as the shader's type (the caller binds a dummy of that type).
  VkImageView View(const TexView* v, bool sampled, int shaderType = 0, const SubRange* range = nullptr);
  // Attachment view: one level, `layers` layers from the view's base, the texture's own format.
  VkImageView RenderView(const TexView* v, SubRange* out = nullptr);
};

// Manifest of one translated stage (see scripts/shader_harness/Program.cs, --nvn mode).
struct MCb { int slot, set, binding; };

struct StageProg {
  bool valid = false;
  char key[16] = {};                   // first 12 hex digits of the translation cache key (draw log)
  char fkey[72] = {};                  // the full translation cache key (nvn_pipeline.cpp reloads the stage from the cache by it)
  int stage = 0;                       // NVN stage: 0 VS 1 FS 2 GS 3 TCS 4 TES 5 CS
  VkShaderModule mod = VK_NULL_HANDLE;
  std::vector<MCb> cb;
  std::vector<MSb> sb;
  std::vector<MTex> tex, img;
  int fragOutputMap = 0;
  std::vector<uint32_t> spv;                      // kept for the fragment stage only (alpha-test patching)
  // fragment module variants (alpha test, output rewrite): key = alphaFunc | nColor << 4 | dual << 8 -> {module, has alpha spec constant}
  std::map<uint32_t, std::pair<VkShaderModule, bool>> fragMods;
  uint32_t inputMask = 0xFFFFFFFFu;    // vertex stage: input locations the shader reads
  std::vector<int> outLocs;            // fragment stage: color output locations, ascending
  VkBuffer constBuf = VK_NULL_HANDLE;  // c[1]: the program's constant-data blob (data section tail)
  VkDeviceMemory constMem = VK_NULL_HANDLE;
  uint64_t constSize = 0;
};
struct ShaderData { uint64_t data; const void* control; };   // [TOTK-NVN] NVNshaderData: {address, control*}
struct ProgramImpl {

  bool setUsed[4] = {};

};

// ---- replay context (shared by nvn_vk.cpp and nvn_draw.cpp) -----------------------------------------------------
struct DrawState;
struct ScratchBuf {
  VkBuffer buf = VK_NULL_HANDLE; VkDeviceMemory mem = VK_NULL_HANDLE;
  uint64_t cap = 0; uint32_t usage = 0; uint8_t* map = nullptr;   // [perf] recyclable when cap != 0 (NewScratch / ReleaseScratch)
};
// GPU -> guest memory transfer finished after a timeline value completes (CopyTextureToBuffer, ReportCounter).
struct Readback {
  VkSemaphore sem = VK_NULL_HANDLE; uint64_t value = 0;
  ScratchBuf sb; uint8_t* map = nullptr;
  uint8_t* dst = nullptr; uint64_t size = 0;
  int kind = 0;           // 0 raw copy, 1 counter report: map = [timestamp ticks][n occlusion results], dst = {counter, timestamp ns}
                          // 3 shader write-back: map = the pool's mapped mirror (no scratch), expect = guest bytes when the GPU took them
  int counterType = 0; uint32_t nOcc = 0;
  struct PoolImpl* pool = nullptr; uint64_t poolOff = 0;   // kind 3
  std::vector<uint8_t> expect;                            // kind 3: the CPU changed the range since the submit if the guest bytes differ
  std::string dumpPath;   // kind 2: debug dump of a texture to this file (NVN_RT_DUMP)
};
struct ReplayCtx {
  Host* h = nullptr;
  VkCommandBuffer cb = VK_NULL_HANDLE;
  QueueImpl* q = nullptr;
  std::vector<VkDescriptorPool>* pools = nullptr;   // descriptor pools used by this command buffer (recycled on reap)
  std::vector<Readback>* readbacks = nullptr;      // moved to Host::readbacks with the submit's timeline value
  bool occOpen = false;                            // an occlusion query is open in the current rendering scope
  std::vector<ScratchBuf>* scratch = nullptr;       // staging/scratch buffers freed when this command buffer retires
  TextureImpl* rt[9] = {};
  TexView rtView[9] = {};          // the NVNtextureView given to SetRenderTargets (level / layer selection)
  bool rtHasView[9] = {};
  TextureImpl* bcDst[8] = {};      // rt[k] is the bcShadow of this block-compressed texture; copied into it when a scope ends
  bool bcDirty = false;
  bool rendering = false;
  bool vpSet = false, scSet = false;
  // guest (unscaled) viewport / scissor 0..3 as last set, re-applied when SetRenderTargets changes the render scale (the game
  // often sets them before binding targets, so a value scaled for the previous target would land in a corner of a scaled one)
  float vpGuest[4][4] = {}; int scGuest[4][4] = {}; uint8_t vpHave = 0, scHave = 0; float vpScale = 1.0f, scScale = 1.0f;
  DrawState* ds = nullptr;
};

struct Host {

  bool validation = false;

  // Synthetic GPU address space: every memory pool gets a range [va, va+size); NVN buffer addresses are
  // poolVa + offset, and replay maps an address back to (pool, offset) with ResolveAddress.

  void UnregisterPool(PoolImpl* p);
  bool ResolveAddress(uint64_t addr, PoolImpl** pool, uint64_t* off);
  std::string cacheDir;                       // shader SPIR-V cache + VkPipelineCache file
  std::mutex pipeMutex;
  std::unordered_map<std::string, VkPipeline> pipelines;
  uint64_t nextProgramId = 1;
  std::mutex compMutex;                       // composite programs (ProgramResolve), keyed by the source program id per stage
  std::map<std::array<uint64_t, 6>, ProgramImpl*> composites;
  VkPipelineLayout clearLayout = VK_NULL_HANDLE;   // masked-clear pipeline layout
  std::vector<VkShaderModule> variantMods;    // patched fragment modules (alpha test / output rewrite); freed at shutdown, guarded by pipeMutex
  struct Dummies* dummies = nullptr;          // fallback resources for unbound descriptors (nvn_draw.cpp)
  // queries (nvn_xfer.cpp): timestamps and samples-passed counters
  VkQueryPool tsPool = VK_NULL_HANDLE, occPool = VK_NULL_HANDLE;
  uint32_t tsNext = 0, occNext = 0, occReported = 0;
  bool hostQueryReset = false;                // feature enabled (core 1.2); without it the query pools are never created
  bool wantSamples = false;                   // a SAMPLES_PASSED report has been recorded: wrap rendering scopes in queries
  uint64_t samplesTotal = 0;                  // running samples-passed counter (CPU side)
  std::mutex rbMutex;
  std::vector<Readback> readbacks;
  // host policy (nvn_host.h): render-target scale, anisotropy override
  float renderScale = 1.0f;
  float anisoOverride = 0.0f;

  bool Init(bool wantValidation);
  void Shutdown();
  uint32_t FindMemoryType(uint32_t typeBits, VkMemoryPropertyFlags want, VkMemoryPropertyFlags avoid = 0) const;
};

// Render-target resolution policy (nvn_entry.cpp). Consulted once per TextureInitialize; off (scale 1) by default.
struct ScalePolicy {
  struct Exempt { int w, h, fmt; bool depthOnly; };   // w/h/fmt == -1 match anything
  float scale = 1.0f;
  std::vector<Exempt> exempt;
  std::vector<uint32_t> exemptTags;
  uint32_t nextTag = 0;                               // consumed by the next TextureInitialize
  int shadowRes = 0;                                  // 0 = original; else side of the 1024x1024 depth shadow maps
  bool scaleDisplay = true;                           // window (DISPLAY) textures follow the scale too, else the output stays 1080p
  float displayScale = 0.0f;                          // [upscale] > 0: window textures take this scale (the upscaler's output), not `scale`
  ScalePolicy();
  float For(const TextureBuilder& b, uint32_t tag) const;   // 1.0 when the texture is not scaled
};
extern ScalePolicy g_scale;

extern bool g_lodBiasAuto;      // SNAP_LOD_BIAS=auto: -log2(render scale)
extern void ApplyHostEnvPolicy();   // SNAP_ANISO, SNAP_LOD_BIAS, SNAP_RENDER_SCALE, SNAP_SHADOW_RES (called from DeviceInitialize)
extern float g_anisoOverride;   // 0 = off; else forced max anisotropy for mipmapped, non-compare samplers
extern double g_paceHz;          // rate of present interval 1; 0 = display-paced only

// Subresource a render target view selects (level, first layer, layer count) -- attachments are one level.
SubRange RtRange(const TextureImpl* t, const TexView* v);   // nvn_vk.cpp
// Host-visible TRANSFER_SRC buffer owned by the replaying command buffer (freed when it retires). nvn_vk.cpp
uint8_t* NewScratch(ReplayCtx& cx, uint64_t size, VkBuffer* buf, VkBufferUsageFlags extra = 0);

// Uploads packaged/pool-resident static texture data (deswizzle, ASTC fallback) into the image; leaves it in

// [perf] VkImage + memory for a builder at host size hw x hh (nvn_vk.cpp; TextureImpl::EnsureImage and the prefetch workers)
struct TexImage { VkImage image = VK_NULL_HANDLE; VkDeviceMemory memory = VK_NULL_HANDLE; uint32_t levels = 1, layers = 1; VkImageCreateFlags flags = 0; };
bool CreateTexImage(Host* host, const TextureBuilder& b, const FormatInfo* fi, uint32_t hw, uint32_t hh, TexImage& out);
bool TexPrefetchTakeImage(TextureImpl* t);   // nvn_tex_vk.cpp: EnsureImage adopts a prefetch worker's image (SNAP_UPLOAD_PREFETCH_IMAGE=1 = on)
void TexPrefetchShutdown();                  // Host::Shutdown: drop staged jobs (and their images) before the device goes
void ScratchPoolDrain(Host* h);              // Host::Shutdown: destroy the recycled scratch buffers (nvn_vk.cpp)
// NVN window-origin -> Vulkan viewport. NVN follows OpenGL clip control: NDC +y is up in both origin modes and window row
// 0 is memory row 0 (the viewport and scissor y are rows from the window origin). Vulkan's NDC +y points down, so
// UPPER_LEFT needs a negative-height viewport: NDC +1 lands on the first row of the viewport rectangle, which is the
// image top. LOWER_LEFT keeps the rectangle's rows as given (row 0 is the image bottom by convention, never presented
// flipped). Scissors are plain window rectangles in both modes. `scale` is the render-target scale (1 = original).
inline VkViewport MakeNvnViewport(int originMode, float x, float y, float w, float h, float scale = 1.0f) {
  x *= scale; y *= scale; w *= scale; h *= scale;
  if (originMode == ORIGIN_UPPER_LEFT) return VkViewport{x, y + h, w, -h, 0.0f, 1.0f};
  return VkViewport{x, y, w, h, 0.0f, 1.0f};
}

  LS_PIPE_SKIP, LS_BC_RECREATE, LS_AA_RESIZE, LS_CUBE_COPY, LS_FLUSH_GPU_OVERLAP, LS_CLEAR_SCISSORED, LS_X_ALPHA_VIEWS, LS_BACKING_RACE,
  LS_COUNT
};
```

`runtime/nvn/nvn_life.cpp`:

```cpp
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Object lifetime against the GPU timeline (analysis/core/review_nvn.md findings 1-4 and 10, worker nvnfix, 2026-11-13).
//  - Command list handles: CommandBufferEndRecording returns an id, not a heap pointer. A submit resolves ids through a table, so a handle
//    whose list was already freed is skipped and counted instead of replaying freed memory, and the same handle twice in one submit (or
//    again while in flight) takes a second reference instead of a double delete.
//  - Graveyard: finalized textures, samplers, memory pools, texture / sampler pools and programs are destroyed only after the queue
//    timeline passes the last submit made before they were retired (the same stamp-at-present rule as OwnPoolReap). Before they are
//    freed, texture / sampler pool slots that still point at them are nulled and the queue's persistent draw state forgets them.
//  - SNAP_NVN_STATS=1: one "[nvnstats]" line every 300 presents with the counters below (measurement only, no behavior change).
#define NOMINMAX
#define WIN32_LEAN_AND_MEAN
#include <windows.h>

#include <algorithm>
#include <cstdlib>
#include <unordered_set>

#include "nvn_internal.h"

namespace nvn {

std::atomic<uint64_t> g_lifeStat[LS_COUNT];

static const char* const kLifeStatName[LS_COUNT] = {
  "resubmit", "staleHandle", "listsMade", "retired", "destroyed", "slotsCleared", "persistScrub", "rbWaitPoolGone",
  "pipeSkip", "bcRecreate", "aaResize", "cubeCopy", "flushGpuOverlap", "clearScissored", "xAlphaViews", "backingRace",
};

// ---- command list handles ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
namespace {
std::mutex g_listMu;
std::unordered_map<uint64_t, CmdList*> g_lists;
uint64_t g_nextList = 0x10000;
}  // namespace

CommandHandle ListRegister(CmdList* l) {
  std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lk(g_listMu);
  l->id = g_nextList++;
  g_lists[l->id] = l;
  LifeCount(LS_LISTS_MADE);
  return l->id;
}

void ListAcquire(int n, const CommandHandle* handles, CmdList** out) {
  std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lk(g_listMu);
  for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
    auto it = g_lists.find(handles[i]);
    if (it == g_lists.end()) {
      out[i] = nullptr;
      static int logged = 0;
      if (logged++ < 8) LogError("QueueSubmitCommands: handle 0x%llx is not a live command list (already retired or never recorded): skipped",
                                 (unsigned long long)handles[i]);
      LifeCount(LS_STALE_HANDLE);
      continue;
    }
    CmdList* l = it->second;
    if (l->submitted) { l->refs++; LifeCount(LS_RESUBMIT); }   // same handle again (in this call or still in flight): one more reference
    else l->submitted = true;                                  // the recording's reference moves to its first submit
    out[i] = l;
  }
}

// [cpuprof 2026-11-13] Recycled command vectors: EndRecording moved the buffer's vector into the list, so every recording grew a fresh
// vector from empty (vector<Cmd>::_Emplace_reallocate + malloc were ~25% of the NVN recording thread mt_asyc_dispatcher_owner_worker).
// A released list's vector is cleared (capacity kept) and handed to the next EndRecording. SNAP_NVN_CMD_RECYCLE=0 restores the old path.
static const bool kCmdRecycle = [] { const char* e = getenv("SNAP_NVN_CMD_RECYCLE"); return !(e && *e == '0'); }();
static std::mutex g_cmdVecMu;
static std::vector<std::vector<Cmd>> g_cmdVecs;
void CmdVecTake(std::vector<Cmd>& out, size_t want) {
  if (kCmdRecycle) {
    std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lk(g_cmdVecMu);
    if (!g_cmdVecs.empty()) { out.swap(g_cmdVecs.back()); g_cmdVecs.pop_back(); }
  }
  if (kCmdRecycle && out.capacity() < want) out.reserve(want);
}
void CmdVecGive(std::vector<Cmd>& v) {
  if (!kCmdRecycle || v.capacity() == 0 || v.capacity() > (1u << 16)) return;
  v.clear();   // destroys the commands (their blobs) outside the pool lock; keeps the capacity
  std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lk(g_cmdVecMu);
  if (g_cmdVecs.size() < 64) { g_cmdVecs.emplace_back(); g_cmdVecs.back().swap(v); }
}

void ListRelease(CmdList* l) {
  if (!l) return;
  {
    std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lk(g_listMu);
    if (--l->refs > 0) return;
    g_lists.erase(l->id);
  }
  CmdVecGive(l->cmds);
  delete l;
}

static size_t ListsLive() { std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lk(g_listMu); return g_lists.size(); }

// ---- live descriptor pools (scanned when a texture or sampler they may still name is freed) ------------------------------------
namespace {
std::mutex g_regMu;
std::vector<TexPoolImpl*> g_texPools;
std::vector<SampPoolImpl*> g_sampPools;
template <class T> void RegSet(std::vector<T*>& v, T* p, bool live) {
  std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lk(g_regMu);
  auto it = std::find(v.begin(), v.end(), p);
  if (live && it == v.end()) v.push_back(p);
  if (!live && it != v.end()) v.erase(it);
}
}  // namespace
void TexPoolLive(TexPoolImpl* p, bool live) { RegSet(g_texPools, p, live); }
void SampPoolLive(SampPoolImpl* p, bool live) { RegSet(g_sampPools, p, live); }

// ---- graveyard ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
namespace {
struct Grave { GraveKind k; void* obj; uint64_t value; };   // value 0 = not stamped yet
std::mutex g_graveMu2;
std::vector<Grave> g_graves;

void DestroyNow(const Grave& g) {
  switch (g.k) {
    case GK_TEXTURE: DestroyTexture(static_cast<TextureImpl*>(g.obj)); break;
    case GK_SAMPLER: {
      auto* s = static_cast<SamplerImpl*>(g.obj);
      if (s->host && s->host->device && s->sampler) vkDestroySampler(s->host->device, s->sampler, nullptr);
      delete s;
      break;
    }
    case GK_POOL: DestroyPool(static_cast<PoolImpl*>(g.obj)); break;
    case GK_TEXPOOL: delete static_cast<TexPoolImpl*>(g.obj); break;
    case GK_SAMPPOOL: delete static_cast<SampPoolImpl*>(g.obj); break;
    case GK_PROGRAM: { auto* p = static_cast<ProgramImpl*>(g.obj); ProgramDestroy(p); delete p; break; }
    case GK_FN: { auto* f = static_cast<std::function<void()>*>(g.obj); (*f)(); delete f; break; }
  }
  LifeCount(LS_DESTROYED);
}

// Null every live pool slot that names a texture / sampler about to be freed. Runs under queueMutex (no replay reads the tables
// meanwhile); loader threads may register concurrently, so texture slots use the TexSlot sequence lock and sampler slots a CAS.
void ScrubSlots(const std::unordered_set<const void*>& deadTex, const std::unordered_set<const void*>& deadSamp) {
  std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lk(g_regMu);
  uint64_t n = 0;
  if (!deadTex.empty())
    for (TexPoolImpl* tp : g_texPools)
      for (auto& ch : tp->slots.chunks) {
        TexSlot* c = ch.load(std::memory_order_acquire);
        if (!c) continue;
        for (unsigned i = 0; i < SlotTable<TexSlot>::kChunk; i++) {
          TexSlot& s = c[i];
          if (!s.tex || !deadTex.count(s.tex)) continue;
          uint32_t q = s.seq.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
          for (;;) {
            if (!(q & 1) && s.seq.compare_exchange_weak(q, q + 1, std::memory_order_acquire, std::memory_order_relaxed)) break;
            YieldProcessor();
            q = s.seq.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
          }
          std::atomic_thread_fence(std::memory_order_release);
          if (s.tex && deadTex.count(s.tex)) { s.tex = nullptr; s.hasView = false; n++; }   // re-check: a registration may have replaced it
          s.seq.store(q + 2, std::memory_order_release);
        }
      }
  if (!deadSamp.empty())
    for (SampPoolImpl* sp : g_sampPools)
      for (auto& ch : sp->slots.chunks) {
        SamplerImpl** c = ch.load(std::memory_order_acquire);
        if (!c) continue;
        for (unsigned i = 0; i < SlotTable<SamplerImpl*>::kChunk; i++) {
          SamplerImpl* cur = __atomic_load_n(&c[i], __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE);
          if (!cur || !deadSamp.count(cur)) continue;
          if (__atomic_compare_exchange_n(&c[i], &cur, (SamplerImpl*)nullptr, false, __ATOMIC_ACQ_REL, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE)) n++;
        }
      }
  if (n) LifeCount(LS_SLOTS_CLEARED, n);
}
}  // namespace

void Retire(GraveKind k, void* obj) {
  if (!obj) return;
  std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lk(g_graveMu2);
  g_graves.push_back({k, obj, 0});
  LifeCount(LS_RETIRED);
}

void RetireFn(std::function<void()> fn) { if (fn) Retire(GK_FN, new std::function<void()>(std::move(fn))); }

void GraveReap(QueueImpl* q) {
  if (!q || !q->host) return;
  std::vector<Grave> dead;
  {
    std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lk(g_graveMu2);
    if (g_graves.empty()) return;
    uint64_t done = 0;
    vkGetSemaphoreCounterValue(q->host->device, q->timeline, &done);
    size_t keep = 0;
    for (auto& g : g_graves) {
      if (!g.value) { g.value = q->value ? q->value : 1; g_graves[keep++] = g; }   // every submit that can use it is <= this value
      else if (g.value <= done) dead.push_back(g);
      else g_graves[keep++] = g;
    }
    g_graves.resize(keep);
  }
  if (dead.empty()) return;
  std::unordered_set<const void*> all, deadTex, deadSamp;
  for (auto& g : dead) {
    all.insert(g.obj);
    if (g.k == GK_TEXTURE) deadTex.insert(g.obj);
    if (g.k == GK_SAMPLER) deadSamp.insert(g.obj);
  }
  ScrubSlots(deadTex, deadSamp);
  PersistScrub(q, all);
  for (auto& g : dead) DestroyNow(g);
}

void GraveDrain(Host* h) {   // Host::Shutdown after vkDeviceWaitIdle: nothing is in flight any more
  (void)h;
  std::vector<Grave> all;
  { std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lk(g_graveMu2); all.swap(g_graves); }
  for (auto& g : all) DestroyNow(g);
}

// ---- memory pool finalize --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The guest frees the pool's storage right after MemoryPoolFinalize. Readbacks still in flight that land in that storage (shader
// write-backs, CopyTextureToBuffer, counters) are completed now, while the storage is still valid; the Vulkan mirror waits for the timeline.
void PoolRetire(PoolImpl* p) {
  if (!p) return;
  TexPrefetchPoolGone(p);   // [perf] no prefetch job may read the storage after this
  Host* h = p->host;
  if (h) {
    h->UnregisterPool(p);   // no later replay resolves an address into it
    bool wait = p->wbPending.load(std::memory_order_relaxed) > 0;
    if (!wait && p->storage) {
      const uint8_t* b = static_cast<const uint8_t*>(p->storage);
      std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lk(h->rbMutex);
      for (auto& rb : h->readbacks)
        if (rb.pool == p || (rb.dst && rb.dst >= b && rb.dst < b + p->size)) { wait = true; break; }
    }
    if (wait) { LifeCount(LS_RB_WAIT_POOL_GONE); FlushReadbacks(h, true); }
  }
  Retire(GK_POOL, p);
}

// ---- stats -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
void LifeStatsTick() {
  static const bool on = [] { const char* e = getenv("SNAP_NVN_STATS"); return e && atoi(e) > 0; }();
  if (!on || g_presentCount % 300 != 0) return;
  char line[1024];
  int o = snprintf(line, sizeof line, "[nvnstats] p%d listsLive=%zu graves=%zu", g_presentCount, ListsLive(),
                   [] { std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lk(g_graveMu2); return g_graves.size(); }());
  for (int i = 0; i < LS_COUNT && o > 0 && o < (int)sizeof line - 40; i++)
    o += snprintf(line + o, sizeof line - o, " %s=%llu", kLifeStatName[i], (unsigned long long)g_lifeStat[i].load(std::memory_order_relaxed));
  fprintf(stderr, "%s\n", line);
  fflush(stderr);
}

}  // namespace nvn
```
