`runtime/nvn/upscale/upscale_xess.cpp`:

```cpp
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Intel XeSS Super Resolution through libxess.dll (XeSS SDK 3.0.2, Intel Simplified Software License; local copy in
// tools\intel\, git-ignored, copied beside the exe by host/build_snap.py). No Intel header is compiled in: the few types
// and entry points used are declared here from the SDK's documented C ABI (xess.h, xess_vk.h). On non-Intel GPUs XeSS runs
// its DP4a path.
// Adapted from the Astral Chain PC recomp, runtime/vk_xess.c (MIT, Copyright (c) 2026 Valiantsin Dzerakh, commit e858fc6;
// see THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md): the ABI declarations, the device feature check and the quality pick.
#ifndef NOMINMAX
#define NOMINMAX
#endif
#include <windows.h>

#include <chrono>
#include <cstring>

#include "upscaler.h"

namespace snap_upscale::xess {
namespace {

typedef int XessResult;   // xess_result_t: 0 success, 1..2 warnings, negative errors
inline bool XessOk(XessResult r) { return r >= 0; }
struct XessCtx;
typedef XessCtx* XessHandle;
struct XessVersion { uint16_t major, minor, patch, reserved; };
struct Xess2d { uint32_t x, y; };
enum { XESS_QUALITY_FIRST = 100, XESS_QUALITY_LAST_SCALED = 105, XESS_QUALITY_AA = 106 };
enum { XESS_FLAG_INVERTED_DEPTH = 1 << 1, XESS_FLAG_LDR = 1 << 6, XESS_FLAG_AUTOEXPOSURE = 1 << 8 };
enum { XESS_LOG_DEBUG, XESS_LOG_INFO, XESS_LOG_WARNING, XESS_LOG_ERROR };
struct XessView { VkImageView imageView; VkImage image; VkImageSubresourceRange subresourceRange; VkFormat format; unsigned width, height; };
struct XessExec {
  XessView color, velocity, depth, exposure, responsive, output;
  float jitterX, jitterY, exposureScale;
  uint32_t resetHistory, inputWidth, inputHeight;
  Xess2d colorBase, mvBase, depthBase, responsiveBase, reserved0, outputBase;
};
struct XessInit {
  Xess2d outputResolution; int qualitySetting; uint32_t initFlags, creationNodeMask, visibleNodeMask;
  VkDeviceMemory tempBufferHeap; uint64_t bufferHeapOffset; VkDeviceMemory tempTextureHeap; uint64_t textureHeapOffset;
  VkPipelineCache pipelineCache;
};
static_assert(sizeof(XessView) == 48, "xess_vk_image_view_info layout");
static_assert(sizeof(XessExec) == 6 * 48 + 24 + 6 * 8, "xess_vk_execute_params_t layout");
static_assert(sizeof(XessInit) == 64, "xess_vk_init_params_t layout");

typedef void (*XessLogFn)(const char* message, int level);
typedef XessResult (*PFN_GetVersion)(XessVersion*);
typedef XessResult (*PFN_InstExts)(uint32_t*, const char* const**, uint32_t*);
typedef XessResult (*PFN_DevExts)(VkInstance, VkPhysicalDevice, uint32_t*, const char* const**);
typedef XessResult (*PFN_DevFeats)(VkInstance, VkPhysicalDevice, void**);
typedef XessResult (*PFN_Create)(VkInstance, VkPhysicalDevice, VkDevice, XessHandle*);
typedef XessResult (*PFN_Build)(XessHandle, VkPipelineCache, bool, uint32_t);
typedef XessResult (*PFN_Init)(XessHandle, const XessInit*);
typedef XessResult (*PFN_Execute)(XessHandle, VkCommandBuffer, const XessExec*);
typedef XessResult (*PFN_Destroy)(XessHandle);
typedef XessResult (*PFN_SetLog)(XessHandle, int, XessLogFn);
typedef XessResult (*PFN_Optimal)(XessHandle, const Xess2d*, int, Xess2d*, Xess2d*, Xess2d*);

struct State {
  HMODULE lib = nullptr;
  PFN_GetVersion version = nullptr; PFN_InstExts instExts = nullptr; PFN_DevExts devExts = nullptr; PFN_DevFeats devFeats = nullptr;
  PFN_Create create = nullptr; PFN_Build build = nullptr; PFN_Init init = nullptr; PFN_Execute execute = nullptr;
  PFN_Destroy destroy = nullptr; PFN_SetLog setLog = nullptr; PFN_Optimal optimal = nullptr;
  bool tried = false, loaded = false, deviceOk = false, failed = false;
  DeviceCtx dc;
  XessHandle ctx = nullptr;
  uint32_t w = 0, h = 0, ow = 0, oh = 0, flags = 0; int quality = 0;
  uint64_t evals = 0;
} X;

void OnLog(const char* message, int level) { if (level >= XESS_LOG_WARNING) Logf("xess: %s: %s", level >= XESS_LOG_ERROR ? "error" : "warning", message); }
bool Fail(const char* what, XessResult r) { Logf("xess: %s failed (%d): XeSS off for this run", what, r); X.failed = true; return false; }

// The feature structures XeSS may ask for that this device setup can satisfy: the core 1.0-1.3 ones (upscale.cpp enables
// every supported core feature while an upscaler is wanted) and VK_EXT_mutable_descriptor_type (chained by upscale.cpp).
bool KnownFeature(VkStructureType s, size_t* size) {
#define FS(stype, type) case VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_##stype: *size = sizeof(type); return true;
  switch (s) {
    FS(PHYSICAL_DEVICE_FEATURES_2, VkPhysicalDeviceFeatures2)
    FS(PHYSICAL_DEVICE_VULKAN_1_1_FEATURES, VkPhysicalDeviceVulkan11Features)
    FS(PHYSICAL_DEVICE_VULKAN_1_2_FEATURES, VkPhysicalDeviceVulkan12Features)
    FS(PHYSICAL_DEVICE_VULKAN_1_3_FEATURES, VkPhysicalDeviceVulkan13Features)
    FS(PHYSICAL_DEVICE_16BIT_STORAGE_FEATURES, VkPhysicalDevice16BitStorageFeatures)
    FS(PHYSICAL_DEVICE_8BIT_STORAGE_FEATURES, VkPhysicalDevice8BitStorageFeatures)
    FS(PHYSICAL_DEVICE_SHADER_FLOAT16_INT8_FEATURES, VkPhysicalDeviceShaderFloat16Int8Features)
    FS(PHYSICAL_DEVICE_SHADER_INTEGER_DOT_PRODUCT_FEATURES, VkPhysicalDeviceShaderIntegerDotProductFeatures)
    FS(PHYSICAL_DEVICE_SUBGROUP_SIZE_CONTROL_FEATURES, VkPhysicalDeviceSubgroupSizeControlFeatures)
    FS(PHYSICAL_DEVICE_SHADER_SUBGROUP_EXTENDED_TYPES_FEATURES, VkPhysicalDeviceShaderSubgroupExtendedTypesFeatures)
    FS(PHYSICAL_DEVICE_DESCRIPTOR_INDEXING_FEATURES, VkPhysicalDeviceDescriptorIndexingFeatures)
    FS(PHYSICAL_DEVICE_SCALAR_BLOCK_LAYOUT_FEATURES, VkPhysicalDeviceScalarBlockLayoutFeatures)
    FS(PHYSICAL_DEVICE_TIMELINE_SEMAPHORE_FEATURES, VkPhysicalDeviceTimelineSemaphoreFeatures)
    FS(PHYSICAL_DEVICE_BUFFER_DEVICE_ADDRESS_FEATURES, VkPhysicalDeviceBufferDeviceAddressFeatures)
    FS(PHYSICAL_DEVICE_VULKAN_MEMORY_MODEL_FEATURES, VkPhysicalDeviceVulkanMemoryModelFeatures)
    FS(PHYSICAL_DEVICE_HOST_QUERY_RESET_FEATURES, VkPhysicalDeviceHostQueryResetFeatures)
    FS(PHYSICAL_DEVICE_SYNCHRONIZATION_2_FEATURES, VkPhysicalDeviceSynchronization2Features)
    FS(PHYSICAL_DEVICE_DYNAMIC_RENDERING_FEATURES, VkPhysicalDeviceDynamicRenderingFeatures)
    FS(PHYSICAL_DEVICE_MAINTENANCE_4_FEATURES, VkPhysicalDeviceMaintenance4Features)
    FS(PHYSICAL_DEVICE_SHADER_DEMOTE_TO_HELPER_INVOCATION_FEATURES, VkPhysicalDeviceShaderDemoteToHelperInvocationFeatures)
    FS(PHYSICAL_DEVICE_MUTABLE_DESCRIPTOR_TYPE_FEATURES_EXT, VkPhysicalDeviceMutableDescriptorTypeFeaturesEXT)
    default: return false;
  }
#undef FS
}

bool FeatureSupported(VkPhysicalDevice pd, const VkBaseOutStructure* want, size_t size) {
  alignas(16) uint8_t have[1024];
  if (size > sizeof have) return false;
  memset(have, 0, size);
  ((VkBaseOutStructure*)have)->sType = want->sType;
  VkPhysicalDeviceFeatures2 f2{VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_PHYSICAL_DEVICE_FEATURES_2};
  const bool isF2 = want->sType == VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_PHYSICAL_DEVICE_FEATURES_2;
  if (!isF2) f2.pNext = have;
  vkGetPhysicalDeviceFeatures2(pd, &f2);
  const VkBool32* w = (const VkBool32*)((const uint8_t*)want + sizeof(VkBaseOutStructure));
  const VkBool32* h = isF2 ? (const VkBool32*)&f2.features : (const VkBool32*)(have + sizeof(VkBaseOutStructure));
  const size_t n = (size - sizeof(VkBaseOutStructure)) / sizeof(VkBool32);
  for (size_t i = 0; i < n; i++)
    if (w[i] && !h[i]) { Logf("xess: the device lacks feature %zu of structure %d", i, (int)want->sType); return false; }
  return true;
}

bool Listed(const std::vector<const char*>& v, const char* s) { for (auto* e : v) if (!strcmp(e, s)) return true; return false; }

int PickQuality(uint32_t w, uint32_t h, uint32_t ow, uint32_t oh) {
  if (w >= ow && h >= oh) return XESS_QUALITY_AA;
  int best = 0; uint32_t bestD = ~0u;
  Xess2d out{ow, oh};
  for (int q = XESS_QUALITY_FIRST; X.optimal && q <= XESS_QUALITY_LAST_SCALED; q++) {
    Xess2d opt{}, lo{}, hi{};
    if (!XessOk(X.optimal(X.ctx, &out, q, &opt, &lo, &hi))) continue;
    if (w < lo.x || h < lo.y || w > hi.x || h > hi.y) continue;
    const uint32_t d = opt.x > w ? opt.x - w : w - opt.x;
    if (d < bestD) { best = q; bestD = d; }
  }
  if (best) return best;
  const double r = (double)ow / w;
  return r >= 2.65 ? 100 : r >= 2.15 ? 101 : r >= 1.85 ? 102 : r >= 1.6 ? 103 : r >= 1.4 ? 104 : 105;
}

double NowMs() { return std::chrono::duration<double, std::milli>(std::chrono::steady_clock::now().time_since_epoch()).count(); }

}  // namespace

bool Load() {
  if (X.tried) return X.loaded;
  X.tried = true;
  char path[MAX_PATH + 32] = {};
  DWORD len = GetModuleFileNameA(nullptr, path, MAX_PATH);
  while (len && path[len - 1] != '\\') len--;
  strcpy(path + len, "libxess.dll");
  X.lib = LoadLibraryA(path);
  if (!X.lib) { Logf("xess: cannot load %s: XeSS unavailable", path); return false; }
#define FN(f, name) X.f = (decltype(X.f))(void*)GetProcAddress(X.lib, name)
  FN(version, "xessGetVersion"); FN(instExts, "xessVKGetRequiredInstanceExtensions"); FN(devExts, "xessVKGetRequiredDeviceExtensions");
  FN(devFeats, "xessVKGetRequiredDeviceFeatures"); FN(create, "xessVKCreateContext"); FN(build, "xessVKBuildPipelines");
  FN(init, "xessVKInit"); FN(execute, "xessVKExecute"); FN(destroy, "xessDestroyContext"); FN(setLog, "xessSetLoggingCallback");
  FN(optimal, "xessGetOptimalInputResolution");
#undef FN
  if (!X.version || !X.instExts || !X.devExts || !X.devFeats || !X.create || !X.init || !X.execute || !X.destroy) {
    Logf("xess: %s lacks Vulkan entry points: XeSS unavailable", path);
    return false;
  }
  XessVersion v{};
  X.version(&v);
  Logf("xess: %s, XeSS %u.%u.%u", path, v.major, v.minor, v.patch);
  return X.loaded = true;
}

void InstanceExtensions(std::vector<const char*>& ext) {
  if (!X.loaded) return;
  uint32_t ni = 0, api = 0;
  const char* const* ie = nullptr;
  if (!XessOk(X.instExts(&ni, &ie, &api))) { Logf("xess: no instance extension list: XeSS unavailable"); X.loaded = false; return; }
  for (uint32_t i = 0; i < ni; i++) if (!Listed(ext, ie[i])) ext.push_back(ie[i]);
}

bool DeviceExtensions(VkInstance inst, VkPhysicalDevice pd, std::vector<const char*>& ext, bool* needMutableDesc) {
  if (!X.loaded) return false;
  uint32_t nd = 0;
  const char* const* de = nullptr;
  if (!XessOk(X.devExts(inst, pd, &nd, &de))) { Logf("xess: no device extension list for this GPU: XeSS unavailable"); return false; }
  uint32_t n = 0;
  vkEnumerateDeviceExtensionProperties(pd, nullptr, &n, nullptr);
  std::vector<VkExtensionProperties> have(n);
  vkEnumerateDeviceExtensionProperties(pd, nullptr, &n, have.data());
  for (uint32_t i = 0; i < nd; i++) {
    bool ok = false;
    for (auto& h : have) if (!strcmp(h.extensionName, de[i])) { ok = true; break; }
    if (!ok) { Logf("xess: the device lacks %s: XeSS unavailable", de[i]); return false; }
  }
  void* chain = nullptr;
  if (!XessOk(X.devFeats(inst, pd, &chain))) { Logf("xess: no device feature list: XeSS unavailable"); return false; }
  for (const VkBaseOutStructure* s = (const VkBaseOutStructure*)chain; s; s = s->pNext) {
    size_t size = 0;
    if (!KnownFeature(s->sType, &size)) { Logf("xess: XeSS asks for features in structure %d, not enabled here: XeSS unavailable", (int)s->sType); return false; }
    if (!FeatureSupported(pd, s, size)) return false;
    if (s->sType == VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_PHYSICAL_DEVICE_MUTABLE_DESCRIPTOR_TYPE_FEATURES_EXT) *needMutableDesc = true;
  }
  for (uint32_t i = 0; i < nd; i++) if (!Listed(ext, de[i])) ext.push_back(de[i]);
  X.deviceOk = true;
  return true;
}

bool Init(const DeviceCtx& c) {
  if (!X.loaded || !X.deviceOk) return false;
  X.dc = c;
  return true;
}

bool Evaluate(const Eval& e) {
  if (!X.loaded || !X.deviceOk || X.failed) return false;
  const uint32_t flags = (e.hdr ? XESS_FLAG_AUTOEXPOSURE : XESS_FLAG_LDR) | (e.invDepth ? XESS_FLAG_INVERTED_DEPTH : 0u);
  if (!X.ctx) {
    const double t0 = NowMs();
    XessResult r = X.create(X.dc.instance, X.dc.phys, X.dc.device, &X.ctx);
    if (!XessOk(r) || !X.ctx) return Fail("context creation", r);
    if (X.setLog) X.setLog(X.ctx, XESS_LOG_WARNING, OnLog);
    if (X.build && !XessOk(r = X.build(X.ctx, VK_NULL_HANDLE, true, flags))) return Fail("pipeline build", r);
    Logf("xess: context made, pipelines built in %.0f ms", NowMs() - t0);
  }
  if (!(X.ow == e.ow && X.oh == e.oh && X.flags == flags && X.w == e.w && X.h == e.h)) {
    const int q = PickQuality(e.w, e.h, e.ow, e.oh);
    XessInit ip{};
    ip.outputResolution = {e.ow, e.oh}; ip.qualitySetting = q; ip.initFlags = flags;
    // XeSS may submit its own copies while it initialises: the caller holds the queue lock (replay), and the GPU must be done
    // with the previous size's work.
    if (X.ow) vkDeviceWaitIdle(X.dc.device);
    XessResult r = X.init(X.ctx, &ip);
    if (!XessOk(r)) return Fail("initialisation", r);
    X.w = e.w; X.h = e.h; X.ow = e.ow; X.oh = e.oh; X.flags = flags; X.quality = q;
    Logf("xess: %ux%u -> %ux%u, quality setting %d%s, %s colour", e.w, e.h, e.ow, e.oh, q, q == XESS_QUALITY_AA ? " (native AA)" : "", e.hdr ? "HDR" : "LDR");
  }
  XessExec p; memset(&p, 0, sizeof p);
  auto vw = [](const Image& m, VkImageAspectFlags a, uint32_t w, uint32_t h) { return XessView{m.view, m.image, {a, 0, 1, 0, 1}, m.format, w, h}; };
  p.color = vw(e.color, VK_IMAGE_ASPECT_COLOR_BIT, e.w, e.h);
  p.velocity = vw(e.mv, VK_IMAGE_ASPECT_COLOR_BIT, e.w, e.h);
  p.depth = vw(e.depth, VK_IMAGE_ASPECT_DEPTH_BIT, e.w, e.h);
  p.output = vw(e.out, VK_IMAGE_ASPECT_COLOR_BIT, e.ow, e.oh);
  p.jitterX = e.jx; p.jitterY = e.jy;
  p.exposureScale = 1.0f;
  p.resetHistory = e.reset ? 1u : 0u;
  p.inputWidth = e.w; p.inputHeight = e.h;
  XessResult r = X.execute(X.ctx, e.cb, &p);
  if (!XessOk(r)) return Fail("evaluation", r);
  X.evals++;
  return true;
}

void Release() {
  if (X.ctx) X.destroy(X.ctx);
  X.ctx = nullptr; X.w = X.h = X.ow = X.oh = 0;
}

}  // namespace snap_upscale::xess

```

`runtime/nvn/upscale/upscaler.h`:

```h
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
// Temporal upscalers for the NVN->Vulkan layer: NVIDIA DLSS / DLAA (the driver's NGX core), AMD FSR 3.1 (FidelityFX API,
// amd_fidelityfx_vk.dll) and Intel XeSS (libxess.dll). One front end (upscale.cpp) finds the scene in the replayed frame,
// jitters its draws, makes camera motion vectors and runs the chosen backend; the backends (upscale_dlss.cpp,
// upscale_fsr.cpp, upscale_xess.cpp) only bring their library up and record one evaluation.
//
// Settings (environment, read once at device creation):
//   SNAP_UPSCALER=off|dlss|dlaa|fsr|xess        dlaa = DLSS at the output size (same as dlss with quality native)
//   SNAP_UPSCALE_QUALITY=native|quality|balanced|performance
//       native: scene = output (DLAA / FSR native AA / XeSS AA); quality 1.5x, balanced ~1.724x, performance 2x per axis.
//   Output size is the window (SNAP_WINDOW_W/H); the game's 1920x1080 targets are scaled to the scene size and the window
//   textures (where the game draws its UI) to the output size.
//   A backend that cannot run falls back to the next in DLSS -> FSR -> XeSS order, then to plain render scale (logged).
//   Test knobs: SNAP_UPSCALE_JITTER=0 (no jitter), SNAP_UPSCALE_MV=0 (zero motion), SNAP_UPSCALE_LOG=1 (per-frame log).
//
// Photo safety: the jitter is applied only to draws into the scene depth target, never to the Evaluation depth target or
// photo passes; frames that run the Evaluation or a photo capture are rendered unjittered and are not upscaled (upscale.cpp,
// "photo frames").
#pragma once
#include <vulkan/vulkan.h>

#include <cstdint>
#include <vector>

namespace snap_upscale {

enum Backend : int { BK_OFF = 0, BK_DLSS = 1, BK_FSR = 2, BK_XESS = 3 };

// One evaluation, as the backends get it. Images are in the layouts named here and are left in them.
//   color, depth, mv: SHADER_READ_ONLY_OPTIMAL (depth: DEPTH_STENCIL_READ_ONLY_OPTIMAL); out: GENERAL.
struct Image {
  VkImage image = VK_NULL_HANDLE;
  VkImageView view = VK_NULL_HANDLE;
  VkFormat format = VK_FORMAT_UNDEFINED;
};
struct Eval {
  VkCommandBuffer cb = VK_NULL_HANDLE;
  Image color, depth, mv, out;
  uint32_t w = 0, h = 0, ow = 0, oh = 0;   // render (scene) size, output size
  float jx = 0, jy = 0;                    // jitter in render pixels, x right, y down (the shift of the picture)
  uint32_t phases = 16;                    // jitter sequence length
  bool reset = false;
  bool hdr = true;                         // linear scene light (auto exposure) vs tonemapped 0..1
  bool invDepth = false;                   // depth 1 = near (reversed z)
  bool infFar = false;                     // no far plane (infinite projection)
  float dtMs = 16.67f;
  float nearZ = 0.1f, farZ = 1000.0f, fovY = 0.6f;
};

struct DeviceCtx {
  VkInstance instance = VK_NULL_HANDLE;
  VkPhysicalDevice phys = VK_NULL_HANDLE;
  VkDevice device = VK_NULL_HANDLE;
  VkQueue queue = VK_NULL_HANDLE;
  uint32_t family = 0;
};

// ---- front end (upscale.cpp), called by the NVN layer -------------------------------------------------------------
// Device creation (nvn_vk.cpp Host::Init): instance extensions, then device extensions and features for every backend
// the setting may fall back to. `chainHead` receives extra feature structures (owned by this module) to link into pNext.
void AddInstanceExtensions(std::vector<const char*>& ext);
void AddDeviceExtensions(VkInstance inst, VkPhysicalDevice pd, std::vector<const char*>& ext, void** chainHead,
                         VkPhysicalDeviceVulkan11Features* f11, VkPhysicalDeviceVulkan12Features* f12,
                         VkPhysicalDeviceVulkan13Features* f13);
void DeviceCreated(const DeviceCtx& c);
void Shutdown();   // device idle

// Setting state (nvn_entry.cpp ApplyHostEnvPolicy): the scene scale and output scale relative to the game's 1920x1080.
bool Wanted();                 // SNAP_UPSCALER names a backend
float SceneScale(float outputScale);   // render scale for the game's scene targets (output scale times the quality ratio)
const char* Name();            // active backend name ("DLSS Quality", "off", ...)
int ActiveBackend();

// ---- backends ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Each: Load (library, before/after the instance as noted), extensions, Init after the device, Evaluate, Release.
namespace dlss {
bool LoadAfterInstance();   // the driver's NGX core beside NVIDIA's Vulkan ICD

}  // namespace fsr

`runtime/os/PROPOSED_SHARED_CHANGES.md`:

```md
# Proposed changes outside runtime/os

These changes are for the owners of `host/` and `runtime/` shared files. runtime/os does not edit those files itself. Most of the wiring is already in `host/boot.cpp`: `bind_host_layers`, `svc_dispatch` -> `os_svc`, `g_spin_gate_fn` = `os_spin_gate`, `g_ticks_fn` = `os_ticks`, and `os_adopt_main_thread` before the initializers. The items below are what is still missing.

## 1. Pass the musl thread-pointer hooks to OsConfig (host/boot.cpp, both os_init calls)

Without these, guest threads created through `nn::os::CreateThread` start with `tpidr_el0 = TLR[0x1f0] = 0`, so musl TLS and errno break on the first access. sdk's thread trampoline (sdk+0x348e80) calls the function stored in the data symbol `nnmuslThreadPointerInitializer` (sdk dynsym 0xd30c08) before the entry, and calls `nnmuslThreadPointerDestroyer` (0xd30c10) after it. runtime/os does the same when it knows where the variables are:

```cpp
OsConfig oc = {};
oc.tp_init_var    = lookup("nnmuslThreadPointerInitializer");   // address of the variable, not its value
oc.tp_destroy_var = lookup("nnmuslThreadPointerDestroyer");
```

`load()` runs before `os_init` today. Either call `os_init` after `load()` (no os call happens before then), or add a setter. If the setter is preferred, runtime/os will add `void os_set_thread_pointer_hooks(uint64_t init_var, uint64_t destroy_var);`.

## 2. Main thread: keep the os TLR

`os_adopt_main_thread(c, 0, -1)` replaces `c->tpidrro` with a TLR owned by runtime/os and sets TLR+0x1f8 itself. Two consequences:

- The fake ThreadType and TLR from `new_thread()` (host/loader.cpp:356) are unused once the main thread is adopted. They can be dropped for adopted threads.
- `boot.cpp` line 336 (`*(tpidrro+0x1f8) = os_current_thread_type()`) does nothing and is safe to remove. Line 335 (`TLR+0x1f0 = c->tpidr`) is still needed.

## 3. Resume flag after host-to-guest calls

runtime/os calls guest code in four places: the thread entry, TLS-slot destructors, the musl thread-pointer hooks and fiber functions. It does this through `rt_dispatch` with x30 set to a sentinel (`OS_RET_HOST`).

- **Exception escapes guest code:** `c->resuming` is set when control reaches runtime/os. runtime/os does not check it. It is treated as std::terminate, matching Horizon, where an uncaught exception in a thread entry aborts.
- **Wanted from the loader:** if the loader prefers a diagnostic, export `bool rt_take_resuming(Cpu*)` or similar. runtime/os will call it after each guest call and log the thread name.

## 4. Spin-loop polling in the lifter (recomp/patches.py `spin` list)

`rt_spin_gate` already forwards to `os_spin_gate` (`g_spin_gate_fn`). Its behavior:

- every pass runs `_mm_pause`;
- every 64 passes it yields the virtual core to an equal or better waiter;
- it always honors a pending preemption.

Loops that need it, in priority order:

1. `nn::os::BusyMutex` lock (sdk `LockBusyMutex`/`TryLockBusyMutex`). This is deliberately not overridden, because its state is a guest word that inline code also touches.
2. The job scheduler at main 0x548000-0x54f000. Its workers spin on LL/SC words before falling back to fibers.
3. LDAXR/STLXR retry loops that can fail forever when another thread holds a core: libc++ `__atomic` spin-waits and `std::call_once`.

Plain back-edges without a gate still progress. A thread that Horizon would run but that holds no core gets an overflow core after `overcommit_us` (2 ms). Without a gate, a spinning low-priority thread keeps its core until it blocks.

## 5. Build

`host/build_snap.py` globs `runtime/os/*.cpp`, so the new `os_memory.cpp` (VAMM and heap) is picked up with no change. The os sources must not be compiled with MSVC: `cpu.h` uses `__uint128_t`, and the os code uses GCC/clang `__atomic` builtins.

## 6. Precedence note for the nn::os table

All 197 names in `runtime/os/overrides.tsv` exist in sdk's dynsym; `nnos*` C wrappers are included only where they do more than branch. Two kinds of entry are worth knowing about:

- **`ThreadManager`, `TlsManager` and `VammManager` member functions:** they take `this` in x0, and the host ignores it. They are overridden because their lifted bodies dereference `OsResourceManager` (GOT sdk+0xc88838), which nothing constructs on the host. That null dereference is boot blocker 1 in `analysis/recomp/sdk_and_boot.md`.
- **`nn::os` entry points still lifted that read OsResourceManager:** `SuspendThread`, `ResumeThread`, `GetThreadContext`, `MapSharedMemory`, `MapTransferMemory`, `QueryMemoryInfo`, `AllocateUnsafeMemory`, the `InterProcessEvent`/`InterruptEvent` timed waits, and `nn::os::detail::TimeoutHelper::GetLeftTimeOnTarget`. None of them is on the boot path seen so far. Each would crash on the null singleton, so if a probe run reaches one, report it.

```

`runtime/os/hostprof.cpp`:

```cpp
// Host sampling profiler (load pass, 2026-11-13; debug only, off unless SNAP_HOST_PROF=<output file> is set).
// A host thread suspends every other thread of the process every SNAP_HOST_PROF_MS (default 2) ms, reads its RIP and resumes it.
// Samples between SNAP_HOST_PROF_FROM and SNAP_HOST_PROF_TO seconds (process time; default 0 and 1e9) go into a preallocated
// array (no allocation while a thread is suspended: it may hold the heap lock). Every 10 s and at the window end the file is
// rewritten as "<exe offset hex> <count>" lines (RIPs outside the exe as "ext <module offset> <count>" under a module line).
// Map offsets to lifted functions with analysis/perf/hostprof_report.py and build/<dir>/snap_boot.map.
#include <windows.h>
#include <tlhelp32.h>
#include <psapi.h>

#include <algorithm>
#include <atomic>
#include <cstdio>
#include <cstdlib>
#include <map>
#include <string>
#include <unordered_map>
#include <vector>

namespace {

struct Sample { uint64_t rip; uint32_t tid; };

struct HostProf {
    std::string path;
    double from = 0, to = 1e9;
    DWORD period_ms = 2;
    Sample *buf = nullptr;
    size_t cap = 0, n = 0;
    LARGE_INTEGER f0{}, freq{};

    double now() const {
        LARGE_INTEGER t; QueryPerformanceCounter(&t);
        return (double)(t.QuadPart - f0.QuadPart) / (double)freq.QuadPart;
    }

    void dump() {
        std::unordered_map<uint64_t, uint32_t> cnt;
        for (size_t i = 0; i < n; i++) cnt[buf[i].rip]++;
        HMODULE exe = GetModuleHandleW(nullptr);
        MODULEINFO mi{};
        GetModuleInformation(GetCurrentProcess(), exe, &mi, sizeof mi);
        const uint64_t lo = (uint64_t)mi.lpBaseOfDll, hi = lo + mi.SizeOfImage;
        std::map<std::string, uint64_t> ext;
        std::string tmp = path + ".tmp";
        FILE *f = fopen(tmp.c_str(), "w");
        if (!f) return;
        fprintf(f, "# samples %zu window %.1f-%.1f s period %lu ms\n", n, from, to, period_ms);
        for (auto &kv : cnt) {
            if (kv.first >= lo && kv.first < hi) { fprintf(f, "%llx %u\n", (unsigned long long)(kv.first - lo), kv.second); continue; }
            HMODULE m = nullptr;
            char name[MAX_PATH] = "?";
            if (GetModuleHandleExA(GET_MODULE_HANDLE_EX_FLAG_FROM_ADDRESS | GET_MODULE_HANDLE_EX_FLAG_UNCHANGED_REFCOUNT, (LPCSTR)kv.first, &m) && m)
                GetModuleBaseNameA(GetCurrentProcess(), m, name, sizeof name);
            ext[name] += kv.second;
        }
        for (auto &kv : ext) fprintf(f, "ext %s %llu\n", kv.first.c_str(), (unsigned long long)kv.second);
        fclose(f);
        MoveFileExA(tmp.c_str(), path.c_str(), MOVEFILE_REPLACE_EXISTING);
    }

    void run() {
        const DWORD self = GetCurrentThreadId(), pid = GetCurrentProcessId();
        std::unordered_map<DWORD, HANDLE> threads;
        std::unordered_map<DWORD, ULONG64> cycles;
        double next_scan = 0, next_dump = 10;
        bool final_done = false;
        for (;;) {
            Sleep(period_ms);
            const double t = now();
            if (t < from) continue;
            if (t > to) {
                if (!final_done) { dump(); final_done = true; }
                if (t > to + 1) return;
                continue;
            }
            if (t >= next_scan) {   // refresh the thread list twice a second
                next_scan = t + 0.5;
                HANDLE snap = CreateToolhelp32Snapshot(TH32CS_SNAPTHREAD, 0);
                if (snap != INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE) {
                    THREADENTRY32 te{sizeof te};
                    for (BOOL ok = Thread32First(snap, &te); ok; ok = Thread32Next(snap, &te))
                        if (te.th32OwnerProcessID == pid && te.th32ThreadID != self && !threads.count(te.th32ThreadID))
                            if (HANDLE h = OpenThread(THREAD_SUSPEND_RESUME | THREAD_GET_CONTEXT | THREAD_QUERY_INFORMATION, FALSE, te.th32ThreadID))
                                threads[te.th32ThreadID] = h;
                    CloseHandle(snap);
                }
                for (auto it = threads.begin(); it != threads.end();) {   // drop exited threads
                    DWORD code = 0;
                    if (!GetExitCodeThread(it->second, &code) || code != STILL_ACTIVE) { CloseHandle(it->second); it = threads.erase(it); }
                    else ++it;
                }
            }
            for (auto &kv : threads) {
                if (n >= cap) break;
                ULONG64 cyc = 0;   // only threads that ran since the last sample (blocked threads would all land in ntdll waits)
                QueryThreadCycleTime(kv.second, &cyc);
                ULONG64 &last = cycles[kv.first];
                const bool ran = cyc - last > 20000;
                last = cyc;
                if (!ran) continue;
                if (SuspendThread(kv.second) == (DWORD)-1) continue;
                CONTEXT c{};
                c.ContextFlags = CONTEXT_CONTROL;
                if (GetThreadContext(kv.second, &c)) buf[n++] = Sample{c.Rip, kv.first};
                ResumeThread(kv.second);
            }
            if (t >= next_dump) { next_dump = t + 10; dump(); }
        }
    }
};

HostProf *g_prof;

DWORD WINAPI prof_main(LPVOID) {
    g_prof->run();
    return 0;
}

struct Starter {
    Starter() {
        const char *p = getenv("SNAP_HOST_PROF");
        if (!p || !*p) return;
        g_prof = new HostProf;
        g_prof->path = p;
        if (const char *e = getenv("SNAP_HOST_PROF_FROM")) g_prof->from = atof(e);
        if (const char *e = getenv("SNAP_HOST_PROF_TO")) g_prof->to = atof(e);
        if (const char *e = getenv("SNAP_HOST_PROF_MS")) g_prof->period_ms = (DWORD)std::max(1, atoi(e));
        g_prof->cap = 8u << 20;   // 8 M samples (128 MB, demand-zero pages touched as used)
        g_prof->buf = (Sample *)VirtualAlloc(nullptr, g_prof->cap * sizeof(Sample), MEM_RESERVE | MEM_COMMIT, PAGE_READWRITE);
        if (!g_prof->buf) return;
        QueryPerformanceFrequency(&g_prof->freq);
        QueryPerformanceCounter(&g_prof->f0);
        if (HANDLE h = CreateThread(nullptr, 0, prof_main, nullptr, 0, nullptr)) {
            SetThreadPriority(h, THREAD_PRIORITY_HIGHEST);
            CloseHandle(h);
        }
    }
} g_starter;

}  // namespace

```

`runtime/os/os.h`:

```h
// Host implementation of the Horizon nn::os layer for New Pokemon Snap (written for this project; the override
// convention follows TotK Recomp runtime/host.h @ 7a37fc3, MIT, Copyright (c) 2026 Valiantsin Dzerakh).
//
// Public C interface used by the loader, the SVC backstop, other HLE modules and the tests. Everything else in
// runtime/os is internal. Design, guest layouts and evidence: docs/horizon-os.md.
//
// Model in one paragraph: every guest thread is one host thread with its own Cpu, a guest stack (the one the guest
// passed to CreateThread) and a 0x200-byte guest Thread Local Region (TLR) that c->tpidrro points at. nn::os APIs are
// replaced by mangled symbol (os_override_table) with host functions that keep the real guest object layouts
// up to date. Blocking goes through one host scheduler lock; lock words keep Horizon's owner-handle encoding so that
// lifted sdk code that still touches them (inline arbitration in ReaderWriterLockImpl, IsLockedByCurrentThread)
// agrees with the host. A guest thread runs guest code only while it holds one of three virtual cores.
#pragma once
#include <stddef.h>
#include <stdint.h>

#ifdef __cplusplus
extern "C" {   // cpu.h has no linkage guards; its rt_* services are C functions
#endif
#include "../cpu.h"

// ---- configuration (os_init). Zero-initialised fields take the defaults in brackets.
typedef struct OsConfig {
    int num_cores;               // virtual application cores [3]; -1 = unlimited (free host scheduling)
    int default_core;            // process default core, main.npdm META+0xF [0]
    int main_priority;           // nn::os priority of the adopted main thread; main.npdm META+0xE is kernel 44 -> [16]
    uint32_t overcommit_us;      // a ready thread that Horizon would run (it outranks a core holder, or round-robin is
                                 // due) and still has no core after this long runs on an overflow core [2000]
    uint32_t rr_slice_us;        // round-robin slice of the lowest priority (kernel 59 = nn::os 31) [10000]
    size_t host_stack_size;      // reserved host stack per guest thread; every guest BL is a host call [256 MiB]
    size_t fiber_host_stack;     // reserved host stack per guest fiber [64 MiB]
    uint64_t tp_init_var;        // guest address of sdk's nnmuslThreadPointerInitializer variable (0 = none)
    uint64_t tp_destroy_var;     // guest address of sdk's nnmuslThreadPointerDestroyer variable (0 = none)
    uint64_t tick_base;          // first GetSystemTick value [19.2e6 * 10, i.e. 10 s]
    int trace;                   // 1 = log thread starts/exits, overflow cores, unexpected states to stderr
} OsConfig;

void os_init(const OsConfig *cfg);   // once, before any other os_* call; cfg may be NULL

// ---- threads
// Makes the calling host thread a guest thread. tt = guest ThreadType address to use (0: the runtime allocates one
// and names it "MainThread"), prio = nn::os priority (-1: cfg main_priority). Sets c->tpidrro/c->thread and takes a
// virtual core. Use it for the guest main thread before nnMain / initializers.
void os_adopt_main_thread(Cpu *c, uint64_t tt, int prio);
// Releases the calling thread's virtual core while host code blocks outside guest code (GPU fence waits, file I/O,
// audio device waits). Must be paired, may nest. A host thread that is not a guest thread may call both freely.
void os_host_block_begin(void);
void os_host_block_end(void);
void os_io_begin(void);   // the same around blocking host I/O and retry sleeps, unless SNAP_SCHED_LEGACY=hostblock
void os_io_end(void);
uint64_t os_current_thread_type(void);   // guest ThreadType* of the calling thread, 0 if none

// ---- polling hooks for the lifter and the runtime (proposed wiring in runtime/os/PROPOSED_SHARED_CHANGES.md)
void os_spin_gate(Cpu *c, uint64_t head);   // body of rt_spin_gate: a pass of a spin-wait back-edge
void os_poll(void);                         // honour a pending preemption request (cheap when none)
uint64_t os_ticks(void);                    // cntpct_el0: 19.2 MHz guest ticks; body of rt_ticks
#define OS_TICK_FREQUENCY 19200000ull

// ---- events for HLE services (vi vsync, audio device notification, account async, ...)
// Initialise a guest nn::os::SystemEventType as an intra-process event (state byte +0x28 = 1) and signal or clear it
// from any host thread, guest or not. autoclear: 1 = EventClearMode_AutoClear.
void os_system_event_create(uint64_t sev, int autoclear);
void os_system_event_signal(uint64_t sev);
void os_system_event_clear(uint64_t sev);
void os_event_signal(uint64_t ev);           // the same for a plain nn::os::EventType
// Readable-event handles an HLE service returns to the guest (e.g. a vsync event). The guest binds them with
// nn::os::AttachSystemEvent; os_handle_signal signals every SystemEvent attached to the handle (returns how many).
uint32_t os_handle_alloc(void);
int os_handle_signal(uint32_t handle);

// ---- SVC backstop helpers: return 1 and set c->x[0]/w1 like the kernel if the SVC is handled, else 0.
// Covers the thread and arbitration SVCs that lifted sdk code can still reach (see docs/horizon-os.md).
int os_svc(Cpu *c, uint32_t imm);

// ---- override table: mangled symbol -> host function (TotK HOST_OVERRIDE convention: x0..x7 in, x0 out)
typedef struct OsOverride { const char *sym; GuestFn fn; } OsOverride;

    uint64_t threads_started, threads_exited;
    uint64_t lock_contended, cv_waits, core_waits, preempt_requests, preempt_yields, overflow_grants;
    uint64_t pi_boosts, fiber_switches, spin_yields;
    int max_cores_in_use;
    uint64_t core_wake_rescues;   // core waits ended by the safety-net timeout instead of a handoff (a lost wakeup; should stay 0)
    uint64_t core_starved;        // core waits longer than SNAP_OS_STARVE_MS (50) while another core was free (should stay 0)
    uint64_t migrate_requests, migrations, yield_any;   // holders asked to move to a free core / moved; yields to any thread
} OsStats;

// Internal interface of runtime/os (written for this project). The scheduler design follows the public Horizon
// kernel semantics (KConditionVariable, KAddressArbiter, KScheduler) and the shape of TotK Recomp runtime/kernel.c
// @ 7a37fc3 (MIT, Copyright (c) 2026 Valiantsin Dzerakh): one global scheduler lock, one host condition variable per
// thread, wake order = lower priority value first, then first come. No code is copied from it.
#pragma once
#include <atomic>
#include <chrono>
#include <condition_variable>

#include <cstring>

// ---- guest memory: guest addresses are host addresses (runtime/cpu.h)
template <class T> static inline T gld(uint64_t a) { T v; std::memcpy(&v, (const void *)(uintptr_t)a, sizeof v); return v; }
template <class T> static inline void gst(uint64_t a, T v) { std::memcpy((void *)(uintptr_t)a, &v, sizeof v); }
static inline std::atomic<uint32_t> &gword(uint64_t a) { return *reinterpret_cast<std::atomic<uint32_t> *>((uintptr_t)a); }
static inline uint8_t gld8a(uint64_t a) { return __atomic_load_n((uint8_t *)(uintptr_t)a, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE); }
static inline void gst8a(uint64_t a, uint8_t v) { __atomic_store_n((uint8_t *)(uintptr_t)a, v, __ATOMIC_RELEASE); }
static inline int32_t gld32a(uint64_t a) { return __atomic_load_n((int32_t *)(uintptr_t)a, __ATOMIC_ACQUIRE); }
static inline void gst32a(uint64_t a, int32_t v) { __atomic_store_n((int32_t *)(uintptr_t)a, v, __ATOMIC_RELEASE); }

constexpr uint64_t OS_RET_HOST = 0x70200ff000ull;   // x30 sentinel of host->guest calls (same value as TotK RT_RET_HOST)
constexpr int64_t NS_INFINITE = INT64_MAX;
constexpr uint32_t R_OK = 0, R_TIMEOUT = oslay::RESULT_TIMED_OUT, R_INVALID_HANDLE = 0xe401, R_INVALID_STATE = 0xfa01;
constexpr uint32_t PSEUDO_CURRENT_THREAD = 0xffff8000u;
constexpr uint32_t PSEUDO_CURRENT_PROCESS = 0xffff8001u;
constexpr uint32_t R_INVALID_ENUM_VALUE = 0x7801, R_INVALID_COMBINATION = 0xe001;   // svc module 1, desc 60 / 112
// svcGetInfo memory-region values (os_memory.cpp): types 2-7, 12-17, 21, 22; returns R_OK or the Horizon result.
uint32_t mem_get_info(uint32_t type, uint64_t *out);

enum Wait : int { W_NONE, W_LOCK, W_CVAR, W_KEY, W_JOIN, W_MULTI, W_SLEEP };
// keyed wait queues: a key is the guest address plus the queue kind in the top byte (guest addresses are < 2^48)
enum KeyKind : uint64_t { K_CVAR = 1, K_LIGHT = 2, K_JOIN = 3, K_MULTI = 4, K_RW = 5, K_TIMER = 6, K_JOINERS = 7 };
static inline uint64_t mkkey(KeyKind k, uint64_t addr) { return addr | ((uint64_t)k << 56); }

struct Fiber;

struct Thread {
    uint64_t tt = 0;                 // guest ThreadType
    uint32_t handle = 0;
    uint64_t id = 0;
    uint8_t *tlr = nullptr;          // guest TLR (0x200 bytes, 0x200-aligned)
    Cpu *cpu = nullptr;              // the thread's own context
    Cpu *cur = nullptr;              // the context running now (own or a fiber's)
    bool is_host = false;            // a host helper thread adopted on first use: holds no virtual core
    bool owns_tt = false;            // tt was allocated by the runtime
    uint64_t entry = 0, arg = 0;
    // scheduling (under G)
    int base_prio = 16, eff_prio = 16;
    int ideal = 0;
    uint64_t mask = 1;
    int core = -1, last_core = 0;
    uint64_t core_since = 0, ready_seq = 0;
    int block_depth = 0;
    std::atomic<int> preempt{0};
    bool waiting_core = false;
    bool core_kicked = false;        // a core handoff notify arrived since the waiter last checked (rescue accounting)
    uint64_t core_wait_since = 0;    // now_us() when the current core wait began (watchdog dump, starvation detector)
    uint64_t humble_until = 0;       // after a yield to any thread: do not preempt lower-priority holders before this (now_us)
    int joiners = 0;                 // threads inside thread_wait_exit on this thread (thread_destroy waits for them to leave)
    // current wait (under G)
    std::condition_variable cv;
    int wkind = W_NONE;
    uint64_t wkey = 0, waddr = 0, wseq = 0;
    uint32_t wtag = 0, wresult = 0;
    bool woken = false;
    char waker_name[24] = {};                // name and priority of the thread that last woke this one (perf only; a copy,
    int waker_prio = -1;                     // since the waker may be destroyed before the wait is reported)
    Thread *lock_owner = nullptr;            // W_LOCK: the thread whose lock we wait for
    std::vector<Thread *> lock_waiters;      // threads in W_LOCK on locks we own (priority inheritance)
    // lifecycle
    std::atomic<int> started{0}, exited{0};
    void *host_thread = nullptr;
    // fibers (Win32 host fibers)
    void *base_fiber = nullptr;
    uint64_t own_fiber = 0;                  // guest FiberType standing for the thread's own context
    Fiber *own_shadow = nullptr;
    Fiber *cur_fiber = nullptr;              // nullptr = own context
    Fiber *leaving = nullptr;                // context just switched away from, released once the next one runs
};

struct Fiber {
    uint64_t guest = 0;
    Cpu *cpu = nullptr;
    void *host = nullptr;                    // Win32 fiber
    bool finished = false;                   // its function returned; needs InitializeFiber before reuse
    bool is_thread_ctx = false;              // stands for a thread's own context
    std::atomic<bool> running{false};        // claimed by a thread; released by the next context ("leaving")
};

struct Config {
    int num_cores = 3, default_core = 0, main_priority = 16;
    int app_cores = 3;   // load pass: cores app_cores..num_cores-1 are spare cores (SNAP_OS_SPARE_CORES) any thread may use, whatever its mask
    uint32_t overcommit_us = 2000, rr_slice_us = 10000;
    uint32_t core_rescue_ms = 20;   // an untimed core wait rechecks this often (safety net; counted in core_wake_rescues)
    uint32_t legacy = 0;            // SNAP_SCHED_LEGACY: LG_* bits that restore the pre-2026-11-13 scheduler paths
    uint32_t starve_ms = 50;        // SNAP_OS_STARVE_MS: a core wait this long while a core is free counts in core_starved
    int starve_log = 0;             // SNAP_OS_STARVE_LOG=1: also log each such wait
    uint32_t yield_any_us = 1000;   // SNAP_OS_YIELD_ANY_US: after a yield to any thread, how long the yielder does not preempt it
    size_t host_stack = 256ull << 20, fiber_host_stack = 64ull << 20;
    uint64_t tp_init_var = 0, tp_destroy_var = 0, tick_base = OS_TICK_FREQUENCY * 10;
    int trace = 0;
};
extern Config g_cfg;
// SNAP_SCHED_LEGACY=1|all, or a comma list of the names below: old behavior for that part (review_os.md, 2026-11-13).
enum : uint32_t {
    LG_MIGRATE = 1,      // "migrate": no core migration for pinned waiters (finding 1)
    LG_YIELD_ANY = 2,    // "yield": spin gate and svcSleepThread(-2) yield only to equal or better priority (finding 2)
    LG_UNBOOST = 4,      // "unboost": a holder whose priority gets worse does not notify core waiters (finding 3)
    LG_DEADLINE = 8,     // "deadline": the overflow deadline is armed once per core wait (finding 10)
    LG_HOST_BLOCK = 16,  // "hostblock": VAMM retry sleeps and file reads keep the virtual core (finding 9)
    LG_EVENTS = 32,      // "events": manual-clear TimerEvent/LightEvent waiters re-check only the flag (finding 11)
};
static inline bool legacy(uint32_t bit) { return (g_cfg.legacy & bit) != 0; }
struct Stats {
    std::atomic<uint64_t> threads_started{0}, threads_exited{0}, lock_contended{0}, cv_waits{0}, core_waits{0},
        preempt_requests{0}, preempt_yields{0}, overflow_grants{0}, pi_boosts{0}, fiber_switches{0}, spin_yields{0},
        core_wake_rescues{0},   // a core waiter found a free core on its safety-net timeout: a missed handoff (should stay 0)
        core_starved{0},        // core waits longer than starve_ms while another core was free (finding 1 detector)
        migrate_requests{0}, migrations{0}, yield_any{0};
    std::atomic<int> max_cores_in_use{0};
};
extern Stats g_stats;
